children.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> (latter part) of the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s> with commentary.
Salutation to <s>Śrī Gaṇeśa</s>.
The sages said:
By what means is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> pleased here, the Lord of all lords of gods?
Please tell us, O <s>Sūta</s>, you who are knowledgeable in all matters. (LiP 2,1.1)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Formerly, the great sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> of great splendor was asked

children.text: aṃbarīṣeṇa viprendrās tad vadāmi yathātatham // LiP_2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, O best of Brahmins — I shall tell that as it truly was. (LiP 2,1.2)
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:
O Sage, you who have crossed to the far shore of all <s>dharmas</s>, O Great-Minded One,
O <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, you are ancient, skilled in the meaning of the <s>Purāṇas</s>. (LiP 2,1.3)
Among the divine <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, [tell me] the best and supreme,

children.text: tatkiṃ brūhi mahāprājña bhaktānāmiha suvrata // LiP_2,1.4 //
children.translated_text: tell us that, O greatly wise one, for devotees here, O one of excellent vows. (LiP 2,1.4)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard his words, rising with folded hands,

children.text: smaran nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ kṛṣṇam acyutam avyayam // LiP_2,1.5 //
children.translated_text: remembering Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the imperishable, the immutable — (LiP 2,1.5)
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Hear, O King, according to propriety, the sacred [teaching] centered on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>:

children.text: smaraṇaṃ pūjanaṃ caiva praṇāmo bhaktipūrvakam // LiP_2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: remembrance, worship, and prostration performed with devotion — (LiP 2,1.6)
each one is said to be equal to the <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifice.

children.text: ya ekaḥ puruṣaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ paramātmā janārdanaḥ // LiP_2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: He who is the one supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Supreme Self, <s>Janārdana</s>, (LiP 2,1.7)
from whom [comes] <s>Brahmā</s>, and then all — by taking refuge in him alone, one is liberated.

children.text: dharmamekaṃ pravakṣyāmi yaddṛṣṭaṃ viditaṃ mayā // LiP_2,1.8 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare one <s>dharma</s> which I have seen and known: (LiP 2,1.8)

children.text: purā tretāyuge kaścit kauśiko nāma vai dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: Formerly, in the <s>Tretā Yuga</s>, there was a certain Brahmin named <s>Kauśika</s>,
perpetually devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, always delighting in singing the <s>Sāman</s>. (LiP 2,1.9)
In eating, sitting, and sleeping, his mind always fixed on Him,

children.text: udāracaritaṃ viṣṇor gāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,1.10 //
children.translated_text: singing the noble deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s> again and again. (LiP 2,1.10)
Having reached a sacred place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme abode of <s>Hari</s>,
he sang of <s>Hari</s> there, endowed with rhythm, melody, and tempo. (LiP 2,1.11)
With the union of <s>mūrchanā</s> [melodic progressions] and notes, differentiated by distinctions of <s>śruti</s> [microtones],

children.text: bhaktiyogaṃ samāpanno bhikṣāmātraṃ hi tatra vai // LiP_2,1.12 //
children.translated_text: attaining the yoga of devotion (<s>bhaktiyoga</s>), subsisting there on mere alms. (LiP 2,1.12)
Seeing him singing thus, a certain Brahmin at that time,

children.text: padmākhya iti vikhyātastasmai cānnaṃ dadau tadā // LiP_2,1.13 //
children.translated_text: renowned by the name <s>Padmākṣa</s>, gave him food then. (LiP 2,1.13)

children.text: sakuṭuṃbo mahātejā hyuṣṇamannaṃ hi tatra vai /
children.translated_text: With his family, of great splendor, [he gave] hot food there;

children.text: kauśiko hi tāda hṛṣṭo gāyannāste hariṃ prabhum // LiP_2,1.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, delighted then, continued singing of Lord <s>Hari</s>. (LiP 2,1.14)

children.text: śṛṇvannāste sa padmākhyaḥ kāle kāle vinirgataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Padmākṣa</s> would sit listening, going out from time to time;

children.text: kālayogena saṃprāptāḥ śiṣyā vai kauśikasya ca // LiP_2,1.15 //
children.translated_text: by the course of time, disciples of <s>Kauśika</s> arrived. (LiP 2,1.15)
Seven, born from families of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and Brahmins,
endowed with superior knowledge and learning, pure, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>. (LiP 2,1.16)

children.text: teṣām api tathānnādyaṃ padmākṣaḥ pradadau svayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Padmākṣa</s> himself gave food to them as well;

children.text: śiṣyaiśca sahito nityaṃ kauśiko hṛṣṭamānasaḥ // LiP_2,1.17 //
children.translated_text: together with his disciples, <s>Kauśika</s>, perpetually joyful at heart, (LiP 2,1.17)
stayed at the sacred place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, singing of <s>Hari</s> there according to proper method.

children.text: tatraiva mālavo nāma vaiśyo viṣṇuparāyaṇaḥ // LiP_2,1.18 //
children.translated_text: There too [was] a <s>Vaiśya</s> named <s>Mālava</s>, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, (LiP 2,1.18)
who perpetually offered garlands of lamps to <s>Hari</s>, with a pleased heart.

children.text: mālavī nāma bhāryā ca tasya nityaṃ pativratā // LiP_2,1.19 //
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Mālavī</s>, was perpetually faithful to her husband. (LiP 2,1.19)
Having smeared the sacred ground of <s>Hari</s> all around with cow-dung,

children.text: bhartrā sahāste suprītā śṛṇvatī gānamuttamam // LiP_2,1.20 //
children.translated_text: she stayed delighted with her husband, listening to the excellent singing. (LiP 2,1.20)
From <s>Kuśasthala</s> came Brahmins of praised vows,
fifty arrived, excellent [devotees], for the purpose of singing to <s>Hari</s>. (LiP 2,1.21)
Accomplishing the affairs of the great-souled <s>Kauśika</s>,
knowers of the truth of knowledge and learning, they stayed listening. (LiP 2,1.22)

children.text: khyātamāsīttadā tasya gānaṃ vai kauśikasya tat /
children.translated_text: The singing of <s>Kauśika</s> became famous at that time;

children.text: śrutvā rājā samabhyetya kaliṅgo vākyamabravīt // LiP_2,1.23 //
children.translated_text: having heard [of it], a king named <s>Kaliṅga</s>, approaching, spoke these words: (LiP 2,1.23)

children.text: kauśikādya gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ gāyasveha ca māṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Kauśika</s>, with your company, sing here for me now;

children.text: śṛṇudhvaṃ ca tathā yūyaṃ kuśasthalajanā api // LiP_2,1.24 //
children.translated_text: and you too should listen, O people of <s>Kuśasthala</s>." (LiP 2,1.24)

children.text: tacchrutvā kauśikaḥ prāha rājānaṃ sāṃtvayā girā /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kauśika</s> replied to the king with a gentle voice:

children.text: na jihvā me mahārājan vāṇī ca mama sarvadā // LiP_2,1.25 //
children.translated_text: "O Great King, my tongue and my voice at all times (LiP 2,1.25)

children.text: hareranyamapindraṃ vā stauti naiva ca vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: never praise and never will speak of any lord other than <s>Hari</s>."

children.text: evamukte tu tacchiṣyo vāsiṣṭho gautamo hariḥ // LiP_2,1.26 //
children.translated_text: When this was said, his disciples — <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Hari</s>, (LiP 2,1.26)
<s>Sārasvata</s>, and also <s>Citra</s>, <s>Citramālya</s>, and <s>Śiśu</s> —

children.text: ūcuste pārthivaṃ tadvadyathā prāha ca kauśikaḥ // LiP_2,1.27 //
children.translated_text: spoke likewise to the king, just as <s>Kauśika</s> had said. (LiP 2,1.27)
The listeners too, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, told the king:

children.text: śrotrāṇīmāni śṛṇvanti hareranyaṃ na pārthiva // LiP_2,1.28 //
children.translated_text: "These ears hear [only of] <s>Hari</s> — of no other, O King. (LiP 2,1.28)

children.text: gānakīrtiṃ vayaṃ tasya śṛṇumonyāṃ na ca stutim /
children.translated_text: We listen to the singing glory of Him — not to any other praise."

children.text: tacchrutvā pārthivo ruṣṭo gāyatāmiti cābravīt // LiP_2,1.29 //
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the angry king said, "Sing!" (LiP 2,1.29)

children.text: svabhṛtyānbrāhmaṇā hyete kīrtiṃ śṛṇvanti me yathā /
children.translated_text: "These Brahmins are my subjects; they should hear my glory as

children.text: na śṛṇvanti kathaṃ tasmāt gāyamāne samantataḥ // LiP_2,1.30 //
children.translated_text: they listen — why do they not, when [someone] is singing all around?" (LiP 2,1.30)
Thus commanded, the servants sang [the praises of] the excellent king;

children.text: niruddhamārgā viprāste gāne vṛtte tu duḥkhitāḥ // LiP_2,1.31 //
children.translated_text: the Brahmins, with their path obstructed, were distressed while the singing proceeded. (LiP 2,1.31)
The Brahmins plugged each other's ears with wooden pegs;

children.text: kauśikādyāśca tāṃ jñātvā manovṛttiṃ nṛpasya vai // LiP_2,1.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s> and the others, knowing the king's intention, (LiP 2,1.32)
[thought:] "He will forcibly make us sing — this king is determined about his own glory."

children.text: iti viprāḥ suniyatā jihvāgraṃ cicchiduḥ karaiḥ // LiP_2,1.33 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the disciplined Brahmins cut off the tips of their tongues with their hands. (LiP 2,1.33)
Then the king, greatly enraged, banished them from his territory,

children.text: ādāya sarvaṃ vittaṃ ca tataste jagmuruttarām // LiP_2,1.34 //
children.translated_text: seizing all their wealth — and they went to the northern (LiP 2,1.34)

children.text: tānāgatānyamo dṛṣṭvā kiṃ kartavyamiti sma ha // LiP_2,1.35 /
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, seeing them arrived, [wondered] "What is to be done?" (LiP 2,1.35)

children.text: coṣṭitaṃ tatkṣaṇe rājan brahmā prāha surādhipān /
children.translated_text: At that instant, O King, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to the lords of the gods:
"Settle <s>Kauśika</s> and the other Brahmins comfortably now! (LiP 2,1.36)
Those who perpetually worship <s>Janārdana</s> through the yoga of singing —

children.text: tānānayata bhadraṃ vo yadi devatvamicchatha // LiP_2,1.37 //
children.translated_text: bring them; may it be well with you, if you desire godhood." (LiP 2,1.37)
direction. In time, joined by the law of time [death],
Thus addressed, the world-guardians, crying out "<s>Kauśika</s>!" again and again,

children.text: mālaveti tathā kecit padmākṣeti tathā pare // LiP_2,1.38 //
children.translated_text: some [calling] "<s>Mālava</s>!" and others "<s>Padmākṣa</s>!" (LiP 2,1.38)
calling out, approaching, and taking them through the sky,

children.text: brahmalokaṃ gatāḥ śīghraṃ muhūrtenaiva te surāḥ // LiP_2,1.39 //
children.translated_text: those gods went quickly to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, in just a moment. (LiP 2,1.39)
Then, seeing <s>Kauśika</s> and the others, <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the world,
went out to receive them and honored them properly with [the cry of] "Welcome!" (LiP 2,1.40)
Then there arose a great commotion, of extreme solemnity,

children.text: brahmaṇā caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā devānāṃ nṛpasattama // LiP_2,1.41 //
children.translated_text: the gods seeing the conduct of <s>Brahmā</s>, O Best of Kings. (LiP 2,1.41)
Lord <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> [Brahmā], restraining those best of gods,
taking <s>Kauśika</s> and the other sages, surrounded by gods, (LiP 2,1.42)
went quickly to <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
There, Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with the residents of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, (LiP 2,1.43)
with <s>siddhas</s> who are lords of <s>jñānayoga</s>, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, concentrated,
divine beings resembling <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, auspicious, bearing four arms, (LiP 2,1.44)
endowed with the marks of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, radiant, sinless,
being served by eighty-eight thousand great beings, (LiP 2,1.45)
by us, by <s>Nārada</s> and others, by <s>Sanaka</s> and others who are sinless,
by various beings, and by divine women all around — (LiP 2,1.46)
being served in the midst, enclosed by a thousand doors,
extending a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, divine, made of gems, auspicious, (LiP 2,1.47)
in a celestial chariot, pure and wondrous, on an auspicious throne — [sat] <s>Hari</s>,
<s>Mādhava</s>, his gaze fixed upon those engaged in the affairs of the worlds. (LiP 2,1.48)
At that time, Lord [Brahmā], surrounded by <s>Kauśika</s> and the others,
approaching and bowing before him, praised the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>. (LiP 2,1.49)
Then, looking upon them, Lord <s>Hari</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Master,
said "<s>Kauśika</s>!" with affection, and [addressed] all of them in order. (LiP 2,1.50)
A great cry of "Victory!" arose as the great wonder unfolded;

children.text: brahmāṇamāha viśvātmā śṛṇu brahman mayoditam // LiP_2,1.51 //
children.translated_text: the Soul of the Universe said to <s>Brahmā</s>: "Hear what I declare, O <s>Brahmā</s>. (LiP 2,1.51)
These Brahmins of <s>Kauśika</s>, devoted to the goal and its means,
have set forth for [the world's] welfare, residents of <s>Kuśasthala</s>. (LiP 2,1.52)
Devoted to hearing My glory, skilled in the truth of knowledge,
having devotion to no other deity — let these become gods of the <s>Sādhya</s> [class]." (LiP 2,1.53)
"Bearing a divine form, glorious, hearing the singing here as lord,

children.text: āsva nityaṃ yathākāmaṃ yāvallokā bhavanti vai // LiP_2,1.54 //
children.translated_text: dwell perpetually as you wish, as long as the worlds endure. (LiP 2,1.54)
The Lord said to <s>Padmākṣa</s>: "Become a bestower of wealth, O <s>Mādhava</s>;

children.text: dhanānāmīśvaro bhūtvā yathākālaṃ hi māṃ punaḥ // LiP_2,1.55 //
children.translated_text: having become lord of riches, come again to Me in due time." (LiP 2,1.55)

children.text: mālabaṃ mālavīṃ caivaṃ prāha dāmodaro hariḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s> <s>Hari</s> spoke thus to <s>Mālava</s> and <s>Mālavī</s>:

children.text: mama loke yathākālaṃ bhāryayā saha mālava // LiP_2,1.56 //
children.translated_text: "In My world, in due time, together with your wife, O <s>Mālava</s>, (LiP 2,1.56)
bearing a divine form, glorious, hearing the singing here as lord,

children.text: āsva nityaṃ yathākāmaṃ yāvallokā bhavanti vai // LiP_2,1.57 //
children.translated_text: dwell perpetually as you wish, as long as the worlds endure." (LiP 2,1.57)
The Lord said to <s>Padmākṣa</s>: "Become a bestower of wealth, O <s>Mādhava</s>;

children.text: dhanānāmīśvaro bhūtvā yathākālaṃ hi māṃ punaḥ // LiP_2,1.58 //
children.translated_text: having become lord of riches, come again to Me in due time; (LiP 2,1.58)

children.text: āgamya dṛṣṭvā māṃ nityaṃ kuru rājyaṃ yathāsukham /
children.translated_text: coming, seeing Me perpetually, rule your kingdom happily."
Having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> said this to <s>Brahmā</s>: (LiP 2,1.59)

children.text: kauśikasyāsya gānena yoganidrā ca me gatā /
children.translated_text: "By the singing of this <s>Kauśika</s>, My <s>yoganidrā</s> [cosmic sleep] has departed;

children.text: viṣṇusthale ca māṃ stauti śiṣyaireṣa samantataḥ // LiP_2,1.60 //
children.translated_text: at <s>Viṣṇusthala</s>, he praises Me, surrounded by his disciples. (LiP 2,1.60)
Banished by the cruel king <s>Kaliṅga</s>, the mighty one,

children.text: sa jihvācchedanaṃ kṛtvā hareranyaṃ kathañcana // LiP_2,1.61 //
children.translated_text: having cut off his tongue, [declaring:] 'I shall never (LiP 2,1.61)

children.text: na stoṣyāmīti niyataḥ prāptosau mama lokatām /
children.translated_text: praise anyone other than <s>Hari</s>' — thus resolved, he has attained My world.

children.text: ete ca viprā niyatā mama bhaktā yaśasvinaḥ // LiP_2,1.62 //
children.translated_text: These disciplined Brahmins are My devoted, glorious [servants]. (LiP 2,1.62)
Piercing the openings of their ears with pegs, [they declared to] each other:

children.text: śroṣyāmo naiva cānyadvai hareḥ kīrtimitisma ha // LiP_2,1.63 //
children.translated_text: 'We shall never hear anything other than the glory of <s>Hari</s>.' (LiP 2,1.63)

children.text: ete viprāsca devatvaṃ mama sānnidhyameva ca /
children.translated_text: These Brahmins [have attained] divinity and My very presence.

children.text: mālavo bhāryayā sārdhaṃ matkṣetraṃ parimṛjya vai // LiP_2,1.64 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mālava</s>, together with his wife, having swept My sacred ground, (LiP 2,1.64)
with garlands of lamps and other [offerings], perpetually worshipping Me constantly,
listens to the singing, disciplined, filled with My glory and deeds — (LiP 2,1.65)
by that, he has attained My eternal world, O <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: padmākṣosau dadau bhojyaṃ kauśikasya mahātmanaḥ // LiP_2,1.66 //
children.translated_text: <s>Padmākṣa</s> gave food to the great-souled <s>Kauśika</s>; (LiP 2,1.66)
he has obtained lordship over wealth and My very presence."
Having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s>, honored by the worlds, in that assembly — (LiP 2,1.67)
at that moment, arrived [she] with sweet and skillful words,
skilled in the principles of the <s>vīṇā</s> strings, expert in the art of music, (LiP 2,1.68)
the Goddess, gently smiling, adorned with various ornaments,
singing as she came — <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (LiP 2,1.69)
Surrounded by a thousand crores of women all around.
Then, seeing the chiefs of the <s>gaṇas</s>, armed with <s>bhuśuṇḍī</s> [mace] and <s>parigha</s> [iron club] weapons, (LiP 2,1.70)
threatening <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, the sages and gods all around,
clearing the way, delighted, standing firm like mountains — (LiP 2,1.71)

children.text: sarve vayaṃ hi niryātāḥ sārdhaṃ vai brahmaṇā suraiḥ /
children.translated_text: we all came out, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and the gods.
At that moment, the great sage <s>Tumburu</s> was summoned. (LiP 2,1.72)

children.text: praviveśa samīpaṃ vai devyā devasya caiva hi /
children.translated_text: He entered into the presence of the Goddess and the God;
seated there as was fitting, endowed with various melodic progressions (<s>mūrcchā</s>), (LiP 2,1.73)
he sang delightfully in measured syllables and played the <s>vīṇā</s>.
Adorned with various jewels and the finest divine ornaments, (LiP 2,1.74)
honored with divine garlands, bright and auspicious, the best of sages,

children.text: nirgatastuṃbarurhṛṣṭo anye ca ṛṣayaḥ surāḥ // LiP_2,1.75 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> departed joyfully, along with other sages and gods. (LiP 2,1.75)
Seeing him worshipped and departing in fitting manner, O subduer of foes,

children.text: nāradotha munirdṛṣṭvā tuṃbaroḥ satkriyāṃ hareḥ // LiP_2,1.76 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s>, the sage, having seen the honor shown to <s>Tumburu</s> by <s>Hari</s>, (LiP 2,1.76)
with a mind overcome by grief, his heart and eyes burning with anguish,
fell into anxious thought there, overwhelmed by the swoon of sorrow. (LiP 2,1.77)
'By what means shall I attain union with the Goddess in <s>Hari</s>'s presence?

children.text: aho tuṃbaruṇā prāptaṃ dhiṅmāṃ mūḍhaṃ vicetasam // LiP_2,1.78 //
children.translated_text: Alas, what <s>Tumburu</s> has obtained! Shame on me, the fool, the witless one! (LiP 2,1.78)
I, who was near <s>Hari</s>, was driven out by the <s>Bhūtas</s> — how?
Where shall I live now? Alas, what <s>Tumburu</s> has done!' (LiP 2,1.79)
Thus pondering, the brahmin sage undertook austerity,
for a divine thousand years, holding his breath. (LiP 2,1.80)
Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he sat remembering the honor shown to <s>Tumburu</s>,

children.text: rodamāno muhurvidvān dhiṅmāmiti ca cintayan // LiP_2,1.81 //
children.translated_text: weeping repeatedly, the learned one, thinking 'Shame on me!' (LiP 2,1.81)
What <s>Viṣṇu</s> did there — hear that, O King. (LiP 2,1.82)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge kauśikavṛttakathanaṃ nāma prathamodhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled 'The Narration of <s>Kauśika</s>'s Story.'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: tato nārāyaṇo devastasmai sarvaṃ pradāya vai /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the God, having given everything to him,

children.text: kālayogena viśvatmā samaṃ cakre 'tha tuṃbaroḥ // LiP_2,2.1 //
children.translated_text: by the course of time, the Soul of the Universe, made [<s>Nārada</s>] equal to <s>Tumburu</s>. (LiP 2,2.1)
<s>Nārada</s>, the tiger among sages — thus it happened long ago:

children.text: nārāyaṇasya gītānāṃ gānaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,2.2 //
children.translated_text: the singing of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s songs, the best singing, again and again. (LiP 2,2.2)
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, propitiated by song, bestowing fame, knowledge, and splendor,

children.text: dadāti tuṣṭiṃ sthānaṃ ca yathāsau kauśikasya vai // LiP_2,2.3 //
children.translated_text: grants satisfaction and a [heavenly] abode, just as he did for <s>Kauśika</s>. (LiP 2,2.3)
To <s>Padmākṣa</s> and others too, <s>Hari</s> granted perfection.
Therefore, by you, O great king, especially at <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s sacred site, (LiP 2,2.4)
worship, singing, dancing, and the like, accompanied by music and festivals,
should be performed constantly by devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O King. (LiP 2,2.5)

children.text: śrotavyaṃ ca sadā nityaṃ śrotavyosau haristathā /
children.translated_text: One should always listen unceasingly; <s>Hari</s> too should be listened to.

children.text: viṣṇukṣetre tu yo vidvān kārayedbhaktisaṃyutaḥ // LiP_2,2.6 //
children.translated_text: And the learned one who, at <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s sacred site, with devotion causes to be performed (LiP 2,2.6)
singing, dancing, and the like, and the narration of stories about <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: jatismṛtiṃ ca medhāṃ ca tathaivoparame smṛtim // LiP_2,2.7 //
children.translated_text: he obtains memory of past births, intellect, and at death, remembrance; (LiP 2,2.7)
he attains union with <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the truth, O Lord of Kings.

children.text: etatte kathitaṃ rājan yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi // LiP_2,2.8 //
children.translated_text: This has been told to you, O King, what you ask of me. (LiP 2,2.8)

children.text: kiṃ vadāmi ca te bhūto vada dharmabhṛtāṃ vara // LiP_2,2.9 //
children.translated_text: What more shall I tell you? Speak, O best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>! (LiP 2,2.9)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge viṣṇumāhātmyaṃ nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled '<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s Greatness.'
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:
O <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, great sage, by what means did
the illustrious sage <s>Nārada</s> obtain the art of song? (LiP 2,3.1)
And when did he attain equality with <s>Tumburu</s>?

children.text: etadācakṣva me sarvaṃ sarvajñosi mahāmate // LiP_2,3.2 //
children.translated_text: Tell me all this — you are omniscient, O great-minded one! (LiP 2,3.2)
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
I heard this matter from <s>Nārada</s> himself, the seer of the gods.
He himself, of great splendor, that <s>Nārada</s> of great wisdom — (LiP 2,3.3)
the illustrious one, performing austerity for a divine thousand years,
holding his breath, remembering the greatness of <s>Tumburu</s> — (LiP 2,3.4)
he performed the most terrible supreme austerity, a treasury of <s>tapas</s>.
Then in the sky, that great sage <s>Nārada</s> heard (LiP 2,3.5)
a divine voice, of great resonance, wondrous and bodiless:
'For what purpose, O tiger among sages, do you perform this difficult austerity? (LiP 2,3.6)

children.text: ulūkaṃ paśya gatvā tvaṃ yadi gāne ratā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Go and see the Owl, if your mind is set on song.
On Mount <s>Mānasottara</s>, he is known as <s>Gānabandhu</s> (Friend of Song). (LiP 2,3.7)

children.text: gaccha śīghraṃ ca paśyainaṃ gānavittvaṃ bhaviṣyasi /
children.translated_text: Go quickly and see him — you shall become a master of song.'

children.text: ityukto vismayā viṣṭo nārado vāgvidāṃ varaḥ // LiP_2,3.8 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Nārada</s>, the best among the eloquent, was filled with wonder, (LiP 2,3.8)
and went to <s>Gānabandhu</s> on Mount <s>Mānasottara</s>.

children.text: gandharvāḥ kinnarā yakṣāstathā cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ // LiP_2,3.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and hosts of <s>Apsarases</s> (LiP 2,3.9)
were seated all around <s>Gānabandhu</s>, here and there,
having mastered the art of song, trained by that bird. (LiP 2,3.10)
Then, seeing <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Gānabandhu</s> spoke: (LiP 2,3.11)
Bowing to him properly, he honored him with welcome.
'For what purpose have you come here, O illustrious great-minded one? (LiP 2,3.12)
With sweet and melodious voices, they sat there, uplifted.

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ hi mayā brahman brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te /
children.translated_text: What task should I perform, O brahmin? Tell me — what shall I do for you?'
<s>Nārada</s> said:
'O lord of owls, O great sage, hear everything just as it truly is. (LiP 2,3.13)

children.text: mama vṛttaṃ pravakṣyāmi purā bhūtaṃ mahādbhutam /
children.translated_text: I shall relate my story — what happened long ago, most wondrous.
In the past age, O learned one, when I was near <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, (LiP 2,3.14)

children.text: māṃ vinirdhūya saṃhṛṣṭaḥ samāhūya ca tuṃbarum /
children.translated_text: driving me away with delight, he summoned <s>Tumburu</s>,
and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, accompanied by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, listened to his supreme song. (LiP 2,3.15)
<s>Brahmā</s> and all the gods were displaced, removed from their positions.

children.text: kauśikādyāḥ samāsīnā gānayogena vai harim // LiP_2,3.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s> and others, seated, propitiated <s>Hari</s> through the practice of song, (LiP 2,3.16)
and having thus worshipped, they obtained the lordship of the <s>Gaṇas</s> comfortably.
Therefore I, extremely tormented by grief, have come here to perform austerity. (LiP 2,3.17)

children.text: yaddattaṃ yaddhutaṃ caiva yathā vā śrutameva ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever has been given, whatever has been offered in oblation, whatever has been heard,

children.text: yadadhītaṃ mayā sarvaṃ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm // LiP_2,3.18 //
children.translated_text: whatever has been studied by me — all of it is not worth a sixteenth part (LiP 2,3.18)
of the practice of song endowed with the glory of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: saṃcintyāhaṃ tapo ghoraṃ tadarthaṃ taptavān dvija // LiP_2,3.19 //
children.translated_text: Reflecting on this, I performed terrible austerity for that purpose, O twice-born one. (LiP 2,3.19)
For a divine thousand years, then I heard again
a voice born from the sky, directed toward you, O bird: (LiP 2,3.20)
'Go to the owl, O divine sage, to <s>Gānabandhu</s>, if your mind

children.text: gāte cedvartate brahman tatra tvaṃ vetsyase cirāt // LiP_2,3.21 //
children.translated_text: is set on song, O brahmin — there you shall learn in due time.' (LiP 2,3.21)
Thus directed by that [voice], I have come to your presence.

children.text: kiṃ karīṣyāmi śiṣyohaṃ tava māṃ pālayāvyaya // LiP_2,3.22 //
children.translated_text: What shall I do? I am your disciple — protect me, O imperishable one!' (LiP 2,3.22)
<s>Gānabandhu</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu nārada yadvṛttaṃ purā mama mahāmate /
children.translated_text: 'Hear, O <s>Nārada</s>, what happened to me long ago, O great-minded one —
most wondrous, purifying all sins, auspicious. (LiP 2,3.23)
There was once a king known as <s>Bhuvaneśa</s>, righteous,
who performed a thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifices and ten thousand <s>Vājapeya</s> rites, (LiP 2,3.24)

children.text: gavāṃ koṭyarbude caiva suvarmasya tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: and gave tens of millions of cows, and likewise of gold,

children.text: vāsasāṃ rathahastīnāṃ kanyāśvānāṃ tathaiva ca // LiP_2,3.25 //
children.translated_text: garments, chariots, elephants, maidens, and horses. (LiP 2,3.25)

children.text: datvā sa rājā viprebhyo medinīṃ pratipālayan /
children.translated_text: Having given [all this] to brahmins, that king, while protecting the earth,

children.text: nivārayan svake rājye geyayogena keśavam // LiP_2,3.26 //
children.translated_text: propitiated <s>Keśava</s> through the practice of song in his own kingdom. (LiP 2,3.26)

children.text: anyaṃ vā geyayogena gāyanyadi sa me bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'If anyone sings through the practice of song to anyone other [than <s>Keśava</s>],

children.text: vadhyaḥ sarvātmanā tasmādvedai rīḍyaḥ paraḥ pumān // LiP_2,3.27 //
children.translated_text: he shall be punishable with death — for no other being is to be praised through the <s>Vedas</s>.' (LiP 2,3.27)
'Let women everywhere always sing through the practice of song!

children.text: sūtamāgadhasaṃghāśca gītaṃ te kārayantu vai // LiP_2,3.28 //
children.translated_text: Let the bards and panegyrists make song!' (LiP 2,3.28)
Having thus commanded, the greatly splendid one protected his kingdom.

children.text: tasya rājñaḥ purābhyāśe harimitra iti śrutaḥ // LiP_2,3.29 //
children.translated_text: Near that king's [capital] there was one known as <s>Harimitra</s>, (LiP 2,3.29)
a brahmin, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from all dualities.

children.text: nadīpulinamāsādya pratimāṃ ca hareḥ śubhām // LiP_2,3.30 //
children.translated_text: Going to a sandbank by the river, [he would worship] an auspicious image of <s>Hari</s>; (LiP 2,3.30)
having worshipped it properly, offering ghee, curds, and more in abundance,

children.text: miṣṭānnaṃ pāyasaṃ dattvā harerāvedya pūpakam // LiP_2,3.31 //
children.translated_text: giving sweet rice, milk-pudding, and presenting cakes to <s>Hari</s>; (LiP 2,3.31)
bowing properly, with his mind fixed there,
he would sing to <s>Hari</s>, with rhythm, melody, and tempo. (LiP 2,3.32)
Filled with exceeding love, his inner self absorbed in Him.
Then, by the king's order, spies arrived there. (LiP 2,3.33)
Having disrupted all his worship and the rest completely,

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ gṛhītvā te rājñe samyaṅnyavedayan // LiP_2,3.34 //
children.translated_text: they seized that brahmin and duly reported to the king. (LiP 2,3.34)
Then the wicked-minded king, having rebuked the best of brahmins,
banished him from the kingdom, seizing all his wealth and possessions. (LiP 2,3.35)

children.text: pratimāṃ ca hareścaiva mlecchā hṛtvā yayuḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mlecchas</s> also seized the image of <s>Hari</s> and departed.
Then, after a great [span of] time, [the king] attained the decree of Death. (LiP 2,3.36)
That king, though honored in all worlds everywhere,

children.text: kṣudhārtaśca tathā khinno yamamāha suduḥ khitaḥ // LiP_2,3.37 //
children.translated_text: afflicted by hunger and distressed, spoke to <s>Yama</s> in great suffering: (LiP 2,3.37)

children.text: kṣuttṛṭ ca vartate deva svargatasyāpi me sadā /
children.translated_text: 'Hunger and thirst afflict me constantly, O God, even though I dwell in heaven.

children.text: mayā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ kiṃ vā kiṃ kariṣyāmi vai yama // LiP_2,3.38 //
children.translated_text: What sin have I committed? What shall I do, O <s>Yama</s>?' (LiP 2,3.38)
<s>Yama</s> said:
'A great sin was committed by you through ignorance and delusion
against <s>Harimitra</s>, who was devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>. (LiP 2,3.39)
The sin committed against <s>Harimitra</s> and against the worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s> —

children.text: tena pāpena saṃprāptaḥ kṣudrogastvāṃ sadā nṛpa // LiP_2,3.40 //
children.translated_text: by that sin, the disease of hunger has befallen you forever, O King. (LiP 2,3.40)
All your gifts and sacrifices have been destroyed, O King.
That great-minded <s>Harimitra</s>, who was singing with music and instruments — (LiP 2,3.41)
you summoned him and seized his wealth,
and all the offerings in the presence of <s>Vāsudeva</s> (LiP 2,3.42)
were plundered by your servants — they committed sin by your command.

children.text: hareḥ kīrtiṃ vinā cānyadbrahmaṇena nṛpottama // LiP_2,3.43 //
children.translated_text: Nothing other than <s>Hari</s>'s glory should be sung by a brahmin, O best of kings. (LiP 2,3.43)

children.text: na geyayoge gātavyaṃ tasmātpāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: Yet [that brahmin was punished for singing] in the practice of song — therefore sin was committed by you.
All your worlds are now destroyed. Go to a mountain cave! (LiP 2,3.44)

children.text: pūrvotsṛṣṭaṃ svadehaṃ taṃ khādannityaṃ nikṛtya vai /
children.translated_text: Gnawing constantly at your previously cast-off body, cutting it apart,

children.text: tasminkoṇe tvimaṃ dehaṃ khādannityaṃ kṣudhanvitaḥ // LiP_2,3.45 //
children.translated_text: in that corner, gnawing at this body, constantly afflicted by hunger, (LiP 2,3.45)
you shall dwell in the great hell for an entire <s>Manvantara</s>.

children.text: manvantare tato 'tīte bhūmyāṃ tvaṃ ca bhaviṣyasi // LiP_2,3.46 //
children.translated_text: When the <s>Manvantara</s> has passed, you will be [reborn] on earth. (LiP 2,3.46)
Then, in the course of time, attaining human birth, you shall understand.'
<s>Gānabandhu</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the wise <s>Yama</s> vanished right there. (LiP 2,3.47)
<s>Harimitra</s>, in a celestial chariot, praised by the lords of the <s>Gaṇas</s>,

children.text: viṣṇulokaṃ gataḥ śrīmān saṃgṛhya gamabāndhavān // LiP_2,3.48 //
children.translated_text: went to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world, the glorious one, taking his kinsmen with him. (LiP 2,3.48)

children.text: bhuvaneśo nṛpo hyasmin koṭare parvatasya vai /
children.translated_text: King <s>Bhuvaneśa</s>, in this cave of the mountain,

children.text: khādamānaḥ śavaṃ nityam āste kṣuttṛṭsamanvitaḥ // LiP_2,3.49 //
children.translated_text: gnawing at a corpse constantly, remains afflicted by hunger and thirst. (LiP 2,3.49)
I saw that king there — he told me all this.
Having observed and understood, I went to <s>Harimitra</s>, (LiP 2,3.50)
who was departing in a sun-colored chariot, surrounded by immortals.
By the grace of <s>Indradyumna</s>, I obtained the supreme lifespan. (LiP 2,3.51)

children.text: tenāhaṃ harimitraṃ vai dṛṣṭavān asmi suvrata /
children.translated_text: Thus I saw <s>Harimitra</s>, O one of good vows.
By the power of his sovereignty, my mind was inspired. (LiP 2,3.52)
I then sat with the <s>Kinnaras</s> to learn the art of song.

children.text: ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ gānayogena me mune // LiP_2,3.53 //
children.translated_text: For sixty thousand years, through the practice of song, O sage, (LiP 2,3.53)
my tongue was refined and made clear; then I learned song.
Then in twice that time, this [mastery] came to me — (LiP 2,3.54)
endowed with the practice of song, ten <s>Manvantaras</s> passed.
I became the teacher of song; <s>Gandharvas</s> and others came [to me]. (LiP 2,3.55)
These hosts of <s>Kinnaras</s> have come to me as their teacher.

children.text: tapasā naiva śakyā vai gānavidyā tapodhana // LiP_2,3.56 //
children.translated_text: The art of song cannot be obtained by austerity alone, O practitioner of <s>tapas</s>! (LiP 2,3.56)
Therefore, equipped with [proper] learning, receive the art of song from me.'

children.text: evamukto munistaṃ vai praṇipatya jagau tadā // LiP_2,3.57 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the sage, having bowed to him, then sang. (LiP 2.3.57)
Listen to that, O best of sages, having saluted <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Thus addressed by the owl, <s>Nārada</s>, the best of sages, (LiP 2.3.58)
endowed with the systematic method of instruction, learned singing there.
The teacher of song (<s>Gānabandhu</s>) then said: 'Be shameless now.' (LiP 2.3.59)
The Owl (<s>Ulūka</s>) said:
In the company of women, in song, in gambling, in the company of discourses,

children.text: vyavahāre tathāhāre tvarthānāṃ ca samāgame // LiP_2,3.60 //
children.translated_text: in business dealings, in eating, and in the gathering of wealth — (LiP 2.3.60)

children.text: āye vyaye tathā nityaṃ tyaktalajjastu vai bhavet /
children.translated_text: in income and expenditure, always one should be free from shame.

children.text: na kuñcitena gūḍhena nityaṃ prāvaramādibhiḥ // LiP_2,3.61 //
children.translated_text: One should never [sing] with crouching, concealment, or constant covering and the like, (LiP 2.3.61)
with hand-waving gestures, with gaping mouth,

children.text: niryātajihvāyogena na geyaṃ hi kathañcana // LiP_2,3.62 //
children.translated_text: or with the tongue thrust out — one should never sing in any way [like that]. (LiP 2.3.62)
One should not sing with arms raised upward, nor ever with upward gaze;

children.text: svāṅgaṃ nirīkṣamāṇena paraṃ saṃprekṣatā tathā // LiP_2,3.63 //
children.translated_text: nor while gazing at one's own body, nor while looking at another. (LiP 2.3.63)

children.text: saṃghaṭṭe ca tathotthāne kaṭisthānaṃ na śasyate /
children.translated_text: In ensemble [singing] and in rising [from a seated position], the waist-position is not recommended.

children.text: hāso roṣastathā kaṃpastathānyatra smṛtiḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,3.64 //
children.translated_text: Laughter, anger, trembling, and distracted remembrance of other things — (LiP 2.3.64)
these are not praiseworthy forms in the practice of singing, O great sage.
Keeping time (<s>tāla</s>) cannot be done with one hand alone, O sage. (LiP 2.3.65)
By one afflicted with hunger, by one afflicted with fear, by one afflicted with thirst,

children.text: gānayoge na kartavyo nāndhakāre kathañcana // LiP_2,3.66 //
children.translated_text: the practice of singing should not be done, nor in darkness under any circumstance. (LiP 2.3.66)
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Thus instructed by that one with rules and characteristics,
the blessed one learned divine singing for a thousand years. (LiP 2.3.67)
These and other such things should not be done by one who sings.
Then, fully accomplished in the introductory elements of song (<s>gītaprastāra</s>) and the like,
accomplished in the <s>vīṇā</s> and other [instruments], a knower of all distinctions of notes (<s>svara</s>) — (LiP 2.3.68)
thirty-six thousand hundreds [i.e., 3,600,000]
of notes, through the combination of distinctions — the best of sages came to know. (LiP 2.3.69)
Then the hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s> and of <s>Kinnaras</s> likewise,

children.text: muninā saha saṃyuktāḥ prītiyuktā bhavanti te // LiP_2,3.70 //
children.translated_text: united with the sage, became filled with joy. (LiP 2.3.70)
The sage said to the teacher of song, having attained the supreme singing:

children.text: tvāṃ samāsādya saṃpannastvaṃ hi gītaviśāradaḥ // LiP_2,3.71 //
children.translated_text: 'Having found you, I have become accomplished; you are indeed expert in song. (LiP 2.3.71)
O enemy of crows, O greatly wise one, what can I do for you as teacher?'
The teacher of song (<s>Gānabandhu</s>) said:

children.text: brahmaṇo divase brahman manavastu caturdaśa // LiP_2,3.72 //
children.translated_text: 'In a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, there are fourteen <s>Manus</s>; (LiP 2.3.72)
thereafter, the dissolution of the three worlds will occur, O great sage.

children.text: tāvanme tvāyuṣo bhāvastāvanme paramaṃ śubham // LiP_2,3.73 //
children.translated_text: Until then is the extent of my life; until then is my supreme auspiciousness. (LiP 2.3.73)
Let what has been contemplated in my mind be [my] fee, O best of sages.'
<s>Nārada</s> said:
'At the conjunction of the past <s>kalpa</s>, you shall become <s>Garuḍa</s>. (LiP 2.3.74)

children.text: svasti te 'stu mahāprājña gamiṣyāmi prasīda mām /
children.translated_text: May it be well with you, O greatly wise one. I shall go; be gracious to me.'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Having spoken thus, <s>Nārada</s> then went to <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). (LiP 2.3.75)
In <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), he sang songs to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).

children.text: tatra śrutvā tu bhagavānnāradaṃ prāha mādhavaḥ // LiP_2,3.76 //
children.translated_text: Having heard there, the blessed <s>Mādhava</s> said to <s>Nārada</s>: (LiP 2.3.76)
'You are not yet superior to <s>Tumburu</s> in songs, O <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: yadā viśiṣṭo bhavitā taṃ kālaṃ pravadāmyaham // LiP_2,3.77 //
children.translated_text: When you shall become superior, I shall tell you that time. (LiP 2.3.77)
Having found the teacher of song, you have become knowledgeable in the purpose of singing.
In the twenty-eighth <s>yuga</s> of <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>, (LiP 2.3.78)
I shall be your [contemporary] in <s>Dvāpara</s> [age], born in the lineage of the <s>Yadu</s> clan,

children.text: devakyāṃ vasudevasya kṛṣṇo nāmnā mahāmate // LiP_2,3.79 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Devakī</s>, son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, by the name <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O great sage. (LiP 2.3.79)
At that time, having found Me, you shall remind Me of all this as it was.

children.text: tatra tvāṃ gītasaṃpannaṃ kariṣyāmi mahāvratam // LiP_2,3.80 //
children.translated_text: Then I shall make you, accomplished in song, a great <s>vrata</s>-observer — (LiP 2.3.80)
equal to <s>Tumburu</s> and even surpassing him.
Until that time, as is proper, in the births of gods and <s>Gandharvas</s>, (LiP 2.3.81)
practice according to rule.' Having said this, He disappeared.
Then the sage, having bowed to Him, endowed with such extraordinary [powers], (LiP 2.3.82)
the divine sage (<s>Devarṣi</s>), god-like in appearance, adorned with all ornaments,
a supreme treasure of austerities, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, (LiP 2.3.83)
taking the <s>vīṇā</s> on his shoulder, wandered through all the worlds.
The western (<s>Vāruṇa</s>), southern (<s>Yāmya</s>), southeastern (<s>Āgneya</s>), eastern (<s>Aindra</s>), and northern (<s>Kaubera</s>) [quarters], (LiP 2.3.84)

children.text: vāyavyaṃ ca tatheśānaṃ saṃsadaṃ prāpya dharmavit /
children.translated_text: the northwestern (<s>Vāyavya</s>) and the northeastern (<s>Aiśāna</s>) — having reached each assembly, the knower of <s>dharma</s>,
singing of <s>Hari</s> perfectly, skilled in <s>vīṇā</s>-playing, (LiP 2.3.85)
honored everywhere by hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>,
he reached <s>Brahmaloka</s> at a certain turn of time. (LiP 2.3.86)
<s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s>, the two <s>Gandharvas</s>, expert in song and instrumental music,

children.text: brahmaṇo gāyakau divyau nityau gandharvasattamau // LiP_2,3.87 //
children.translated_text: divine singers of <s>Brahmā</s>, eternal, the best of <s>Gandharvas</s> — (LiP 2.3.87)

children.text: tatra tābhyāṃ samāsādya gāyamāno hariṃ prabhum /
children.translated_text: there, having met those two, singing of <s>Hari</s> the Lord,

children.text: brahmaṇā ca mahātejāḥ pūjito munisattamaḥ // LiP_2,3.88 //
children.translated_text: the best of sages, of great brilliance, was honored by <s>Brahmā</s>. (LiP 2.3.88)
Having bowed to that great soul, the grandsire of all worlds,

children.text: cacāra ca yathākāmaṃ sarvalokeṣu nāradaḥ // LiP_2,3.89 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> wandered at will through all the worlds. (LiP 2.3.89)

children.text: tataḥ kālena mahatā gṛhaṃ prāpya ca tuṃbaroḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, having reached the home of <s>Tumburu</s>,
the great sage, taking up the <s>vīṇā</s>, sang there. (LiP 2.3.90)

children.text: svarakalpāstu tatrasthāḥ ṣaḍjādyāḥ sapta vai matāḥ /
children.translated_text: The seven notes (<s>svara</s>) beginning with <s>ṣaḍja</s>, arranged in their [proper] forms, were there.
The Lord, seeing him playing, came out very quickly. (LiP 2.3.91)
Through instruction, the great-minded one [<s>Tumburu</s>] taught him extensively in various places.
<s>Nārada</s>, the great sage too, was engaged with the effort of practice. (LiP 2.3.92)
Seeing the seven note-ladies (<s>svarāṅganā</s>), the expert in the science of singing,

children.text: āsīdvīṇā samāyoge na tāstantryaḥ prapedire // LiP_2,3.93 //
children.translated_text: when he played the <s>vīṇā</s>, those [note-ladies] did not enter the strings. (LiP 2.3.93)
Then, on <s>Raivataka</s> [mountain], having bowed to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the great sage

children.text: vijñāpayadaśeṣaṃ tu śvetadvīpe tu yat purā // LiP_2,3.94 //
children.translated_text: reported everything that formerly in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (LiP 2.3.94)
had been told by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> about the supreme yoga of singing.

children.text: tacchrutvā prāhasankṛṣṇaḥ prāha jāṃbavatīṃ mudā // LiP_2,3.95 //
children.translated_text: Having heard that, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to <s>Jāmbavatī</s> with joy: (LiP 2.3.95)
'O virtuous one, instruct this best of sages according to proper method

children.text: vīṇāgāna samāyoge tathetyuktvā ca sā harim // LiP_2,3.96 //
children.translated_text: in the combination of <s>vīṇā</s> and song.' Having said 'So be it' to <s>Hari</s>, she (LiP 2.3.96)
laughingly instructed that sage according to the proper method.

children.text: tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe punarāgamya mādhavam // LiP_2,3.97 //
children.translated_text: Then, at the completion of a year, having come again to <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), (LiP 2.3.97)
having bowed, he stood before Him. <s>Keśava</s> said again:
'Go near <s>Satyā</s> [<s>Satyabhāmā</s>]; learn according to proper method.' (LiP 2.3.98)
Having said 'So be it,' the sage bowed to <s>Satyabhāmā</s> and sang.

children.text: tayā sa sikṣito vidvān pūrṇe saṃvatsare punaḥ // LiP_2,3.99 //
children.translated_text: Instructed by her, the learned one, at the completion of [another] year, (LiP 2.3.99)
There, by the women and maidservants, the best of sages (LiP 2.3.100)
accompanied by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, went to the abode of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.

children.text: ukto 'sau gāyamānopi na svaraṃ vetsi vai mune /
children.translated_text: was told, even while he was singing: 'You do not know the notes, O sage!'
Then, with great effort, over a period of three years, (LiP 2.3.101)

children.text: śikṣitosau tadā devyā rukmiṇyāpi jagau muniḥ /
children.translated_text: he was instructed by that goddess <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, and then the sage sang.

children.text: tataḥ svarāṅganāḥ prāpyaḥ tantrīyogaṃ mahāmuneḥ // LiP_2,3.102 //
children.translated_text: Then, the note-ladies should be obtained through the union of strings, O great sage. (LiP 2.3.102)
The blessed Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself, summoning the great sage,
the immeasurable Self, taught [him] the supreme yoga of singing. (LiP 2.3.103)
Then, having attained excellence surpassing <s>Tumburu</s>, the best of sages,

children.text: tato nanarta devarṣiḥ praṇipatya janārdanam // LiP_2,3.104 //
children.translated_text: the divine sage danced, having bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>. (LiP 2.3.104)
<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> said: 'You are now all-knowing, O great sage.

children.text: prahasya gānayogena gāyasva mama sannidhau // LiP_2,3.105 //
children.translated_text: Laugh with joy and sing before Me through the yoga of song. (LiP 2.3.105)

children.text: etatte prārthitaṃ prāptaṃ mama loke tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: This wish of yours has been fulfilled, and in My world likewise.

children.text: nityaṃ tuṃbaruṇā sārdhaṃ gāyasva ca yathātatham // LiP_2,3.106 //
children.translated_text: Always sing together with <s>Tumburu</s> as is proper.' (LiP 2.3.106)
Thus addressed, the sage practiced there as was proper.

children.text: yadā saṃpūjayan kṛṣṇo rudraṃ bhuvananāyakam // LiP_2,3.107 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> worshipped <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of the worlds, (LiP 2.3.107)
then [<s>Nārada</s>] sang for <s>Śaṅkara</s>, by the command of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: rukmiṇyā saha satyā ca jāṃbavatyā mahāmuniḥ // LiP_2,3.108 //
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, the great sage, (LiP 2.3.108)
and with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O best of kings — expert in <s>śruti</s> and <s>jāti</s> [musical terms].

children.text: eṣa vo muniśārdūlāḥ prokto gītakramo muneḥ // LiP_2,3.109 //
children.translated_text: This, O tigers among sages, is the described sequence of the sage's singing. (LiP 2.3.109)
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, singing the [hymn] called <s>Vāsudeva</s> abundantly, O king,
attains residence in the same world as <s>Hari</s> (<s>sālokya</s>); one who sings of <s>Rudra</s> becomes even greater. (LiP 2.3.110)
Otherwise, one who sings of something else goes to hell.
By action, mind, and speech, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, (LiP 2.3.111)

children.text: gāyan śṛṇvaṃstamāpnoti tasmādgeyaṃ paraṃ viduḥ // LiP_2,3.112 //
children.translated_text: singing and hearing, one attains Him — therefore the wise know that singing is supreme. (LiP 2.3.112)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge vaiṣṇavagītakathanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [ends] the third chapter, named 'The Narration of <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> Song.'
The sages said:
Those who are called <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s> —

children.text: kāni cihnāni teṣāṃ vai tanno brahi mahāmate // LiP_2,4.1 //
children.translated_text: what are their marks? Tell us that, O great sage. (LiP 2.4.1)

children.text: teṣāṃ vā kiṃ karotyeṣa bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And what does this blessed Lord, the creator of beings, do for them?
Tell us all of this, O <s>Sūta</s>, O most knowledgeable of all purposes. (LiP 2.4.2)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When asked by <s>Ambarīṣa</s> long ago, the sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>

children.text: yuṣmabhiradya yat proktaṃ tadvadāmi yathātatham // LiP_2,4.3 //
children.translated_text: [said] what you have now asked — I shall tell that as it truly is. (LiP 2.4.3)
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Hear, O king, according to propriety, what you ask of me.

children.text: yatrāste viṣṇubhaktastu tatra nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ // LiP_2,4.4 //
children.translated_text: Where a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> resides, there <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is established. (LiP 2.4.4)

children.text: viṣṇureva hi sarvatra yeṣāṃ vai devatā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is everywhere the deity of those [devotees].

children.text: kīrtyamāne harau nityaṃ romāñco yasya vartate // LiP_2,4.5 //
children.translated_text: He in whom horripilation constantly arises when <s>Hari</s> is glorified, (LiP 2.4.5)
trembling, perspiration, and tear-drops are seen in [his] eyes —
[he who is] endowed with devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, following <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> [rites], (LiP 2.4.6)

children.text: prīto bhavati yo dṛṣṭvā vaiṣṇavo 'sau prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: he who becomes pleased upon seeing [such devotees] — he is declared a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
A <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> would not cover with cloth another [devotee] in the world's arena. (LiP 2.4.7)
He who, seeing a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> approaching, stands face-to-face

children.text: praṇāmādi karotyevaṃ vāsudeve yathā tathā // LiP_2,4.8 //
children.translated_text: and performs salutation and the like, just as to <s>Vāsudeva</s> [Himself] — (LiP 2.4.8)

children.text: sa vai bhakta iti jñeyaḥ sa jayī syājjagattraye /
children.translated_text: he is to be known as a [true] devotee; he shall be victorious in the three worlds.
He who, hearing harsh words spoken from a <s>Bhāgavata</s> [devotee], (LiP 2.4.9)

children.text: praṇāmapūrvaṃ kṣāntyā vai yo vadedvaiṣṇavo hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: responds with salutation first and with patience — he is indeed a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.

children.text: gandhapuṣpādi kaṃ sarvaṃ śirasā yo hi dhārayet // LiP_2,4.10 //
children.translated_text: He who bears on his head all [offerings of] fragrance, flowers, and the like, (LiP 2.4.10)
thinking 'All this belongs to <s>Hari</s>' — he is regarded as a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
He who does only auspicious deeds in the domain of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, with love, (LiP 2.4.11)
and who always worships the image of <s>Hari</s> with a controlled self,

children.text: viṣṇubhaktaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ karmaṇā manasā girā // LiP_2,4.12 //
children.translated_text: he is to be known as a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — by action, mind, and speech. (LiP 2.4.12)
Always devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he is indeed a great <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

children.text: bhojanārādhanaṃ sarvaṃ yathāśaktyā karoti yaḥ // LiP_2,4.13 //
children.translated_text: He who performs all [acts of] food-offering and worship according to his ability — (LiP 2.4.13)

children.text: viṣṇubhaktasya ca sadā yathānyāyaṃ hi kathyate /
children.translated_text: this is always said, according to propriety, of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The learned one devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose food, [given] with a pleased mind, (LiP 2.4.14)
[another] eats — that food has gone to <s>Hari</s>'s mouth, without doubt.

children.text: svārcanādapi viśvātmā prīto bhavati mādhavaḥ // LiP_2,4.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s>, the Soul of the universe, becomes more pleased than by one's own worship, (LiP 2.4.15)
seeing that [offering given] to a great <s>Bhāgavata</s> — He, the lover of devotees.
Seeing a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, whose sins are burnt away, (LiP 2.4.16)
even the gods, frightened, go to him with salutations, as they came.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ hi purāvṛttaṃ viṣṇubhaktasya vaibhavam // LiP_2,4.17 //
children.translated_text: Hear the glory of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, an ancient occurrence. (LiP 2.4.17)

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yamo 'pi vai bhaktaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ dagdhakilbiṣam /
children.translated_text: Even <s>Yama</s> (Death), seeing a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> devotee whose sins are burnt away,
rising and joining his palms, bowed to the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>. (LiP 2.4.18)
Therefore, a person should worship <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> with devotion, as [one would worship] <s>Viṣṇu</s> [himself];

children.text: sa yāti viṣṇusāmīpya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // LiP_2,4.19 //
children.translated_text: he attains proximity to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — there should be no deliberation in this. (LiP 2.4.19)
Among thousands of devotees of other [deities], a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is distinguished;
among thousands of devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, a devotee of <s>Rudra</s> is distinguished;
there is none higher than a devotee of <s>Rudra</s> in the world — there is no doubt. (LiP 2.4.20)
Therefore, whether a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> or a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>,
one should worship [them] with every effort — for <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation. (LiP 2.4.21)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge viṣṇubhaktakathanaṃ nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, entitled 'The Description of <s>Viṣṇu</s> Devotees,' in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
<s>Ambarīṣa</s>, of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> [dynasty], was devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>;
he ruled the earth, proceeding by the command of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (LiP 2.5.1)
We have heard [of] this, O one of great wisdom — you should tell all of that;
his disc of <s>Hari</s>, constantly [destroys] enemies, diseases, fears, and the like — (LiP 2.5.2)
so it is heard in the world — of that righteous and great-souled one.

children.text: aṃbarīṣasya caritaṃ tatsarvaṃ brūhi sattama // LiP_2,5.3 //
children.translated_text: Tell us the entire story of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, O best [of sages]. (LiP 2.5.3)
His greatness, his glory, and his unsurpassed <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (path of devotion) —
we wish to hear as it was — you are capable of telling, O <s>Sūta</s>. (LiP 2.5.4)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hear, O tigers among sages, the story of that wise one;
the greatness of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> — supreme, destroying all sins. (LiP 2.5.5)
The beloved wife of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, adorned with all auspicious marks,
was the mother of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, always endowed with purity. (LiP 2.5.6)
She [worshipped] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the great soul, who has ascended <s>Yoganidrā</s> (cosmic sleep), reclining on the couch of <s>Śeṣa</s>,
born from the lotus of the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), (LiP 2.5.7)
known as <s>Kālarudra</s> through <s>tamas</s> (darkness), born as the golden one through <s>rajas</s> (passion),
and as the all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s> through <s>sattva</s> (purity) — saluted by all gods. (LiP 2.5.8)
She worshipped [him] constantly through speech, mind, and bodily actions;
all offerings of garlands and the like — she herself performed. (LiP 2.5.9)
The preparation of fragrance and other [offerings], incense materials and the like,
the smearing of the ground and such [rites], and the cooking of oblations — (LiP 2.5.10)
filled with that eagerness, she herself performed all that,

children.text: śubhā padmāvatī nityaṃ vācā nārāyaṇeti vai // LiP_2,5.11 //
children.translated_text: the auspicious <s>Padmāvatī</s>, constantly [uttering] the word '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' with her voice. (LiP 2.5.11)
'<s>Ananta</s>!' — constantly speaking thus, that devoted wife,
for ten thousand years, with her innermost self devoted to Him, (LiP 2.5.12)
worshipped <s>Govinda</s> with fragrance, flowers, and the like, [remaining] pure.
The greatly fortunate <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> devotees, free from all sins — (LiP 2.5.13)
she constantly pleased them with gifts, honors, worship, wealth, and jewels.

children.text: tataḥ kadācitsā devī dvādaśīṃ samupoṣya vai // LiP_2,5.14 //
children.translated_text: Then, on one occasion, that goddess, having fasted on <s>Dvādaśī</s> (the twelfth lunar day), (LiP 2.5.14)
the greatly fortunate one, slept before <s>Hari</s> together with her husband.
There, the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Being), spoke to her: (LiP 2.5.15)

children.text: kim icchasi varaṃ bhadre mattas tvam brūhi bhāmini /
children.translated_text: 'What boon do you desire from me, O blessed one? Speak, O beautiful lady.'

children.text: sā dṛṣṭvā tu varaṃ vavre putro me vaiṣṇavo bhavet // LiP_2,5.16 //
children.translated_text: Seeing [him], she chose this boon: 'May my son be a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, (LiP 2.5.16)
a sovereign ruler, of great brilliance, devoted to his own duties, pure.'

children.text: tathetyuktvā dadau tasyai phalam ekaṃ janārdanaḥ // LiP_2,5.17 //
children.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' <s>Janārdana</s> gave her a single fruit. (LiP 2.5.17)

children.text: sā prabuddhā phalaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhartre sarvaṃ nyavedayat /
children.translated_text: She, having awakened and seeing the fruit, reported everything to her husband;
she ate it joyfully, her mind absorbed in that [boon]. (LiP 2.5.18)

children.text: tataḥ kālena sā devī putraṃ kulavivardhanam /
children.translated_text: Then, in time, that goddess gave birth to a son who was the increaser of the family,
of righteous conduct, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>. (LiP 2.5.19)
Endowed with auspicious marks, with the disc-mark on his body,

children.text: jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitā putraṃ kriyāḥ sarvāścakāra vai // LiP_2,5.20 //
children.translated_text: seeing the newborn son, the father performed all the [birth] rites. (LiP 2.5.20)
Known as <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, the lord became [famous] in the world;
when his father passed away, the illustrious one was consecrated, [like] a great sage. (LiP 2.5.21)

children.text: mantriṣvādhāya rājyaṃ ca tapa ugrañcakāra saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having entrusted the kingdom to his ministers, he performed fierce austerities,
for a thousand years, reciting [the name of] Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, (LiP 2.5.22)
who dwells in the center of the heart-lotus, within the orb of the sun,
holding conch, disc, mace, and lotus — four-armed, (LiP 2.5.23)
resembling pure <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, embodying <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
adorned with all ornaments, wearing yellow garments — the Lord, (LiP 2.5.24)
with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark on his chest, the god, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>).
Then, mounting <s>Garuḍa</s>, praised by all the gods, (LiP 2.5.25)
the soul of the universe, saluted by all worlds, arrived.
<s>Hari</s>, having made <s>Garuḍa</s> inconceivably [large] like <s>Airāvata</s> [the divine elephant], (LiP 2.5.26)
sat like <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself and spoke to that best of kings:

children.text: indro 'hamasmi bhadraṃ te kiṃ dadāmi varaṃ ca te // LiP_2,5.27 //
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Indra</s> — blessings upon you! What boon shall I grant you? (LiP 2.5.27)
I, the lord of all worlds, have come to protect you.'
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:
'It was not with you in mind that I undertook austerity here. (LiP 2.5.28)

children.text: tvayā dattaṃ ca neṣyāmi gaccha śakra yathāsukham /
children.translated_text: I shall not accept what is given by you. Go, <s>Śakra</s>, as you please.

children.text: mama nārāyaṇo nāthastaṃ nāmāmi jagatpatim // LiP_2,5.29 //
children.translated_text: My lord is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — I bow to him, the lord of the world. (LiP 2.5.29)
Go, <s>Indra</s> — do not create confusion in my mind here.'
Then, laughing, the blessed Lord (<s>Hari</s>) revealed his true form — (LiP 2.5.30)
<s>Janārdana</s>, holding the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, disc, mace, and sword in his hands,
the soul of all, atop <s>Garuḍa</s> — like another blue mountain. (LiP 2.5.31)
Praised all around by hosts of gods and <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: praṇamya sa ca saṃtuṣṭastuṣṭāva garuḍadhvajam // LiP_2,5.32 //
children.translated_text: he [Ambarīṣa], bowing with satisfaction, praised the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>: (LiP 2.5.32)
'Be gracious, O Lord of the World-protectors, my Lord, O <s>Janārdana</s>!
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O Lord of the Universe, saluted by all worlds! (LiP 2.5.33)
You are the beginning, you are without beginning, you are infinite — the Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), the Lord.
Immeasurable, all-pervading, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, lotus-eyed! (LiP 2.5.34)
Born from the body of <s>Maheśvara</s>, in the midst is <s>Puṣkara</s> (Brahmā), the sky-going bird-rider.

children.text: kavyavāhaḥ kapālī tvaṃ havyavāhaḥ prabhañjanaḥ // LiP_2,5.35 //
children.translated_text: You are <s>Kavyavāha</s> (fire of the ancestors), the skull-bearer (<s>Kapālī</s>), <s>Havyavāha</s> (sacrificial fire), and the Destroyer (<s>Prabhañjana</s>). (LiP 2.5.35)
The primordial god, bliss of action, the supreme self, established in the self.
I have taken refuge in you, O <s>Govinda</s>! Victory, O son of <s>Devakī</s>!

children.text: jaya deva jagannātha pāhi māṃ puṣkarekṣaṇa // LiP_2,5.36 //
children.translated_text: Victory, O God, Lord of the Universe! Protect me, O lotus-eyed one! (LiP 2.5.36)

children.text: nānyā gatistvadanyā me tvameva śaraṇaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: There is no other refuge for me besides you — you alone are my shelter.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tamāha bhagavānviṣṇuḥ kiṃ te hṛdi cikīrṣitam // LiP_2,5.37 //
children.translated_text: The blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> said to him: 'What is the desire in your heart? (LiP 2.5.37)

children.text: tatsarvaṃ te pradāsyāmi bhaktosi mama suvrata /
children.translated_text: I shall grant you all of that — you are my devotee, O one of excellent vows.
I am always pleased by devotion; therefore I have come here to give.' (LiP 2.5.38)
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:

children.text: lokanātha parānanda nityaṃ me vartate matiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O Lord of the World, O supreme bliss! My mind is always constant:
always devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s> through speech, mind, and bodily actions. (LiP 2.5.39)
Just as you are [devoted] to <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), the supreme soul, the god of gods —

children.text: tathā bhavāmyahaṃ viṣṇo tava deva janārdana // LiP_2,5.40 //
children.translated_text: so may I be to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O God, O <s>Janārdana</s>! (LiP 2.5.40)

children.text: pāliyiṣyāmi pṛthivīṃ kṛtvā vai vaiṣṇavaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: I shall rule the earth, having made the world <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>;
through sacrifices, fire-offerings, and worship, I shall satisfy the greatest of gods. (LiP 2.5.41)
I shall protect <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> and destroy enemies;

children.text: lokatāpabhaye bhīta iti me dhīyate matiḥ // LiP_2,5.42 //
children.translated_text: frightened by the fear of worldly suffering — thus is my resolve established.' (LiP 2.5.42)
The Blessed Lord said:
'So be it, as you wish. This disc, <s>Sudarśana</s>,

children.text: purā rudraprasādena labdhaṃ vai durlabhaṃ mayā // LiP_2,5.43 //
children.translated_text: was formerly obtained by me through the grace of <s>Rudra</s> — difficult to obtain. (LiP 2.5.43)
Suffering from sages' curses and the like, from enemies, diseases, and the like —
it shall always destroy [them] for you.' Having said this, he disappeared. (LiP 2.5.44)
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ praṇamya mudito rājā nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum /
children.translated_text: Then, bowing with delight, the king [worshipped] Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
entering the beautiful city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, he ruled. (LiP 2.5.45)
He engaged <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and other <s>varṇas</s> (classes) in their respective duties;
always devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, [he protected] the sinless devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — (LiP 2.5.46)
the king of men protected [them] with a joyful heart, with special [care].
Having performed a hundred <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices) and a hundred <s>vājapeya</s> [sacrifices], (LiP 2.5.47)
he ruled this earth bounded by oceans.
In every home, <s>Hari</s> was present; in every home, the chanting of the <s>Vedas</s>; (LiP 2.5.48)
the recitation of the names of <s>Hari</s>, and likewise the sounds of sacrifices —
these were [heard] when that tiger among kings was ruling the kingdom. (LiP 2.5.49)
The earth was not without grain, not without grass, not afflicted by famine and the like;
the people were always free from passion and free from all calamities. (LiP 2.5.50)
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> of great brilliance ruled the earth.
While he was thus [ruling], a lotus-eyed daughter [was born] — (LiP 2.5.51)
renowned by the name <s>Śrīmatī</s>, endowed with all auspicious marks,
having reached the age of betrothal — beautiful like a divine <s>māyā</s>. (LiP 2.5.52)
At that time, the illustrious sage <s>Nārada</s> arrived

children.text: aṃbarīṣasya rājño vai parvataśca mahāmatiḥ // LiP_2,5.53 //
children.translated_text: at king <s>Ambarīṣa</s>'s [court], along with the great-minded <s>Parvata</s>. (LiP 2.5.53)
Seeing both of them arrived, bowing according to proper rites,

children.text: aṃbarīṣo mahātejāḥ pūjayāmāsa tāv ṛṣī // LiP_2,5.54 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ambarīṣa</s> of great brilliance worshipped those two sages. (LiP 2.5.54)

children.text: kanyāṃ tāṃ ramamāṇāṃ vai meghamadhye śatahradām /
children.translated_text: Seeing that maiden playing — like lightning within a cloud —

children.text: prāha tāṃ prekṣya bhagavān nāradaḥ sasmitas tadā // LiP_2,5.55 //
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Nārada</s>, gazing at her, then said with a smile: (LiP 2.5.55)
'Who is this greatly fortunate maiden, O king, resembling a daughter of the gods?
Tell [us], O best of the righteous — adorned with all auspicious marks.' (LiP 2.5.56)
The king said:

children.text: duhiteyaṃ mama vibho śrīmatī nāma nāmataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is my daughter, O Lord — <s>Śrīmatī</s> by name.
Having reached the age of betrothal, the auspicious one seeks a husband.' (LiP 2.5.57)
Thus told, the tiger among sages, <s>Nārada</s>, desired her, O twice-born ones;

children.text: parvatopi munistāṃ vai cakame munisattamāḥ // LiP_2,5.58 //
children.translated_text: and the sage <s>Parvata</s> too desired her, O best of sages. (LiP 2.5.58)
Taking leave of the king, <s>Nārada</s> spoke these words,
calling [him] aside in private: 'O righteous one, give me this daughter of yours.' (LiP 2.5.59)

children.text: parvato hi tathā prāha rājānaṃ rahasi prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Parvata</s> likewise spoke to the king in private, the lord [saying the same].

children.text: tāvubhau saha dharmātmā praṇipatya bhayārditaḥ // LiP_2,5.60 //
children.translated_text: The righteous [king], bowing to both, afflicted with fear, [said]: (LiP 2.5.60)

children.text: ubhau bhavantau kanyāṃ me pārthayānau kathaṃ tvaham /
children.translated_text: 'Both of you seek my daughter — what shall I do?

children.text: kariṣyāmi mahāprājña śṛṇu nārada me vacaḥ // LiP_2,5.61 //
children.translated_text: O greatly wise one, hear my words, <s>Nārada</s>! (LiP 2.5.61)

children.text: tvaṃ ca parvata me vākyaṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi yatprabho /
children.translated_text: And you, <s>Parvata</s>, hear my words — I shall speak what [I must], O Lord.
This maiden shall choose one of you two as her husband, if she so wishes, the auspicious one. (LiP 2.5.62)

children.text: tasmai kanyāṃ prayacchāmi nānyathā śaktirasti me /
children.translated_text: To him I shall give the maiden — I have no power to do otherwise.'

children.text: tathetyuktvā tato bhūyaḥ śvo yāsyāva iti sma ha // LiP_2,5.63 //
children.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' [they replied]: 'Tomorrow we shall come again.' (LiP 2.5.63)
Having said this, the two tigers among sages departed with joyful hearts,
both always devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the foremost among knowers of wisdom. (LiP 2.5.64)

children.text: viṣṇu lokaṃ tato gatvā nārado munisattamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having gone to <s>Viṣṇuloka</s> (the world of Viṣṇu), <s>Nārada</s>, the best of sages,
bowing to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (Viṣṇu), spoke these words: (LiP 2.5.65)
'There is something to be heard, O Blessed One, O Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, O Master!

children.text: rahasi tvāṃ pravakṣyāmi namaste bhuvaneśvara // LiP_2,5.66 //
children.translated_text: I shall tell you in private — salutations to you, O Lord of the Universe!' (LiP 2.5.66)

children.text: tataḥ prahasya govindaḥ sarvānutsārya taṃ munim /
children.translated_text: Then, laughing, <s>Govinda</s>, having dismissed all others, [addressed] the sage;

children.text: brūhītyāha ca viśvātmā munirāha ca keśavam // LiP_2,5.67 //
children.translated_text: 'Speak!' said the soul of the universe — and the sage spoke to <s>Keśava</s>: (LiP 2.5.67)
'Your [devotee], the illustrious king <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, the ruler of the earth —

children.text: tasya kanyā viśālākṣī śrīmatī nāma nāmataḥ // LiP_2,5.68 //
children.translated_text: his wide-eyed daughter, <s>Śrīmatī</s> by name — (LiP 2.5.68)
I have gone there desiring to marry [her] — hear [my] words.
This illustrious sage <s>Parvata</s>, your servant, a treasury of austerities — (LiP 2.5.69)
he too desired her, O Blessed One. And the king told us both:
"<s>Ambarīṣa</s> of great brilliance [said]: 'This maiden of you two — the husband (LiP 2.5.70)
whom she chooses, endowed with beauty — to him I shall give [her].'"
Thus the king told us both — and saying 'So be it,' I have come here.' (LiP 2.5.71)

children.text: āgamiṣyāmi te rājan śvaḥ prabhāte gṛhaṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: 'I shall come to your house, O king, tomorrow at dawn' —

children.text: āgatohaṃ jagannātha kartumarhasi me priyam // LiP_2,5.72 //
children.translated_text: 'I have come, O Lord of the Universe; please do me a favor.' (LiP 2.5.72)
'Make it so that, just as the face of a mountain shines with monkeys,

children.text: tathā kuru jagannātha mama cedicchasi priyam // LiP_2,5.73 //
children.translated_text: so too [should his face appear], O Lord of the Universe, if you wish to do me a favor.' (LiP 2.5.73)
'So be it,' said <s>Govinda</s>, laughing, the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>:

children.text: tvayoktaṃ ca kariṣyāmi gaccha saumya yathāgatam // LiP_2,5.74 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall do what you have asked; go in peace, gentle one, as you came.' (LiP 2.5.74)
Having spoken thus, the sage, delighted, bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: manyamānaḥ kṛtātmānaṃ tathāyodhyāṃ jagāma saḥ // LiP_2,5.75 //
children.translated_text: considering himself fulfilled, and went to <s>Ayodhyā</s>. (LiP 2.5.75)
After that best of sages had departed, the great sage <s>Parvata</s> too,

children.text: praṇamya mādhavaṃ hṛṣṭo rahasyenamuvāca ha // LiP_2,5.76 //
children.translated_text: bowing joyfully to <s>Mādhava</s>, spoke to him in private: (LiP 2.5.76)
Having first informed the Lord of the Universe about <s>Nārada</s>'s doings,

children.text: golāṅgūlamukhaṃ yadvanmukhaṃ bhāti tathā kuru // LiP_2,5.77 //
children.translated_text: [he said:] 'Make it so that his face shines like a monkey's face.' (LiP 2.5.77)
Hearing this, Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> [said]: 'I shall do what you have asked.

children.text: gaccha śīghramayodhyāṃ vai māvedīrnāradasya vai // LiP_2,5.78 //
children.translated_text: Go quickly to <s>Ayodhyā</s>; do not reveal [this] to <s>Nārada</s>.' (LiP 2.5.78)

children.text: tvayā me saṃvidaṃ tatra tathetyuktvā jagāma saḥ /
children.translated_text: '[I shall keep] your agreement there' — having said 'so be it,' he departed.

children.text: tato rājā samājñāya prāptau munivarau tadā // LiP_2,5.79 //
children.translated_text: Then the king, learning that both great sages had arrived, (LiP 2.5.79)
adorned all of <s>Ayodhyā</s> — decked with banners and garlands —
with various auspicious [decorations], with flowers and parched rice all around. (LiP 2.5.80)
With doorways of houses sprinkled with water, with marketplaces and highways moistened,
endowed with divine fragrant essences, perfumed with celestial incense. (LiP 2.5.81)

children.text: kṛtvā ca nagarīṃ rājā maṇḍayāmāsa tāṃ sabhām /
children.translated_text: Having thus [prepared] the city, the king adorned that assembly hall
with divine fragrances, incenses, and various gems. (LiP 2.5.82)
Adorned with jeweled pillars, embellished with manifold garlands,
furnished with most precious carpets and divine auspicious seats. (LiP 2.5.83)

children.text: kṛtvā nṛpendrastāṃ kanyāṃ hyādāya praviveśa ha /
children.translated_text: Having prepared [the hall], the lord of men entered, bringing that maiden —
adorned with all ornaments, with large eyes like <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) herself. (LiP 2.5.84)
Her waist measured by the hand, smooth in five [features], with an auspicious face,

children.text: strībhiḥ parivṛtāṃ divyāṃ śrīmatīṃ saṃśritāṃ tadā // LiP_2,5.85 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by women, divine, beautiful, graced [with splendor] — she stood there then. (LiP 2.5.85)

children.text: sabhā ca sā bhūpapeḥ samṛddhā maṇipravekottamaratnacitrā /
children.translated_text: And that assembly of the king was prosperous, wondrous with the finest gems and jewels,

children.text: nyastā sanā mālyavatī subaddhā tāmāyayuste nararājavargāḥ // LiP_2,5.86 //
children.translated_text: well-arranged, garlanded, well-built — groups of princes came to it. (LiP 2.5.86)
Then the other one — the son of <s>Brahmā</s>'s boon, learned in the three <s>Vedas</s>, the glorious great soul —

children.text: saparvato brahmavidāṃva riṣṭho mahāmunirnārada ājagāma // LiP_2,5.87 //
children.translated_text: the great sage <s>Nārada</s>, accompanied by <s>Parvata</s>, the foremost among knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, arrived. (LiP 2.5.87)
Seeing those two arrive, the king, with agitated mind,
took divine seats and worshipped them both. (LiP 2.5.88)

children.text: ubhau devarṣisiddhau tau ubhau jñānavidāṃ varau /
children.translated_text: Both were divine sages and <s>Siddhas</s>; both were the best among knowers;
both great souls, the best of sages, were seated — [having come] for the maiden's sake. (LiP 2.5.89)

children.text: tāvubhau praṇipatyāgre kanyāṃ tāṃ śrīmatīṃ śubhām /
children.translated_text: Having first bowed to them both, [the king] presented that beautiful and auspicious maiden,

children.text: sutāṃ kamalapatrākṣīṃ prāha rājā yaśasvinīm // LiP_2,5.90 //
children.translated_text: his daughter, lotus-petal-eyed — the king said to the illustrious one: (LiP 2.5.90)
'Whichever of these two, O blessed one, you desire in your heart as husband,
to him give this garland, bowing as is proper.' (LiP 2.5.91)

children.text: evamuktā tu sā kanyā strībhiḥ parivṛtā tadā /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that maiden, surrounded by women,
taking a divine golden garland, the beautiful-eyed one, (LiP 2.5.92)
went and stood where those two great souls were seated,

children.text: vīkṣamāṇā muniśreṣṭhau nāradaṃ parvataṃ tathā // LiP_2,5.93 //
children.translated_text: gazing upon the two best of sages — <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>. (LiP 2.5.93)

children.text: muniśreṣṭhaṃ na paśyāmi nāradaṃ parvataṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: 'I do not see the best of sages — neither <s>Nārada</s> nor <s>Parvata</s>.
But in their midst [I see] one — of nearly sixteen years of age.' (LiP 2.5.94)
With agitated mind, there she stood, trembling like a plantain tree in the wind.

children.text: tasthau tāmahā rājāsau vatse kiṃ tvaṃ kariṣyasi // LiP_2,5.95 //
children.translated_text: The king said to her: 'Daughter, what will you do? (LiP 2.5.95)
Choose one of these two and give this garland, O auspicious one.'

children.text: sā prāha pitaraṃ trastā imau tau naravānarau // LiP_2,5.96 //
children.translated_text: She said to her father, frightened: 'These two are man-monkeys! (LiP 2.5.96)

children.text: muniśreṣṭhaṃ na paśyāmi nāradaṃ parvataṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: I do not see the best of sages — neither <s>Nārada</s> nor <s>Parvata</s>.
But in their midst [I see] one — of nearly sixteen years of age, (LiP 2.5.97)
adorned with all ornaments, resembling an <s>atasī</s> (flax) flower [in complexion],
with long arms, with wide eyes, with a noble and lofty chest, (LiP 2.5.98)
with lines marked on his waist and neck, with reddish, large, elongated eyes,
adorned with a pair of handsome brows arching like bent bows, (LiP 2.5.99)
with clearly separated triple folds [on the belly], with navel visible on his auspicious abdomen,
clad in golden garments, with lofty jeweled nails, auspicious,
with lotus-shaped hands — him, lotus-faced, lotus-eyed. (LiP 2.5.100)
With a fine nose, with a lotus-heart, with <s>Padmanābha</s> (lotus-navel), surrounded by <s>Śrī</s> (splendor),
with rows of teeth exceedingly resembling jasmine (<s>kunda</s>) buds. (LiP 2.5.101)

children.text: hasaṃtaṃ māṃ samālokya dakṣiṇaṃ ca prasārya vai /
children.translated_text: Smiling while gazing at me, extending his right

children.text: pāṇiṃ sthitamamuṃ tatra paśyāmi śubhamūrdhajam // LiP_2,5.102 //
children.translated_text: hand, standing there — him I see, with beautiful hair.' (LiP 2.5.102)
With agitated mind, trembling there like a plantain tree,

children.text: sthitāṃ tāmāha rājāsau vatse kiṃ tvaṃ kariṣyasi // LiP_2,5.103 //
children.translated_text: she stood — the king said to her: 'Daughter, what will you do?' (LiP 2.5.103)
When this was said, the sage <s>Nārada</s>, having fallen into doubt, spoke:

children.text: kiyanto bāhavastasya kanye brūhi yathātatham // LiP_2,5.104 //
children.translated_text: 'How many arms does he have, O maiden? Tell me truly.' (LiP 2.5.104)
'I see two arms,' said the maiden with a pure smile.

children.text: prāha tāṃ parvatastatra tasya vakṣaḥsthale śubhe // LiP_2,5.105 //
children.translated_text: <s>Parvata</s> then asked her there: 'On his auspicious chest, (LiP 2.5.105)

children.text: kiṃ paśyasi ca me brūhi kare kiṃ vāsya paśyasi /
children.translated_text: what do you see? Tell me. And what do you see in his hand?'

children.text: kanyā tamāha mālāṃ vai pañcarūpāmanuttamām // LiP_2,5.106 //
children.translated_text: The maiden said to him: 'I see an unsurpassed garland of five colors. (LiP 2.5.106)
On his chest I see [the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark]; in his hand, a bow and arrows.'
Thus addressed, the two best of sages, [each] unsurpassed, (LiP 2.5.107)

children.text: manasā cintayantau tau māyeyaṃ kasyacid bhavet /
children.translated_text: both pondered mentally: 'Whose illusion (<s>māyā</s>) could this be?'

children.text: māyāvī taskaro nūnaṃ svayameva janārdanaḥ // LiP_2,5.108 //
children.translated_text: 'The trickster is surely none other than <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) himself! (LiP 2.5.108)
He has come but has not acted [as promised] — how has this happened to our faces,
this monkey-likeness?' — thus <s>Nārada</s> pondered. (LiP 2.5.109)
<s>Parvata</s> too [thought] accordingly: 'How has this monkey-form
befallen me?' — thus he too fell into mental anguish. (LiP 2.5.110)

children.text: tato rājā praṇamyāsau nāradaṃ parvataṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Then the king, bowing to <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>,

children.text: bhavadbhyāṃ kimidaṃ tatra kṛtaṃ buddhivimohajam // LiP_2,5.111 //
children.translated_text: [said:] 'What is this that you two have done there — born of delusion of the mind? (LiP 2.5.111)
