children.text: svasthau bhavantau tiṣṭhetāṃ yathā kanyārtha mudyatau /
children.translated_text: May you both remain composed, as [befits] those who have come for the maiden's hand.'
Thus addressed, the two best of sages said to the king, agitated: (LiP 2.5.112)
'It is you who are producing the delusion — we are not [deluded] at all.
Let her choose one of us two — do not delay!' (LiP 2.5.113)
Then that maiden again, having bowed to her chosen deity,
[saw the one] who stood in their midst, assuming <s>māyā</s>, composed — (LiP 2.5.114)
adorned with all ornaments, resembling an <s>atasī</s> flower,
with long arms, well-nourished limbs, with eyes extending to the ears — (LiP 2.5.115)

children.text: pūrvavatpuruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā mālāṃ tasmai dadau hi sā /
children.translated_text: seeing that person as before, she gave the garland to him.

children.text: anantaraṃ hi sā kanyā na dṛṣṭā manujaiḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,5.116 //
children.translated_text: Immediately thereafter, that maiden was not seen again by mortals. (LiP 2.5.116)
Then there arose a cry: 'What is this?' — they were astonished.

children.text: tāmādāya gato viṣṇuḥ svasthānaṃ puruṣottamaḥ // LiP_2,5.117 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, taking her, went to his own abode, the Supreme Person. (LiP 2.5.117)
Long ago, for that very purpose, that beautiful woman had performed austerities constantly.

children.text: śrīmatī sā samutpannā sā gatā ca tathā harim // LiP_2,5.118 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Śrīmatī</s> was born [for this]; and thus she went to <s>Hari</s>. (LiP 2.5.118)
Both those tiger-among-sages, humiliated and deeply pained,

children.text: vāsudevaṃ prati tadā jagmaturbhavanaṃ hareḥ // LiP_2,5.119 //
children.translated_text: went then to <s>Vāsudeva</s>'s abode — the house of <s>Hari</s>. (LiP 2.5.119)
Seeing those two arrive, Lord <s>Hari</s> said to <s>Śrīmatī</s>:
'The two best of sages have come — hide yourself here.' (LiP 2.5.120)

children.text: tathetyuktvā ca sā devī prahasaṃtī cakāra ha /
children.translated_text: 'So be it,' said the Goddess, and did so, laughing.

children.text: nāradaḥ praṇipatyāgre prāha dāmodaraṃ harim // LiP_2,5.121 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s>, having bowed first, said to <s>Dāmodara</s> <s>Hari</s>: (LiP 2.5.121)

children.text: priyaṃ hi kṛtavānadya mama tvaṃ parvatasya hi /
children.translated_text: 'You have done a fine deed today — for me and for <s>Parvata</s>!

children.text: tvameva nūnaṃ govinda kanyāṃ tāṃ hṛtavānāsi // LiP_2,5.122 //
children.translated_text: Surely it was you, O <s>Govinda</s>, who stole that maiden! (LiP 2.5.122)
Having deluded us both with your own wit, having deceived [us], O best of the gods!'
Thus addressed, the person <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the imperishable one, covering his ears

children.text: pāṇibhyāṃ prāha bhagavān bhavadbhyāṃ kimudīritam // LiP_2,5.123 //
children.translated_text: with both hands, said: 'What have you two said? (LiP 2.5.123)
Even one filled with desire — is this the conduct of a sage? Oh indeed!'

children.text: evamukto muniḥ prāha vāsudevaṃ sa nāradaḥ // LiP_2,5.124 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the sage <s>Nārada</s> said to <s>Vāsudeva</s>: (LiP 2.5.124)
'Why [did you give me] a monkey's face?' — [speaking] at the base of his ear.

children.text: karṇamūle tamāhedaṃ vānaratvaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // LiP_2,5.125 //
children.translated_text: At the base of his ear, he told him: 'The monkey-form was made by me. (LiP 2.5.125)
On <s>Parvata</s>'s [request], O learned one, I made you a monkey-face.

children.text: mayā tava kṛtaṃ tatra priyārthaṃ nānyathā tviti // LiP_2,5.126 //
children.translated_text: It was done by me for your benefit, not otherwise.' (LiP 2.5.126)
<s>Parvata</s> too asked likewise; to him too [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] spoke the same way.
As both listened there, <s>Dāmodara</s> spoke [these] words: (LiP 2.5.127)
'I did you both a favor — by truth I swear upon myself.'

children.text: nāradaḥ prāha dharmātmā āvayormadhyataḥ sthitaḥ // LiP_2,5.128 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s>, the righteous one, said: 'Who was that person who stood in our midst, (LiP 2.5.128)

children.text: dhanuṣmān puruṣaḥ ko ḥtra tāṃ hṛtvā gatavānkila /
children.translated_text: holding a bow — who took her and departed?'

children.text: tac chrutvā vāsudevo 'sau prāha tau munisattamau // LiP_2,5.129 //
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Vāsudeva</s> said to those two best of sages: (LiP 2.5.129)
'There are many great-souled wielders of illusion, O best ones.

children.text: tatra sā śrīmatī nūnamadṛṣṭvā munisattamau // LiP_2,5.130 //
children.translated_text: As for that <s>Śrīmatī</s> — surely, [she chose] without seeing the two best of sages.' (LiP 2.5.130)
'I am always the disc-bearer, four-armed — thus I remain.

children.text: tāṃ tathā nāhamaicchaṃ vai bhavadbhyāṃ viditaṃ hi tat // LiP_2,5.131 //
children.translated_text: I did not desire her at all — you both know that.' (LiP 2.5.131)
Thus addressed, bowing to him, they spoke with pleased minds:

children.text: ko 'tra doṣastava vibho nārāyaṇa jagatpate // LiP_2,5.132 //
children.translated_text: 'What fault is there in you, O Lord, O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, master of the universe? (LiP 2.5.132)
The wickedness was that king's alone — he created the illusion.'
Having spoken thus, the sages <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s> departed from there. (LiP 2.5.133)
Having reached <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, [<s>Nārada</s>] pronounced a curse upon him:
'O <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>! Since we two came here, (LiP 2.5.134)
having invited [us], you afterwards gave the maiden to another by trickery.
Therefore, by [this] <s>māyā</s>-connection, darkness shall overcome you. (LiP 2.5.135)
And through that, you shall know your own self exceedingly and truly.'
When this curse was pronounced, a mass of darkness arose. (LiP 2.5.136)

children.text: nṛpaṃ prati tataścakraṃ viṣṇoḥ prādurabhūt kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Then, toward the king, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus (<s>cakra</s>) instantly appeared.

children.text: cakravitrāsitaṃ ghoraṃ tāvubhau tama abhyagāt // LiP_2,5.137 //
children.translated_text: Terrified by the discus, that terrible mass of darkness — [together with] those two — was engulfed. (LiP 2.5.137)
Then, trembling in all limbs, the two great sages fled,
looking behind at the discus and the irresistible mass of darkness. (LiP 2.5.138)
'The maiden-<s>siddhi</s> has indeed been obtained by us!' — [they cried] as they sped along,
running ceaselessly to the ends of the world, tormented by fear. (LiP 2.5.139)
'Save [us]! Save [us]!' — crying out to <s>Govinda</s>, tormented by fear,

children.text: viṣṇulokaṃ tato gatvā nārāyaṇa jagatpate // LiP_2,5.140 //
children.translated_text: they went to <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>: 'O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, Lord of the Universe! (LiP 2.5.140)
O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, O <s>Padmanābha</s>, O <s>Janārdana</s>!
Save us, O <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>! You are our protector, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>!' (LiP 2.5.141)
Then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the glorious one bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, reflecting,

children.text: nivārya cakraṃ dhvāntaṃ ca bhaktānugrahakāmyayā // LiP_2,5.142 //
children.translated_text: halted the discus and the darkness, out of desire to grace his devotees: (LiP 2.5.142)
'<s>Ambarīṣa</s> is my devotee, and these two are the best of sages.

children.text: anayorasya ca tathā hitaṃ kāryaṃ mayādhunā // LiP_2,5.143 //
children.translated_text: I must now act for the welfare of both them and him.' (LiP 2.5.143)

children.text: āhūya tattamaḥ śrīmān girā prahlādayan hariḥ /
children.translated_text: Having summoned that darkness, the glorious <s>Hari</s>, gladdening [them] with his voice,

children.text: provāca bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śṛṇutāṃ ma idaṃvacaḥ // LiP_2,5.144 //
children.translated_text: the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> spoke: 'Hear this word of mine: (LiP 2.5.144)

children.text: ṛṣiśāpo na caivāsīdanyathā ca varo mama /
children.translated_text: The curse of the sage cannot be otherwise, nor can my boon.'

children.text: datto nṛpāya rakṣārthaṃ nāsti tasyānyathā punaḥ // LiP_2,5.145 //
children.translated_text: [He was] given to the king for protection — there is no alternative for that. (LiP 2,5.145)
The son of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>'s son's grandson, of great fame,

children.text: śrīmāndasaratho nāma rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ // LiP_2,5.146 //
children.translated_text: the glorious one named <s>Daśaratha</s>, shall become a righteous king. (LiP 2,5.146)
I shall be his eldest son, named <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tatra me dakṣiṇobāhurbharato nāma vai bhavet // LiP_2,5.147 //
children.translated_text: My right arm shall be [the one] named <s>Bharata</s>; (LiP 2,5.147)

children.text: śatrughno nāma savyaśca śeṣo 'sau lakṣmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śatrughna</s> shall be [my] left, and the remaining one is known as <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra māṃ samupāgaccha gacchedānīṃ nṛpaṃ vinā // LiP_2,5.148 //
children.translated_text: There, come to me — go now, without the king, (LiP 2,5.148)

children.text: muniśreṣṭhau ca hitvā tvamiti smāha ca mādhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: and leaving the two best of sages' — thus spoke <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: evam uktaṃ tamo nāśaṃ tatkṣaṇāc ca jagāma vai // LiP_2,5.149 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the darkness vanished that very instant, (LiP 2,5.149)
and <s>Hari</s>'s discus was restrained and stood as before.
The two best of sages, freed from fear, having bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>, (LiP 2,5.150)
departed, burning with grief, and said to each other:
'From this day until the end of our bodies, we two shall never accept a maiden (LiP 2,5.151)

children.text: na kariṣyāva ityuktvā pratijñāya ca tāvṛṣī /
children.translated_text: [in marriage]' — having spoken thus and vowed, those two sages,
devoted to <s>yoga</s> and meditation, pure, remained as before. (LiP 2,5.152)
King <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, having protected the earth,
endowed with servants and kinsmen, went to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world. (LiP 2,5.153)
For the honor of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> and also of the two lion-like sages,
<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, became [incarnate], though the Lord did not reveal Himself. (LiP 2,5.154)
And all the sages, <s>Bhṛgu</s> and other best of sages,

children.text: māyā na kāryā vidvadbhirityāhuḥ prekṣyataṃ harim // LiP_2,5.155 //
children.translated_text: said, 'The wise should not employ <s>māyā</s> (illusion)' — looking upon <s>Hari</s>. (LiP 2,5.155)
<s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>, having long understood the deception,
condemning the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, became devoted to <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2,5.156)
All this has been told by me to you today —

children.text: aṃbarīṣasya māhātmyaṃ māyāvitvaṃ ca vai hareḥ // LiP_2,5.157 //
children.translated_text: the greatness of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> and the illusory nature of <s>Hari</s>. (LiP 2,5.157)
Whoever reads, hears, or causes others to hear this,

children.text: māyāṃ visṛjya puṇyātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati // LiP_2,5.158 //
children.translated_text: that meritorious soul, abandoning illusion, goes to <s>Rudra</s>'s world. (LiP 2,5.158)
This is the most sacred, supreme, meritorious [text], proclaimed by the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātaḥ paṭhennityaṃ viṣṇoḥ sāyujyamāpnuyāt // LiP_2,5.159 //
children.translated_text: One who reads it daily, morning and evening, attains union with <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (LiP 2,5.159)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge śrīmatyākhyānaṃ nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled 'The Narrative of <s>Śrīmat</s>.'
The sages said:
The illusory nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the God of Gods, the wise one, has been heard.
How did <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> originate from <s>Janārdana</s>, the God of Gods? (LiP 2,6.1)
Please tell us this truly, O <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The glorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the creator, without beginning or end, the Lord — (LiP 2,6.2)
the Lord of the world created this twofold universe for the sake of delusion.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed [created] the brahmins, the <s>Vedas</s>, the eternal Vedic <s>dharmas</s>, (LiP 2,6.3)
<s>Śrī</s>, the excellent <s>Padmā</s> (Lotus-Goddess) — he made [these] one portion.
<s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Alakṣmī</s> (Misfortune), the inauspicious one, those outside the <s>Vedas</s>, the lowest of men, (LiP 2,6.4)
and <s>adharma</s> — the greatly splendid one fashioned as another portion.
Having created <s>Alakṣmī</s> first, and <s>Padmā</s> afterwards, <s>Janārdana</s> — (LiP 2,6.5)
therefore <s>Alakṣmī</s> is called <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (the Elder), O best of twice-born ones.
At the time of the churning of the nectar, right after the terrible poison, (LiP 2,6.6)

children.text: aśubhā sā tathotpannā jyeṣṭhā iti ca vai śrutam /
children.translated_text: that inauspicious one arose — thus she is known as <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śrīśca samutpannā padmā viṣṇuparigrahaḥ // LiP_2,6.7 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śrī</s> arose, <s>Padmā</s>, the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (LiP 2,6.7)
A brahmin-sage named <s>Duḥsaha</s> married that inauspicious one,

children.text: jyeṣṭhāṃ tāṃ paripūrṇo 'sau manasā vīkṣya dhiṣṭhitām // LiP_2,6.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, seeing her full and well-established, with [his] mind [set]. (LiP 2,6.8)

children.text: lokaṃ cacāraṃ hṛṣṭātmā tayā saha munistadā /
children.translated_text: The sage then wandered the world with her, his heart delighted.

children.text: yasmin ghoṣo hareścaiva harasya ca mahātmanaḥ // LiP_2,6.9 //
children.translated_text: Wherever the sounds of <s>Hari</s> and of the great-souled <s>Hara</s> [were heard], (LiP 2,6.9)
and the chanting of the <s>Vedas</s>, and brahmins, and likewise the smoke of <s>homa</s> offerings,

children.text: bhasmāṅgino vā yatrāsaṃstatra tatra bhayārditā // LiP_2,6.10 //
children.translated_text: or wherever those whose bodies were smeared with ash resided — there, stricken with fear, (LiP 2,6.10)
covering her ears, she would flee, running here and there.
Seeing <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> behaving thus, <s>Duḥsaha</s> became bewildered. (LiP 2,6.11)

children.text: tayā saha vanaṃ gatvā cacāra sa mahāmuniḥ /
children.translated_text: Going with her to the forest, that great sage wandered.

children.text: tapo mahadvane ghore yāti kanyā pratigraham // LiP_2,6.12 //
children.translated_text: [He thought:] 'Great austerity in the terrible forest — [since] she will accept no maiden's (LiP 2,6.12)

children.text: na kariṣyāmi cetyuktvā pratijñāya ca tāmṛṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: [replacement] — I shall not [remarry].' Having vowed thus regarding her, the sage,

children.text: yogajñānaparaḥ śuddho yatra yogīśvaro muniḥ // LiP_2,6.13 //
children.translated_text: devoted to <s>yoga</s> and knowledge, pure — where [he found] the lord of <s>yogīs</s>, the sage, (LiP 2,6.13)
there he saw the great-souled <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> approaching.
Bowing to the great soul, <s>Duḥsaha</s> said to the sage: (LiP 2,6.14)
'This wife of mine, O illustrious one, will not stay anywhere!

children.text: kiṃ karomīti viprarṣe hyanayā saha bhāryayā // LiP_2,6.15 //
children.translated_text: What shall I do, O brahmin-sage, with this wife? (LiP 2,6.15)

children.text: praviśāmi tathā kutra kuto na praviśāmyaham /
children.translated_text: Where shall I enter, and where shall I not enter?'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
'Hear, O <s>Duḥsaha</s>! Everywhere, ill-repute, accompanied by inauspiciousness — (LiP 2,6.16)
this incomparable <s>Alakṣmī</s> is called <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.
Where those devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, following the path of the <s>Vedas</s>, (LiP 2,6.17)
great-souled devotees of <s>Rudra</s> whose bodies are dusted with ash,

children.text: sthitā yatra janā nityaṃ mā viśethāḥ kathañcana // LiP_2,6.18 //
children.translated_text: where such people always abide — you must never enter there! (LiP 2,6.18)
[Where people chant:] "<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>,
<s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, (LiP 2,6.19)

children.text: rudra rudreti rudreti śivāya ca namo namaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>! Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>!
Salutation to the most auspicious one! To <s>Śaṅkara</s>, always!" (LiP 2,6.20)
[Where they proclaim:] "<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>!"

children.text: umāyāḥ pataye caiva hiraṇyapataye sadā // LiP_2,6.21 //
children.translated_text: And [salute] the lord of <s>Umā</s>, the lord of gold, (LiP 2,6.21)
"Salutations to the golden-armed one, to the bull-bannered one!"

children.text: nṛsiṃhavāmanācintya mādhaveti ca ye janāḥ // LiP_2,6.22 //
children.translated_text: And [where people say] "<s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, O inconceivable <s>Mādhava</s>!" — (LiP 2,6.22)
where brahmins and <s>kṣatriyas</s> constantly and joyfully utter [these names],

children.text: vaiśyāḥ śūdrāśca ye nityaṃ teṣāṃ dhanagṛhādiṣu /
children.translated_text: and <s>vaiśyas</s> and <s>śūdras</s> too always — in their homes, wealth, and possessions,

children.text: ārāme caiva goṣṭheṣu na viśethāḥ kathañcana // LiP_2,6.23 //
children.translated_text: in their gardens and cow-pens — you must never enter! (LiP 2,6.23)
The terrifying garland of flames, blazing like a thousand suns,

children.text: cakraṃ viṣṇoratīvograṃ teṣāṃ hanti sadāśubham // LiP_2,6.24 //
children.translated_text: the exceedingly fierce discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — it always destroys inauspiciousness in their [homes]. (LiP 2,6.24)

children.text: svāhākāro vaṣaṭkāro gṛhe yasmin hi vartate /
children.translated_text: In whichever house the <s>svāhā</s>-offering and the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-call are performed —

children.text: taddhitvā cānyamāgaccha samāghoṣetha yatra vā // LiP_2,6.25 //
children.translated_text: leave that and go elsewhere, or wherever there is no such invocation. (LiP 2,6.25)
Those constantly devoted to Vedic study, dedicated to daily rites,
devoted to the worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s> — avoid them from afar! (LiP 2,6.26)

children.text: agnihotraṃ gṛhe yeṣāṃ liṅgārcā vā gṛheṣu ca /
children.translated_text: In whose homes there is the sacred fire, or worship of the <s>liṅga</s>,
or the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, or where <s>Caṇḍikā</s> resides — (LiP 2,6.27)
go far away, leaving them, those who are free from all sin.
Those who worship <s>Maheśvara</s> with obligatory and occasional sacrifices — (LiP 2,6.28)

children.text: tān hitvā vraja cānyatra duḥsahatvaṃ sahānayā /
children.translated_text: leaving them, go elsewhere, O <s>Duḥsaha</s>, together with her.

children.text: śrotriyā brāhmaṇā gāvo guravo 'tithayaḥ sadā // LiP_2,6.29 //
children.translated_text: Vedic scholars, brahmins, cows, teachers, guests — always (LiP 2,6.29)
and devotees of <s>Rudra</s> are honored — where they are, avoid those [places]!
<s>Duḥsaha</s> said:

children.text: yasminpraveśo yogyo me tadbrūhi munisattama // LiP_2,6.30 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, O best of sages, where I am fit to enter! (LiP 2,6.30)
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: na śrotriyā dvijā gāvo guravo 'tithayaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: 'Where there are no Vedic scholars, twice-born, cows, teachers, or guests,

children.text: yatra bhartā ca bhāryā ca parasparavirodhinau // LiP_2,6.31 //
children.translated_text: where husband and wife are mutually hostile — (LiP 2,6.31)
By your words, freed from fear — [tell me] in whose houses I may always enter.'
with your wife, you may enter that house without fear.
Where the God of Gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, Lord of the Three Worlds, (LiP 2,6.32)
is reviled — enter there without fear.
Where there is no devotion to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, where <s>Sadāśiva</s> is absent, (LiP 2,6.33)

children.text: japahomādikaṃ nāsti bhasma nāsti gṛhe nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: where there is no <s>japa</s>, <s>homa</s>, and the like, where there is no sacred ash in the house,
where there is no worship on festival days, especially on the fourteenth (<s>caturdaśī</s>), (LiP 2,6.34)
on <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> (the dark eighth), where [people] at twilight are devoid of ash,

children.text: caturdaśyāṃ mahādevaṃ na yajanti ca yatra vai // LiP_2,6.35 //
children.translated_text: where on the fourteenth they do not worship <s>Mahādeva</s> — (LiP 2,6.35)
those who are bereft of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s name, associated with evil souls —

children.text: namaḥ kṛṣṇāya śarvāya śivāya parameṣṭhine // LiP_2,6.36 //
children.translated_text: [where people do not say] "Salutation to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>, to the Supreme Being, (LiP 2,6.36)
brahmins and men, deluded, evil-natured, do not utter [these names] —

children.text: tatraiva satataṃ vatsa sabhāryastvaṃ samāvisa // LiP_2,6.37 //
children.translated_text: there, always, O child, enter with your wife. (LiP 2,6.37)

children.text: vedaghoṣo na yatrāsti gurupūjādayo na ca /
children.translated_text: Where there is no chanting of the <s>Vedas</s>, no worship of the teacher,
those devoid of rites for the ancestors — enter there with your wife. (LiP 2,6.38)

children.text: rātrau rātrau gṛhe yasmin kalaho vartate mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: In whichever house there is quarreling night after night,

children.text: anayā sārdhamaniśaṃ viśa tvaṃ bhayavarjitaḥ // LiP_2,6.39 //
children.translated_text: enter there constantly with her, without fear. (LiP 2,6.39)

children.text: liṅgārcanaṃ yasya nāsti yasya nāsti japādikam /
children.translated_text: Where there is no worship of the <s>liṅga</s>, where there is no <s>japa</s> and the like,

children.text: rudrabhaktirvinindā ca tatraiva viśa nirbhayaḥ // LiP_2,6.40 //
children.translated_text: and devotion to <s>Rudra</s> is reviled — enter there fearlessly. (LiP 2,6.40)
Where no guest, no Vedic scholar, no teacher, no <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>,

children.text: na saṃti yadgṛhe gāvaḥ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa // LiP_2,6.41 //
children.translated_text: no cows are present in the house — enter there with your wife. (LiP 2,6.41)
Where [people] eat delicacies while children watch,

children.text: bhakṣyāṇi tatra saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa // LiP_2,6.42 //
children.translated_text: without giving [to them] — enter there gleefully with your wife. (LiP 2,6.42)
Where <s>Mahādeva</s> or <s>Vāsudeva</s> is not worshipped,

children.text: ahutvā vidhivadyatra tatra nityaṃ samāviśa // LiP_2,6.43 //
children.translated_text: where oblations are not offered according to rule — always enter there. (LiP 2,6.43)
Where the deluded, engaged in sinful deeds, devoid of compassion toward one another,

children.text: gṛhe yasminsamāsaṃte deśe vā tatra saṃviśa // LiP_2,6.44 //
children.translated_text: dwell in that house or region — enter there. (LiP 2,6.44)
Where the compound walls and buildings are in ruins, where the housewife is not venerated —

children.text: tadgṛhaṃ tu samāsādya vasa nityaṃ hi hṛṣṭadhīḥ // LiP_2,6.45 //
children.translated_text: go to that house and dwell there always with a glad mind. (LiP 2,6.45)
Where there are thorny trees, where there are bean-creepers,
and where there is a <s>Brahma</s>-tree (palāśa) — enter there with your wife. (LiP 2,6.46)
<s>Agastya</s>, <s>arka</s> (sun-plant) and the like, <s>bandhujīva</s> (pentapetes) in the houses,
<s>karavīra</s> (oleander) especially, or <s>nandyāvarta</s> (jasmine), (LiP 2,6.47)

children.text: mallikā vā gṛhe yeṣāṃ sabhāryāstvaṃ samāviśa /
children.translated_text: or <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) in whose houses — enter there with your wife.

children.text: kanyā ca yatra vai vallī drohī vā ca jaṭī gṛhe // LiP_2,6.48 //
children.translated_text: Where there is a maiden-creeper, or a traitor, or a matted-haired one in the house, (LiP 2,6.48)
where there are many plantains — enter there with your wife.

children.text: tālaṃ tamālaṃ bhallātaṃ tittiḍīkhaṇḍameva ca // LiP_2,6.49 //
children.translated_text: Palm tree, <s>tamāla</s>, marking nut (<s>bhallāta</s>), and <s>tittiḍī</s> grove, (LiP 2,6.49)
<s>kadamba</s> or <s>khadira</s> (acacia) — enter there with your wife.

children.text: nyagrodhaṃ vā gṛhe yeṣāmaśvatthaṃ cūtameva vā // LiP_2,6.50 //
children.translated_text: In whose houses there is a banyan tree, a <s>pipal</s> tree, or a mango, (LiP 2,6.50)
or a cluster fig (<s>udumbara</s>) or jackfruit — enter there with your wife.

children.text: yasya kākagṛhaṃ niṃbe ārāme vā gṛhepi vā // LiP_2,6.51 //
children.translated_text: Where crows nest in a neem tree, in the garden or the house, (LiP 2,6.51)
or a staff-bearing or shaven-headed [ascetic is present] — enter there with your wife.

children.text: ekā dāsī gṛhe yatra trigavaṃ pañcamāhiṣam // LiP_2,6.52 //
children.translated_text: Where there is a single maidservant in the house, three cows, five buffaloes, (LiP 2,6.52)
six horses, seven elephants — enter there with your wife.

children.text: yasya kālī gṛhe devī pretarūpā ca ḍākinī // LiP_2,6.53 //
children.translated_text: Where the dark goddess <s>Kālī</s> [is worshipped], or a ghost-formed <s>Ḍākinī</s>, (LiP 2,6.53)
or where a <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> [field-guardian deity] resides — enter there with your wife.

children.text: bhikṣubiṃbaṃ ca vai yasya gṛhe kṣapaṇakaṃ tathā // LiP_2,6.54 //
children.translated_text: Where there is a mendicant's image, or a Jain image in the house, (LiP 2,6.54)

children.text: bauddhaṃ vā biṃbamāsādya tatra pūrṇaṃ samāviśa /
children.translated_text: or upon finding a Buddhist image — enter there fully.
At times of sleeping, sitting, eating, wandering, and daily activities, (LiP 2,6.55)

children.text: yeṣāṃ vadati no vāṇī nāmāni ca hareḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: those whose speech never utters the names of <s>Hari</s> —

children.text: tadgahaṃ te samākhyātaṃ sabhāryasya niveśitum // LiP_2,6.56 //
children.translated_text: that house is declared fit for you and your wife to settle in. (LiP 2,6.56)
Those devoted to heretical practices, excluded from <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> [rites],
devoid of devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, revilers of <s>Mahādeva</s>, (LiP 2,6.57)
atheists and deceivers — where they are, enter with your wife.

children.text: sarvasmādadhikatvaṃ ye na vadanti pinākinaḥ // LiP_2,6.58 //
children.translated_text: Those who do not declare the supremacy of <s>Pinākin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) above all, (LiP 2,6.58)
who regard Him as merely ordinary — enter there with your wife.'

children.text: brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śakraḥ sarvasureśvaraḥ // LiP_2,6.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Indra</s>, the lord of all gods — (LiP 2,6.59)
that they are born from the grace of <s>Rudra</s> — evil-minded [people] do not say this.

children.text: brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śakraśca sama eva ca // LiP_2,6.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Indra</s> are equal — (LiP 2,6.60)

children.text: vadanti mūḍhāḥ khadyotaṃ bhānuṃ vā mūḍhacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: thus say the deluded, confused minds, [comparing] a firefly to the sun.

children.text: teṣāṃ gṛhe tathā kṣetra āvāse vā sadānayā // LiP_2,6.61 //
children.translated_text: In their houses, fields, and dwellings — enter perpetually, O <s>Anayā</s> [Misfortune]; (LiP 2,6.61)

children.text: viśa bhuṅkṣva gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ api pūrṇamananyadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: enter their houses, even [if they are] full, O single-minded one.

children.text: ye 'śranti kevalaṃ mūḍhāḥ pakvamannaṃ vicetasaḥ // LiP_2,6.62 //
children.translated_text: Those who are merely deluded fools, witless, cooking food [without ritual], (LiP 2,6.62)

children.text: snānamaṅgalahīnāś ca teṣāṃ tvaṃ gṛham āviśa /
children.translated_text: devoid of bathing and auspicious rites — enter their houses.
A woman who has fallen from purity, devoid of bodily sacraments, (LiP 2,6.63)
always devoted to eating everything [without discrimination] — enter her abode.
Those mortals whose faces are dirty, who wear soiled garments, (LiP 2,6.64)
householders with filthy teeth — enter their houses.
Those free from [the practice of] washing feet, sleeping at twilight time, (LiP 2,6.65)

children.text: saṃdhyāyāma śrute ye vai gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
children.translated_text: who indeed [sleep] during the <s>Sandhyā</s> [twilight prayers] — enter their houses.
Mortals addicted to overeating, men addicted to excessive drinking, (LiP 2,6.66)
deluded by the practice of gambling and quarreling — enter their houses.

children.text: brahmasvahāriṇo ye cāyogyāṃścaiva yajanti vā // LiP_2,6.67 //
children.translated_text: Those who steal sacred property (<s>brahmasva</s>), or who worship unworthy [recipients], (LiP 2,6.67)
or who eat food from <s>Śūdras</s> — enter their houses.
Those sinners devoted to drinking liquor, devoted to eating meat, (LiP 2,6.68)
mortals given to other men's wives — enter their houses.

children.text: parvaṇyanarcābhiratā maithune vā divā ratāḥ // LiP_2,6.69 //
children.translated_text: Those who do not worship on sacred days (<s>parvan</s>), or who engage in intercourse by day, (LiP 2,6.69)

children.text: saṃdhyāyāṃ maithunaṃ yeṣāṃ gṛhe teṣāṃ samāviśa /
children.translated_text: those who have intercourse at twilight — enter their houses.

children.text: pṛṣṭhato maithunaṃ yeṣāṃ śvānavanmṛgavacca vā // LiP_2,6.70 //
children.translated_text: Those who copulate from behind, like dogs or animals, (LiP 2,6.70)
or who copulate in water — enter [their houses] together with [your] husband.

children.text: rajasvalāṃ striyaṃ gaccheccāṇḍālīṃ vā narādhamaḥ // LiP_2,6.71 //
children.translated_text: The lowest of men who goes to a menstruating woman, or to a <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, (LiP 2,6.71)

children.text: kanyāṃ vā gogṛhe vāpi gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
children.translated_text: or a virgin, or in a cow-shed — enter their houses.
What use of much prattling? Those excluded from daily rites, (LiP 2,6.72)
those devoid of devotion to <s>Rudra</s> — enter their houses.

children.text: śṛṅgairdivyauṣadhaiḥ kṣudraiḥ śepha ālipya gacchati // LiP_2,6.73 //
children.translated_text: He who smears the penis with horns [shavings], divine herbs, or mean [substances] and engages [in intercourse], (LiP 2,6.73)
causing the vulva to discharge — enter [his house] together with [your] husband.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ityuktvā sa muniḥ śrīmān nirmārjya nayane tadā // LiP_2,6.74 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that illustrious sage, wiping his eyes then, (LiP 2,6.74)
the <s>Brahmarṣi</s>, resembling <s>Brahmā</s>, vanished right there.

children.text: duḥsahaśca tathoktāni stānāni ca samīyivān // LiP_2,6.75 //
children.translated_text: <s>Duḥsaha</s> then went to the places [that were] described; (LiP 2,6.75)
especially [the houses] of those of vile nature who disrespect the God of Gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: sabhāryo muniśārdūlaḥ saiṣā jyeṣṭhā iti smṛtā // LiP_2,6.76 //
children.translated_text: together with his wife. She is known as <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> [the Elder]. (LiP 2,6.76)
<s>Duḥsaha</s> said this to her, between a reservoir and a hermitage:

children.text: āsva tvamatra cāhaṃ vai pravekṣyāmi rasātalam // LiP_2,6.77 //
children.translated_text: "You stay here, and I shall enter the netherworld (<s>Rasātala</s>). (LiP 2,6.77)
Having found a dwelling place for us two,

children.text: āgamiṣyāmi te pārśvamityuktā tamuvāca sā // LiP_2,6.78 //
children.translated_text: I shall come back to your side." Thus told, she said to him: (LiP 2,6.78)

children.text: kimaśrāmi mahābhāga ko me dāsyati vai balim /
children.translated_text: "What shall I eat, O greatly fortunate one? Who will give me offerings?"

children.text: ityuktastāṃ muniḥ prāha yāḥ striyastvāṃ yajanti vai // LiP_2,6.79 //
children.translated_text: Thus asked, the sage told her: "The women who worship you (LiP 2,6.79)

children.text: balibhiḥ puṣpadhūpaiśca na tāsāṃ ca gṛhaṃ viśa /
children.translated_text: with offerings, flowers, and incense — do not enter their houses."
Having said this, he entered the netherworld there through a burrow. (LiP 2,6.80)

children.text: adyāpi ca vinirmagno muniḥ sa jalasaṃstare /
children.translated_text: Even today, that sage has not emerged from the water-surface.
The inauspicious one [Jyeṣṭhā/Alakṣmī] perpetually dwells outside villages and mountains. (LiP 2,6.81)
Incidentally, the God of Gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, Lord of the Three Worlds,

children.text: lakṣmyā dṛṣṭastayā lakṣmīḥ sā tamāha janārdanam // LiP_2,6.82 //
children.translated_text: was seen by <s>Lakṣmī</s> together with her [Alakṣmī]; <s>Lakṣmī</s> spoke to <s>Janārdana</s>: (LiP 2,6.82)

children.text: bhartā gato mahābāho bilaṃ tyaktvā sa māṃ prabho /
children.translated_text: "My husband has gone, O Mighty-Armed, into the burrow, abandoning me, O Lord!

children.text: anāthāhaṃ jagannātha vṛttiṃ dehi namostu te // LiP_2,6.83 //
children.translated_text: I am without protector, O Lord of the Universe — give me livelihood! Salutations to you!" (LiP 2,6.83)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed, Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, laughing, said
to <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, [who is] <s>Alakṣmī</s> [Misfortune] — the God of Gods, <s>Mādhava</s>, Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>: (LiP 2,6.84)
<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> said:
"Those who revile <s>Rudra</s> — the sinless, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Blue-Red One —

children.text: aṃbāṃ haimavatīṃ vāpi janitrīṃ jagatāmapi // LiP_2,6.85 //
children.translated_text: or <s>Ambā</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s> [Pārvatī], the mother of the worlds — (LiP 2,6.85)
or who revile My devotees — their wealth is indeed yours.

children.text: yepi caiva mahādevaṃ vinindyaiva yajanti mām // LiP_2,6.86 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having reviled <s>Mahādeva</s>, worship Me — (LiP 2,6.86)

children.text: mūḍhā hyabhāgyā madbhaktā api teṣāṃ dhanaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: deluded, unfortunate [are] My devotees too — their wealth is yours.

children.text: yasyājñayā hyahaṃ brahmā prasādādvartate sadā // LiP_2,6.87 //
children.translated_text: He by whose command I and <s>Brahmā</s> always function through his grace — (LiP 2,6.87)
those who worship [Me] while reviling [Him] are producers of enmity toward Me.

children.text: madbhaktā naiva te bhaktā iva vartanti durmadāḥ // LiP_2,6.88 //
children.translated_text: They are not My devotees — they merely act as devotees, intoxicated with pride. (LiP 2,6.88)

children.text: teṣāṃ gṛhaṃ dhanaṃ kṣetramiṣṭāpūrtaṃ tavaiva hi /
children.translated_text: Their houses, wealth, fields, and merit of sacrifices and public works are indeed yours."
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ityuktvā tāṃ parityajya lakṣmyālakṣmīṃ janārdanaḥ // LiP_2,6.89 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Janārdana</s>, dismissing that <s>Alakṣmī</s> with <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s [permission], (LiP 2,6.89)
recited the mantra of Lord <s>Rudra</s> for the destruction of <s>Alakṣmī</s>.
Therefore, offerings should always be given to her, O lords of sages, (LiP 2,6.90)
by devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — no doubt — with all effort, always.
She should always be worshipped by women with various offerings, O twice-born ones. (LiP 2,6.91)
Whoever reads, hears, or causes the best of twice-born ones to hear
the account of <s>Alakṣmī</s>, sinless, attains the state of one with <s>Lakṣmī</s>. (LiP 2,6.92)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge alakṣmīvṛttaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhe 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the sixth chapter named 'The Account of <s>Alakṣmī</s>.'
The sages said:
"By reciting what is a being freed from fears of all worlds and the like,
completely freed from all sins, and attains the supreme destination? (LiP 2,7.1)
Abandoning <s>Alakṣmī</s>, shall a mortal go by recitation
to become a dwelling of <s>Lakṣmī</s>? O <s>Sūta</s>, please tell us here." (LiP 2,7.2)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
"What was formerly told by the Grandfather [<s>Brahmā</s>] to the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: vakṣye saṃkṣepataḥ sarvaṃ sarvalokahitāya vai // LiP_2,7.3 //
children.translated_text: I shall tell in summary — everything for the welfare of all worlds. (LiP 2,7.3)
Let all hear these words, having bowed to <s>Janārdana</s>,
the God of Gods, unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the imperishable, the immutable, (LiP 2,7.4)
the destroyer of all sins, the pure one, the bestower of liberation, the expounder of <s>Brahman</s>.
The wise one who performs meritorious deeds, with mind, action, and speech, (LiP 2,7.5)
should always recite [the name of] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, bowing to the Supreme Person.
While sleeping — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> the God; while walking — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> likewise; (LiP 2,7.6)
while eating — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, O Brahmins; while standing, while awake — the Eternal One.
Whether opening or closing the eyes — '<s>Namo Nārāyaṇa</s>' indeed. (LiP 2,7.7)

children.text: bhojyaṃ peyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca namo nārāyaṇeti ca /
children.translated_text: Food to be eaten, drink, and food to be licked — [saying] '<s>Namo Nārāyaṇa</s>',

children.text: abhimantrya spṛśanbhuṅkte sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // LiP_2,7.8 //
children.translated_text: having consecrated [it] with the mantra, touching and eating — he goes to the supreme destination. (LiP 2,7.8)
Completely freed from all sins, he attains the destination of the righteous.

children.text: alakṣmīśca mayā proktā patnī yā duḥsahasya ca // LiP_2,7.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Alakṣmī</s>, whom I have described as the wife of <s>Duḥsaha</s> — (LiP 2,7.9)
hearing the word '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' she departs — there is no doubt.

children.text: yā lakṣmīrdevadevasya hareḥ kṛṣṇasya vallabhā // LiP_2,7.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who is the beloved of <s>Hari</s> <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the God of Gods, (LiP 2,7.10)
dwells in the house, field, dwelling, and body [of such a person], O ones of excellent vows.

children.text: āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,7.11 //
children.translated_text: Having examined all scriptures and deliberated again and again, (LiP 2,7.11)
this one [conclusion] is well-established: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> should always be meditated upon.

children.text: kiṃ tasya bahubhirmantraiḥ kiṃ tasya bahubhirvrataiḥ // LiP_2,7.12 //
children.translated_text: What need has he of many mantras? What need of many vows? (LiP 2,7.12)
'<s>Namo Nārāyaṇāya</s>' — this mantra accomplishes all purposes.

children.text: tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu namo nārāyaṇeti ca // LiP_2,7.13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, at all times, [saying] '<s>Namo Nārāyaṇa</s>' — (LiP 2,7.13)
one who recites [this] goes, O best of Brahmins, to <s>Viṣṇuloka</s> with his kinsmen.
And another [teaching] about the God of Gods — hear, O best of sages. (LiP 2,7.14)
A mantra formerly practiced by me, accomplishing the purpose of all <s>Vedas</s>,
composed of twelve syllables, the twelve-fold, ancient [mantra]. (LiP 2,7.15)
I shall briefly describe to you its very greatness.
A certain greatly wise Brahmin, having performed austerities somehow, (LiP 2,7.16)
having produced a single son through her [his wife], with sacraments in due order,
having initiated him in due time, having performed the <s>upanayana</s> [sacred thread ceremony], (LiP 2,7.17)

children.text: adhyāpayāmāsa tadā sa ca novāca kiñcana /
children.translated_text: began to teach [him] then — but he did not say anything.

children.text: na jihvā spandate tasya duḥkhito 'bhūddvijottamaḥ // LiP_2,7.18 //
children.translated_text: His tongue did not move — the best of Brahmins became distressed. (LiP 2,7.18)
The <s>Aitareya</s> [the son] would constantly say only '<s>Vāsudeva</s>.'

children.text: pitā tasya tathā cānyāṃ pariṇīya yathāvidhi // LiP_2,7.19 //
children.translated_text: His father then married another [wife] according to proper rites, (LiP 2,7.19)
and produced sons, likewise according to prescribed methods.
Having studied the <s>Vedas</s>, accomplished, they became universally respected. (LiP 2,7.20)
<s>Aitareya</s>'s mother, distressed and overwhelmed with grief,
said: 'The [other] sons are accomplished, having mastered the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, (LiP 2,7.21)

children.text: brāhmaṇaiḥ pūjyamānā vai modayanti ca mātaram /
children.translated_text: honored by Brahmins, and they delight their mother.

children.text: mama tvaṃ bhāgyahīnāyāḥ putro jāto nirākṛtiḥ // LiP_2,7.22 //
children.translated_text: But you, son of my ill fortune, were born formless [incompetent]. (LiP 2,7.22)

children.text: mamātra nidhanaṃ śreyo na kathañcana jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Death would be better for me here — not life by any means.'

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa ca nirgamya yajñavāṭaṃ jagāma vai // LiP_2,7.23 //
children.translated_text: Thus spoken to, he went out and proceeded to the sacrificial enclosure. (LiP 2,7.23)

children.text: tasminyāte dvijānāṃ tu na mantrāḥ pratipedire /
children.translated_text: When he arrived, the mantras of the Brahmins did not come forth;
with <s>Aitareya</s> standing there, the Brahmins were confounded. (LiP 2,7.24)
Then speech arose [from him], from the chanting of '<s>Vāsudeva</s>';

children.text: aitareyasya te viprāḥ praṇipatya yatātatham // LiP_2,7.25 //
children.translated_text: the Brahmins, bowing to <s>Aitareya</s> in truth, (LiP 2,7.25)
performed worship, and then the sacrifice proceeded on its own.

children.text: tataḥ samāpya taṃ yajñamaitareyo dhanādibhiḥ // LiP_2,7.26 //
children.translated_text: Then, completing that sacrifice, <s>Aitareya</s>, with wealth and other [gifts], (LiP 2,7.26)
declared all the <s>Vedas</s> with six auxiliary sciences to the assembly, concentrated.

children.text: tuṣṭuvuśca tathā viprā brahmādyāśca tathā dvijāḥ // LiP_2,7.27 //
children.translated_text: The Brahmins praised [him], as did <s>Brahmā</s> and others, O twice-born ones; (LiP 2,7.27)
the sky-dwellers, <s>Siddhas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s> showered flowers.

children.text: evaṃ samāpya vai yajñamaitareyo dvijottamāḥ // LiP_2,7.28 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having completed the sacrifice, <s>Aitareya</s>, O best of twice-born, (LiP 2,7.28)

children.text: mātaraṃ pūjayitvā tu viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ jagāma ha /
children.translated_text: having honored his mother, went to the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
This entire [account of the] glory of the twelve-syllable [mantra] has been told. (LiP 2,7.29)
For those who read and hear [it] perpetually — it destroys great sins.
A person who perpetually recites the imperishable twelve-syllable [mantra] (LiP 2,7.30)
goes to the divine, incomparable supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Even one of sinful conduct, devoted to the twelve-syllable [mantra], (LiP 2,7.31)

children.text: prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
children.translated_text: attains the supreme abode — no deliberation is needed here.
How much more so those established in their own <s>dharma</s>, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s> — (LiP 2,7.32)

children.text: divyaṃ sthānaṃ mahātmānaḥ prāpnuvantīti suvratāḥ // LiP_2,7.33 //
children.translated_text: those great souls attain the divine abode, O ones of excellent vows. (LiP 2,7.33)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the seventh chapter named 'The Praise of the Twelve-Syllable [Mantra].'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The eight-syllable [mantra], O best of twice-born, is '<s>Namo Nārāyaṇa</s>';
and the twelve-syllable mantra is the supreme [mantra] of the Supreme Self. (LiP 2,8.1)
The six-syllable mantra, O Brahmins, is the repository of the meaning of all <s>Vedas</s> —
that which is '<s>Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya</s>' — a mantra accomplishing all purposes. (LiP 2,8.2)
And '<s>Śivatarāya</s>' [to the most auspicious] — the divine, auspicious five-syllable [mantra];

children.text: mayaskarāya cetyevaṃ namaste śaṅkarāya ca // LiP_2,8.3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mayaskarāya</s>' [to the bestower of happiness] — and likewise '<s>Namaste Śaṅkarāya ca</s>.' (LiP 2,8.3)
This seven-syllable [mantra] of <s>Rudra</s>, who is both <s>Pradhāna</s> [primal matter] and <s>Puruṣa</s> [spirit];

children.text: brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ // LiP_2,8.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and all the gods including <s>Indra</s> — (LiP 2,8.4)
with these mantras, O best of twice-born, the sages worship him,
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, the God of Gods, <s>Mayaskara</s>, born from the Unborn, (LiP 2,8.5)
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the God of Gods, Lord of <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: prāhurnamaḥ śivāyoti namaste śaṅkarāya ca // LiP_2,8.6 //
children.translated_text: They declare: '<s>Namaḥ Śivāya</s>' and '<s>Namaste Śaṅkarāya ca</s>,' (LiP 2,8.6)
'<s>Mayaskarāya Rudrāya</s>' and likewise '<s>Śivatarāya ca</s>.'

children.text: japtvā mucyeta vai vipro brahmahatyādibhiḥ kṣaṇāt // LiP_2,8.7 //
children.translated_text: Having recited [these], a Brahmin is freed from the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> [killing a Brahmin] and the like instantly. (LiP 2,8.7)

children.text: purā kaściddvijaḥ śakto dhundhumūka iti śrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Long ago, there was a powerful twice-born (<s>dvija</s>), known as <s>Dhundhumūka</s>;

children.text: āsīttṛtīye tretāyāmāvartte ca manoḥ prabhoḥ // LiP_2,8.8 //
children.translated_text: he lived in the third <s>Tretā</s> [age], in the cycle of <s>Manu</s>, the lord. (LiP 2.8.8)
In the <s>Meghavāhana</s> (Cloud-vehicle) <s>kalpa</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>, the Supreme Self,
having become a cloud, <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the god of gods, [carried] <s>Mahādeva</s>, the lord clad in hide, (LiP 2.8.9)
with great respect, [carrying] <s>Rudra</s>.
Exhausted by the excessive weight of <s>Rudra</s>, deprived of breath and exhalation, (LiP 2.8.10)
having informed the blue-throated (<s>Śitikaṇṭha</s>) [<s>Śiva</s>], the lotus-eyed one performed austerity.

children.text: tapasā paramaiśvaryaṃ balaṃ caiva tathādbhutam // LiP_2,8.11 //
children.translated_text: Through austerity, supreme sovereignty and also wonderful strength (LiP 2.8.11)
he obtained from the Supreme Lord <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Supreme Self.
Therefore, that <s>kalpa</s> was [known] by the name <s>Meghavāhana</s>. (LiP 2.8.12)
In that <s>kalpa</s>, by a sage's curse, the offspring of <s>Dhundhumūka</s> [was born];

children.text: dhundhumūkātmajastena durātmā ca babhūva saḥ // LiP_2,8.13 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s> — that wicked-souled one came into being. (LiP 2.8.13)
Long ago, <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, attached [to worldly pleasures], was deluded along with his wife;

children.text: tasyāṃ vai sthāpito garbhaḥ kāmāsaktena cetasā // LiP_2,8.14 //
children.translated_text: an embryo was placed in her by him, his mind attached to desire. (LiP 2.8.14)
On the very day of the new moon (<s>amāvāsyā</s>), in a <s>muhūrta</s> presided by <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: antarvatnī tadā bhāryā muktā tena yathāsukham // LiP_2,8.15 //
children.translated_text: the pregnant wife was released by him as he pleased. (LiP 2.8.15)

children.text: asūta sā ca tanayaṃ viśalyākhyā prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: She, named <s>Viśalyā</s>, gave birth with effort to a son,

children.text: rudre muhurte mandena vīkṣite munisattamāḥ // LiP_2,8.16 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Rudra</s>'s <s>muhūrta</s>, with inauspicious [planets] in view, O best of sages. (LiP 2.8.16)
Born inauspicious for mother, father, and for himself,
two sages said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Dhundhumūka</s> at that time: (LiP 2.8.17)
those two most excellent ones, <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> by name, [said] 'a bad son.'

children.text: vasiṣṭhaḥ prāha nīco 'pi prabhāvādvai bṛhaspateḥ // LiP_2,8.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> declared: 'Though low-born, by the power of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, (LiP 2.8.18)
this foolish son of yours shall still be freed from sin.'

children.text: duḥkhito dhundhumūko 'sau dṛṣṭvā putram avasthitam // LiP_2,8.19 //
children.translated_text: Distressed, <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, seeing the son [thus] situated, (LiP 2.8.19)
performed the birth-rites (<s>jātakarma</s>) and the like, according to rule, by himself,

children.text: adhyāpayāmāsa ca taṃ vidhinaiva dvijottamāḥ // LiP_2,8.20 //
children.translated_text: and educated him according to procedure, O best of twice-born. (LiP 2.8.20)
Studied according to propriety, the son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, O virtuous ones,
having married, then went forth, devoted to serving his teacher. (LiP 2.8.21)
This very son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, O best of sages, through wicked pride,
having enjoyed another woman, a <s>śūdra</s> woman, while seeing his own wife, day and night — (LiP 2.8.22)
sharing the same bed and seat, the son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, lowest of the twice-born,

children.text: tathā cacāra durbuddhistyaktvā dharmagatiṃ parām // LiP_2,8.23 //
children.translated_text: thus behaved, evil-minded, having abandoned the supreme path of <s>dharma</s>. (LiP 2.8.23)

children.text: mādhvī pītā tayā sārdhaṃ tena rāgavivṛddhaye /
children.translated_text: Honey-wine (<s>mādhvī</s>) was drunk by him together with her, to increase passion;
for some reason, on her account, O best of twice-born — (LiP 2.8.24)

children.text: nihatā sā ca pāpena vṛṣalī gatamaṅgalā /
children.translated_text: that <s>śūdra</s> woman was killed by that sinner, her auspiciousness destroyed.
Then, her brothers killed his father. (LiP 2.8.25)
And the mother of that evil-minded son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, the virtuous one,

children.text: bhāryā ca tasya durbuddheḥ śyālāste cāpi suvratāḥ // LiP_2,8.26 //
children.translated_text: and the wife of that evil-minded one, and his brothers-in-law too, O virtuous ones — (LiP 2.8.26)

children.text: rājñā kṣaṇādaho naṣṭa kulaṃ tasyāśca tasya ca /
children.translated_text: by the king, in an instant, destroyed was the family of both her and him.

children.text: gatvāsau dhaindhumūkaśca yena kenāpi līlayā // LiP_2,8.27 //
children.translated_text: Having gone, that son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, somehow, by chance, (LiP 2.8.27)
saw a best of sages devoted to the recitation of <s>Rudra</s>'s [name],

children.text: labdhvā pāśupataṃ tadvai purā devānmaheśvarāt // LiP_2,8.28 //
children.translated_text: who had formerly obtained the <s>Pāśupata</s> [vow] from the great Lord. (LiP 2.8.28)
Having obtained the five-syllable [mantra] and the supreme six-syllable [mantra],

children.text: punaḥ pañcākṣaraṃ caiva japtvā lakṣaṃ pṛthak pṛthak // LiP_2,8.29 //
children.translated_text: and again the five-syllable one — having recited each a hundred thousand times separately, (LiP 2.8.29)

children.text: vrataṃ kṛtvā ca vidhinā divyaṃ dvādaśamāsikam /
children.translated_text: and having performed the divine twelve-month vow according to rule,

children.text: kāladharmaṃ gataḥ kalpe pūjitaśca yamena vai // LiP_2,8.30 //
children.translated_text: he died according to the law of time, and was honored by <s>Yama</s> himself. (LiP 2.8.30)

children.text: uddhṛtā ca tathā mātā pitā śyālāśca suvratāḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus his mother was uplifted, and father, and brothers-in-law, O virtuous ones,

children.text: patnī ca subhagā jātā susmitā ca pativratā // LiP_2,8.31 //
children.translated_text: and his wife became fortunate, smiling, and devoted to her husband. (LiP 2.8.31)
Ascending celestial chariots (<s>vimāna</s>) with them, praised by the gods with <s>Indra</s>,
having attained the rank of <s>Gaṇapati</s> (lord of Śiva's hosts), he became dear to <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2.8.32)
Therefore, compared to the eight-syllable mantra and the twelve-syllable [mantra],

children.text: bhavetkoṭiguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // LiP_2,8.33 //
children.translated_text: [the five-syllable mantra] yields merit ten million times more — no deliberation is needed here. (LiP 2.8.33)
Therefore, the wise one should always recite, by the previously stated method,

children.text: śaktibījasamāyuktaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // LiP_2,8.34 //
children.translated_text: [the mantra] endowed with the <s>śakti</s>-seed — he goes to the supreme state. (LiP 2.8.34)
All this has been told to you — the entire essence of the narrative.
He who reads, or hears, or causes the best of twice-born to hear [this] — (LiP 2.8.35)

children.text: sa yāti brahmalokaṃ tu rudrajāpyamanuttamam // LiP_2,8.36 //
children.translated_text: he goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, [through] the supreme recitation of <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2.8.36)
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [ends] the eighth chapter.
The sages said:

children.text: devaiḥ purā kṛtaṃ divyaṃ vrataṃ pāśupataṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: The divine and auspicious <s>Pāśupata</s> vow was formerly performed by the gods,

children.text: brahmaṇā ca svayaṃ sūta kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā // LiP_2,9.1 //
children.translated_text: and by <s>Brahmā</s> himself, O <s>Sūta</s>, and by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of effortless deeds, (LiP 2.9.1)

children.text: patitena ca vipreṇa dhaindhumūkena vai tathā /
children.translated_text: and also by the fallen <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Dhundhumūka</s> —

children.text: kṛtvā japtvā gatiḥ prāptā kathaṃ pāśupataṃ vratam // LiP_2,9.2 //
children.translated_text: having performed and recited it, [he] attained [the supreme] goal. How [does] the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow [work]? (LiP 2.9.2)
How is <s>Paśupati</s>, the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme Lord?

children.text: vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ // LiP_2,9.3 //
children.translated_text: Please tell us — we are extremely curious. (LiP 2.9.3)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, freed from a curse, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, of great renown,
came here from the desert region to the god of gods, <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2.9.4)
Having abandoned the camel-body by the grace of <s>Rudra</s>, by his command,
and having approached the son of <s>Śilāda</s> [i.e. <s>Nandin</s>], bowing according to rule — (LiP 2.9.5)
the best of sages, stationed on <s>Meru</s>, having heard the supreme <s>dharma</s>

children.text: māheśvaraṃ muniśreṣṭhā hyapṛcchacca punaḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,9.6 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Maheśvara</s>, O best of sages, asked again and again. (LiP 2.9.6)
Having bowed to <s>Nandin</s>: 'How is <s>Paśupati</s>, the Lord?

children.text: vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ tatsarvaṃ ca tadāha saḥ // LiP_2,9.7 //
children.translated_text: Please tell us all that.' And he then said: (LiP 2.9.7)
All that was heard by <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s>, the lord.
Having heard from him, I now tell it to you. (LiP 2.9.8)

children.text: sarve śṛṇvaṃ tu vacanaṃ namaskṛtvā maheśvaram /
children.translated_text: All should listen to [these] words, having saluted <s>Maheśvara</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ paśupatirdevaḥ paśavaḥ ke prakīrtitāḥ // LiP_2,9.9 //
children.translated_text: 'How is <s>Paśupati</s> the god? Who are called the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls)? (LiP 2.9.9)

children.text: kaiḥ pāśaiste nibadhyante vimucyante ca te katham /
children.translated_text: By what bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) are they bound, and how are they released?'
<s>Śailādi</s> [<s>Nandin</s>] said:

children.text: sanatkumāra vakṣyāmi sarvam etad yathātatham // LiP_2,9.10 //
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, I shall tell all this as it truly is. (LiP 2.9.10)
To you, a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>, peaceful, of auspicious mind —
[all beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable [things], of the wise God of gods — (LiP 2.9.11)
are called <s>paśus</s> (bound souls), subject to the power of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ patitvādbhagavān rudraḥ paśupatiḥ smṛtaḥ // LiP_2,9.12 //
children.translated_text: Because of His lordship (<s>pati</s>-ship) over them, the blessed <s>Rudra</s> is called <s>Paśupati</s>. (LiP 2.9.12)
The beginningless and endless Creator, the blessed, imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s> —
the Supreme Lord binds [them] like animals with the bond of <s>māyā</s>. (LiP 2.9.13)
He alone is their liberator, served through the yoga of knowledge.
For those bound by the bond of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), no other liberator is accepted. (LiP 2.9.14)
Without Him, the Supreme Self, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Supreme Lord —
the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s> are indeed the bonds of the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2.9.15)
By those bonds, the one <s>Śiva</s>, worshipped by souls, liberates.
The one [Lord] binds the <s>paśus</s> with the twenty-four bonds, (LiP 2.9.16)
and that same blessed <s>Rudra</s>, when served, also liberates.
From bonds consisting of the ten sense-organs and arising from the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) — (LiP 2.9.17)
and from the bonds of elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>), the Lord liberates the <s>paśus</s>.

children.text: indriyārthamayaiḥ pāśair baddhvā viṣayinaḥ prabhuḥ // LiP_2,9.18 //
children.translated_text: Having bound the sense-enjoyers with bonds consisting of sense-objects, the Lord — (LiP 2.9.18)
quickly they become devotees through the service of the Supreme Lord.

children.text: bhaja ityeṣa dhātur vai sevāyāṃ parikīrtitaḥ // LiP_2,9.19 //
children.translated_text: The root <s>bhaj</s> is indeed declared [to mean] 'service.' (LiP 2.9.19)
Therefore, service is called by the wise <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) in the fullest sense.
Having bound the <s>paśus</s>, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a pillar, <s>Maheśvara</s>, (LiP 2.9.20)
with the three bonds consisting of the <s>guṇas</s>, Himself causes [all] activity to be performed.
When worshipped by the <s>paśus</s> with firm <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (devotion), (LiP 2.9.21)
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Supreme Lord, liberates them immediately.
Worship (<s>bhajana</s>) is called <s>bhakti</s> — by speech, mind, and bodily acts. (LiP 2.9.22)
Because it is the cause of all [liberation], it is most effective in cutting the bonds.

children.text: satyaḥ sarvaga ityādi śivasya guṇacintanā // LiP_2,9.23 //
children.translated_text: 'True, all-pervading' and the like — the contemplation of <s>Śiva</s>'s qualities, (LiP 2.9.23)
and contemplation of [His] form and material [aspect] — this is known as mental worship.

children.text: vācikaṃ bhajanaṃ dhīrāḥ praṇavādijapaṃ viduḥ // LiP_2,9.24 //
children.translated_text: The wise know verbal worship as the recitation of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and the like. (LiP 2.9.24)
Bodily worship is said by the good to be <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) and the like.
This bondage of embodied beings is through bonds of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. (LiP 2.9.25)
<s>Śiva</s> alone is the one liberator, the blessed Supreme Lord.
The twenty-four <s>tattvas</s>, <s>māyā</s>, <s>karma</s>, and the <s>guṇas</s> — (LiP 2.9.26)
along with sense-objects, are declared to be the bonds, because they bind the soul.
Those bound [by them] are freed only through devotion to <s>Śiva</s> — all embodied beings. (LiP 2.9.27)
<s>Śaṅkara</s> binds the <s>paśus</s> with bonds consisting of the five <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: sa eva mocakastoṣāṃ bhaktyā samyagupāsitaḥ // LiP_2,9.28 //
children.translated_text: He alone is their liberator, when properly worshipped with devotion. (LiP 2.9.28)

children.text: avidyāmasmitāṃ rāgaṃ dveṣaṃ ca dvipadāṃ varāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), O best of bipeds,
and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) — these are called the <s>kleśas</s>, which have become bonds. (LiP 2.9.29)
<s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom) —
and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) — thus the learned declare <s>avidyā</s> to be fivefold. (LiP 2.9.30)
Those souls, O tigers among sages, all of them, through <s>avidyā</s>,
the glorious <s>Śiva</s> liberates — no other whatsoever is the liberator. (LiP 2.9.31)
<s>Avidyā</s> is called <s>tamas</s>; <s>asmitā</s> is also [called] <s>moha</s>;

children.text: mahāmoha iti prājñā rāgaṃ yogaparāyaṇāḥ // LiP_2,9.32 //
children.translated_text: the wise, devoted to yoga, [call] <s>rāga</s> (attachment) <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion). (LiP 2.9.32)
<s>Dveṣa</s> (aversion) is called <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness);
and likewise <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) — [all are] false knowledge, [say] the discriminating. (LiP 2.9.33)
<s>Tamas</s> has eight subdivisions; <s>moha</s> is also known as eightfold;
the subdivisions of <s>mahāmoha</s> are considered by the wise to be ten. (LiP 2.9.34)
<s>Tāmisra</s> is said by the discerning to be of eighteen kinds;
and the divisions of <s>andhatāmisra</s> are likewise known as eighteen. (LiP 2.9.35)
Connection with <s>avidyā</s> [applies to souls] — neither past nor future [applies to God].
Through <s>rāga</s> (attachment), connection with the God who dwells in the body of [<s>Umā</s>] — (LiP 2.9.36)

children.text: kāleṣu triṣu saṃbandhastasya dveṣeṇa no bhavet /
children.translated_text: in the three times, there is no connection for Him through <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion).
For the God <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, the all-pervading One, who has transcended <s>māyā</s> — (LiP 2.9.37)
likewise through <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging), there is never any connection
for <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Refuge, <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Self. (LiP 2.9.38)
There is no connection for Him with meritorious or demeritorious actions.
In the three times, for <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, who has transcended <s>avidyā</s> — (LiP 2.9.39)

children.text: vipākaiḥ karmaṇāṃ vāpi na bhavedeva saṃgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: nor is there any contact with the fruits of actions.

children.text: kāleṣu triṣu sarvasya śivasya śivadāyinaḥ // LiP_2,9.40 //
children.translated_text: In the three times, for <s>Śiva</s>, the bestower of auspiciousness — (LiP 2.9.40)
untouched by pleasures and pains that exist in the three times.

children.text: sa tair vinaśvaraiḥ śaṃbhur bodhānandātmakaḥ paraḥ // LiP_2,9.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, whose nature is consciousness and bliss, the Supreme — is [untouched] by those perishable [things]. (LiP 2.9.41)
Untouched by latent impressions (<s>āśaya</s>) that belong to the three times —

children.text: dhiyāṃ patiḥ svabhūreṣa mahādevo maheśvaraḥ // LiP_2,9.42 //
children.translated_text: this Lord of intellects, self-existent, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2.9.42)
Untouchable by <s>karma</s>-impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) that exist in the three times,
and likewise by experience-impressions (<s>bhogasaṃskāra</s>) — the blessed Destroyer of Death (<s>Antakāntaka</s>). (LiP 2.9.43)
The God, the blessed Supreme Lord, surpassing [all] individual souls (<s>puruṣa</s>),
transcendent beyond the entire phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) of conscious and unconscious [beings]. (LiP 2.9.44)
In the world, knowledge and sovereignty are seen with degrees of superiority;
the wise call <s>Śiva</s> supreme because His [knowledge and sovereignty] are unsurpassable. (LiP 2.9.45)
At each [cycle of] re-creation, for those born, [He teaches] <s>Brahmā</s> the elaborate scripture,
He alone is the first teacher, for those who exist within the divisions of time. (LiP 2.9.46)
He is the teacher even of teachers who are limited by time;
the Lord of all, free from limitation by time. (LiP 2.9.47)
This relation is beginningless — supreme, between knowledge and eminence;
of those two thus established — all [this] is entirely pure by nature. (LiP 2.9.48)
In the absence of self-interest, compassion for others alone
is the purpose of all actions — [such is] the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). (LiP 2.9.49)
<s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) is the verbal designator of that <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Self;
even among the words '<s>Śiva</s>,' '<s>Rudra</s>,' and the like, <s>Praṇava</s> is considered supreme. (LiP 2.9.50)
Through meditation on <s>Śambhu</s>, who is designated by <s>Praṇava</s>, and through its recitation (<s>japa</s>),

children.text: yā siddhiḥ svaparāprāpyā bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ // LiP_2,9.51 //
children.translated_text: that accomplishment which is unattainable by oneself or by others — it certainly arises, without doubt. (LiP 2.9.51)
The essence of knowledge, through effort, is <s>Yoga</s> — the supreme <s>Pāśupata</s> [path];
it was declared by the God of Gods, out of compassion for all. (LiP 2.9.52)

He [Yājñavalkya] said thus: That which the yogis, [disciples of] <s>Gārgya</s>, describe as the Imperishable — gross, infinite, wondrous, not long, not red, not dark, not tawny, and purifying; without contact, without smell, without taste, without sight, without hearing, without speech, without mind, without radiance, without measure, without enjoyment, without name, without lineage, without death, without old age, without disease, immortal, of the sound 'Oṃ,' immortal, uncovered, without prior, without posterior, infinite, without exterior — it consumes nothing, nor does anything consume it. (LiP 2.9.53)

children.text: abhivadanti sthūlamanantaṃ mahāścaryamadīrghamalohitamamastakamāsāyamata evo punānasamasaṃgamagandhamarasamackṣuṣkamaśrotramavāṅmanotejaskamapramāṇamanusukhamanāmagotramamaramajaramanāmayamamṛtamoṃśabdamamṛtamasaṃvṛtamapūrvamanaparamanantamabāhyaṃ tadaśrāti kiñcana na tāśrāti kiñcana // LiP_2,9.53 //
children.translated_text: Having known this at the dissolution of time — the supreme <s>Pāśupata</s> Lord,
and in this supreme <s>Pāśupata Yoga</s> — for whom there is purpose indeed — (LiP 2.9.54)

children.text: yoge pāśupate cāsmin yasyārthaḥ kila uttame // LiP_2,9.54 //
children.translated_text: Having made <s>Oṃkāra</s> a lamp, seek the Householder (Śiva), subtle, dwelling within beginning and end; having controlled the door-dwelling [breath], most swift as wind, the leader of the senses —

children.text: kṛtvoṅkāraṃ pradīpaṃ mṛgaya gṛhapatiṃ sūkṣmamādyantarasthaṃ saṃyamya dvāravāsaṃ pavanapaṭutaraṃ nāyakaṃ condriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: for what reason do you babble with nets of words? No fear is seen whatsoever.

children.text: vāgjālaiḥ kasya hetorvibhaṭasi tu bhayaṃ dṛśyate naiva kiñciddehasthaṃ paśya śaṃbhuṃ bhramasi kimu pare sāstrajālendhakāre // LiP_2,9.55 //
children.translated_text: See <s>Śambhu</s> dwelling in the body — why do you wander in the darkness of the net of scriptures? (LiP 2.9.55)
Having thus been properly known by the wise, and as declared by <s>Śiva</s> to the sages,

children.text: asamarasaṃ pañcadhā kṛtvābhavaṃ cātmani yojayet // LiP_2,9.56 //
children.translated_text: having divided the incomparable essence fivefold, one should unite the unborn with the self. (LiP 2.9.56)
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me again the greatness of the Lord of <s>Umā</s>,
O great wise one, devotee of <s>Bhava</s>, O Blessed <s>Nandikeśvara</s>! (LiP 2.10.1)
<s>Śailādi</s> (Nandikeśvara) said:
O <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, I shall tell you briefly yet completely
the greatness of <s>Maheśa</s> (Great Lord), <s>Bhava</s>, the Supreme One (<s>Parameṣṭhin</s>). (LiP 2.10.2)
There was no bondage of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) for him, nor any bondage of intellect;
nor was there bondage of ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), nor did bondage of mind exist. (LiP 2.10.3)
There was no bondage of consciousness (<s>citta</s>) for him, nor was there bondage of hearing;

children.text: na tvacāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ vāpi bandho jajñe kadācana // LiP_2,10.4 //
children.translated_text: nor did bondage of skin or of sight ever arise. (LiP 2.10.4)
There was no bondage of tongue for him, nor any bondage of smell;
bondage of feet, bondage of hands, and bondage of speech, O one of excellent vows — (LiP 2.10.5)
bondage of the generative organ, and bondage of elements and subtle elements —
[none of these existed,] for by his eternally pure nature, he is eternally awakened by nature. (LiP 2.10.6)
He is declared 'eternally liberated' by sages who know the truth —
<s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme One, who has no beginning, middle, or end. (LiP 2.10.7)

children.text: buddhiṃ sūte niyogena prakṛtiḥ puruṣasya ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> produces intellect by the command of <s>Puruṣa</s> (Śiva);
intellect produces ego — by his command. (LiP 2.10.8)
Of him who is well-known as the Inner Controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>) in [all] bodies, the Self-existent —

children.text: indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca tanmātrāṇi ca śāsanāt // LiP_2,10.9 //
children.translated_text: the ten senses and one [mind], and the subtle elements — by [his] command — (LiP 2.10.9)
ego abundantly produces [them all] — of <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme One.

children.text: tanmātrāṇi niyogena tasya saṃsuvate prabho // LiP_2,10.10 //
children.translated_text: The subtle elements, by his command, produce [their effects], O Lord. (LiP 2.10.10)
The great elements entirely [arise from] the wise <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: brahmādīnāṃ tṛṇāntaṃ hi dehināṃ dehasaṃgatim // LiP_2,10.11 //
children.translated_text: For embodied beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — their bodily existence — (LiP 2.10.11)
all the great elements produce by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.
The intellect determines all objects by the command of the all-pervading Lord, (LiP 2.10.12)
of him who is well-known as the Inner Controller in [all] bodies, the Self-existent.
His sovereignty is self-established; his powers [arise] from his very nature. (LiP 2.10.13)
By his command, ego greatly conceives all objects;

children.text: cittaṃ cetayate cāpi manaḥ saṃkalpayatyapi // LiP_2,10.14 //
children.translated_text: consciousness cognizes, and mind resolves as well. (LiP 2.10.14)

children.text: śrotraṃ śṛṇoti tacchaktyā śabdasparśādikaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: The ear hears by his power — sound, touch, and the like —
by the force of the command of <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, the Supreme One. (LiP 2.10.15)
Speech produces utterances — never sounds and the like [independently] —
of all bodies whatsoever, by the command of that God. (LiP 2.10.16)
The hand performs grasping — never movement and the like [independently] —
of all creatures whatsoever, by the rule of the Creator. (LiP 2.10.17)
The foot performs movement — never excretion and the like [independently] —
of the multitude of all embodied beings, by the command of <s>Śiva</s> alone. (LiP 2.10.18)
The anus performs excretion — it would never speak —
of every born creature, by the command of the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2.10.19)
The generative organ constantly produces bliss, by the word of the all-pervading Lord;
of all beings whatsoever, by the command of the Lord alone. (LiP 2.10.20)
Space provides room for all beings

children.text: ākāśaṃ sarvadā tasya paramasyaiva śāsanāt // LiP_2,10.21 //
children.translated_text: at all times, by the command of that Supreme One. (LiP 2.10.21)
By the direction of <s>Śiva</s> himself, with its own divisions beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>,
wind (<s>Prabhañjana</s>) sustains the bodies of all beings. (LiP 2.10.22)
By the direction of the God of Gods, wind, present in the seven branches,
carries on the course of the world through its own divisions such as <s>Āvaha</s> and the rest. (LiP 2.10.23)
With its five divisions beginning with <s>Nāga</s>, [wind] operates in bodies
by the indication of the supreme God, the wind (<s>Samīraṇa</s>). (LiP 2.10.24)
Fire carries oblations (<s>havya</s>) to the gods, and offerings (<s>kavya</s>) to the ancestors (<s>kavyāśin</s>);

children.text: pākaṃ ca kurute vahniḥ śaṅkarasyaiva śāsanāt // LiP_2,10.25 //
children.translated_text: and fire performs cooking — by the command of <s>Śaṅkara</s> alone. (LiP 2.10.25)
Whatever food is eaten — the fire dwelling in the belly
cooks it for all embodied beings, by the command of the Lord of the Universe (<s>Viśveśvara</s>). (LiP 2.10.26)
The waters enliven all beings by his command;

children.text: avilaṅghyā hi sarveṣāmājñā tasya garīyasī // LiP_2,10.27 //
children.translated_text: indeed, the command of that most venerable one is inviolable by all. (LiP 2.10.27)
The earth supports all beings, moving and unmoving, by his command.

children.text: ājñayā tasya devasya devadevaḥ purandaraḥ // LiP_2,10.28 //
children.translated_text: By the command of that God, the God of Gods, <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) — (LiP 2.10.28)
afflicts the living with diseases and the dead with hundreds of torments;
the sustainer of the universe, for all time, by [his command] that cannot be transgressed by all worlds — (LiP 2.10.29)
casts down the gods, slays the celestials, standing throughout the three worlds;

children.text: adhārmikāṇāṃ vai nāśaṃ karoti śivaśāsanāt // LiP_2,10.30 //
children.translated_text: he brings about the destruction of the unrighteous — by the command of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2.10.30)
<s>Varuṇa</s> nourishes the worlds with waters by [his] command;
by his command, he drowns [the wicked] and binds demons with nooses. (LiP 2.10.31)
In accordance with merit, to all living beings,
<s>Vitteśvara</s> (Kubera, Lord of Wealth) bestows wealth — by the command of the Supreme One. (LiP 2.10.32)
Performing rising and setting, creating time by [his] command —
<s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) [acts thus] of that eternal, true Supreme Self. (LiP 2.10.33)
He causes flowers and medicinal plants to bloom and delights the creatures;
the nectar-rayed one (Moon), bearer of digits, [acts] by the command of the Time of Time (<s>Kālakāla</s>). (LiP 2.10.34)
The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s>,
and all other deities — are fashioned by his command. (LiP 2.10.35)
<s>Gandharvas</s>, divine messengers, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
<s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s> — stand in the ordinances of the Creator. (LiP 2.10.36)
Planets, constellations, stars, sacrifices, <s>Vedas</s>, and austerities,

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca gaṇāḥ sarve śāsanaṃ tasya dhiṣṭhitāḥ // LiP_2,10.37 //
children.translated_text: and all the hosts of sages — are established by his command. (LiP 2.10.37)
The hosts of the ancestors, the seven oceans, mountains and rivers,

children.text: śāsane tasya vartante kānanāni sarāṃsi ca // LiP_2,10.38 //
children.translated_text: forests and lakes — abide in his command. (LiP 2.10.38)
Fractions (<s>kalā</s>), instants (<s>kāṣṭhā</s>), eye-blinks (<s>nimeṣa</s>), <s>muhūrtas</s>, days, nights,
seasons, years, fortnights, and months — are established by his command. (LiP 2.10.39)
<s>Yugas</s> and <s>Manvantaras</s> stand by the command of <s>Śambhu</s>;
<s>Parās</s> and <s>Parārdhās</s> and other divisions of time [likewise]. (LiP 2.10.40)
Eight classes of gods, five classes of animals,
and humans — operate [by the will] of the wise God of Gods. (LiP 2.10.41)
The multitudes of beings born in the fourteen types of wombs,
situated in all worlds — stand by his command alone. (LiP 2.10.42)

children.text: caturdaśasu lokeṣu sthitā jātāḥ prajāḥ prabhoḥ /
children.translated_text: The creatures born and dwelling in the fourteen worlds
are subject to the command of that very Lord of All. (LiP 2.10.43)
All the netherworlds (<s>Pātāla</s>) and [upper] worlds by his command,

children.text: brahmāṇḍāni ca śeṣāṇi tathā sāvaraṇāni ca // LiP_2,10.44 //
children.translated_text: and the cosmic eggs (<s>Brahmāṇḍas</s>) with all their coverings — (LiP 2.10.44)
all the present cosmic eggs exist by his command,
endowed with all beings on every side. (LiP 2.10.45)
Innumerable past cosmic eggs [existed] by his command,
endowed with hosts of entities on every side. (LiP 2.10.46)
Future cosmic eggs, together with their constituent realities,
shall carry out the command of <s>Śiva</s>, with all their coverings. (LiP 2.10.47)
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me the manifestations (<s>vibhūtis</s>) of <s>Śiva</s> and [<s>Śivā</s>], O Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>,
O best among those who know the higher and lower [realities], O one absorbed in the Supreme Lord! (LiP 2.11.1)
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Indeed, I shall tell you the manifestations of <s>Śiva</s> and [<s>Śivā</s>],
O <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, O lord of yogis, O best son of <s>Brahmā</s>! (LiP 2.11.2)

children.text: paramātmā śivaḥ proktaḥ śivāsā ca prakīrtitā /
children.translated_text: The Supreme Self is called <s>Śiva</s>; and she is called <s>Śivā</s>.
<s>Śiva</s> himself is called the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>); the wise know <s>Māyā</s> as <s>Gaurī</s>. (LiP 2.11.3)

children.text: puruṣaṃ śaṅkaraṃ prāhurgaurīṃ ca prakṛtiṃ dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: The twice-born call <s>Śaṅkara</s> the <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person) and <s>Gaurī</s> the <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).

children.text: arthaḥ śaṃbhuḥ śivā vāṇī divaso 'jaḥ śivā niśā // LiP_2,11.4 //
children.translated_text: Meaning is <s>Śambhu</s>, speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>) is <s>Śivā</s>; day is <s>Aja</s> (the unborn), night is <s>Śivā</s>. (LiP 2.11.4)
The seven-threaded [sacrifice] is <s>Mahādeva</s>; <s>Rudrāṇī</s> is called the sacrificial fee (<s>Dakṣiṇā</s>).

children.text: ākāśaṃ śaṅkaro devaḥ pṛthivī śaṅkarapriyā // LiP_2,11.5 //
children.translated_text: Space is the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>; earth is the beloved of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2.11.5)
The ocean is the blessed <s>Rudra</s>; the shoreline is the daughter of the Mountain-king.

children.text: vṛkṣaḥ śūlāyudho devaḥ śūlapāṇipriyā latā // LiP_2,11.6 //
children.translated_text: The tree is the god who bears the trident; the creeper is the beloved of the Trident-bearer. (LiP 2.11.6)
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Hari</s> too — <s>Sāvitrī</s> is the half-bodied one of <s>Śaṅkara</s>;
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is <s>Maheśvara</s>; <s>Lakṣmī</s> is <s>Bhavānī</s>, the Supreme Goddess. (LiP 2.11.7)
The wielder of the thunderbolt (<s>Indra</s>) is <s>Mahādeva</s>; <s>Śacī</s> is the daughter of the Mountain-king.

children.text: jātavedāḥ svayaṃ rudraḥ svāhā śarvārdhakāyinī // LiP_2,11.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire) is <s>Rudra</s> himself; <s>Svāhā</s> is the half-bodied one of <s>Śarva</s>. (LiP 2.11.8)
<s>Yama</s> is the three-eyed god; his beloved is the daughter of the Mountain.

children.text: varuṇo bhagavān rudro gaurī sarvārthadāyinī // LiP_2,11.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> is the blessed <s>Rudra</s>; <s>Gaurī</s> is the bestower of all aims. (LiP 2.11.9)
Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) is the one with the young-crescent crest; <s>Śivā</s> is she who delights <s>Śiva</s>'s mind.
The lord of <s>Yakṣas</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) is the one with the half-crescent crown; prosperity (<s>Ṛddhi</s>) itself is known as <s>Śivā</s>. (LiP 2.11.10)
The one with the half-crescent diadem is the Moon; <s>Rohiṇī</s> is the beloved of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: saptasaptiḥ śivaḥ kāntā umādevī suvarcalā // LiP_2,11.11 //
children.translated_text: The seven-horsed one (Sun) is <s>Śiva</s>; his beloved <s>Umā Devī</s> is <s>Suvarcalā</s> (the Sun's wife). (LiP 2.11.11)
The six-faced destroyer of <s>Tripura</s> — <s>Devasenā</s> is the beloved of <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: umā prasūtīrvai jñeyā dakṣo devo maheśvaraḥ // LiP_2,11.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s> is to be known as <s>Prasūti</s> (the progenitress); <s>Dakṣa</s> is the god <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2.11.12)
<s>Manu</s>, called <s>Puruṣa</s>, is <s>Śambhu</s>; <s>Śatarūpā</s> is the beloved of <s>Śiva</s>.
The wise know <s>Bhavānī</s> as <s>Ākūti</s>, and <s>Ruci</s> as the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2.11.13)
<s>Bhṛgu</s> is the god who destroyed <s>Bhaga</s>'s eyes; <s>Khyāti</s> is the beloved of the three-eyed one.
<s>Marīci</s> is the blessed <s>Rudra</s>; <s>Saṃbhūti</s> is the beloved of the Lord. (LiP 2,11.14)
They know <s>Bhavānī</s> as the beautiful one, and <s>Kavi</s> as the Supreme Lord;

children.text: gaṅgādharegirā jñeyaḥ smṛtiḥ sākṣādumā smṛtā // LiP_2,11.15 //
children.translated_text: by the words of <s>Gaṅgādhara</s> (the bearer of the Ganges), <s>Smṛti</s> is to be known as <s>Umā</s> herself. (LiP 2,11.15)
<s>Pulastya</s> is the moon-crested one; <s>Prīti</s> is the beloved of the trident-bearer.
<s>Pulaha</s> is the destroyer of the three cities; <s>Dayā</s> is the beloved of the enemy of <s>Kāla</s>. (LiP 2,11.16)
