<s>Kratu</s> is the destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice; <s>Saṃnati</s> is the consort of the Lord.
The three-eyed <s>Atri</s> — <s>Umā</s> herself, known by the wise as <s>Anasūyā</s>. (LiP 2,11.17)
They call <s>Ūrjā</s> the venerable <s>Umā</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: śaṅkaraḥ puruṣāḥ sarve striyaḥ sarvā maheśvarī // LiP_2,11.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkara</s> is all males; all females are <s>Maheśvarī</s>. (LiP 2,11.18)

children.text: pulliṅgaśabdavācyā ye te ca rudāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those denoted by masculine-gender words — they are declared to be <s>Rudras</s>;

children.text: strīliṅgaśabdavācyā yāḥ sarvā gauryā vibhūtayaḥ // LiP_2,11.19 //
children.translated_text: those denoted by feminine-gender words — all are the glories (<s>vibhūtis</s>) of <s>Gaurī</s>. (LiP 2,11.19)
All men and women are said to be the glories of those two alone.
Whatever powers (<s>śaktis</s>) reside in all entities — those the wise know as <s>Gaurī</s>. (LiP 2,11.20)

children.text: sāsā viśveśvarī devī sa ca sarvo maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: She is that <s>Viśveśvarī</s> (sovereign of the universe), the Goddess; and He is the all-encompassing <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: śaktimantaḥ padārthā ye sa sa sarvo maheśvaraḥ // LiP_2,11.21 //
children.translated_text: Those entities that possess power (<s>śakti</s>) — He is that all-encompassing <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2,11.21)
The eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (primary natures) are declared to be the forms (<s>mūrtis</s>) of the Goddess,
and likewise the <s>vikṛtis</s> (modifications) are Her body-bound glories. (LiP 2,11.22)

children.text: visphuliṅgā yathā tāvadagnau ca bahudhā smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as sparks, being many, are [produced] from fire,

children.text: jīvāḥ sarve tathā śarvo dvandvasattvamupāgataḥ // LiP_2,11.23 //
children.translated_text: so all <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) — <s>Śarva</s> has entered into the state of dualities. (LiP 2,11.23)
All the bodies of embodied beings are forms of <s>Gaurī</s>;
and all the embodied souls are established as portions of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2,11.24)
All that is to be heard is the form of <s>Umā</s>; the hearer is the God <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The Lord assumes the nature of the experiencer; <s>Umā</s> assumes the nature of the experienced. (LiP 2,11.25)
The totality of things to be created is sustained by <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s beloved;

children.text: sraṣṭā sa eva viśvātmā bālacandrārdhaśekharaḥ // LiP_2,11.26 //
children.translated_text: the creator is He alone, the Soul of the universe, who bears the crescent moon on His crest. (LiP 2,11.26)
The visible world in the form of progeny is sustained by <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> (sovereign of the worlds);
the seer is <s>Viśveśvara</s>, the God who has the moon-fragment as His crest-jewel. (LiP 2,11.27)
All that is to be tasted is the form of <s>Umā</s>; all that is to be smelled is likewise [Her form];

children.text: devo rasayitā śaṃbhurghrātā ca bhuvaneśvaraḥ // LiP_2,11.28 //
children.translated_text: the taster is <s>Śambhu</s>, and the smeller is <s>Bhuvaneśvara</s> (Lord of the worlds). (LiP 2,11.28)
<s>Mahādevī Maheśvarī</s> sustains the nature of all that is to be thought;

children.text: mantā sa eva viśvātmā mahādevo maheśvaraḥ // LiP_2,11.29 //
children.translated_text: the thinker is He alone, the Soul of the universe, <s>Mahādeva Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2,11.29)

children.text: boddhavyaṃ vastu rūpaṃ ca bibharti bhavavallabhā /
children.translated_text: That which is to be known in its essential form is sustained by the beloved of <s>Bhava</s>;

children.text: devaḥ sa eva bhagavān boddhā bālenduśekharaḥ // LiP_2,11.30 //
children.translated_text: that blessed God, the knower, is He who wears the young crescent moon on His crest. (LiP 2,11.30)
The Goddess <s>Umā</s> has the form of the pedestal (<s>pīṭha</s>); <s>Śaṅkara</s> has the form of the <s>liṅga</s>.
Having installed [them] with effort, gods and demons worship [them]. (LiP 2,11.31)
Whatever entities bear the mark of the <s>liṅga</s> — they are the glories of <s>Śarva</s>;

children.text: arthā bhagāṅkitā yeye teta gauryā vibhūtayaḥ // LiP_2,11.32 //
children.translated_text: whatever entities are marked with the <s>bhaga</s> (yoni) — they are the glories of <s>Gaurī</s>. (LiP 2,11.32)
The entire cosmos — heaven, the netherworld, the worlds up to the eight coverings of the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) —

children.text: jñeyaṃ sarvamumārūpaṃ jñātā devo maheśvaraḥ // LiP_2,11.33 //
children.translated_text: all this is to be known as the form of <s>Umā</s>; the knower is the God <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2,11.33)
The Goddess, the beloved of the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, sustains the nature of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>);
and the blessed slayer of <s>Andhaka</s> holds the nature of the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). (LiP 2,11.34)
That king who abandons the <s>Śivaliṅga</s> and worships other deities —

children.text: sa nṛpaḥ saha deśena rauravaṃ narakaṃ vrajet // LiP_2,11.35 //
children.translated_text: along with his kingdom, he goes to the terrible <s>Raurava</s> hell. (LiP 2,11.35)

children.text: śivabhakto na yo rājā bhakto 'nyeṣu sureṣu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: A king who is not devoted to <s>Śiva</s> but is devoted to other gods —

children.text: svapatiṃ yuvatis tyaktvā yathā jāreṣu rājate // LiP_2,11.36 //
children.translated_text: [he is] like a young wife who, having abandoned her husband, shines among paramours. (LiP 2,11.36)
<s>Brahmā</s> and all the gods, kings of great splendor,

children.text: mānavā munayaścaiva sarve liṅgaṃ yajanti ca // LiP_2,11.37 //
children.translated_text: humans and sages too — all worship the <s>liṅga</s>. (LiP 2,11.37)

children.text: viṣṇunā rāvaṇaṃ hatvā sasainyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sutam /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> along with [his] army, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: sthāpitaṃ vidhivadbhaktyā liṅgaṃ tīre nadīpateḥ // LiP_2,11.38 //
children.translated_text: installed the <s>liṅga</s> with devotion according to proper rites on the shore of the lord of rivers [the ocean]. (LiP 2,11.38)
Even having committed thousands of sins and killed a hundred Brahmins,

children.text: bhāvātsamāśrito rudraṃ mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // LiP_2,11.39 //
children.translated_text: one who has taken refuge in <s>Rudra</s> with devotion is liberated — there is no doubt here. (LiP 2,11.39)

children.text: sarve liṅgamayā lokāḥ sarve liṅge pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All worlds are pervaded by the <s>liṅga</s>; all are established in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Therefore one should worship the <s>liṅga</s> if one desires the eternal abode. (LiP 2,11.40)
These two [<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>], of all forms, are established — by people desiring welfare, the auspicious pair

children.text: pūjanīyau namaskāryau cintanīyau ca sarvadā // LiP_2,11.41 //
children.translated_text: should always be worshipped, saluted, and contemplated. (LiP 2,11.41)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the eleventh chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me the eight forms of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the great soul,
of the God whose form is the universe, O <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> (lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>), O great-minded one. (LiP 2,12.1)
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Behold, I shall tell you the greatness of the Lord of <s>Umā</s>,
of the God whose form is the universe, O one born from the lotus-born [<s>Brahmā</s>]. (LiP 2,12.2)

children.text: bhūr āpo ḥgnir marud vyoma bhāskaro dīkṣitaḥ śaśī /
children.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, wind, space, the sun, the initiated one, and the moon —

children.text: bhavasya mūrtayaḥ proktāḥ śivasya parameṣṭhanaḥ // LiP_2,12.3 //
children.translated_text: these are declared to be the forms of <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2,12.3)
Space, moon, fire, sun, water, earth, wind — thus

children.text: tasyāṣṭa mūrtayaḥ proktā devadevasya dhīmataḥ // LiP_2,12.4 //
children.translated_text: eight forms are declared of the God of Gods, the wise one. (LiP 2,12.4)
When the <s>agnihotra</s> is offered in His sun-form, the great-souled one,
by that glory, all the gods are always satisfied. (LiP 2,12.5)
Just as by watering the root of a tree, the branches and sub-branches [are nourished],

children.text: tathā tasyārcayā devās tathā syus tadvibhūtayaḥ // LiP_2,12.6 //
children.translated_text: so by worshipping Him, the gods become His glories. (LiP 2,12.6)

children.text: tasya dvādaśadhā bhinnaṃ rūpaṃ sūryātmakaṃ prabhoḥ /
children.translated_text: His form as the sun-soul, the Lord, is divided twelve-fold;
containing all gods, worthy of sacrifice — the best of sages worship it. (LiP 2,12.7)
The ray called <s>Amṛtā</s> (nectar) of that one who has the form of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) in its entirety —

children.text: bhūtasaṃjīvanī ceṣṭā lokosmin pīyate sadā // LiP_2,12.8 //
children.translated_text: its activity revives beings; it is always drunk in this world. (LiP 2,12.8)
The rays called <s>Candra</s> (moon) of that <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (matted-haired one) in His sun-form —
for the growth of medicinal herbs, they spread cool rain. (LiP 2,12.9)
The rays called <s>Śuklā</s> (bright) of that <s>Śambhu</s> in His sun-form —
they spread <s>dharma</s> in the world, being the cause of the ripening of crops and such. (LiP 2,12.10)
Of Him in His <s>Divākara</s> (day-maker) form, the ray called <s>Harikeśa</s> —
it nourishes the constellations (<s>nakṣatras</s>), the well-known [ray] of the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2,12.11)
The ray called <s>Viśvakarman</s> nourishes <s>Budha</s> (Mercury),
belonging to the Lord of all, the God in His form of the seven-horsed [sun]. (LiP 2,12.12)
The ray called <s>Viśvavyacas</s> of that trident-bearing one —
it is known as the nourisher of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), belonging to the sun-formed one. (LiP 2,12.13)
The ray called <s>Saṃyadvasu</s> of the trident-bearer,
nourishes <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars, the red-limbed one), belonging to the thousand-rayed one. (LiP 2,12.14)
The ray called <s>Arvāvasu</s> of that trident-bearer
always nourishes <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), belonging to the burning one. (LiP 2,12.15)
The ray called <s>Svarāṭ</s> (self-luminous) of <s>Śiva</s> —
it nourishes <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) day and night, belonging to the one whose horses are tawny. (LiP 2,12.16)
Of the God in His sun-form, the source of the universe, the Lord of <s>Umā</s> —

children.text: suṣumṇākhyaḥ sadā raśmiḥ puṣṇāti śiśiradyutim // LiP_2,12.17 //
children.translated_text: the ray always called <s>Suṣumṇā</s> nourishes the cool-rayed one [the moon]. (LiP 2,12.17)
Having assumed the nature of the source of all gentle, wealth-producing things,

children.text: tasya somāhvayā mūrtiḥ śaṅkarasya jagadguroḥ // LiP_2,12.18 //
children.translated_text: that moon-form of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the teacher of the world, [is supreme]. (LiP 2,12.18)
His form as the moon-soul is established as the seminal essence (<s>śukra</s>)
in all embodied beings — belonging to the God who commands Death. (LiP 2,12.19)
Established in the mind of all embodied beings without exception —
the moon-formed body of <s>Śambhu</s>, the teacher of all the worlds. (LiP 2,12.20)
Of <s>Śambhu</s>, whose essence is the nectar-ray, divided sixteen-fold,
the supreme form called <s>Soma</s> (moon) [resides] in the bodies of all beings. (LiP 2,12.21)
It nourishes the gods and the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) always with divine nectar —

children.text: mūrtiḥ somāhvayā tasya devadevasya śāsituḥ // LiP_2,12.22 //
children.translated_text: the form called <s>Soma</s> of that God of Gods, the ruler. (LiP 2,12.22)
It nourishes all classes of herbs for the self-purification of embodied beings —
that body called <s>Soma</s> of His — one should designate it as <s>Bhavānī</s>. (LiP 2,12.23)
In the form of the lord of sacrifices, of beings, and of austerities —
this well-known form is indeed the moon-form of the Lord of <s>Umā</s>. (LiP 2,12.24)
As the lord of waters and herbs, it is renowned —
the moon-formed body of that <s>Śambhu</s>, the blessed Lord. (LiP 2,12.25)
The golden, pure God, the discriminator among all,
among all the sense-organs, the formless deity of deities — (LiP 2,12.26)
when that <s>Śiva</s>, the Lord in His moon-form, is established as the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul),
the sweetness dissolves — she who protects all the worlds. (LiP 2,12.27)
The form called <s>Yajamāna</s> (the sacrificer), belonging to <s>Śiva</s> who bestows auspiciousness,

children.text: puṣṇāti devatāḥ sarvāḥ kavyaiḥ pitṛgaṇānapi // LiP_2,12.28 //
children.translated_text: nourishes all the gods with offerings (<s>havya</s>) day and night, and the hosts of <s>pitṛs</s> with oblations (<s>kavya</s>). (LiP 2,12.28)
That body called <s>Yajamāna</s>, born of oblations —

children.text: vṛṣṭyā bhāvayati spaṣṭaṃ sarvameva parāparam // LiP_2,12.29 //
children.translated_text: through rain, it clearly nourishes everything, both superior and inferior. (LiP 2,12.29)

children.text: antaḥsthaṃ ca bahiḥsthaṃ ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ sthitaṃ jalam /
children.translated_text: The water situated inside and outside the cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍas</s>),
and within the bodies of beings — [that is] the mighty form of <s>Śambhu</s>. (LiP 2,12.30)
The nectar of rivers, of all streams always,

children.text: samudrāṇāṃ ca sarvatra vyāpī sarvamumāpatiḥ // LiP_2,12.31 //
children.translated_text: and of all oceans everywhere — the all-pervading Lord of <s>Umā</s>. (LiP 2,12.31)
The life-giving, purifying [form] of all beings,

children.text: aṃbikā prāṇasaṃsthā yā mūrtilaṃbumayī parā // LiP_2,12.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ambikā</s>, established in the vital breath — the supreme form made of water. (LiP 2,12.32)

children.text: antaḥsthaś ca bahiḥsthaś ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ vibhāvasuḥ /
children.translated_text: Situated inside and outside the cosmic eggs, the fire (<s>Vibhāvasu</s>),
residing within sacrifices and bodies — the mighty form of <s>Śambhu</s>. (LiP 2,12.33)
Residing within the bodies of beings, the auspicious sovereign form;

children.text: mūrtiḥ pāvaka saṃsthā yā śaṃbhoratyantapūjitā // LiP_2,12.34 //
children.translated_text: the form of <s>Śambhu</s> established in fire — it is supremely worshipped. (LiP 2,12.34)
Forty-nine divisions are enumerated by the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: havyaṃ vahati devānāṃ śaṃbhoryajñātmakaṃ vapuḥ // LiP_2,12.35 //
children.translated_text: The sacrifice-formed body of <s>Śambhu</s> carries the oblations (<s>havya</s>) of the gods. (LiP 2,12.35)
It conveys the offerings (<s>kavya</s>) of the hosts of ancestors, offered by the twice-born —
the supreme fire-formed body of <s>Śambhu</s>, comprising all gods. (LiP 2,12.36)
Those who know the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s> proclaim and worship it according to proper rites.
The wind (<s>Samīraṇa</s>), situated inside and outside the cosmic eggs, (LiP 2,12.37)
residing within the bodies of beings — [that is] the swift <s>Śaiva</s> form.
<s>Prāṇa</s> and others, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s> and others, <s>Āvaha</s> and other winds — (LiP 2,12.38)
all are declared as divisions of the single form of <s>Īśāna</s>.

children.text: antaḥsthaṃ jagadaṇḍānāṃ bahiḥsthaṃ ca viyadvibhoḥ // LiP_2,12.39 //
children.translated_text: Space (<s>viyat</s>) situated inside and outside the cosmic eggs, of the all-pervading Lord — (LiP 2,12.39)
situated within the bodies of beings — the mighty form of <s>Śambhu</s>.
The earth-sustaining form of <s>Śambhu</s> — the presiding deity of all <s>brahman</s> — (LiP 2,12.40)
it is known for sustaining all beings, moving and unmoving.
The bodies of all beings, moving and unmoving — the wise know (LiP 2,12.41)
are always composed of the fivefold [grouping] of these [eight] forms.
The five elements, moon, sun, and the <s>ātman</s> — O best of sages, (LiP 2,12.42)
these are declared as the eight forms of <s>Śiva</s>, the God of Gods, the wise one.
The <s>ātman</s> is His eighth, supreme form called <s>Yajamāna</s> (the sacrificer). (LiP 2,12.43)
It is established in all bodies of moving and unmoving [beings].

children.text: dīkṣitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ prāhurātmānaṃ ca munīśvarāḥ // LiP_2,12.44 //
children.translated_text: The initiated Brahmin — the lords of sages call him the <s>ātman</s>. (LiP 2,12.44)
The form called <s>Yajamāna</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, the bestower of auspiciousness —
these eight forms of <s>Śiva</s> are to be reverenced with effort, (LiP 2,12.45)

children.text: śreyo ḥrthibhir narair nityaṃ śreyasāmekahetavaḥ // LiP_2,12.46 //
children.translated_text: always by people desiring welfare — they are the sole cause of all blessings. (LiP 2,12.46)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the twelfth chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me once more, O <s>Nandin</s>, the greatness of the Lord of <s>Umā</s> —
Of <s>Maheśa</s>, the eight-formed one, <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Being: (LiP 2,13.1)
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
I shall tell you the greatness of <s>Maheśa</s>, the Lord of <s>Umā</s>,
the eight-formed one, the Supreme Being who pervades the universe. (LiP 2,13.2)
The sustainer of all beings, moving and unmoving, whose nature is the earth-bearing one —
he is called <s>Śarva</s> by those who have mastered the meaning of all scriptures. (LiP 2,13.3)
Of that Supreme Being <s>Śarva</s>, whose nature is the earth-bearing one,

children.text: vikeśī kathyate patnī tanayoṅgārakaḥ smṛtaḥ // LiP_2,13.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vikeśī</s> is said to be his wife, and <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars) is known as his son. (LiP 2,13.4)
He is called <s>Bhava</s> by the illustrious Vedic scholars —
the Supreme Self who vivifies all the worlds. (LiP 2,13.5)

children.text: umā saṃkīrtitā devī sutaḥ śukraśca sūribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s> is declared as his goddess, and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) as his son, by the wise.
Pervading the seven world-spheres, the sole protector of all worlds, (LiP 2,13.6)
the illustrious god whose nature is fire is known as <s>Paśupati</s> by the wise.

children.text: svāhā patnyātmanastasya proktā paśupateḥ priyā // LiP_2,13.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Svāhā</s> is called the beloved wife of that <s>Paśupati</s> whose nature is the self. (LiP 2,13.7)

children.text: ṣaṇmukho bhagavān devo budhaiḥ putra udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The illustrious god <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (six-faced <s>Skanda</s>) is said to be his son by the wise.
Pervading all the worlds, the sustainer of all embodied beings, (LiP 2,13.8)
the god whose nature is wind is celebrated by the wise as <s>Īśāna</s>.
Of that god <s>Īśāna</s>, the creator of the universe, whose nature is wind, (LiP 2,13.9)
<s>Śivā</s> is said to be his goddess by the wise, and <s>Manojava</s> (swift as thought) is his son.
The grantor of all desires to all beings, moving and unmoving, (LiP 2,13.10)
the illustrious god whose nature is space is called <s>Bhīma</s> by the wise.
Of the god <s>Bhīma</s>, of supreme glory, whose nature is the sky, (LiP 2,13.11)

children.text: diśo daśa smṛtā devyaḥ sutaḥ sargaśca sūribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: the ten directions are said to be his goddesses, and <s>Sarga</s> (Creation) is his son, by the wise.

children.text: sūryātmā bhagavāndevaḥ sarveṣāṃ ca vibhūtidaḥ // LiP_2,13.12 //
children.translated_text: The illustrious god whose nature is the sun, the bestower of prosperity to all, (LiP 2,13.12)
is called <s>Rudra</s> by the gods, the illustrious one who grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: sūryātma kasya rudrasya bhaktānāṃ bhaktidāyinaḥ // LiP_2,13.13 //
children.translated_text: Of that <s>Rudra</s> whose nature is the sun, the bestower of devotion to his devotees, (LiP 2,13.13)
<s>Suvarcalā</s> is said to be his goddess, and <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is his son.
Renowned as the source of all gentle substances, (LiP 2,13.14)
the god whose nature is the moon is known by the wise as <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Of that god <s>Mahādeva</s> whose nature is the moon, by the wise, (LiP 2,13.15)
<s>Rohiṇī</s> is called his beloved, and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is his body-born son.
Maintaining the oblations for the gods and ancestors, and feeding those who consume them, (LiP 2,13.16)
the god whose nature is the sacrificer — [this] <s>Mahādeva</s>, the Lord, by the wise
is called <s>Ugra</s> by the good, and <s>Īśāna</s> by others. (LiP 2,13.17)
Of the god called <s>Ugra</s>, whose nature is the sacrificer, the Lord —

children.text: dīkṣā patnī budhairuktā saṃtānākhyaḥ sutastathā // LiP_2,13.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration) is called his wife by the wise, and his son is named <s>Saṃtāna</s>. (LiP 2,13.18)
In the bodies of all embodied beings, the hard [element], like that in <s>Koṅkaṇa</s> and elsewhere —
that earthy form should be known as the <s>Śarva</s>-principle by those seeking to understand. (LiP 2,13.19)
In body after body, the imperishable element that belongs to embodied beings,
which has the nature of material substance — that is of <s>Bhava</s>, the Supreme Self; (LiP 2,13.20)
it should be known by those who know the principles, who have mastered all Vedic meanings.

children.text: āgneyaḥ pariṇāmo yo vigraheṣu śarīriṇām // LiP_2,13.21 //
children.translated_text: The fiery transformation that occurs in the bodies of embodied beings — (LiP 2,13.21)
that form should be known as <s>Paśupati</s> by those wishing to know the truth.

children.text: vāyavyaḥ pariṇāmo yaḥ śarīreṣu śarīriṇām // LiP_2,13.22 //
children.translated_text: The aerial transformation in the bodies of embodied beings — (LiP 2,13.22)

children.text: budhairīśoti sā tasya tanurjñeyā na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: by the wise, that form of his should be known as <s>Īśa</s>, without doubt.
The hollow space within the body of all embodied beings — (LiP 2,13.23)
that should be known as the form of <s>Bhīma</s> by those desiring knowledge of the principles.
The radiance situated in the eyes and other [organs] in the bodies of embodied beings — (LiP 2,13.24)
that too should be known as the form of <s>Rudra</s> by those seeking the ultimate truth.
The mind, which is of the nature of the moon, in the bodies of all beings — (LiP 2,13.25)
that should be understood as the form of <s>Mahādeva</s> by thinkers on the principles.
The self (<s>ātman</s>), called the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), residing in the bodies of all beings — (LiP 2,13.26)
that should be known as the form of <s>Ugra</s> by those seeking to know the Supreme Self.

children.text: jātānāṃ sarva bhūtānāṃ caturdaśasu yoniṣu // LiP_2,13.27 //
children.translated_text: Of all beings born in the fourteen types of wombs, (LiP 2,13.27)
the great sages declare non-difference from the eight-formed one.
They say that the limbs of embodied beings consist of seven forms of the Lord; (LiP 2,13.28)
the self (<s>ātman</s>) is his eighth form, dwelling in the bodies of all beings.
This god, the eight-formed one, whose nature is all the worlds, the all-pervading Lord — (LiP 2,13.29)
worship him with your entire being, if you wish to attain the highest good.

children.text: prāṇino yasya kasyāpi kriyate yadyanugrahaḥ // LiP_2,13.30 //
children.translated_text: Whenever grace is shown to any living being whatsoever, (LiP 2,13.30)
that becomes worship of the eight-formed <s>Maheśa</s>.

children.text: nigrahaścet kṛto loke dehino yasya kasyacit // LiP_2,13.31 //
children.translated_text: And if punishment is inflicted upon any embodied being in the world, (LiP 2,13.31)
that very same [punishment] is directed at the eight-formed <s>Maheśa</s>.

children.text: yadyavajñā kṛtā loke yasya kasya cidaṅginaḥ // LiP_2,13.32 //
children.translated_text: If contempt is shown toward any embodied being in the world, (LiP 2,13.32)
that contempt is directed at the all-pervading eight-formed <s>Maheśa</s>.

children.text: abhayaṃ yat pradattaṃ syādaṅgino vasya kasyacit // LiP_2,13.33 //
children.translated_text: Whatever fearlessness is granted to any embodied being — (LiP 2,13.33)
thereby worship of the eight-formed one is accomplished, without doubt.
The performance of all beneficial deeds and the granting of fearlessness — (LiP 2,13.34)
that is worship of the eight-formed god, without doubt.
The performance of all beneficial deeds and the granting of grace to all — (LiP 2,13.35)
that is called the supreme worship of the eight-formed one by the lords of sages.
You should bestow grace upon other embodied beings, (LiP 2,13.36)
and grant fearlessness to all, [if you are] one who desires the worship of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,13.37)
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me, O <s>Nandin</s>, O best of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, the five <s>Brahmans</s>,
which are the cause of well-being and are purifying for embodied beings. (LiP 2,14.1)
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
The five forms of <s>Śiva</s> himself, called the <s>Brahmans</s> —
I shall tell you according to the truth, O best son of <s>Padmayoni</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). (LiP 2,14.2)
The sole destroyer of all worlds, the sole protector of all worlds,
the sole creator of all worlds — <s>Śiva</s> has the nature of the five <s>Brahmans</s>. (LiP 2,14.3)
That which is both the material cause and

children.text: nimittakāraṇaṃ cāhussa śivaḥ pañcadhā smṛtaḥ // LiP_2,14.4 //
children.translated_text: the efficient cause of all worlds — that <s>Śiva</s> is known as fivefold. (LiP 2,14.4)

children.text: mūrtayaḥ pañca vikhyātāḥ pañca brahmāhvayāḥ parāḥ /
children.translated_text: Five renowned forms, called the five supreme <s>Brahmans</s>,
belong to <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Self, the refuge of all worlds. (LiP 2,14.5)
The <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) is the first form of <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Being —
the enjoyer of the realm of <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), designated as <s>Īśāna</s>. (LiP 2,14.6)
The second form of <s>Sthāṇu</s> is called <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> —

children.text: prakṛtiḥ sā hi vijñeyā paramātmaguhātmikā // LiP_2,14.7 //
children.translated_text: it should be known as <s>Prakṛti</s>, dwelling within the Supreme Self as a hidden essence. (LiP 2,14.7)
The third and most venerable form of <s>Śambhu</s> is called <s>Aghora</s>;
that is said to be the form of <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), endowed with eight limbs beginning with <s>dharma</s>. (LiP 2,14.8)
The fourth, called <s>Vāmadeva</s>, is the most venerable form of <s>Śambhu</s>,
established pervading all through its nature as <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego). (LiP 2,14.9)
The fifth form of <s>Śambhu</s> is called <s>Sadyojāta</s>,
established in all embodied beings through its nature as the <s>Manas</s> (mind) principle. (LiP 2,14.10)
<s>Īśāna</s>, the supreme god, the Supreme Being, the Eternal,
is established in all beings through its nature as the sense of hearing. (LiP 2,14.11)
<s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, the god, is established in the bodies of embodied beings
through its nature as the sense of touch — so say those who know the principles. (LiP 2,14.12)
<s>Aghora</s> too, the great god, is said by the wise
to be established in the bodies of all beings through its nature as sight. (LiP 2,14.13)
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is also renowned [as established] through its nature as the sense of taste
in the bodies of all embodied beings. (LiP 2,14.14)
<s>Sadyojāta</s> is known by the wise [as established] through its nature as the sense of smell
in the bodies of all who bear life. (LiP 2,14.15)
Established in the bodies of all who bear life,
through its nature as the organ of speech — by the wise he is called <s>Īśāna</s>. (LiP 2,14.16)
Through its nature as the organ of hands, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> is established
in the bodies of all who bear forms — so say the wise. (LiP 2,14.17)
In the body of all embodied beings, <s>Aghora</s> too is established
through its nature as the organ of feet — so say those who know the principles. (LiP 2,14.18)
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is established through its nature as the organ of excretion
in the bodies of all communities of beings — so say the sages. (LiP 2,14.19)
Through its nature as the generative organ, the god <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the Lord, abides
in the bodies of all who bear life — so say those who know the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s>. (LiP 2,14.20)
The god <s>Īśāna</s> of all living beings, whose form is the subtle element of sound,
is declared to be the generator of space by the sages, the foremost of the divine assemblies. (LiP 2,14.21)
The god <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, whose nature is the subtle element of touch,
is declared to be the generator of wind — thus say the lords of sages about the illustrious one. (LiP 2,14.22)
The god <s>Aghora</s>, whose form is the subtle element of form (<s>rūpa</s>), though terrible,
is declared by the foremost Vedic scholars to be the generator of fire. (LiP 2,14.23)
Because his form is the subtle element of taste, those who know the principles
declare <s>Vāmadeva</s> to be established as the generator of waters. (LiP 2,14.24)
<s>Sadyojāta</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, whose form is the subtle element of smell,
whose nature is the earth — all who know the meaning of all principles praise him. (LiP 2,14.25)
<s>Īśāna</s>, whose nature is space, the primordial god —
the lords of sages declare him to be wondrous, born of supreme greatness. (LiP 2,14.26)
The Lord <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, the god, the wind, whose nature is wind —
because he pervades all the worlds, he is renowned — so the wise know. (LiP 2,14.27)
<s>Aghora</s>, known by his fiery splendor, whose nature is fire —
the great souls who know the meaning of Vedic statements speak of him. (LiP 2,14.28)
<s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, whose nature is water, the delightful one —
the sages declare him to be described as the vivifier of the world. (LiP 2,14.29)
<s>Sadyojāta</s>, the god whose nature is the earth-bearer, the teacher of the world —
the foremost poets know him as the sole sustainer of all that moves and does not move. (LiP 2,14.30)
The entire universe, moving and unmoving, has the nature of the five <s>Brahmans</s>.
The seers who perceive the truth call that the bliss of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,14.31)
The twenty-five-principled one who is seen in the manifest world —

children.text: pañcabrahmātmakatvena sa śivo nānyatāṃ gataḥ // LiP_2,14.32 //
children.translated_text: through his nature as the five <s>Brahmans</s>, he is <s>Śiva</s> and has not gone to any other state. (LiP 2,14.32)
<s>Śiva</s>, the twenty-five-principled one, the five-<s>Brahman</s>-natured —
should be contemplated constantly and with effort by those seeking the highest good. (LiP 2,14.33)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge pañcabrahmakathanaṃ nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled 'The Exposition of the Five <s>Brahmans</s>.'
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me yet more of the greatness of <s>Śiva</s>, O great-minded one!

children.text: sarvajño hyasi bhūtānā madhinātha mahāguṇa // LiP_2,15.1 //
children.translated_text: You are omniscient among beings, O Lord of lords, O one of great virtues! (LiP 2,15.1)
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Hear with concentrated mind — I shall tell you the greatness of <s>Śiva</s>, O sage,
which has been celebrated by the best of sages in many ways and with many words. (LiP 2,15.2)
Some say his form is both existent and non-existent (<s>sadasat</s>); and [he is] the lord of the existent and non-existent.

children.text: taṃ śivaṃ munayaḥ kecitpravadanti ca sūrayaḥ // LiP_2,15.3 //
children.translated_text: Some sages and wise ones declare him to be <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,15.3)
By the second [aspect] — the modification of the states of existence — he is spoken of [as manifest].
Because he is devoid of that [manifest aspect], he is [also] called the unmanifest, the non-existent. (LiP 2,15.4)

children.text: ubhe te śivarūpe hi śivādanyaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Both these are indeed the forms of <s>Śiva</s> — apart from <s>Śiva</s>, nothing else exists.
Because of his lordship over both, <s>Śiva</s> is called the Lord of the existent and non-existent. (LiP 2,15.5)
Some sages, contemplators of reality, declare <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
to be constituted of the perishable and imperishable (<s>kṣarākṣarātmaka</s>), and also beyond the perishable and imperishable. (LiP 2,15.6)
The imperishable is said to be the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>); the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) is declared to be the perishable.

children.text: rūpe te śaṅkarasyaiva tasmānna para ucyate // LiP_2,15.7 //
children.translated_text: These are the forms of <s>Śaṅkara</s> himself — therefore none is said to be higher [than him]. (LiP 2,15.7)

children.text: tayoḥ paraḥ śivaḥ śāntaḥ kṣarākṣaraparo budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond both [is] <s>Śiva</s>, the peaceful one — beyond the perishable and imperishable, the wise
declare in the highest sense [to be] <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2,15.8)

children.text: samastavyaktarūpaṃ tu tataḥ smṛtvā sa mucyate /
children.translated_text: Then, having contemplated the form of the totality of the manifest, one is liberated.
The form of the aggregate (<s>samaṣṭi</s>) and the individual (<s>vyaṣṭi</s>), and the cause of aggregate and individual — (LiP 2,15.9)
some teachers declare <s>Śiva</s> to be the supreme cause.

children.text: samaṣṭiṃ viduravyaktaṃ vyaṣṭiṃ vyaktaṃ munīśvarāḥ // LiP_2,15.10 //
children.translated_text: Lords of sages know the aggregate as the unmanifest, the individual as the manifest. (LiP 2,15.10)
These two forms of <s>Śambhu</s> have been declared — there is no other entity arising [besides him].

children.text: tayoḥ kāramabhāvena śivo hi parameśvaraḥ // LiP_2,15.11 //
children.translated_text: Being the cause of both, <s>Śiva</s> is indeed the Supreme Lord — (LiP 2,15.11)
so declare the knowers of <s>Yogaśāstra</s> — the cause of aggregate and individual.
By some, <s>Śiva</s> is described as having the form of <s>kṣetra</s> (field) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field). (LiP 2,15.12)
The Supreme Self, the Supreme Light, the Blessed Lord, the Supreme Lord.
The twenty-four <s>tattvas</s>, the cause of aggregate and individual — (LiP 2,15.13)
by the term '<s>kṣetrajña</s>' they designate the enjoyer, the <s>Puruṣa</s>;
the field and the knower of the field — these two are the forms of that Self-born One. (LiP 2,15.14)
Nothing exists other than <s>Śiva</s> — thus declare the wise.
Some say <s>Śiva</s> has the form of <s>Aparabrahman</s> (lower Brahman) and is in essence <s>Parabrahman</s> (Supreme Brahman), (LiP 2,15.15)
<s>Mahādeva</s>, the Lord without beginning or end.
Constituted of the elements, sense-organs, inner faculties, <s>pradhāna</s>, and sense-objects — (LiP 2,15.16)

children.text: aparaṃ brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma cidātmakam /
children.translated_text: this is designated as <s>Aparabrahman</s>; <s>Parabrahman</s> is of the nature of pure consciousness.

children.text: brahmaṇī te maheśasya śivasyāsya svayaṃbhuvaḥ // LiP_2,15.17 //
children.translated_text: These two [levels of] <s>Brahman</s> are [the forms] of <s>Maheśa</s>, of this <s>Śiva</s>, the Self-born, (LiP 2,15.17)
of <s>Śaṅkara</s> the Supreme — nothing exists other than <s>Śiva</s>.
By some, <s>Śaṅkara</s> is said to have the form of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), (LiP 2,15.18)
the sustainer and ordainer of the worlds, the primordial god, <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Lords of sages call Him both 'knowledge' and 'ignorance.' (LiP 2,15.19)
The entire manifold of phenomena — these are his forms, of the Self-born One.
Delusion, knowledge, and the supreme — [constitute] the unsurpassed form of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,15.20)
Some sages, knowers of the <s>Āgamas</s>, attained [this understanding] through yoga.
In matters of many forms, cognition [of multiplicity] is called delusion (<s>bhrānti</s>); (LiP 2,15.21)
awareness in the form of the Self is celebrated by the wise as knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>);
the reality free from conceptual construction is designated as the supreme (<s>para</s>). (LiP 2,15.22)
This is the third form of the Lord — nothing else exists anywhere.
By some, <s>Śiva</s> is described as having the form of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower; (LiP 2,15.23)

children.text: vidhātā sarva lokānāṃ dhātā ca parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: the ordainer and sustainer of all worlds, the Supreme Lord.
The learned declare the twenty-three <s>tattvas</s> by the term 'manifest'; (LiP 2,15.24)
by the term 'unmanifest' they speak of the supreme <s>Prakṛti</s>;
by the term 'knower' they speak of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the experiencer of the <s>guṇas</s>. (LiP 2,15.25)
This triad is the form of <s>Śaṅkara</s> — nothing else is apart from <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2,15.26)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the fifteenth chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
O one of great intellect, I wish to hear again, in truth,
that which has been described by the lords of sages in many ways with many words. (LiP 2,16.1)
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ pravakṣyāmi śivarūpāṇi te mune /
children.translated_text: Again and again I shall describe to you the forms of <s>Śiva</s>, O Sage,
described by lords of sages in many ways with many words. (LiP 2,16.2)
By some teachers who have crossed the ocean of the <s>Āgamas</s>,
[<s>Śiva</s> is] called <s>kṣetrajña</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>vyakta</s> (the manifest), and <s>Kālātman</s> (the soul of Time). (LiP 2,16.3)

children.text: kṣetrajñaṃ puruṣaṃ prāhuḥ pradhānaṃ prakṛtiṃ budhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise call the <s>kṣetrajña</s> the <s>Puruṣa</s>; <s>Prakṛti</s> [they call] the <s>Pradhāna</s>;
the entire set of modifications born from <s>Prakṛti</s> — [this is called] the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>). (LiP 2,16.4)
Time (<s>kāla</s>) is the sole cause of transformation of <s>Pradhāna</s> and the manifest;
this fourfold [division] is the fourfold [form] of the Lord's forms. (LiP 2,16.5)
Some teachers call <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Lord, as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>,
<s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s>, and the manifest-formed. (LiP 2,16.6)
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the creator; the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the enjoyer of the universe;

children.text: vikārajātaṃ vyaktākhyaṃ pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ param // LiP_2,16.7 //
children.translated_text: the manifest is the set of modifications; <s>Pradhāna</s> is the supreme cause. (LiP 2,16.7)
This fourfold [division] of intellect is the fourfold form of <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: procyate śaṅkarādanyadasti vastu na kiñcana // LiP_2,16.8 //
children.translated_text: it is declared: there is no entity whatsoever other than <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2,16.8)
By some, the Lord is described as having the form of individual (<s>piṇḍa</s>) and universal (<s>jāti</s>);
all bodies of the moving and stationary [beings] are called <s>piṇḍa</s>; (LiP 2,16.9)
all the universals, and the great universal [as well],

children.text: kathyante jātiśabdena tāni rūpāṇi dhīmataḥ // LiP_2,16.10 //
children.translated_text: are called by the term '<s>jāti</s>' — these are the forms of the Wise One. (LiP 2,16.10)
By some, the Lord is described as <s>Virāṭ</s> and <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> in nature;
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the cause of the worlds; <s>Virāṭ</s> is the embodiment of the worlds. (LiP 2,16.11)
Some describe that <s>Śiva</s> as having the form of <s>sūtra</s> (thread) and <s>avyākṛta</s> (the unresolved);

children.text: avyākṛtaṃ pradhānaṃ hi tadrūpaṃ parameṣṭhanaḥ // LiP_2,16.12 //
children.translated_text: the unresolved is indeed <s>Pradhāna</s> — that is the form of the Supreme One. (LiP 2,16.12)

children.text: lokā yenaiva tiṣṭhanti sūtre maṇigaṇā iva /
children.translated_text: The worlds abide in Him like gems on a string;
that thread-form (<s>sūtra</s>) is to be known — of wondrous power. (LiP 2,16.13)
By some He is called the Inner Controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>); by some, the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) is proclaimed —
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, self-luminous, self-known. (LiP 2,16.14)
<s>Śiva</s> is remembered as the Inner Controller of all beings;
being beyond all beings, He is called the Supreme (<s>para</s>). (LiP 2,16.15)
The Supreme Self, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Supreme Lord.
They know His three forms as <s>Prājña</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Viśva</s>. (LiP 2,16.16)
Deep sleep, dreaming, and waking — that is the triad of states;
[named] <s>Virāṭ</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and by the term <s>Avyākṛta</s>. (LiP 2,16.17)
Of this <s>Śiva</s> who is the Fourth (<s>Turīya</s>), traversing the three states,

children.text: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ puruṣaḥ kāla ity eva kīrtitāḥ // LiP_2,16.18 //
children.translated_text: [the forms are] called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and Time (<s>Kāla</s>). (LiP 2,16.18)
The three states are the causes of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the world;
the triad of states of the Ruler is called <s>Bhava</s> [Śiva], <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Viriñca</s> [Brahmā]. (LiP 2,16.19)

children.text: ārādhya bhaktyā muktiṃ ca prāpnuvanti śarīriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Worshipping [Him] with devotion, embodied beings attain liberation.

children.text: kartā kriyā ca kāryaṃ ca karaṇaṃ ceti sūribhiḥ // LiP_2,16.20 //
children.translated_text: The doer, the action, the result, and the instrument — by the wise, (LiP 2,16.20)
these are proclaimed as the four forms of <s>Śambhu</s>, the Supreme One.

children.text: pramātā ca pramāṇaṃ ca prameyaṃ pramitistathā // LiP_2,16.21 //
children.translated_text: The knower (<s>pramātā</s>), the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), and the resultant knowledge (<s>pramiti</s>) — (LiP 2,16.21)
these four are the forms of <s>Śiva</s> alone — no doubt.
<s>Īśvara</s>, the unresolved (<s>avyākṛta</s>), <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>Virāṭ</s>, constituted of elements and sense-organs — (LiP 2,16.22)
this is indeed the modification of <s>Śiva</s>, like waves of the ocean.
They call <s>Īśvara</s> the efficient (<s>nimitta</s>) cause of the worlds; (LiP 2,16.23)
the unresolved [is] indeed <s>Pradhāna</s> — so declare the exponents of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prāṇākhyo virāṭ lokātmakaḥ smṛtaḥ // LiP_2,16.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is called <s>Prāṇa</s>; <s>Virāṭ</s> is the embodiment of the worlds. (LiP 2,16.24)

children.text: mahā bhūtāni bhūtāni kāryāṇi indriyāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: The great elements, the elements, the products, and the sense-organs —
the best of sages declare these to be the forms of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,16.25)
There is no Supreme Self other than <s>Śiva</s> — thus the seers know.
The <s>tattvas</s> born from <s>Śiva</s> — twenty-five, according to the wise — (LiP 2,16.26)
have been described; nothing is other than that — like multitudes of waves from water.
Beyond the twenty-five categories, they know the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> as the supreme; (LiP 2,16.27)
those [categories] are not different from it — like a bracelet [is not different] from gold.
The <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, from the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> — (LiP 2,16.28)
are born, not different from it — like a pot [is not different] from the material of clay.

children.text: māyā vidyā kriyā śaktirjñānaśaktiḥ kriyāmayī // LiP_2,16.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Kriyā-śakti</s>, <s>Jñāna-śakti</s>, [and] <s>Kriyā-mayī</s> [action-power] — (LiP 2,16.29)

children.text: jātāḥ śivānna saṃdehaḥ kiraṇā iva sūryataḥ /
children.translated_text: are born from <s>Śiva</s>, no doubt — like rays from the sun.
Worship <s>Śiva</s> the God, who is the Self of all, the establisher of all refuges, (LiP 2,16.30)
with your whole being, if you wish to attain the highest good. (LiP 2,16.31)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the sixteenth chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Again, O best of the host of gods, [tell me] the supreme greatness of <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: śṛṇvato nāsti me tṛptistva dvākyāmṛtapānataḥ // LiP_2,17.1 //
children.translated_text: from drinking the nectar of your words, I have no satiation in hearing. (LiP 2,17.1)
How is the Blessed One embodied? Why is <s>Rudra</s> mighty?

children.text: sarvātmā ca kathaṃ śambhuḥ kathaṃ pāśupataṃ vratam // LiP_2,17.2 //
children.translated_text: How is <s>Śambhu</s> the Self of all? What is the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow? (LiP 2,17.2)

children.text: kathaṃ vā devamukhyaiśca śruto dṛṣṭaśca śaṅkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: And how was <s>Śaṅkara</s> heard and seen by the foremost gods?
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
From the Unmanifest arose <s>Sthāṇu</s> [Śiva], the Supreme Cause. (LiP 2,17.3)
He, endowed with all causes, a seer, the Lord of all transformations,

children.text: devānāṃ prathamaṃ devaṃ jāyamānaṃ mukhāmbujāt // LiP_2,17.4 //
children.translated_text: saw the first god of the gods, born from the lotus-face [of the cosmic being] — (LiP 2,17.4)
<s>Brahmā</s> — and first beheld [him], and by [Śiva's] command gazed upon him.

children.text: dṛṣṭo rudreṇa deveśaḥ sasarja sakalaṃ ca saḥ // LiP_2,17.5 //
children.translated_text: Seen by <s>Rudra</s>, the Lord of Gods created everything. (LiP 2,17.5)
<s>Virāṭ</s> established the ordering of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>;
he created <s>Soma</s> for the sake of sacrifice; from <s>Soma</s>, all this was born: (LiP 2,17.6)
the oblation-vessel (<s>caru</s>), fire (<s>vahni</s>), sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), the thunderbolt-wielder (<s>Indra</s>), the husband of <s>Śacī</s>,

children.text: viṣṇurnārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān sarvaṃ somamayaṃ jagat // LiP_2,17.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> the glorious — the entire world is pervaded by <s>Soma</s>. (LiP 2,17.7)
With the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s> [hymn], those gods praised <s>Rudra</s>, the Lord;
the Lord stood in the midst of the gods with a serene face. (LiP 2,17.8)
And <s>Maheśvara</s>, having withdrawn [their] knowledge,

children.text: devā hyapṛcchaṃstaṃ devaṃ ko bhavāniti śaṅkaram // LiP_2,17.9 //
children.translated_text: the gods asked that god <s>Śaṅkara</s>: 'Who are you?' (LiP 2,17.9)
Lord <s>Rudra</s> said: 'I am the one, the ancient one;

children.text: āsaṃ prathama evāhaṃ vartāmi ca surottamāḥ // LiP_2,17.10 //
children.translated_text: I was the first, and I exist [now], O best of gods; (LiP 2,17.10)
and I shall be in this world — there is nothing else from anywhere other than Me.
Nothing exists separate from Me, nothing else whatsoever, O best of gods. (LiP 2,17.11)
I am the eternal and the temporal; I am the sinless, the <s>Brāhma</s> [sacred], the Lord of <s>Brahman</s>;
I am the directions and the intermediate directions; I am <s>Prakṛti</s> and I am <s>Puruṣa</s>. (LiP 2,17.12)
<s>Triṣṭubh</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — I am the [Vedic] meters, <s>Śiva</s> who consists of them.
I am Truth, all-pervading, peaceful; [I am] the triple fire, weightiness, the Teacher. (LiP 2,17.13)
I am the golden one; I am the abyss; I perpetually range through the impenetrable.
I am the eldest of all <s>tattvas</s>; I am the greatest, the Lord of waters. (LiP 2,17.14)
I am the waters; I am the Blessed Lord; I am radiance; I am also the sacrificial altar.
I am the <s>Ṛg Veda</s>, I am the <s>Yajur Veda</s>, I am the <s>Sāma Veda</s>, I am the Self-born. (LiP 2,17.15)
I am the <s>Atharva Veda</s>, I am the mantra, and the best of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>;
I am the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>; I am the <s>Kalpa</s> [ritual procedure]; I am also imagination. (LiP 2,17.16)

children.text: akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ cāhaṃ kṣāntiḥ śāntirahaṃ kṣamā /
children.translated_text: I am the imperishable and the perishable; I am forbearance, tranquility, and patience.
I am the secret in all the <s>Vedas</s>; I am the most excellent; I am also the unborn. (LiP 2,17.17)

children.text: puṣkaraṃ ca pavitraṃ ca madhyaṃ cāhaṃ tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: I am the lotus; I am the purifier; I am the middle, and beyond that.
I am the outside, and also the inside; I am the front; I am the imperishable. (LiP 2,17.18)
I am light, and I am darkness; [I am] <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>;
I am intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), I am ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), the subtle elements (<s>tanmātrāṇi</s>), and the sense-organs. (LiP 2,17.19)

children.text: evaṃ sarvaṃ ca māmeva yo veda sura sattamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever knows all this as Me alone, O best of gods,

children.text: sa eva sarvavitsarvaṃ sarvātmā parameśvaraḥ // LiP_2,17.20 //
children.translated_text: he is indeed the knower of all, [is] all, the Self of all, the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2,17.20)
Cows with cows, all Brahmins with the sacred, oblations with
lifespan with lifespan, and truth with truth, O best of gods — (LiP 2,17.21)
<s>dharma</s> with <s>dharma</s> — I satisfy all with My own splendor.
Having spoken thus at the beginning, the Blessed Lord disappeared right there. (LiP 2.17.22)
Then they could not see the god <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme cause;

children.text: te devāḥ paramātmānaṃ rudraṃ dhyāyanti śaṅkaram // LiP_2,17.23 //
children.translated_text: those gods meditate upon <s>Rudra</s>, the Supreme Self, <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2.17.23)
The gods along with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, along with <s>Indra</s>, and the sages likewise —

children.text: tathordhvabāhavo devā rudraṃ stunvanti saṃkaram // LiP_2,17.24 //
children.translated_text: then, with arms raised upward, the gods praise <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2.17.24)
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The gods said:
He who is the blessed <s>Rudra</s> — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and <s>Skanda</s> as well, and also <s>Indra</s>, the fourteen worlds,

children.text: aśvinau grahatārāsca nakṣatrāṇi ca khaṃ diśaḥ // LiP_2,18.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Aśvins</s>, the planets and stars, the constellations, the sky, and the directions — (LiP 2.18.1)

children.text: bhūtāni ca tathā sūryaḥ somaścāṣṭau grahāstathā /
children.translated_text: the elements as well, and the Sun, the Moon, and the eight planets;

children.text: prāṇaḥ kālo yamo mṛtyuramṛtaḥ parameśvaraḥ // LiP_2,18.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), Time, <s>Yama</s> (death-god), Death, Immortality — [he is] the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2.18.2)
The past, the future, the yet-to-be, and the present — [all are] <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: viśvaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ satyaṃ tasmai namonamaḥ // LiP_2,18.3 //
children.translated_text: The entire universe, all the world, the truth — salutations again and again to him! (LiP 2.18.3)

children.text: tvamādau ca tathā bhūto bhūrbhuvaḥ svastathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: You are in the beginning, and likewise the [primordial] being; <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s> as well;

children.text: ante tvaṃ viśvarūpo 'si śīrṣaṃ tu jagataḥ saṃdā // LiP_2,18.4 //
children.translated_text: at the end, you are the cosmic form — you are forever the head of the world. (LiP 2.18.4)
You alone are <s>Brahman</s> — two-fold, three-fold in purpose, and below too, O Lord of the Gods.

children.text: śāntiśca tvaṃ tathā puṣṭistuṣṭiścāpyahutaṃ hutam // LiP_2,18.5 //
children.translated_text: You are peace, you are nourishment, you are contentment; [you are] the unoffered and the offered. (LiP 2.18.5)
The manifest and the unmanifest, the given and the not-given — the Lord;
the done and the undone — the God; the supreme and the lower — the unchanging;

children.text: parāyaṇaṃ satāṃ caiva hyasatāmapi śaṅkaram // LiP_2,18.6 //
children.translated_text: the refuge of the good, and indeed of the wicked too — <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2.18.6)

children.text: apāma somam amṛtā abhūmāganma jyotiravidāma devān /
children.translated_text: 'We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>, we have become immortal, we have attained the light, we have found the gods.

children.text: kiṃ nūnamasmānkṛṇavadarātiḥ kimu dhūrtiramṛtaṃ martyasya // LiP_2,18.7 //
children.translated_text: What can the enemy do to us now? What indeed can the deceit of a mortal [accomplish]?' (LiP 2.18.7) [Ṛgveda 8.48.3]
This world, beneficent, divine, imperishable, subtle, and inexhaustible — (LiP 2.18.8)
belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>, pure, gentle, ungraspable, and inexhaustible;

children.text: agrāhyeṇāpi vā grāhyaṃ vāyavyena samīraṇaḥ // LiP_2,18.9 //
children.translated_text: yet graspable even by the ungraspable — by the airy [nature], the Wind [grasps it]. (LiP 2.18.9)

children.text: saumyena saumyaṃ grasati tejasā svena līlayā /
children.translated_text: The gentle one devours the gentle by his own radiance, playfully.
Salutations to that withdrawer [of all], the great devourer, the Trident-bearer! (LiP 2.18.10)

children.text: hṛdisthā devatāḥ sarvā hṛdi prāṇe pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All deities are seated in the heart; they are established in the heart, in the <s>Prāṇa</s>.

children.text: hṛdi tvamasi yo nityaṃ tisro mātrāḥ parastu saḥ // LiP_2,18.11 //
children.translated_text: You are he who is eternally in the heart — [consisting of] three <s>mātrās</s> (syllabic measures), and beyond that. (LiP 2.18.11)
His head is to the north, and his feet to the south;

children.text: yo vai cottarataḥ sākṣātsa oṅkāraḥ sanātanaḥ // LiP_2,18.12 //
children.translated_text: he who is directly to the north — that is the eternal <s>Oṃkāra</s>. (LiP 2.18.12)

children.text: oṅkāro yaḥ sa eveha praṇavo vyāpya tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: He who is the <s>Oṃkāra</s> — that very <s>Praṇava</s> pervades and abides here;

children.text: anantastārasūkṣmaṃ ca śuklaṃ vaidyutameva ca // LiP_2,18.13 //
children.translated_text: infinite, subtle as the star [-syllable], white, and lightning-like. (LiP 2.18.13)

children.text: paraṃ brahmā sa īśāna ekorudraḥ sa eva ca /
children.translated_text: He is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, he is <s>Īśāna</s>, he is the one <s>Rudra</s>,
<s>Bhava</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s> directly, <s>Mahādeva</s> — there is no doubt. (LiP 2.18.14)
He who leads upward — he is celebrated as <s>Oṃkāra</s>;
because he enlivens the vital breaths — therefore he is celebrated as <s>Praṇava</s>. (LiP 2.18.15)
Because he pervades everything — therefore [he is] the eternal all-pervader.
<s>Brahmā</s> and the blessed <s>Hari</s> did not ascertain his beginning or end. (LiP 2.18.16)
And likewise all others — therefore <s>Rudra</s> is infinite, the supreme cause.
Because he causes one to cross the cycle of existence (<s>saṃsāra</s>) — he is called <s>Tāra</s> (savior). (LiP 2.18.17)
Having become subtle, he always presides over all bodies;
therefore the Blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s> (Blue-Red one) is declared 'subtle.' (LiP 2.18.18)
Blue and red — by the connection with <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s>;

children.text: skandate 'sya yataḥ śukraṃ tathā śukramapaitica // LiP_2,18.19 //
children.translated_text: from him the seed (<s>śukra</s>) flows forth, and likewise the seed returns [to him]. (LiP 2.18.19)
Because he illumines — therefore he is sung as 'lightning-like' (<s>vaidyuta</s>).
From greatness and from causing expansion — to the great one, the higher and lower — (LiP 2.18.20)
because he expands — therefore he is celebrated as the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
The non-dual Blessed Lord, the fourth (<s>Turīya</s>), the Supreme Lord — (LiP 2.18.21)
the ruler (<s>Īśāna</s>) of this world, the eye of the heaven-seers, the Lord —
<s>Indra</s> and the other gods [declare him] the <s>Īśāna</s> of all, at all times. (LiP 2.18.22)
<s>Īśāna</s> of all knowledge — that is why he is called <s>Īśāna</s>;
and whatever the Blessed One beholds — that [becomes] 'to be beheld,' by [his] command. (LiP 2.18.23)
<s>Mahādeva</s> himself leads to self-knowledge and <s>Yoga</s>;
the Blessed One is called God, the God of Gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2.18.24)
He who seizes all worlds in sequence — <s>Maheśvara</s>;
the Lord of the Gods releases [them] and causes [them] to dwell — playfully. (LiP 2.18.25)

children.text: eṣo hi devaḥ pradiśo 'nusarvāḥ pūrvo hi jātaḥ sa u garbhe antaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This God indeed [pervades] all the directions; he was born first, and he is within the womb;

children.text: sa eva jātaḥ sa janiṣyamāṇaḥ pratyaṅmukhāstiṣṭhati sarvatomukhaḥ // LiP_2,18.26 //
children.translated_text: he alone has been born, he is to be born — he stands facing all beings, facing all directions.' (LiP 2.18.26) [Śvetāśvatara Up. 2.16]
That imperishable [reality] should be worshipped with effort by the good;

children.text: yato vāco nivartante hyaprāpya manasā saha // LiP_2,18.27 //
children.translated_text: 'from which speech turns back, not reaching [it], together with the mind.' (LiP 2.18.27) [Taittirīya Up. 2.9]
The very non-grasping of that — that which speech strives to express;

children.text: aparaṃ ca paraṃ veti parāyaṇamiti svayam // LiP_2,18.28 //
children.translated_text: 'the lower and the higher' — [he is] the refuge, by his own [nature]. (LiP 2.18.28)
The voices of the omniscient declare <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Blue-Red one.

children.text: eṣa sarvo namastasmai puruṣaḥ piṅgalaḥ śivaḥ // LiP_2,18.29 //
children.translated_text: He is all — salutations to that tawny (<s>piṅgala</s>) Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), <s>Śiva</s>! (LiP 2.18.29)

children.text: sa eṣa sa mahārudro viśvaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: He is that great <s>Rudra</s> — the universe, what has been and what will be;
the world born manifold, being born here and there. (LiP 2.18.30)
The Blessed Lord with golden arms, the golden master, the Lord,
the husband of <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, the golden-seeded one, bearing the bull-banner; (LiP 2.18.31)
the husband of <s>Umā</s>, the oblique-eyed one, the creator of the universe, the bearer of the universe —

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ vidadhe yo 'sau putramagre sanātanam // LiP_2,18.32 //
children.translated_text: he who fashioned <s>Brahmā</s>, the eternal, as [his] son at the beginning, (LiP 2.18.32)
and transmitted to him the self-illuminating knowledge of the Self.

children.text: tamekaṃ puruṣaṃ rudraṃ puruhutaṃ puruṣṭutam // LiP_2,18.33 //
children.translated_text: That one <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Rudra</s> — much-invoked, much-praised — (LiP 2.18.33)

children.text: bālāgramātraṃ hṛdayasya madhye viśvandevaṃ vahnirūpaṃ vareṇyam /
children.translated_text: 'Of the measure of a hair-tip, in the center of the heart, the God of the universe, of the form of fire, the excellent —

children.text: tamātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrāsteṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām // LiP_2,18.34 //
children.translated_text: those wise ones who see him as dwelling in the self — theirs is eternal peace, not of others.' (LiP 2.18.34) [Śvetāśvatara Up. 4.17, adapted]
He who is greater than the great, and more minute than the minute — imperishable,
the Self hidden in the cave of the creature — <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2.18.35)
Having become the dwelling of this universe, he is situated in the lotus of the heart himself;

children.text: gahvaraṃ gahanaṃ tatsthaṃ tasyāntaścordhvataḥ sthitaḥ // LiP_2,18.36 //
children.translated_text: the cavern, the deep [place], that which dwells within it — he is established within and above. (LiP 2.18.36)
Even there, in the tiny space (<s>dahra</s>), the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the Supreme Lord —
of the measure of a hair-tip, in its midst — the truth (<s>ṛta</s>), the supreme cause. (LiP 2.18.37)
The truth, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, dark-and-tawny,
with seed directed upward, <s>Īśāna</s>, the oblique-eyed one, born of the unborn — (LiP 2.18.38)

children.text: adhitiṣṭhati yoniṃ yo yoniṃ vācaika īśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: he who presides over the womb — the one Lord of the womb of speech,

children.text: dehaṃ pañcavidhaṃ yena tamīśānaṃ purātanam // LiP_2,18.39 //
children.translated_text: by whom the fivefold body [is governed] — that ancient <s>Īśāna</s>. (LiP 2.18.39)

children.text: prāṇeṣvantarmanaso liṅgamāhuryasminkrodho yā ca tṛṣṇā kṣamā ca /
children.translated_text: 'They call [him] the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) within the vital breaths and the mind, in whom are anger, craving, and forbearance;

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ chittvā hetujālasya mūlaṃ buddhyācintyaṃ sthāpayitvā ca rudre // LiP_2,18.40 //
children.translated_text: having cut craving — the root of the net of causes — and having established the inconceivable in <s>Rudra</s> through intelligence.' (LiP 2.18.40)
They call him the one <s>Rudra</s>, eternal, the Supreme Lord,
higher than the highest, and higher than the highest — the unchanging. (LiP 2.18.41)
The father of <s>Brahmā</s>, of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of fire, of wind — <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: dhyātvāgninā ca śodhyāṅgaṃ viśodhya ca pṛthakpṛthak // LiP_2,18.42 //
children.translated_text: Having meditated [on him] and purified the body with fire, purifying each [part] separately, (LiP 2.18.42)
having restrained the five elements according to the order of <s>mātrā</s>-methods and <s>guṇas</s>,

children.text: mātrāḥ pañca catasraśca trimātrādistataḥ param // LiP_2,18.43 //
children.translated_text: five <s>mātrās</s>, four [<s>mātrās</s>], three <s>mātrās</s> — and thence beyond, (LiP 2.18.43)
one <s>mātrā</s> and the <s>mātrā</s>-less — established at the twelfth [point above the head].

children.text: sthitvā sthāpyāmṛto bhūtvā vrataṃ pāśupataṃ caret // LiP_2,18.44 //
children.translated_text: Having stood [there], having been established, having become immortal — one should practice the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow. (LiP 2.18.44)
'I shall practice this <s>Pāśupata</s> vow' — [one should resolve] in brief.
Having established the sacred fire according to the rites, born of <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> [Vedas], (LiP 2.18.45)
having fasted, pure, bathed, wearing white garments by himself,
with a white sacred thread, with white garlands and unguents — (LiP 2.18.46)
the learned one, free from passion, should offer oblations and shall become free from passion.
May the five winds be purified — speech, mind, feet, and the rest; (LiP 2.18.47)

children.text: śrotraṃ jihvā tataḥ prāṇastato buddhistathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: the ear, the tongue, then the vital breath, then the intellect likewise,
the head, the hands, then the sides, the back and belly next, (LiP 2.18.48)

children.text: jaṅghe śiśramupasthaṃ ca pāyurmeḍhraṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: the shanks, the penis, the generative organ, the anus, and the phallus likewise,

children.text: tvacā māṃsaṃ ca rudhiraṃ medo 'sthīni tathaiva ca // LiP_2,18.49 //
children.translated_text: the skin, the flesh, and the blood, the fat, and the bones likewise; (LiP 2.18.49)

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhastathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell likewise,

children.text: bhūtāni caiva śudhyantāṃ dehe medādayastathā // LiP_2,18.50 //
children.translated_text: and the elements — may they be purified; in the body, fat and the rest likewise; (LiP 2.18.50)

children.text: annaṃ prāṇe mano jñānaṃ śudhyantāṃ vai śivecchayā /
children.translated_text: food, breath, mind, knowledge — may they be purified by the will of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: hutvājyena samidbhiśca caruṇā ca yathākramam // LiP_2,18.51 //
children.translated_text: Having offered with ghee, fuel-sticks, and rice-oblation in proper sequence, (LiP 2.18.51)
having withdrawn the <s>Rudra</s>-fire, having carefully taken the sacred ash (<s>bhasma</s>),
the wise one should touch his limbs, smearing [them] with [the mantra beginning] '<s>Agni</s> [is]...' (LiP 2.18.52)
This is the divine <s>Pāśupata</s> vow, the liberator from bondage (<s>pāśa</s>);

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ hitaṃ proktaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tathaiva ca // LiP_2,18.53 //
children.translated_text: it is declared beneficial for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and likewise for <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, (LiP 2.18.53)
for worthy <s>Vaiśyas</s> as well, and especially for renunciants (<s>yati</s>);
for those in the forest-dweller stage (<s>vānaprastha</s>) and for righteous householders too. (LiP 2.18.54)
Liberation [comes] by this method — having seen [this], even for celibate students.
Having taken ash produced from the sacred fire, with [the mantra beginning] '<s>Agni</s> [is]...' (LiP 2.18.55)
that <s>Pāśupata</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too should touch his limbs, smearing [them].
A twice-born one, learned, covered with sacred ash — from the great sins that arise, (LiP 2.18.56)

children.text: pāpaurvimucyate sadyo mucyate ca na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: from sins one is freed instantly — one is freed, there is no doubt.
Since fire has its power from ash — one becomes powerful through union with ash. (LiP 2.18.57)
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> devoted to bathing in ash, sleeping in ash, with senses controlled,
freed from all sins — attains union with <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śivasāyujya</s>). (LiP 2.18.58)
Therefore, with every effort, the wise one should worship the body with ash (<s>bhūti</s>);
're-re' sounds should not be made, nor 'tun-tuṅ' sounds likewise. (LiP 2.18.59)

children.text: na tatkṣamati deveśo brahmā vā yadi keśavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord of the Gods does not tolerate [such disrespect] — even if it were <s>Brahmā</s> or <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: mama putro bhasmadhārī gaṇeśaśca varānane // LiP_2,18.60 //
children.translated_text: 'My son is the ash-bearer, and <s>Gaṇeśa</s> too, O Fair-faced One; (LiP 2.18.60)

children.text: teṣāṃ viruddhaṃ yattyājyaṃ sa yāti narakārṇavam /
children.translated_text: whatever is hostile to them should be abandoned — [such a person] goes to the ocean of hell.'

children.text: gṛhastho brahmahīnopi tripuṇḍraṃ yo na kārayet // LiP_2,18.61 //
children.translated_text: A householder, even devoid of Vedic learning, who does not apply the <s>tripuṇḍra</s> (three-line ash mark) — (LiP 2.18.61)

children.text: pūjā karma kriyā tasya dānaṃ snānaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: his worship, ritual actions, deeds, charity, bathing, and the like —

children.text: niṣphalaṃ jāyate sarvaṃ yathā bhasmani vai hutam // LiP_2,18.62 //
children.translated_text: all become fruitless, like an oblation cast into ash. (LiP 2.18.62)
Therefore, in all activities, the wise one should wear the <s>tripuṇḍra</s>.

children.text: ityuktvā bhagavānbrahmā stutvā devaiḥ samaṃ prabhuḥ // LiP_2,18.63 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, praising the Lord together with the gods, (LiP 2.18.63)
himself covered with ash, among those covered with ash — rested, O lord of the people.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ prasādārthaṃ paśūnāṃ patirīśvaraḥ // LiP_2,18.64 //
children.translated_text: Then, for the sake of granting them grace, the Lord of beasts (<s>Paśupati</s>), the Lord, (LiP 2.18.64)
came together with <s>Ambā</s> (Pārvatī) and manifested his presence, the Lord.

children.text: atha saṃnihitaṃ rudraṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ surapuṅgavam // LiP_2,18.65 //
children.translated_text: Then, [seeing] <s>Rudra</s> present, [the gods] praised the chief of the gods, (LiP 2.18.65)
the Lord of All, the God of Gods, the husband of <s>Umā</s>, with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s> (Rudra hymn).
The God too, seeing the gods, the Bull-bannered one, with compassion, (LiP 2.18.66)

children.text: tuṣṭosmītyāha devebhyo varaṃ dātuṃ surārihā // LiP_2,18.67 //
children.translated_text: 'I am pleased,' said [he] to the gods, [ready] to grant a boon — the slayer of the enemies of the gods. (LiP 2.18.67)
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> (Nandikeśvara) said:
Having bowed to that Lord whose mind was pleased, the Bull-bannered one,
the sages and gods asked [him], their skin bristling with joy: (LiP 2.19.1)
The gods said:
'O Blessed One, by what path should [you] be worshipped by the twice-born?

children.text: kutra vā kena rūpeṇa vaktumarhasi śaṅkaraḥ // LiP_2,19.2 //
children.translated_text: Where, and in what form — please tell [us], O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.' (LiP 2.19.2)
Who has the authority for worship? How [is it] for a <s>brahmana</s>, O Lord?

children.text: kṣatriyāṇāṃ kathaṃ deva vaiśyānāṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja // LiP_2,19.3 //
children.translated_text: How for <s>ksatriyas</s>, O God? How for <s>vaisyas</s>, O Bull-bannered One? (LiP 2.19.3)

children.text: strīśūdrāṇāṃ kathaṃ vāpi kuṇḍagolādināṃ tu vā /
children.translated_text: And how for women and <s>sudras</s>? Or for <s>kundas</s>, <s>golas</s>, and the like?
For the welfare of the worlds, please tell us everything. (LiP 2.19.4)
<s>Suta</s> said:
Perceiving the sentiment of those sages, the Blue-and-Red One (<s>Nilalohita</s>),

children.text: prāha gaṃbhīrayā vācā maṇḍalasthaḥ sadāśivaḥ // LiP_2,19.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sadasiva</s>, stationed in the <s>mandala</s> (sacred circle), spoke with a deep voice: (LiP 2.19.5)
In the <s>mandala</s>, gazing forward at the God of Gods together with <s>Uma</s>,
the gods and all the sages [beheld Him], with brilliance equal to ten million lightnings, (LiP 2.19.6)
eight-armed, four-faced, twelve-eyed, with mighty arms,
the God <s>Ardhanarishvara</s> (the Lord who is half-woman), wearing a crown of matted hair, (LiP 2.19.7)
endowed with all ornaments, with red garlands and unguents,
wearing red garments, the maker of creation, preservation, and dissolution. (LiP 2.19.8)
His eastern face is yellow, serene, of the nature of <s>Purusa</s>.
The southern face is <s>Aghora</s>, resembling a mass of dark collyrium, (LiP 2.19.9)
terrible with protruding fangs, extremely fierce, surrounded by a garland of flames,
with red beard and matted locks; the northern one has the luster of coral, (LiP 2.19.10)
serene, called <s>Vamadeva</s>, boon-granting, of universal form.

children.text: paścimaṃ vadanaṃ tasya gokṣīradhavalaṃ śubham // LiP_2,19.11 //
children.translated_text: His western face is white as cow's milk, auspicious, (LiP 2.19.11)
adorned with necklaces of pearls, radiant with a <s>tilaka</s>-mark —
the divine <s>Sadyojata</s> face of <s>Bhaskara</s> (the Sun), the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (Kama). (LiP 2.19.12)
Seeing the Sun (<s>Aditya</s>) in front, four-faced as before,

children.text: bhāskaraṃ purato devaṃ caturvakraṃ ca pūrvavat // LiP_2,19.13 //
children.translated_text: the resplendent god in front, four-faced as before; (LiP 2.19.13)

children.text: bhānuṃ dakṣiṇato devaṃ caturvaktraṃ ca pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: the Sun-god to the south, four-faced as before;
and seeing the Sun to the north, four-faced as before. (LiP 2.19.14)

children.text: vistārāṃ maṇḍale pūrve uttarāṃ dakṣiṇe sthitām /
children.translated_text: <s>Vistara</s> [Sakti] in the eastern <s>mandala</s>; <s>Uttara</s> stationed in the south;

children.text: bodhanīṃ paścime bhāge maṇḍalasya prajāpateḥ // LiP_2,19.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhani</s> (the Awakener) in the western section of the <s>mandala</s> of <s>Prajapati</s>; (LiP 2.19.15)
<s>Adhyayani</s> (the Study-goddess) in the northern (<s>Kaubera</s>) quarter — each single-faced and four-armed.
Endowed with all ornaments, these <s>Saktis</s> are universally honored. (LiP 2.19.16)

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge viṣṇuṃ vāme janārdanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahma</s> in the southern section, <s>Visnu</s> <s>Janardana</s> in the left (western),
<s>Siva</s>, consisting of the threefold form, by the path of <s>Rg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Saman</s> [Vedas]; (LiP 2.19.17)
<s>Isana</s>, the boon-granting god, <s>Isana</s>, the Supreme Lord,
seated on <s>Brahma</s>'s seat, the best, upon the seat of <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Jnana</s>, (LiP 2.19.18)
endowed with <s>Vairagya</s> (renunciation) and <s>Aisvarya</s> (sovereignty), abundant, pure,

children.text: sāraṃ sarveśvaraṃ devamārādhyaṃ paramaṃ sukham // LiP_2,19.19 //
children.translated_text: the essence, the Lord of All, the God to be worshipped, supreme bliss. (LiP 2.19.19)
Stationed in the midst of a white lotus, surrounded by <s>Dipta</s> (Radiant) and others —

children.text: dīptāṃ dīpaśikhākārāṃ sūkṣmāṃ vidyutprabhāṃ śubhām // LiP_2,19.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dipta</s>, lamp-flame-shaped, subtle, with the luster of lightning, auspicious; (LiP 2.19.20)
<s>Jaya</s>, fire-flame-shaped, with the brilliance of gold;
<s>Vibhuti</s>, coral-like, pure, lotus-resembling; (LiP 2.19.21)
<s>Amogha</s>, shaped like a pistil, <s>Vidyut</s> (Lightning), of all colors;

children.text: caturvaktrāṃ caturvarṇāṃ devīṃ vai sarvatomukhīm // LiP_2,19.22 //
children.translated_text: the Goddess, four-faced, of four colors, facing all directions. (LiP 2.19.22)
The Moon (<s>Soma</s>), Mars (<s>Angaraka</s>), the god Mercury (<s>Budha</s>), the best of the wise;

children.text: bṛhaspatiṃ bṛhadvuddhiṃ bhārgavaṃ tejasāṃ nidhim // LiP_2,19.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brhaspati</s> (Jupiter), of vast intellect; <s>Bhargava</s> (Venus), a treasury of brilliance; (LiP 2.19.23)

children.text: mandaṃ mandagatiṃ caiva samantāttasya te sadā /
children.translated_text: and <s>Manda</s> (Saturn), the slow-moving one — all around Him always.

children.text: sūryaṃ śivo jagannāthaḥ somaḥ sākṣādumā svayam // LiP_2,19.24 //
children.translated_text: The Sun is <s>Siva</s>, the Lord of the world; the Moon is directly <s>Uma</s> herself. (LiP 2.19.24)
The remaining five elements — and the entire movable and immovable [creation] is pervaded by them.
Having seen the God of Gods, the Lord of <s>Uma</s>, all the sages, (LiP 2.19.25)
with joined palms — all the sages and gods likewise,
praised the boon-granting Blue-and-Red One with desired words. (LiP 2.19.26)
The sages said:
Salutation to <s>Siva</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Kadrudra</s>, to the Wise One (<s>Pracetas</s>),
to <s>Midhustama</s> (the most bountiful), to the All, to <s>Sipivista</s>, to the Swift One. (LiP 2.19.27)

children.text: prabhūte vimale sāre hyādhāre parame sukhe /
children.translated_text: Abundant, pure, essential, the foundation, supreme bliss —

children.text: navaśaktyāvṛtaṃ devaṃ padmasthaṃ bhāskaraṃ prabhum // LiP_2,19.28 //
children.translated_text: the God stationed on a lotus, enclosed by the nine <s>Saktis</s>, the radiant Lord. (LiP 2.19.28)

children.text: ādityaṃ bhāskaraṃ bhānuṃ raviṃ devaṃ divākaram /
children.translated_text: <s>Aditya</s>, <s>Bhaskara</s>, <s>Bhanu</s>, <s>Ravi</s>, the God, the Maker of Day (<s>Divakara</s>) —

children.text: umāṃ prabhāṃ tathā prajñāṃ saṃdhyāṃ sāvitrikāmapi // LiP_2,19.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Uma</s>, <s>Prabha</s> (Radiance), <s>Prajna</s> (Wisdom), <s>Sandhya</s> (Twilight), and <s>Savitri</s> — (LiP 2.19.29)
<s>Vistara</s>, <s>Uttara</s>, the Goddess <s>Bodani</s> — I bow to [them all].

children.text: āpyāyanīṃ ca varadāṃ brahmāṇaṃ keśavaṃ haram // LiP_2,19.30 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Apyayani</s>, the boon-granting one, <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Kesava</s>, and <s>Hara</s>. (LiP 2.19.30)
Having worshipped the host [of planets] beginning with <s>Soma</s>, in sequence, with mantras in the prescribed order,

children.text: smarāmi devaṃ ravimaṇḍalasthaṃ sadāśivaṃ śaṅkaramādidevam // LiP_2,19.31 //
children.translated_text: I meditate upon the God stationed in the solar disc — <s>Sadasiva</s>, <s>Sankara</s>, the Primal God. (LiP 2.19.31)
And upon <s>Indra</s> and the other gods, and the Lords, <s>Narayana</s>, the lotus-born [<s>Brahma</s>], the Primal God,

children.text: prāgādyadhordhvaṃ ca yathākrameṇa vajrādipadmaṃ ca tathā smarāmi // LiP_2,19.32 //
children.translated_text: from the east and other [directions], below and above, in sequence, and I meditate upon the thunderbolt-and-lotus [symbols]. (LiP 2.19.32)
To You, of vermilion color, with [Your] <s>mandala</s>, adorned with golden thunderbolt-ornaments,
with lotus-like eyes, seated on a lotus, the cause of <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Narayana</s>. (LiP 2.19.33)

children.text: rathaṃ ca saptāśvamanūruvīraṃ gaṇaṃ tathā saptavidhaṃ krameṇa /
children.translated_text: The chariot with seven horses, the hero <s>Anuru</s> [the charioteer], and the host, sevenfold in sequence,

children.text: ṛtupravāheṇa ca vālīkhilyānsmarāmi mandehagaṇakṣayaṃ ca // LiP_2,19.34 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Valakhilyas</s> (thumb-sized sages) with the flow of seasons — I meditate, and upon the <s>Mandeha</s> host and [its] destruction. (LiP 2.19.34)

children.text: hutvā tilādyairvividhaistathāgnau punaḥ samāpyaiva tathaiva sarvam /
children.translated_text: Having offered oblations with sesame and various [substances] into the fire, then completing all again,

children.text: udvāsya hṛtpaṅkajamadhyasaṃsthaṃ smarāmi biṃbaṃ tava devadeva // LiP_2,19.35 //
children.translated_text: I dismiss [the external image] and meditate upon Your form stationed in the lotus of the heart, O God of Gods. (LiP 2.19.35)
I meditate upon the images in sequence — red, with lotus-pure eyes,

children.text: padmaṃ ca savye varadaṃ ca vāme kare tathā bhūṣitabhūṣaṇāni // LiP_2,19.36 //
children.translated_text: a lotus in the right hand, the boon-gesture in the left — adorned with ornaments. (LiP 2.19.36)

children.text: daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ tava divyavaktraṃ vidyutprabhaṃ daityayaṅkaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Your divine face, terrible with fangs, with the luster of lightning, and destroyer of <s>Daityas</s> —

children.text: smarāmi rakṣābhirataṃ dvijānāṃ mandeharakṣogaṇabhartsanaṃ ca // LiP_2,19.37 //
children.translated_text: I meditate upon [You], engaged in the protection of the twice-born, and the terrifying of the <s>Mandeha</s> <s>Raksasa</s> hosts. (LiP 2.19.37)
The Moon (<s>Soma</s>) — white; Mars (<s>Bhumija</s>) — fire-colored; Mercury (<s>Budha</s>), son of the Moon — gold-like;

children.text: bṛhaspatiṃ kāñcanasannikāśaṃ śukraṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇataraṃ ca mandam // LiP_2,19.38 //
children.translated_text: Jupiter (<s>Brhaspati</s>) — gold-resembling; Venus (<s>Sukra</s>) — white; Saturn (<s>Manda</s>) — very dark. (LiP 2.19.38)
I meditate upon the right hand [granting] fearlessness, the left [placed] on the thigh, excellent —

children.text: sarveṣāṃ mandaparyantaṃ mahādevaṃ ca bhāskaram // LiP_2,19.39 //
children.translated_text: for all [planets] up to Saturn, and upon <s>Mahadeva</s> as <s>Bhaskara</s> (the Sun). (LiP 2.19.39)

children.text: pūrṇenduvarṇena ca puṣpadhaprasthena toyane śubhena pūrṇam /
children.translated_text: With a vessel of full-moon color, filled with flowers and auspicious water,

children.text: pātraṃ dṛḍhaṃ tāmramayaṃ prakalpya dāsye tavārdhyaṃ bhagavanprasīda // LiP_2,19.40 //
children.translated_text: having prepared a firm copper vessel, I shall offer You the <s>arghya</s> (water-offering) — be gracious, O Blessed One! (LiP 2.19.40)
Salutation to <s>Siva</s>, the God, to <s>Isvara</s>, to the one with matted hair (<s>Kapardin</s>),

children.text: rudrāya viṣṇave tubhyaṃ brahmaṇe sūryamūrtaye // LiP_2,19.41 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Visnu</s>, to You, to <s>Brahma</s>, to the Sun-formed One. (LiP 2.19.41)
<s>Suta</s> said:

children.text: yaḥ śivaṃ maṇḍalaṃ devaṃ saṃpūjyaivaṃ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, having worshipped the God <s>Siva</s> in the <s>mandala</s> with concentration,
recites this supreme hymn at morning, midday, and evening — (LiP 2.19.42)

children.text: itthaṃ śivena sāyujyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ // LiP_2,19.43 //
children.translated_text: he attains union (<s>sayujya</s>) with <s>Siva</s> — there is no doubt about this. (LiP 2.19.43)
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the <s>Uttarabhaga</s> of the glorious <s>Linga Mahapurana</s>.
<s>Suta</s> said:
Thus, <s>Rudra</s> <s>Mahadeva</s>, stationed in the <s>mandala</s>, the Grandsire,

children.text: pūjyo vai brāhmaṇānāṃ ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ // LiP_2,20.1 //
children.translated_text: is to be worshipped by <s>brahmanas</s> and especially by <s>ksatriyas</s>. (LiP 2.20.1)
