children.text: vaiśyānāṃ naiva śūdrāṇāṃ śuśruṣāṃ pūjakasya ca /
children.translated_text: By <s>vaisyas</s>, but not by <s>sudras</s> — [they may perform only] service of the worshipper.

children.text: strīṇāṃ naivādikāro 'sti pūjādiṣu na saṃśayaḥ // LiP_2,20.2 //
children.translated_text: Women also have no authority in worship and the like, without doubt. (LiP 2.20.2)
For women and <s>sudras</s>, through the worship [performed] by the best of twice-born, that [same] fruit results.
For the benefit of kings, especially by <s>brahmanas</s> and others — (LiP 2.20.3)
thus should <s>brahmanas</s> and others worship <s>Sadasiva</s>.
Having said this, the blessed <s>Rudra</s> disappeared there, by Himself. (LiP 2.20.4)

children.text: te devā munayaḥ sarve śivamuddiśya śaṅkaram /
children.translated_text: Those gods and all the sages, directing [their minds] toward <s>Siva</s> <s>Sankara</s>,
bowed — those great souls, overwhelmed by meditation on <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2.20.5)
The gods departed as they had come, and the sages rich in austerity.
Therefore, one should always worship the Sun (<s>Aditya</s>) as <s>Siva</s>'s form, (LiP 2.20.6)
for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, <s>kama</s>, <s>artha</s>, and liberation — by mind, action, and speech.
The sages said:
O <s>Romaharsana</s>, O omniscient one, O best among bearers of all scriptures! (LiP 2.20.7)
O disciple of <s>Vyasa</s>, O greatly fortunate one, tell us now about the <s>Vahniya</s> (fire-related rites).
By <s>Siva</s>, the God of Gods, desiring the welfare of devotees, (LiP 2.20.8)
having extracted from the <s>Vedas</s> with their six <s>Angas</s>, and from <s>Sankhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> entirely,
and having performed vast austerity, difficult for gods and demons — (LiP 2.20.9)
endowed with [knowledge of] purposes, places, and the like, secret, condemned by the ignorant,
sometimes contrary to and sometimes consistent with the <s>dharmas</s> established by <s>varna</s> and <s>asrama</s> — (LiP 2.20.10)
the scripture spoken by <s>Siva</s> for <s>dharma</s>, <s>kama</s>, <s>artha</s>, and liberation,

children.text: śatakoṭipramāṇena tatra pūjā kathaṃ vibhoḥ // LiP_2,20.11 //
children.translated_text: extending to a hundred crore [verses] — how therein is the worship of the Lord? (LiP 2.20.11)

children.text: snānayogādayo vāpi śrotuṃ kautuhalaṃ hi naḥ /
children.translated_text: The bathing-rites and the like too — we are curious to hear.
<s>Suta</s> said:
Long ago, by <s>Sanatkumara</s>, on the beautiful peak of <s>Meru</s>, (LiP 2.20.12)
<s>Nandisvara</s>, the god <s>Sailadi</s> (son of the mountain), approved by <s>Siva</s>, was asked.
Asked thus, having bowed, by the chief sages from all sides — (LiP 2.20.13)
to that <s>Sanatkumara</s>, by <s>Nandin</s>, the delight of [his] family,
was told the knowledge of <s>Siva</s> — hear, O bulls among sages! (LiP 2.20.14)
The <s>Saiva</s> [teaching], summarized, as spoken in the <s>Vedas</s>, expounded by <s>Siva</s>,
free from praise and blame, producing immediate conviction, (LiP 2.20.15)
divine, born from the guru's grace, granting liberation without effort.
<s>Sanatkumara</s> said:
O Blessed One, O Lord of All Beings, O <s>Nandisvara</s>, O <s>Mahesvara</s>! (LiP 2.20.16)
How do worship and the like of <s>Sambhu</s> [lead to] <s>dharma</s>, <s>kama</s>, <s>artha</s>, and liberation?
Please tell [me], O <s>Sailadi</s>, who has come with humility. (LiP 2.20.17)
<s>Suta</s> said:
The blessed <s>Nandin</s>, having considered, hearing the words again,
spoke — the best of speakers — about time, occasion, authority, and the like. (LiP 2.20.18)
<s>Sailadi</s> [<s>Nandin</s>] said:
From the guru and from the scripture, I shall declare the authority [for worship].
The designation [<s>Acarya</s>] is from reverence alone — [it belongs to] the <s>Siva-Acarya</s>, not otherwise. (LiP 2.20.19)
He who himself practices the conduct and also establishes others in [right] conduct,
and who gathers the meanings of the scriptures — he is called an <s>Acarya</s> (teacher). (LiP 2.20.20)
Therefore, a devotee should seek as guru an <s>Acarya</s> who knows the truth of the <s>Vedas</s>,
who sleeps on ashes, fortunate, of pleasing appearance, (LiP 2.20.21)
accepted [by tradition], a delight to people, following the path of <s>Sruti</s> and <s>Smrti</s>,
a giver of fearlessness through knowledge, free from fickleness and restlessness, (LiP 2.20.22)
a guardian of [right] conduct, steadfast, established in the observances.
Seeing him, with one's whole being, one should worship the guru as <s>Siva</s>. (LiP 2.20.23)
With oneself and with wealth, according to one's faith and means,
a disciple should serve [the guru] so long until he becomes pleased. (LiP 2.20.24)
When that greatly fortunate one is well-pleased, the destruction of bonds (<s>pasa</s>) occurs immediately.

children.text: gururmānyo guruḥ pūjyo gurureva sadāśivaḥ // LiP_2,20.25 //
children.translated_text: The guru is to be honored, the guru is to be worshipped — the guru is <s>Sadasiva</s> Himself. (LiP 2.20.25)
For three years, or [otherwise], one should test the disciples, the <s>brahmanas</s>,
through the giving of life-breath and wealth, and through commands here and there. (LiP 2.20.26)
The superior [student] should be assigned to inferior [tasks]; the lowly to superior objects.

children.text: ākṛṣṭāstāḍitā vāpi ye viṣādaṃ na yānti vai // LiP_2,20.27 //
children.translated_text: Those who, when dragged or beaten, do not fall into despondency — (LiP 2.20.27)
they are fit, devoted to <s>Siva</s>'s <s>dharma</s>, dedicated to the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Siva</s>,
self-controlled, endowed with <s>dharma</s>, following the path of <s>Sruti</s> and <s>Smrti</s>, (LiP 2.20.28)
enduring all pairs of opposites, steadfast, with minds ever engaged,
devoted to helping others, delighting in service to the guru, (LiP 2.20.29)
straightforward, gentle, self-possessed, agreeable, sweet-speaking,
free from pride, intelligent, having abandoned rivalry and craving. (LiP 2.20.30)
Endowed with the qualities of purity and good conduct, free from pride and jealousy —

children.text: yogyā evaṃ dvijāḥ sarve śivabhaktiparāyaṇāḥ // LiP_2,20.31 //
children.translated_text: all such twice-born ones are worthy [of initiation], devoted to <s>Śiva</s>-<s>bhakti</s>. (LiP 2,20.31)
Those who are endowed with such conduct, through actions of speech, mind, and body,

children.text: śodhyā evaṃvidhāścaiva tattvānāṃ ca viśuddhaye // LiP_2,20.32 //
children.translated_text: should be purified in this manner for the purification of the principles (<s>tattvas</s>). (LiP 2,20.32)
One who is pure, endowed with humility, free from falsehood and harshness,
and who obeys the guru's command — such a disciple deserves grace (<s>anugraha</s>). (LiP 2,20.33)
And a guru should be learned in the <s>śāstras</s>, wise, ascetic, compassionate toward people,
devoted to worldly conduct — such a knower of principles is declared to be a bestower of liberation. (LiP 2,20.34)
One who is endowed with all marks and proficient in all <s>śāstras</s>,
who knows the methods of all means — for one devoid of [knowledge of] the principles, [all this is] fruitless. (LiP 2,20.35)

children.text: svasaṃvedya pare tattve niścayo yasya nātmani /
children.translated_text: One whose conviction in the supreme principle, which is self-evident, does not [reside] in his own self —
there is no grace for his own self; how then can there be grace for another? (LiP 2,20.36)

children.text: prabuddhastu dvijo yastu sa śuddhaḥ sādhayatyapi /
children.translated_text: That twice-born one who is awakened — he is pure and can accomplish [liberation] as well.

children.text: tattvahīne kuto bodhaḥ kuto hyātmaparigrahaḥ // LiP_2,20.37 //
children.translated_text: Where there is no [knowledge of] the principles, whence can there be awakening? Whence self-possession? (LiP 2,20.37)
Those who are devoid of [self-]possession — all of them are called <s>paśus</s> (bound souls).

children.text: paśubhiḥ preritā ye tu sarve te paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ // LiP_2,20.38 //
children.translated_text: And those who are directed by <s>paśus</s> — all of them too are considered <s>paśus</s>. (LiP 2,20.38)

children.text: tasmāt tattvavido ye tu te muktā mocayanty api /
children.translated_text: Therefore those who are knowers of the principles — they are liberated and also liberate others.
The principle (<s>tattva</s>) is that which generates direct knowledge (<s>saṃvitti</s>), born of supreme bliss. (LiP 2,20.39)

children.text: tattvaṃ tu viditaṃ yena sa evānandadarśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: He by whom the principle is known — he alone is the seer of bliss;
not by name alone — one who is devoid of [direct] knowledge. (LiP 2,20.40)

children.text: anyo 'nyaṃ tārayennaiva kiṃ śilā tārayec chilām /
children.translated_text: One cannot save another [if he himself is not saved] — can a stone save a stone?
Those for whom liberation comes by name alone — that is liberation in name only. (LiP 2,20.41)
From the mere sight of yogins, or from their touch, or from their speech,
knowledge is immediately born — that which destroys the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>). (LiP 2,20.42)
Or, by the path of <s>yoga</s>, having entered the body of the disciple,

children.text: bodayedeva yogena sarvatattvāni śodhya ca // LiP_2,20.43 //
children.translated_text: [the guru] should awaken [him] through <s>yoga</s>, having purified all the principles. (LiP 2,20.43)
The purification of the six and a half [paths] is prescribed for yogins through <s>jñāna-yoga</s>.

children.text: śiṣyaṃ parīkṣya dharmajñaṃ dhārmikaṃ vedapāragam // LiP_2,20.44 //
children.translated_text: Having examined the disciple — one who knows <s>dharma</s>, righteous, proficient in the <s>Vedas</s>, (LiP 2,20.44)
whether a Brahmin, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or <s>Vaiśya</s>, free from many faults —

children.text: jñānena jñeyamālokya karṇāt karṇāgatena tu // LiP_2,20.45 //
children.translated_text: having illuminated the knowable through knowledge, transmitted from ear to ear, (LiP 2,20.45)

children.text: bhauvanaṃ ca padaṃ caiva varṇākhyaṃ mātramuttamam // LiP_2,20.46 /
children.translated_text: should [transmit] the cosmic path (<s>bhauvana</s>), the word-path (<s>pada</s>), the letter-path (<s>varṇa</s>), and the supreme <s>mātrā</s>. (LiP 2,20.46)
The time-path (<s>kālādhvan</s>), O greatly fortunate one, and the principle-path (<s>tattvādhvan</s>), accepted by all —
are split by whose power, by mere command, in all directions. (LiP 2,20.47)
just as one lamp is kindled from another, the guru, following the proper method,
His <s>siddhi</s> and liberation are born from the guru's compassion.

children.text: pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni āviśanti ca bhauvane // LiP_2,20.48 //
children.translated_text: The elements beginning with earth enter into the cosmic path (<s>bhauvana</s>). (LiP 2,20.48)

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśastathā rūpaṃ raso gandhaśca bhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — in their true nature;
the word-path (<s>pada</s>) called <s>varṇa</s>, O Brahmin, is the differentiation of the cognitive senses. (LiP 2,20.49)

children.text: karmendriyāṇi mātraṃ hi mano buddhirataḥ param /
children.translated_text: The action-senses are indeed the <s>mātrā</s> (measure); mind and intellect are beyond these;
ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) and then the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) — this is known as the time-path (<s>kālādhvan</s>). (LiP 2,20.50)
From <s>Puruṣa</s> up to <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), the transcendence (<s>unmanatva</s>), the supreme beyond the supreme,
and then <s>Īśatva</s> (lordship) — this is declared to be the illuminator of the meaning of all principles. (LiP 2,20.51)

children.text: ayogī naiva jānāti tattvaśuddhiṃ śivātmikām // LiP_2,20.52 //
children.translated_text: A non-yogin does not know the purification of the principles, which has the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,20.52)
Thus ends the twentieth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having examined the ground according to proper rites — by smell, color, taste, and so forth —
having adorned it with canopies and such, fit for invoking the Lord, (LiP 2,21.1)
one should prepare a <s>maṇḍala</s> of one arm's length;
one should draw a lotus in the center, endowed with five gems. (LiP 2,21.2)

children.text: cūrṇairaṣṭadalaṃ vṛttaṃ sitaṃ vā raktameva ca /
children.translated_text: With colored powders, [draw] an eight-petaled circle, white or red,
accompanied by attendant [deities], endowed with great beauty. (LiP 2,21.3)
Having invoked <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause, into the pericarp,
one should worship [Him] with all effort, according to one's means and capacity. (LiP 2,21.4)
On the petals, the <s>siddhis</s> are declared; in the pericarp, O great sage,
[is] the stalk of detachment and knowledge, and the root of <s>dharma</s>, which is delightful. (LiP 2,21.5)

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca kālī vikaraṇī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Vikaraṇī</s>,
<s>Balavikaraṇī</s>, and <s>Balapramathinī</s> in sequence, (LiP 2,21.6)
and <s>Sarvabhūtadamanī</s> — [these are] the powers (<s>śaktis</s>) on the filaments;
<s>Manonmanī</s>, <s>Mahāmāyā</s> — on <s>Śiva</s>'s seat in the pericarp. (LiP 2,21.7)
Together with <s>Vāmadeva</s> and others, one should arrange [them] in pairs;
<s>Manonmana</s>, the great God, with <s>Manonmanī</s> in the center. (LiP 2,21.8)
Connected with sun, moon, and fire, [the deity] called <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: puruṣaṃ vinyasedvaktraṃ pūrve patre raviprabham // LiP_2,21.9 //
children.translated_text: one should place the <s>Puruṣa</s> face, radiant as the sun, on the eastern petal. (LiP 2,21.9)
<s>Aghora</s> on the southern petal, resembling a mass of dark collyrium;
<s>Vāmadeva</s> on the northern [petal], resembling a <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flower. (LiP 2,21.10)
<s>Sadya</s> [<s>Sadyojāta</s>] one should place on the western petal, white as cow's milk;
<s>Īśāna</s> in the pericarp, resembling pure crystal. (LiP 2,21.11)
Resembling the orb of the moon — with the mantra '<s>Hṛdayāya</s>' (to the heart);
in the southeastern direction, in <s>Rudra</s>'s quarter, '<s>Śirase</s>' (to the head), smoke-colored. (LiP 2,21.12)

children.text: śikhāyai ca namaścoti raktābhe nairṛte dale /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śikhāyai ca namaḥ</s>' (salutation to the crest) — on the southwestern petal, of red hue;
'<s>Kavacāya</s>' (to the armor), collyrium-colored — one should place on the northwestern petal. (LiP 2,21.13)
'<s>Astrāya</s>' (to the weapon), having the color of fire's tip — one should place in the [intermediate] directions;
'<s>Netrebhyaḥ</s>' (to the eyes), tawny — one should place in the northeast. (LiP 2,21.14)

children.text: śivaṃ sadā śivaṃ devaṃ maheśvaramataḥ param /
children.translated_text: One should [contemplate] <s>Śiva</s>, the ever-auspicious God, <s>Maheśvara</s>, beyond whom [there is nothing],

children.text: rudraṃ viṣṇuṃ viriñciṃ ca sṛṣṭinyāyena bhāvayet // LiP_2,21.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā) — one should meditate in the order of creation. (LiP 2,21.15)
To <s>Śiva</s>, of <s>Rudra</s>-form, to <s>Śambhu</s> who transcends the <s>Śāntyatīta</s> [level],
to the Peaceful, to the subduer of demons, salutation to the Moon — (LiP 2,21.16)
to the Knowable, to the support of knowledge, to Fire, of fiery splendor,

children.text: kālāyai ca pratiṣṭhāyai tārakāyāntakāya ca // LiP_2,21.17 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Kālī</s>, to the Foundation, to the Deliverer, to the Destroyer [of death], (LiP 2,21.17)
to <s>Nivṛtti</s>, to the lord of wealth, to the Stream, to the Support —
with these mantras, [one should worship] <s>Sadāśiva</s> whose form is the great elements. (LiP 2,21.18)
The God whose crown is <s>Īśāna</s>, whose face is <s>Puruṣa</s>, the primordial one,

children.text: aghora hṛdayaṃ hṛṣṭaṃ vāmaguhyaṃ maheśvaram // LiP_2,21.19 //
children.translated_text: whose heart is <s>Aghora</s>, the joyful one, whose secret [parts] are <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s> — (LiP 2,21.19)
one should contemplate the God of <s>Sadya</s> [<s>Sadyojāta</s>]-form, the cause of the manifest existent and non-existent,
five-faced, ten-armed, consisting of thirty-eight <s>kalās</s> (rays). (LiP 2,21.20)
Dividing <s>Sadya</s> [<s>Sadyojāta</s>] eightfold, consisting of <s>kalās</s>;
dividing <s>Vāmadeva</s> thirteen-fold, the pervading Lord; (LiP 2,21.21)
making <s>Aghora</s> eightfold, established in the form of <s>kalās</s>;

children.text: puruṣaṃ ca caturdhā vai vibhajya ca kalāmayam // LiP_2,21.22 //
children.translated_text: and dividing <s>Puruṣa</s> fourfold, consisting of <s>kalās</s>; (LiP 2,21.22)
making <s>Īśāna</s> fivefold — established through the five forms,
with the mantra '<s>Haṃsa Haṃsa</s>,' endowed with devotion to <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,21.23)
<s>Oṃkāra</s> as the <s>mātrā</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s> as the <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s>, of identical form;

children.text: ā ī ū e tathā aṃbānukrameṇātmarūpiṇam // LiP_2,21.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ā</s>, <s>Ī</s>, <s>Ū</s>, <s>E</s>, and <s>Aṃ</s> — in sequence, of the nature of the Self. (LiP 2,21.24)
The God accompanied by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), free from dissolution and creation,
subtler than the subtle, unborn, greater than the great. (LiP 2,21.25)
The celibate (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>) <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, Lord of <s>Umā</s>,
the thousand-headed God, thousand-eyed, eternal, (LiP 2,21.26)
with a thousand hands and feet, [extending] to the end of <s>nāda</s> (cosmic sound), whose body is <s>nāda</s>,
resembling a firefly in form, the Lord whose shape is a streak of moonlight. (LiP 2,21.27)
At the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger-breadths above the head), between the eyebrows, in the center of the palate, at the throat, in succession,
in the heart region — the God established [there], self-blissful, immortal <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,21.28)
Resembling a circle of lightning, equal in radiance to ten million lightning bolts,
dark and red, of crescent form, seated upon the three <s>Śaktis</s>. (LiP 2,21.29)
One should contemplate <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the God endowed with the three principles,
of the form of <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) — one should worship the God in proper sequence. (LiP 2,21.30)
One should worship the world-guardians (<s>lokapālas</s>) with the weapon-mantra, beginning from the east, separately,

children.text: caruṃ ca vidhināsādya śivāya vinivedayet // LiP_2,21.31 //
children.translated_text: and having prepared the oblation (<s>caru</s>) according to rites, one should offer it to <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,21.31)

children.text: ardhaṃ śivāya dattvaiva śeṣardhena tu homayet /
children.translated_text: Having given half to <s>Śiva</s>, with the remaining half one should perform the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering).
With the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra], one should then give the disciple the best [oblation-remnant] to eat. (LiP 2,21.32)
Having sipped water and become purified, one should worship <s>Puruṣa</s> according to rites.
Then, having consumed the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>), consecrated with the <s>Īśāna</s> [mantra], (LiP 2,21.33)
with the <s>Vāmadeva</s> [mantra], having ash on the limbs, one should dust with ash in sequence.
In [the disciple's] ears, one should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> with <s>Rudra</s> as its deity. (LiP 2,21.34)
With a thread, with a cover, wrapped in a pair of garments,
first with heaps of gold and gems, scented, golden — (LiP 2,21.35)
one should place five water-pots; then with five Brahmins
one should perform the <s>homa</s> with the oblation, according to one's means and capacity. (LiP 2,21.36)

children.text: śiṣyaṃ ca vāsayedbhaktaṃ dakṣiṇe maṇḍalasya tu /
children.translated_text: One should seat the devoted disciple on the south side of the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
mounted on a bed of <s>darbha</s> grass, intent on meditation upon <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,21.37)
With the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra], according to proper method, one hundred and eight times again,

children.text: ghṛtena hutvā duḥsvapnaṃ prabhāte śodhayenmalam // LiP_2,21.38 //
children.translated_text: having offered ghee, one should purify the impurity of bad dreams at dawn. (LiP 2,21.38)
The disciple who has thus observed fasting, bathed, his body adorned,
wearing new garments and upper cloth, with turban, auspicious marks made — (LiP 2,21.39)
having blindfolded [his] eyes with a fine silk cloth, one should lead [him] in,
with an offering mixed with gold and flowers, according to one's means and capacity. (LiP 2,21.40)
With the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra, one should make a flower-offering (<s>puṣpāñjali</s>) to the Lord,

children.text: pradakṣiṇātrayaṃ kṛtvā rudrādhyāyena vā punaḥ // LiP_2,21.41 //
children.translated_text: and having performed three circumambulations, [reciting] the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, or alternatively, (LiP 2,21.41)
with <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) alone, intent on meditation upon <s>Śiva</s>,
having meditated on the Lord of the Gods of Gods, one should withdraw [everything] into <s>Īśāna</s>. (LiP 2,21.42)
On whichever mantra the flower falls — that mantra becomes effective for him.

children.text: śivāṃbhasā tu saṃspṛśya avoreṇa ca bhasmanā // LiP_2,21.43 //
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled with <s>Śiva</s>-water, and with ash [consecrated] by the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra], (LiP 2,21.43)
having placed [it] on the disciple's head, one should worship the disciple with sandalwood paste and such.

children.text: vāruṇaṃ paramaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dvāraṃ vai sarvavarṇinām // LiP_2,21.44 //
children.translated_text: The western [gate] is the supreme, best entrance for all <s>varṇas</s> (castes). (LiP 2,21.44)

children.text: kṣattriyāṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa dvāraṃ vai paścimaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Especially for <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, the western gate is prescribed.
Having removed the eye-covering, one should then show [him] the <s>maṇḍala</s>. (LiP 2,21.45)
Having seated [him] on a <s>kuśa</s>-grass seat, assuming the <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s> (south-facing) posture,
one should then perform the purification of the principles (<s>tattvaśuddhi</s>) through the five-principle method. (LiP 2,21.46)
Through <s>Nivṛtti</s> [kalā], up to <s>Rudra</s> — O son born from the cosmic egg,
through <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> [kalā], above that, up to the range of the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>), (LiP 2,21.47)
through the <s>Vidyā</s> [kalā] up to <s>Viśveśvara</s>, by the <s>kalā</s> measure, O one of good vows;

children.text: tadūrdhvamārgaṃ saṃśodhya śivabhaktyā śivaṃ nayet // LiP_2,21.48 //
children.translated_text: having purified the path above that, with <s>Śiva</s>-devotion, one should lead [the soul] to <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,21.48)
For the worship of that principle, of that Lord of enjoyment,
through the division of the three principles, or through four [divisions] as well, (LiP 2,21.49)
one should offer oblations with the limb-mantras (<s>aṅgamantras</s>) to <s>Sadāśiva</s> who transcends <s>Śānti</s>,

children.text: sadyādibhistu śāntyantaṃ caturbhiḥ kalayā pṛthak // LiP_2,21.50 //
children.translated_text: and with <s>Sadya</s> [<s>Sadyojāta</s>] and others up to <s>Śānti</s> [level], with the four <s>kalās</s> separately. (LiP 2,21.50)
The <s>Śāntyatīta</s> level, O best of sages, with <s>Īśāna</s> [mantra], or alternatively,

children.text: pratyekamaṣṭottaraśataṃ diśā homaṃ tu kārayet // LiP_2,21.51 //
children.translated_text: one hundred and eight times each, one should perform the <s>homa</s> in each direction. (LiP 2,21.51)
In the northeast, the fifth, <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is celebrated.

children.text: samidājyacarūṃl lājān sarṣapāṃś ca yavāṃs tilān // LiP_2,21.52 //
children.translated_text: Sacrificial sticks, ghee, oblations (<s>caru</s>), parched grain, mustard seeds, barley, and sesame — (LiP 2,21.52)
these seven substances should be offered, ending with <s>Svāhā</s>, beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> —
Their final oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>), O brahmin, is ordained by the <s>Īśāna</s> [mantra]. (LiP 2,21.53)
With the <s>sahaṃsa</s> [mantra], as is proper, beginning with <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), O one of good vows,

children.text: aghoreṇa ca mantreṇa prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate // LiP_2,21.54 //
children.translated_text: the expiatory rite (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) is ordained with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra. (LiP 2,21.54)
The fire-ritual from the <s>jaya</s> [prayer] up to the <s>sviṣṭa</s> [completion], in sequence,
should be conjoined according to the manner of the enumeration of <s>guṇas</s> and with the principal [mantra]. (LiP 2,21.55)
The elements, with the <s>Brahman</s> [mantras] or silently with seed-syllables and the like,

children.text: atha pradhānamātreṇa prāṇāpānau niyamya ca // LiP_2,21.56 //
children.translated_text: then with the principal [mantra] alone, restraining <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> — (LiP 2,21.56)
with the sixth [mantra], one should pierce the self [up to the] end of <s>praṇava</s>, [both] ordered and disordered.
Withdrawing one into another — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Hara</s>, (LiP 2,21.57)

children.text: rudre rudraṃ tamīśāne śive devaṃ maheśvaram /
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> into <s>Rudra</s>, that into <s>Īśāna</s>, [and <s>Īśāna</s>] into the god <s>Maheśvara</s> of <s>Śiva</s> —
therefore, in the order of creation, one should meditate upon the destroyer of [worldly] existence. (LiP 2,21.58)
Having established this individual self (<s>jīva</s>) — striking, door-revealing,

children.text: dīpanaṃ grahaṇaṃ caiva bandhanaṃ pūjayā saha // LiP_2,21.59 //
children.translated_text: kindling, seizing, and binding together with worship, (LiP 2,21.59)
and immortalizing (<s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s>) — one should perform [all this] according to the prescribed rules.
Ending with the sixth [mantra], conjoined with <s>Sadya</s>[ojāta], combined with the third — (LiP 2,21.60)
ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — this is called the dissolution, according to the manner of the five elements.
Beginning with <s>Sadya</s>[ojāta], combined with the sixth, ending with <s>śikhā</s> (topknot), ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — (LiP 2,21.61)
this is described as the striking and the doorway of the principles for the <s>yogin</s>.

children.text: pradhānaṃ saṃpuṭīkṛtya tṛtīyena ca dīpanam // LiP_2,21.62 //
children.translated_text: Enclosing the principal [mantra] — with the third, the kindling; (LiP 2,21.62)
enclosing with the first — the principal [mantra] is known as the seizing.
Enclosing the principal [mantra] with the first, as before — (LiP 2,21.63)
the binding with the complete [mantra]; and the flooding with the nectar [mantra].

children.text: śāntya tītā tataḥ śāntirvidyā nāma kalāmalā // LiP_2,21.64 //
children.translated_text: Beyond <s>Śānti</s> (peace) is <s>Śānti</s>, the <s>Vidyā</s> named the spotless <s>Kalā</s>; (LiP 2,21.64)
<s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (foundation) and <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation) — this is known as the transition of the <s>Kalās</s>.
Combined with the principles, colors, and <s>kalās</s>, with the cosmic levels in proper sequence, (LiP 2,21.65)

children.text: mantraiḥ pādaiḥ stavaṃ kuryādviśodhya ca yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: one should perform praise with mantras and <s>pādas</s>, having purified according to the rule.

children.text: ādyena yonibījena kalpayitvā ca pūrvavat // LiP_2,21.66 //
children.translated_text: Having arranged with the first seed-syllable as before, (LiP 2,21.66)
know [these as]: the sprinkling of worship, the striking, and the seizing;

children.text: saṃhatasya ca saṃyogaṃ vikṣepaṃ ca yathākramam // LiP_2,21.67
children.translated_text: the conjunction of the united [principles], and the projection, in proper order. (LiP 2,21.67)

children.text: arcanā ca tathā garbhadhāraṇaṃ jananaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: And worship, the bearing of the embryo (<s>garbhadhāraṇa</s>), and birth again;
the qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) of the sun, and the dissolution especially. (LiP 2,21.68)
The highest first, then the last, with the seed-syllable, O one of good vows,

children.text: uddāre prokṣaṇe caiva tāḍane ca mahāmune // LiP_2,21.69 //
children.translated_text: in the extraction, the sprinkling, and the striking, O great sage — (LiP 2,21.69)
with <s>Aghora</s> ending in <s>phaṭ</s>, the dissolution [is accomplished], without doubt.

children.text: pratitattvaṃ kramo hyeṣa yogamārgeṇa suvrata // LiP_2,21.70 //
children.translated_text: This procedure is for each principle, through the path of <s>yoga</s>, O one of good vows. (LiP 2,21.70)
With a fist[-ful of mantras], for as long as is needed, one should lead in sequence,

children.text: viṣuveṇa tu yogena nivṛttyādi śivāntikam // LiP_2,21.71 //
children.translated_text: through the equinoctial <s>yoga</s>, from <s>Nivṛtti</s> up to <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,21.71)

children.text: ekatra samatāṃ yāti nānyathā tu pṛthakpṛthak /
children.translated_text: In one [place] it attains equality — not otherwise, separately for each.

children.text: nāsāgre dvādaśāntena pṛṣṭhena saha yoginām // LiP_2,21.72 //
children.translated_text: At the tip of the nose, at the twelve-ending [point], together with the dorsal [channel], for <s>yogins</s> — (LiP 2,21.72)
this should be endured — such is the command of the God of Gods, O best of brahmins.
With [a vessel] fashioned of gold, silver, copper, and the like, according to the rule, (LiP 2,21.73)
with <s>kuśa</s> grass and cloth, wrapped with thread,
filled with water from sacred sites, containing gems within, O one of good vows, (LiP 2,21.74)
consecrated with the <s>Saṃhitā</s> [mantras], praised with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s> —

children.text: secayecca tataḥ śiṣyaṃ śivabhaktaṃ ca dhārmikam // LiP_2,21.75 //
children.translated_text: one should then sprinkle the disciple who is devoted to <s>Śiva</s> and is righteous. (LiP 2,21.75)

children.text: so 'pi śiṣyaḥ śivasyāgre suroragre ca sādaram /
children.translated_text: That disciple, before <s>Śiva</s>, before the gods,

children.text: vahneśca dīkṣāṃ kurvīta dīkṣitaśca tathācaret // LiP_2,21.76 //
children.translated_text: and before the fire, should undergo initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), and once initiated should so conduct himself. (LiP 2,21.76)
Better to abandon one's life-breath or even to lose one's head,
than to eat without first worshipping the blessed <s>Sadāśiva</s>! (LiP 2,21.77)

children.text: evaṃ dīkṣā prakartavyā pūjā caiva yatākramam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the initiation should be performed, and worship too, in proper sequence.
One should worship the Supreme Lord three times [a day], or [at least] once. (LiP 2,21.78)
The fire-ritual, the <s>Vedas</s>, and sacrifices with abundant fees —
all these are not equal even to a fraction of the worship of the <s>Śiva-liṅga</s>. (LiP 2,21.79)

children.text: sadā yajati yajñena sadā dānaṃ prayacchati /
children.translated_text: He who worships <s>Śiva</s> even once always [in effect] performs sacrifice,
always gives gifts, and always subsists on air alone. (LiP 2,21.80)

children.text: ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ nityameva vā /
children.translated_text: Those who worship <s>Mahādeva</s> once, twice, three times,

children.text: yor'cayānti mahādevaṃ te rudrā nātra saṃśayaḥ // LiP_2,21.81 //
children.translated_text: or constantly — they are <s>Rudras</s>, without doubt. (LiP 2,21.81)
A non-<s>Rudra</s> should not touch <s>Rudra</s>; a non-<s>Rudra</s> should not worship <s>Rudra</s>;
a non-<s>Rudra</s> should not glorify <s>Rudra</s>; a non-<s>Rudra</s> cannot attain <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2,21.82)
Thus has been briefly stated the procedure of qualification and rite,
for the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, granting the fruits of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. (LiP 2,21.83)
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled 'The Rule of Initiation.'
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Having performed the bathing, sacrifice, and other rites of the sun,
one should then perform the <s>Śiva</s>-bathing, the ash-bathing, and the worship of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,22.1)
Taking clay with the sixth [mantra], with devotion placing the clay on the ground,

children.text: dvitīyena tathābhyukṣya tṛtīyena ca śodhayet // LiP_2,22.2 //
children.translated_text: sprinkling with the second [mantra], and purifying with the third. (LiP 2,22.2)
Dividing with the fourth, cleansing impurity with the first;

children.text: snātvā ṣaṣṭhena taccheṣāṃ mṛdaṃ hastagatāṃ punaḥ // LiP_2,22.3 //
children.translated_text: having bathed with the sixth [mantra], the remaining clay in the hand again — (LiP 2,22.3)

children.text: tridhā vibhajya sarvaṃ ca caturbhirmadhyamaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: dividing all threefold, the middle [portion] with four [mantras],
seven times with the sixth [mantra]; the left [side anointed] with the root [mantra].

children.text: daśavāraṃ ca ṣaṣṭhena diśo bandhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // LiP_2,22.4 //
children.translated_text: Ten times with the sixth [mantra] — this is declared as the binding of the directions. (LiP 2,22.4)
With the left [hand], the sacred site; with the right, anointing the body —
having bathed with all [mantras], remembering the sun, one should perform the ablution. (LiP 2,22.5)
With a horn, leaf-cups, a <s>palāśa</s> leaf,

children.text: saurai rebhiśca vividhaiḥ sarvāsiddhikaraiḥ śubhaiḥ // LiP_2,22.6 //
children.translated_text: and with various auspicious solar [mantras], the bestowers of all attainments — (LiP 2,22.6)
I shall now describe the <s>Sāruṇi</s> [mantras], the <s>Bāṣkala</s> and others, O one of good vows,
the essential limb-[mantras] among all the gods, essential in every respect. (LiP 2,22.7)

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ oṃbhuvaḥ oṃsvaḥ oṃ mahaḥ oṃ janaḥ oṃ tapaḥ oṃsatyam oṃ ṛtam oṃ brahmā /
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Bhūḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>Svaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>Mahaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>Janaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>Tapaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>Satyam</s>, Oṃ <s>Ṛtam</s>, Oṃ <s>Brahmā</s>.
This nine-syllabled mantra is proclaimed as the <s>Bāṣkala</s>.
Because 'it does not decay' in the worlds, it is called <s>Ṛtam</s> (Truth), the imperishable.
<s>Satyam</s> (Truth) is also said to be the imperishable — beginning with <s>praṇava</s> and ending with Oṃ. (LiP 2,22.8)

children.text: oṃ bhūrbhavaḥ suvaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi /
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ</s>, <s>Tat Savitur Vareṇyaṃ Bhargo Devasya Dhīmahi</s>,

children.text: oṃ namaḥ sūryāya khakholkāya namaḥ // LiP_2,22.9 //
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Namaḥ Sūryāya Khakholkāya Namaḥ</s>. (LiP 2,22.9)
This is proclaimed as the root-mantra of the great-souled sun-god.
With the nine-syllabled [mantra], [worship] the blazing-mouthed one; with the root-mantra, the sun-god. (LiP 2,22.10)
One should worship [him] — I shall describe the limb-mantras in proper sequence.

children.text: vedādibhiḥ prabhūtādyaṃ praṇavena ca madhyamam // LiP_2,22.11 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with the Vedic [syllables], beginning with the principal [mantra], and with <s>praṇava</s> in the middle: (LiP 2,22.11)

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ brahma hṛdayāya oṃ bhuvaḥ viṣṇuśirase oṃsvaḥ rudraśikhāyai oṃbhūrbhūvaḥ svaḥ jvālāmālinīśikhayai oṃ mahaḥ maheśvarāya kavacāya oñjanaḥ śivāya netrebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Bhūḥ Brahma</s> to the Heart,' 'Oṃ <s>Bhuvaḥ Viṣṇu</s> to the Head,' 'Oṃ <s>Svaḥ Rudra</s> to the Topknot,' 'Oṃ <s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ Jvālāmālinī</s> to the Flame-Topknot,' 'Oṃ <s>Mahaḥ Maheśvara</s> to the Armor,' 'Oṃ <s>Janaḥ Śiva</s> to the Eyes.'

children.text: oṃ tapaḥ tāpakāya astrāya phaṭ mantrāṇi kathitānyevaṃ saurāṇi vividhāni ca /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Tapaḥ</s> to the Scorcher, to the Weapon, <s>Phaṭ</s>.' Thus are described the various solar mantras.
With these vessels — horn and the like — one should perform self-ablution. (LiP 2,22.12)

children.text: tāmrakuṃbhena vā vipraḥ kṣatriyo vaiśya eva ca /
children.translated_text: A brahmin [should use] a copper vessel, and likewise a <s>kṣatriya</s> and a <s>vaiśya</s>,

children.text: sakusena sapuṣpeṇa mantraiḥ sarvai samāhitaḥ // LiP_2,22.13 //
children.translated_text: with <s>kuśa</s> grass and flowers, with all the mantras, concentrating the mind. (LiP 2,22.13)
Wearing red cloth, one should perform the <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) rite according to the rule.

children.text: sūryaścoti divā rātrau cāgniśceti dvijottamaḥ // LiP_2,22.14 //
children.translated_text: 'The Sun [presides]' — by day; 'Fire [presides]' — at night, O best of twice-born. (LiP 2,22.14)
'May the Waters purify' — at midday; this is called the mantra-<s>ācamana</s>.
Having performed purification with the sixth [mantra], one should recite the first, supreme [mantra]. (LiP 2,22.15)
Ending with <s>vauṣaṭ</s>, also the root [mantra], the supreme nine-syllabled one.
On the hand-fingers — one should place [the mantras] on the thumb, middle, and ring fingers. (LiP 2,22.16)
On the palm, the index finger and thumb — one should assign [the mantras to] the fist-parts.
Having made the body nine-syllabled [i.e., sanctified], purified by the limb-[mantras] too, (LiP 2,22.17)
meditating 'I am the Sun,' with these mantras in proper order,
with waters held in the left hand, mixed with sandalwood and mustard, (LiP 2,22.18)
sprinkling with a bunch of <s>kuśa</s> grass, placed eightfold with tips and roots —

children.text: āpo hiṣṭhādibhiścaiva śeṣamāghrādha vai jalam // LiP_2,22.19 //
children.translated_text: and with the '<s>Āpo hiṣṭhā</s>' [hymn] and others; the remaining water one should smell. (LiP 2,22.19)
Through the left nostril, one should invoke <s>Śiva</s> in the body;
taking the <s>arghya</s> (offering), [invoking <s>Śiva</s>] within the body, through the right nostril, (LiP 2,22.20)
with a dark-colored [visualization], one should meditate on [<s>Śiva</s>] outside [the body], established in the [liṅga-]stone.
One should offer libations (<s>tarpana</s>) to all the gods, and especially to the sages, (LiP 2,22.21)
to the spirits (<s>bhūtas</s>) and to the ancestors; and one should present the <s>arghya</s> according to the rule.

children.text: vyāpiniṃ ca parāṃ jyotsnāṃ saṃdhyāṃ samyagupāsayet // LiP_2,22.22 //
children.translated_text: One should properly worship the all-pervading supreme twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>). (LiP 2,22.22)
At morning, midday, and evening, one should offer the <s>arghya</s>.
With water of red sandalwood, on the ground, a <s>maṇḍala</s> the size of a hand-span, (LiP 2,22.23)
well-rounded, one should fashion and pray, O best of twice-born.
Facing east, a copper vessel, fragrant, filled to the measure of a <s>prastha</s>, (LiP 2,22.24)
one should fill with fragrant water and red sandalwood,
with red flowers, sesame seeds, and accompanied by <s>kuśa</s> grass and unbroken rice, (LiP 2,22.25)
with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, <s>apāmārga</s>, cow's [products], and pure ghee,
filling [the vessel] with the root-mantra, the nine-syllabled one,

children.text: jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gatvā deva devaṃ namasya ca // LiP_2,22.26 //
children.translated_text: going to the ground on one's knees, bowing to the God of Gods. (LiP 2,22.26)
Having placed that vessel on the head, one should offer the <s>arghya</s> with the root [mantra].
The fruit that is proclaimed from performing ten thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifices — (LiP 2,22.27)
that fruit one obtains by offering the solar <s>arghya</s>, approved by all.
Having offered the <s>arghya</s>, one should worship the God of Gods, the three-eyed one, with devotion. (LiP 2,22.28)
Alternatively, having worshipped the sun-god, one should perform the fire-bathing.
As before, the <s>Śiva</s>-bathing, differentiated by mantras alone. (LiP 2,22.29)

children.text: dantadhāvanapūrvaṃ ca snānaṃ sauraṃ ca śāṅkaram /
children.translated_text: Beginning with tooth-cleaning, the solar bathing, and [then] the <s>Śiva</s> [bathing];

children.text: vighneśaṃ varuṇaṃ caiva guruṃ tīrthaṃ samarcayet // LiP_2,22.30 //
children.translated_text: one should worship <s>Vighneśa</s> (Gaṇeśa), <s>Varuṇa</s>, the teacher, and the sacred site. (LiP 2,22.30)

children.text: baddhvā padmāsanaṃ tīrthe tathā tīrthaṃ samarcayet /
children.translated_text: Assuming the lotus posture at the sacred site, one should worship the sacred site.

children.text: tīrthaṃ saṃgṛhya vidhinā pūjāsthānaṃ praviśya ca // LiP_2,22.31 //
children.translated_text: Having collected the sacred water according to the rule, entering the place of worship, (LiP 2,22.31)
by the path [sanctified with] the <s>arghya</s>-purification, and stepping on the foot-rest —
one should perform the hand-placement and the body-placement as before.

children.text: tīrthaṃ saṃgṛhya vidhinā pūjāsthānaṃ pravisya ca // LiP_2,22.32 //
children.translated_text: Having collected the sacred water according to the rule, entering the place of worship, (LiP 2,22.32)
the preparation of the <s>arghya</s> has been briefly described.

children.text: baddhvā padmāsanaṃ yogī prāṇāyāmaṃ samabhyaset // LiP_2,22.33 //
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s>, having assumed the lotus posture, should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control). (LiP 2,22.33)
Gathering red flowers, one should meditate on lotuses and the like.

children.text: ātmano dakṣiṇe sthāpya jalabhāṇḍaṃ ca vāmataḥ // LiP_2,22.34 //
children.translated_text: Placing [them] to one's right, and a water-vessel to the left — (LiP 2,22.34)
copper vessels [are used] for solar [worship], for the attainment of all desires.

children.text: ārghyapātraṃ samādāya prakṣālya ca yathāvidhi // LiP_2,22.35 //
children.translated_text: Taking the <s>arghya</s>-vessel, having washed it according to the rule, (LiP 2,22.35)
together with the previously described water, and in the water-vessel likewise,
with <s>astra</s>-water and the <s>arghya</s> equipped with <s>arghya</s>-substances, (LiP 2,22.36)
having consecrated [it] with <s>Saṃhitā</s> mantras, and worshipped with the first [mantra],
covering with the fourth [mantra], one should place it around oneself. (LiP 2,22.37)
The foot-water (<s>pādya</s>), the sipping-water (<s>ācamanīya</s>), accompanied by fragrance and flowers,
in vessels purified with water, one should place [them] separately as before.
And having placed the <s>Saṃhitā</s> [mantras], covering with the armor [mantra] — (LiP 2,22.38)
Having sprinkled the ritual materials with the <s>arghya</s> (offering) water, especially,

children.text: ādityaṃ ca japed devaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtam // LiP_2,22.39 //
children.translated_text: one should recite [the mantra of] the god <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), saluted by all gods: (LiP 2.22.39)

children.text: ādityo vai teja ūrjo balaṃ yaśo vivirdhati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Āditya</s> indeed is radiance, vigor, strength, and glory — he makes [them] increase.'
Having saluted with this and the like, one should prepare the seat of the Lord. (LiP 2.22.40)
Abundant, pure, excellent, desirable, supremely blissful —
in the southeast and other corners, and in the center, one should mentally place the inner [throne]. (LiP 2.22.41)
One should ritually place the limb[-parts], and also the seed and the sprout,
the stalk with its hollow, endowed with filaments and thorns, (LiP 2.22.42)

children.text: dalaṃ dalāgraṃ suśvetaṃ hemābhaṃ raktameva ca /
children.translated_text: the petal and petal-tip — bright white, golden, and also red,
furnished with pericarp and filaments, surrounded by the <s>Śaktis</s> beginning with <s>Dīptā</s>. (LiP 2.22.43)
<s>Dīptā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Vibhūti</s>, <s>Vimalā</s> — in order;
<s>Aghorā</s> and <s>Vikṛtā</s> as well — [these are] the eight <s>Śaktis</s> beginning with <s>Dīptā</s>. (LiP 2.22.44)
All with faces radiant like the sun, with palms joined in reverence, auspicious;
or with lotuses in their hands, adorned with all ornaments. (LiP 2.22.45)
In the center, one should install the boon-granting Goddess, facing all directions;
then one should invoke the Goddess and <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun), the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2.22.46)
With the nine-syllable mantra declared by <s>Bāṣkala</s> — [invoke] <s>Bhāskara</s>;
in the invocation and establishment of presence, this very [mantra] is employed. (LiP 2.22.47)
And the <s>mudrā</s> called <s>padmamudrā</s> (lotus-gesture) [is used] for the great-souled <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: mūle nārghyaṃ tato dadyātpādyamācamanaṃ pṛthak // LiP_2,22.48 //
children.translated_text: At the base, one should then offer <s>arghya</s>, <s>pādya</s> (foot-water), and <s>ācamana</s> (mouth-rinsing water) separately. (LiP 2.22.48)
With the offering of <s>arghya</s> again, according to the <s>Bāṣkala</s> rite properly,
red lotuses and flowers, and red sandalwood, (LiP 2.22.49)
lamp, incense, and food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>), mouth-freshener and the like,
betel, wick-lamp, and the rest — [all] are performed with the <s>Bāṣkala</s> [mantra]. (LiP 2.22.50)
In the southeast, northeast, southwest, and the region of the northwest,

children.text: pūrvasyāṃ paścime caiva paṭprakāraṃ vidhīyate // LiP_2,22.51 //
children.translated_text: in the east and in the west — six types of [worship] are performed. (LiP 2.22.51)
Having worshipped up to the eye[-mantra] according to the rite, beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> and ending with <s>Namaḥ</s>,
having placed [the deity] in the pericarp [of the lotus], one should perform meditation on [his] form. (LiP 2.22.52)
All [forms] have the radiance of lightning; the peaceful [form] and the <s>Raudra</s> (fierce) weapon-form are declared —
with a face terrible with fangs — the eight-formed, fearsome [aspect]. (LiP 2.22.53)
The right hand [in] boon-granting [gesture], the left adorned with a lotus;
all [forms] endowed with all ornaments, with red garlands and unguents, (LiP 2.22.54)
all wearing red garments — the forms of his are established [thus].
The great god with [his] <s>maṇḍala</s> — with a body red like vermilion, (LiP 2.22.55)
lotus in hand, nectar-faced, two-armed, two-eyed — the Lord,
adorned with red ornaments, with red garlands and unguents. (LiP 2.22.56)
One should meditate on <s>Bhāskara</s>, the Lord of the Universe, bearing this form.

children.text: padmabāhye śubhaṃ cātra maṇḍaleṣu samantataḥ // LiP_2,22.57 //
children.translated_text: Outside the lotus, here in the <s>maṇḍalas</s> all around — [place] the auspicious [deities]: (LiP 2.22.57)
the Moon (<s>Soma</s>), Mars (<s>Aṅgāraka</s>), and Mercury (<s>Budha</s>) — the best among the intelligent;

children.text: bṛhaspatiṃ mahābuddhiṃ rudraputraṃ ca bhārgavam // LiP_2,22.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) of great wisdom, the son of <s>Rudra</s> (i.e. <s>Śanaiścara</s>), and <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus); (LiP 2.22.58)

children.text: śanaiścaraṃ tathā rāhuṃ ketuṃ dhūmraṃ prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), and also <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s> — [the latter] declared as smoky-hued.
All are two-eyed and two-armed; <s>Rāhu</s> has only an upper body. (LiP 2.22.59)
With mouth agape, making <s>añjali</s> (salutation gesture), with furrowed brows and curved gaze;
<s>Śanaiścara</s> is fang-faced, holding boon-granting and fear-dispelling hands. (LiP 2.22.60)
Each with their own qualities and their own names, beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> and ending with <s>Namaḥ</s>,
should be worshipped with effort — for the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth. (LiP 2.22.61)
The seven-times-seven classes [of attendants] one should also worship outside [the image of] the God:
sages, divine <s>Gandharvas</s>, hosts of serpents and <s>Apsarases</s>, (LiP 2.22.62)
village-chiefs, <s>Yātudhānas</s> (sorcerers), and <s>Yakṣas</s> — primarily.
One should worship first the seven horses [of the Sun], embodying the seven meters, of the Lord. (LiP 2.22.63)
And the host of <s>Vālakhilya</s> [sages] — [and perform] the removal of old offerings of the Lord.
One should worship the seat of <s>Sūrya</s> and also worship the deity. (LiP 2.22.64)

children.text: arghyaṃ ca dāpayetteṣāṃ pṛthageva vidhā nataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Arghya</s> should be offered to them separately, according to the rite;

children.text: āvāhane ca pūjānte teṣāmudvāsane tathā // LiP_2,22.65 //
children.translated_text: in the invocation, at the end of worship, and likewise in the dismissal. (LiP 2.22.65)

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā /
children.translated_text: A thousand, or half of that, or one hundred and eight —

children.text: bāṣkalaṃ ca japedagre dhaśāṃśena ca yojayet // LiP_2,22.66 //
children.translated_text: one should recite the <s>Bāṣkala</s> [mantra] first, and join [it] with a tenth [as oblation]. (LiP 2.22.66)

children.text: kuṇḍaṃ ca paścime kuryādvartulaṃ caiva mekhalam /
children.translated_text: The fire-pit should be made on the west side, circular, with a rim,
of four <s>aṅgula</s> measure in both height and width; (LiP 2.22.67)
of one <s>hasta</s> (cubit) measure — for regular and occasional [rites].
Having made a navel in the fire-pit in the shape of an <s>aśvattha</s> (pipal) leaf, of ten <s>aṅgulas</s>, (LiP 2.22.68)
half that in the front — said to resemble an elephant's lip;
the neck of one <s>aṅgula</s>, and the remainder double in width. (LiP 2.22.69)
According to that measure of the fire-pit, leaving [space], one should make the rim.

children.text: yatnena sādhayitvaiva paścādvomaṃ ca kārayet // LiP_2,22.70 //
children.translated_text: Having carefully prepared [it], afterwards one should make the canopy. (LiP 2.22.70)
With a sixth, one should dig a trench; one should sprinkle again with water.
One should prepare a seat in the center, with the first [mantra], attentively. (LiP 2.22.71)
Then one should place the <s>Śakti</s> <s>Prabhāvatī</s> with the primary [mantra] itself;
having worshipped with the <s>Bāṣkala</s> [mantra], with fragrance, flowers, and the rest in sequence. (LiP 2.22.72)
With the <s>Bāṣkala</s> mantra itself, one should sacrifice separately for each rite;
with the root-mantra, according to the rite, afterwards the full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>) should be [offered]. (LiP 2.22.73)
Thus, in sequence by this procedure, the <s>Sūrya</s>-fire is produced.

children.text: pūrvoktena vidhānena prāguktaṃ kamalaṃ nyaset // LiP_2,22.74 //
children.translated_text: By the previously stated procedure, one should place the lotus as described before. (LiP 2.22.74)
Having worshipped above the face, the Lord <s>Bhāskara</s> as before,
ten oblations should be given with the <s>Bāṣkala</s> [mantra], O great sage. (LiP 2.22.75)

children.text: aṅgānāṃ ca tathaikaikaṃ saṃhitābhiḥ pṛthak punaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for each limb [mantra], one each, with the <s>Saṃhitā</s> texts separately;
from <s>Jayādi</s> through <s>Sviṣṭa</s> — and the casting of fuel-sticks as well. (LiP 2.22.76)
This is common to all paths, according to the traditional sequence.
Having offered to the God of Gods, <s>Bhāskara</s>, the infinite-souled, (LiP 2.22.77)
all worship, fire-offering, and the rest, having offered <s>arghya</s> and circumambulation,

children.text: aṅgaiḥ saṃpūjya saṃkṣipya hṛdyudvāsya namasya ca // LiP_2,22.78 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped with the limb[-mantras], having concluded, having dismissed in the heart and saluted — (LiP 2.22.78)
one should then perform <s>Śiva</s>-worship for the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.

children.text: evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ yajanaṃ bhāskarasya ca /
children.translated_text: Thus has been declared in brief the worship of <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun);
endowed with all sovereignty and of incomparable brilliance is that [worshipper]. (LiP 2.22.79)
One who worships even once the God, the God of Gods, the Guru of the World,

children.text: bhāskaraṃ paramātmānaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // LiP_2,22.80 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s>, the Supreme Self — he attains the supreme destination. (LiP 2.22.80)
Freed from all sins, devoid of all sins,
endowed with all sovereignty and of incomparable brilliance is he. (LiP 2.22.81)
Surrounded by sons, grandsons, friends, and kinsmen on all sides,

children.text: bhuktvaiva vipulān bhogānihaiva dhana dhānyavān // LiP_2,22.82 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed abundant pleasures right here, possessing wealth and grain, (LiP 2.22.82)
endowed with vehicles and conveyances, and with various ornaments —

children.text: kālaṃ gatopi sūryeṇa modate kālamakṣayam // LiP_2,22.83 //
children.translated_text: even after passing time [i.e. dying], he rejoices with <s>Sūrya</s> for an imperishable time. (LiP 2.22.83)
Then, returning here again, he becomes a righteous king;
or he is born here as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, endowed with the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>. (LiP 2.22.84)
Again, by the force of previous impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), righteous, one who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s>,
worshipping <s>Sūrya</s> once more — he attains union with <s>Sūrya</s>. (LiP 2.22.85)
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> (Nandikeśvara) said:
Now I shall tell you the unsurpassed worship of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: trisaṃdhyam arcayed īśam agnikāryaṃ ca śaktitaḥ // LiP_2,23.1 //
children.translated_text: One should worship the Lord at the three <s>sandhyās</s> (junctions of the day), and perform the fire-rite according to ability. (LiP 2.23.1)

children.text: śivasnānaṃ purā kṛtvā tattvaśuddhiṃ ca pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: Having first performed the <s>Śiva</s>-bath and the purification of principles (<s>tattvaśuddhi</s>) as before,
with flowers in hand, one should then enter the place of worship, attentively. (LiP 2.23.2)
Having performed three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls), and the burning and flooding [purifications],
with hands perfumed with fragrance and the like, one should perform the great <s>mudrā</s>. (LiP 2.23.3)
Having fashioned the body through knowledge, from the fire of <s>Brahman</s> itself, with effort —
a body born of the unmanifest, intellect, ego, and subtle elements, (LiP 2.23.4)
purified with the nectar of <s>Śiva</s>, in accordance with <s>Śiva</s>'s [nature] —

children.text: adhoniṣṭhyā vitastyāṃ tu nābhyāmupari tiṣṭhati // LiP_2,23.5 //
children.translated_text: it is situated below, at a span from the navel, upward. (LiP 2.23.5)
One should know that as the heart — the great abode of the universe.
In the pericarp of the heart-lotus — the God <s>Sadāśiva</s> himself, (LiP 2.23.6)
five-faced, ten-armed, adorned with all ornaments,
three-eyed on each face, with the crescent moon as his crest — (LiP 2.23.7)
seated in <s>baddhapadmāsana</s> (bound lotus posture), resembling pure crystal.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ vaktraṃ sitaṃ dhyāyetpūrvaṃ kuṅkumasannibham // LiP_2,23.8 //
children.translated_text: The upper face one should meditate as white; the eastern, like saffron; (LiP 2.23.8)
the southern face, blue-hued; the northern, intensely red;
the western face of the Supreme One — divine, white as cow's milk. (LiP 2.23.9)

children.text: śūlaṃ paraśukhaṅgaṃ ca vajraṃ śaktiṃ ca dakṣiṇe /
children.translated_text: Trident, axe, sword, thunderbolt, and spear in the right [hands];

children.text: vāme pāśāṅkuśaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ nāgaṃ nārācamuttamam // LiP_2,23.10 //
children.translated_text: in the left — noose, goad, bell, serpent, and the excellent arrow (<s>nārāca</s>). (LiP 2.23.10)
Or [showing] boon-granting and fear-dispelling hands; the rest as before.
<s>Śiva</s>, adorned with all ornaments, wearing variegated garments, (LiP 2.23.11)
the God whose body is [comprised of] the <s>Brahmāṅgas</s> (Brahman-limbs), the highest of all gods —
one should worship with complete devotion the Lord of <s>Brahman</s> with the <s>Brahmāṅga</s> [mantras]. (LiP 2.23.12)

children.text: uktāni pañca brahmāṇi śivāṅgāni śṛṇuṣva me /
children.translated_text: The five <s>Brahmans</s> (Brahma-mantras) have been stated; hear from me the limbs of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: śaktibhūtāni ca tathā hṛdayādīni suvrata // LiP_2,23.13 //
children.translated_text: and likewise those that are the <s>Śaktis</s> — the heart[-mantra] and the rest, O one of excellent vows: (LiP 2.23.13)

children.text: oṃ īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāṃ hṛdayāya śaktibījāya namaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ! <s>Īśāna</s>, [lord] of all knowledge — to the heart, to the seed of <s>Śakti</s>, salutations!'
'Oṃ! <s>Īśvara</s>, [lord] of all beings — to the immortal one, to the head, salutations!' (LiP 2.23.14)
'Oṃ! Lord of <s>Brahman</s>, to <s>Kālāgni</s>-<s>Rupa</s> (the form of the fire of time), to the topknot, salutations!'

children.text: oṃ brahmaṇodhipataye kālacaṇḍamārutāya kavacāya namaḥ // LiP_2,23.15 //
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ! Lord of <s>Brahman</s>, to <s>Kālacaṇḍamāruta</s> (the fierce wind of time), to the armor, salutations!' (LiP 2.23.15)

children.text: oṃ brahmaṇe bṛṃhaṇāya jñānamūrtaye netrāya namaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ! To <s>Brahman</s>, to the expander, to the embodiment of knowledge, to the eye, salutations!'

children.text: oṃ śivāya sadāśivāya pāśupatāsrāya apratihatāya phaṭphaṭ // LiP_2,23.16 //
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ! To <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, to the <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon — irresistible! <s>Phaṭ</s>! <s>Phaṭ</s>!' (LiP 2.23.16)

children.text: oṃ sadyojātāya bhavebhavenāti bhave bhavasya māṃ bhavodbhavāya śivamūrtaye namaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ! To <s>Sadyojāta</s> — to <s>Bhava</s>, again and again to <s>Bhava</s>, of <s>Bhava</s>, to the one born of <s>Bhava</s>, to the form of <s>Śiva</s>, salutations!'

children.text: oṃ haṃsaśikhāya vidyādehāya ātmasvarūpāya parāparāya śivāya śivatamāya namaḥ // LiP_2,23.17 //
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ! To the swan-crested one, to the body of knowledge, to the form of the Self, to the higher and the lower, to <s>Śiva</s>, to the most auspicious, salutations!' (LiP 2.23.17)

children.text: kathitāni śivāṅgāni mūrtividyā ca tasya vai /
children.translated_text: The limbs of <s>Śiva</s> have been stated, and his form-knowledge (<s>mūrtiVidyā</s>) as well;
together with the <s>Brahmāṅga</s>-form and the limb-knowledge — in the ordinance of <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2.23.18)
And I shall declare the <s>Saura</s> (solar) [mantras], beginning with the <s>Bāṣkala</s>, O one of excellent vows —
the limb[-mantras] which are the essence of all <s>Vedas</s>, O one of excellent vows: (LiP 2.23.19)

children.text: oṃbhūḥ oṃbhuvaḥ oṃ svaḥ oṃmahaḥ oñjanaḥ ontapaḥ oṃsatyam oṃṛtam oṃbrahmānavākṣaramayaṃ mantraṃ bāṣkalaṃ parikīrtitam /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Bhūḥ</s>! Oṃ <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! Oṃ <s>Svaḥ</s>! Oṃ <s>Mahaḥ</s>! Oṃ <s>Janaḥ</s>! Oṃ <s>Tapaḥ</s>! Oṃ <s>Satyam</s>! Oṃ <s>Ṛtam</s>!' — This imperishable mantra of <s>Brahman</s> is celebrated as the <s>Bāṣkala</s>.
It does not perish in this world — therefore it is called 'imperishable' (<s>akṣara</s>);

children.text: satyam akṣaram ity uktaṃ praṇavādinamo ḥntakam // LiP_2,23.20 //
children.translated_text: 'The truth is the imperishable' — so it is said, beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> and ending with <s>Namaḥ</s>. (LiP 2.23.20)

children.text: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Bhūr</s> <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> <s>Svaḥ</s>! <s>Tat Savitur Vareṇyam</s>, <s>Bhargo Devasya Dhīmahi</s>,
<s>Dhiyo Yo Naḥ Pracodayāt</s>!'
'Salutations to <s>Sūrya</s>, to <s>Khakholkā</s> (sky-meteor), salutations!' (LiP 2.23.21)
This is declared the root-mantra of the great-souled <s>Bhāskara</s>.
With the nine-syllable [mantra], beginning with <s>Dīptā</s>, and the root-mantra — [one should worship] <s>Bhāskara</s>. (LiP 2.23.22)
One should worship — I shall declare the limb-mantras in brief.

children.text: vedādibhiḥ prabhūtādyaṃ praṇavena tu madhyamam // LiP_2,23.23 //
children.translated_text: With the <s>Veda</s>-[mantras] and the rest, the primary [mantra] first, <s>Praṇava</s> in the middle. (LiP 2.23.23)

children.text:
oṃbhūḥ brahmaṇe hṛdayāya namaḥ /
oṃbhuvaḥ viṣṇave śirase namaḥ /
oṃsvaḥ rudrāya śikhāyai namaḥ oṃbhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ jvālāmāninyai devāya namaḥ oṃmahaḥ maheśvarāya kavacāya namaḥ /

children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ Janaḥ</s> — to <s>Śiva</s>, salutation to the Eyes.
<s>Oṃ Tapaḥ</s> — to <s>Tāpana</s> [the Scorcher], salutation to the Weapon.
Thus, incidentally, here have been described the solar [mantras]

children.text: śaivāni ca samāsena nyāsayogena suvrata // LiP_2,23.24 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Śaiva</s> [mantras] in summary, along with the method of installation (<s>nyāsa</s>), O one of good vows. (LiP 2,23.24)

<s>Oṃ Bhūḥ</s> — to <s>Brahmā</s>, salutation to the Heart. <s>Oṃ Bhuvaḥ</s> — to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, salutation to the Head. <s>Oṃ Svaḥ</s> — to <s>Rudra</s>, salutation to the Top-knot. <s>Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ</s> — to <s>Jvālāmāninī Devā</s>, salutation. <s>Oṃ Mahaḥ</s> — to <s>Maheśvara</s>, salutation to the Armor.
Thus one should worship the god, who is constituted of mantras, in the lotus of the heart;

children.text: nābhau homaṃ tu kartavyaṃ janayitvā yathākramam // LiP_2,23.25 //
children.translated_text: the fire-offering (<s>homa</s>) should be performed at the navel, having kindled [the fire] in due order. (LiP 2,23.25)
With the mind, all rites [should be performed] in the fire of <s>Śiva</s>, for the god, the Lord,
the form of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, born from the limbs of the five <s>Brahmā</s>-mantras. (LiP 2,23.26)
Seated on a red lotus-seat, having made [him] complete (<s>sakalīkṛtya</s>) with effort,
with the root-mantra, the form-mantra, and the <s>Brahmāṅga</s>-[mantras], O one of good vows, (LiP 2,23.27)
having offered oblations of sticks and ghee, one should mentally [visualize]
from the moon-sphere, a full stream [of nectar] arising from the moon-station. (LiP 2,23.28)
By the method of the full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>), according to <s>Śiva</s>'s teaching for the knowers,

children.text: śivaṃ vaktragataṃ dhyāyettejomātraṃ ca śāṅkaram // LiP_2,23.29 //
children.translated_text: one should meditate on <s>Śiva</s> present in the face, as pure radiance of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2,23.29)
On the forehead one should [meditate on] the God of Gods, or between the eyebrows one should again contemplate;

children.text: yacca hṛtkamale sarvaṃ samāpya vidhivistaram // LiP_2,23.30 //
children.translated_text: and having concluded everything in the heart-lotus, with the full elaborate procedure, (LiP 2,23.30)
one should contemplate [Him] in the form of a pure lamp-flame — the Destroyer of worldly existence.

children.text: liṅge ca pūjayeddevaṃ sthaṇḍile vā sadāśivam // LiP_2,23.31 //
children.translated_text: One should worship the God in the <s>liṅga</s>, or <s>Sadāśiva</s> on a [consecrated] platform. (LiP 2,23.31)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, <s>Uttarabhāga</s>, [this is] the twenty-third chapter.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
I shall explain in summary the method of worship,
according to the path prescribed in the <s>Śivaśāstra</s>, as told by <s>Śiva</s> formerly. (LiP 2,24.1)

children.text: athobhau candanacarcitau hastau vauṣaḍantenādyañjaliṃ kṛtvā mūrtividyāśivādīni japtvā aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhikānta īśānādyaṃ kaniṣṭhikādimadhyamāntaṃ hṛdayāditṛtīyāntaṃ turīyamaṅguṣṭhenānāmikayā pañcamaṃ taladvayena ṣaṣṭhaṃ tarjanyaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nārācastraprayogeṇa punarapi mūlaṃ japtvā turīyenāvaguṇṭhya śivahastamityucyate // LiP_2,24.2 //
children.translated_text: Then, having anointed both hands with sandal paste, making the first <s>añjali</s> [gesture] ending with <s>vauṣaṭ</s>, having recited the <s>mūrti</s>-<s>vidyā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, etc., [placing them] from the thumb to the little finger, <s>Īśāna</s> etc. from the little finger to the middle finger, the <s>hṛdaya</s> [heart-mantra] etc. to the third, the fourth with the thumb and ring finger, the fifth with both palms, the sixth with the index finger and thumb using the <s>nārāc-astra</s> gesture, then again reciting the root[-mantra], veiling with the fourth [mantra] — this is called the <s>Śiva-hand</s>. (LiP 2,24.2)
The worship of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed with that hand. (LiP 2,24.3)
Having established oneself as situated in the <s>tattvas</s>, one should perform <s>tattva</s>-purification as before. (LiP 2,24.4)

children.text: kṣmāmbhognivāyuvyomāntaṃ pañcacatuḥśuddhakoṭyante dhārāsahitena vyavasthāpya tattśuddhiṃ pūrvaṃ kuryāt // LiP_2,24.5 //
children.translated_text: Ending with earth, water, fire, air, and space — having established [the sequence] ending with the tip of the four-five purifications together with the stream [of nectar], one should perform the <s>tattva</s>-purification first. (LiP 2,24.5)

children.text: tattvaśuddhiḥ ṣaṣṭhena sadyena tṛtīyena phaḍantāddharāśuddhiḥ // LiP_2,24.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tattva</s>-purification: with the sixth [mantra] and <s>Sadya</s> [<s>Sadyojāta</s>], by the third ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — earth-purification. (LiP 2,24.6)

children.text: ṣaṣṭhasahitena sadyena tṛtīyena phaḍantena vāritattvaśuddhiḥ // LiP_2,24.7 //
children.translated_text: With the sixth combined with <s>Sadya</s>, by the third ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — water-<s>tattva</s>-purification. (LiP 2,24.7)
With the fire-[mantra]-third ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — fire-purification. (LiP 2,24.8)
With the wind-[mantra]-fourth combined with the sixth ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — wind-purification. (LiP 2,24.9)
With the sixth combined with <s>Sadya</s>, by the third ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — space-purification. (LiP 2,24.10)

children.text: upasaṃhṛtyaivaṃ sadyaṣaṣṭhena tṛtīyena mūlena phaḍantena tāḍanaṃ tṛtīyena saṃpuṭīkṛtyagrahaṇaṃ mūlameva yonibījena saṃpuṭīkṛtvā bandhanaṃ bandhaḥ // LiP_2,24.11 //
children.translated_text: Having thus withdrawn [the elements], with <s>Sadya</s>-sixth-third-root ending with <s>phaṭ</s> — striking; with the third, enclosing — seizing; enclosing the root itself with the <s>yoni-bīja</s> — binding. This is the binding [procedure]. (LiP 2,24.11)

children.text: evaṃ kṣāntātītādinivṛttiparyantaṃ pūrvavatkṛtvā praṇavena tattvatrayakamanudhyāya ātmānaṃ dīpaśikhākāraṃ puryaṣṭakasahitaṃ trayātītaṃ śaktikṣobheṇāmṛtadhārāṃ suṣumṇāyāṃ dhyātvā // LiP_2,24.12 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having performed [the sequence] from <s>kṣānta</s> [tranquility-transcending] etc. to <s>nivṛtti</s> [cessation] as before, meditating through <s>praṇava</s> on the triad of <s>tattvas</s>, [visualizing] oneself in the form of a lamp-flame together with the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> [subtle body of eight], transcending the three, meditating in the <s>suṣumnā</s> on the stream of nectar [produced] by the agitation of <s>Śakti</s> — (LiP 2,24.12)

children.text: śāntyatītādinivṛttiparyantānāṃ cāntarnādabindvakārokāramakārāntaṃ śivaṃ sadāśivaṃ rudraviṣṇubrahmāntaṃ sṛṣṭimeṇāmṛtīkaraṇaṃ brahmanyāsaṃ kṛtvā pañcavaktreṣu pañcadaśanayanaṃ vinyasya mūlena pādādikeśāntaṃ mahāmudrāmapi baddhvā śivohamiti dhyātvā śaktyādīni vinyasyahṛdi śaktyābījāṅkurānantarātsasuṣirasūtrakaṇṭakapatrakesaradharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasūryasomāgnivāmājyeṣṭhāraudrīkālīkalavikaraṇībalavikaraṇībala prathamanīsarvabhūtadamanīḥ kesareṣu karṇikāyāṃ manonmanīmapi dhyātvā // LiP_2,24.13 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Śāntyatīta</s> etc. to <s>Nivṛtti</s>, within [these] — <s>nāda</s>, <s>bindu</s>, <s>akāra</s>, <s>ukāra</s>, <s>makāra</s> ending — <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s>-<s>Brahmā</s> ending — having performed the creation-sequence nectar-making and <s>Brahma-nyāsa</s>, placing the fifteen eyes on the five faces, from feet to hair with the root-mantra, having also bound the <s>mahāmudrā</s>, meditating 'I am <s>Śiva</s>,' placing the <s>Śaktis</s> etc., in the heart — from the seed-sprout after the <s>Śakti-bīja</s>: the hollow, the thread, the thorn, the leaf, the filaments — <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, <s>vairāgya</s>, <s>aiśvarya</s>, <s>sūrya</s>, <s>soma</s>, <s>agni</s> — <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Kalavikaraṇī</s>, <s>Balavikaraṇī</s>, <s>Balaprathamānī</s>, <s>Sarvabhūtadamanī</s> on the filaments, and <s>Manonmanī</s> on the pericarp — having thus meditated — (LiP 2,24.13)

children.text: āsanaṃ parikalpyaivaṃ sarvopacārasahitaṃ bahiryogopacāreṇāntaḥkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā nābhau vahnikuṇḍe pūrvavadāsanaṃ parikalpya sadāśivaṃ dhyātvā binduto 'mṛtadhārāṃ śivamaṇḍale nipatitāṃ dhyātvā lalāṭe maheśvaraṃ dīpaśikhākāraṃ dhyātvā ātmaśuddhiritthaṃ prāṇāpānau saṃyamya suṣumṇayā vāyuṃ vyavasthāpya ṣaṣṭhena tālumudrāṃ kṛtvā digbandhaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṣṭhena sthānaśuddhirvastrādi pūtāntararghyapātrādiṣu praṇavena tattvatrayaṃ vinyasya tadupari bunduṃ dhyātvā vipūrya dravyāṇi ca vidhāya amṛtaplāvanaṃ kṛtvā pādyapātrādiṣu teṣāmarghyavadāsanaṃ parikalpya saṃhitayābhimantryādyenābhyarcya dvitīyenāmṛtīkṛtvā tṛtīyena viśodhyacaturthenāvaguṇṭhya pañcamonāvalokyaṣaṣṭhena rakṣāṃvidhāya caturthena kuśapuñjenārghyāṃbhasābhyukṣya ātmānamapi dravyāṇi punarghyāṃbhasābyukṣya sapuṣpeṇa sarvadravyāṇi pṛthakpṛthak śodhayet // LiP_2,24.14 //
children.translated_text: having thus prepared the seat with all accessories, performing the inner process by the method of outer worship-accessories, in the fire-pit at the navel having prepared the seat as before, meditating on <s>Sadāśiva</s>, meditating on the stream of nectar from the <s>bindu</s> fallen into the <s>Śiva-maṇḍala</s>, on the forehead meditating on <s>Maheśvara</s> in lamp-flame form — thus is self-purification. Then restraining <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, establishing the breath through the <s>suṣumnā</s>, performing the palate-<s>mudrā</s> with the sixth [mantra], performing directional sealing, purification of the place with the sixth [mantra], filling the vessels for <s>arghya</s> etc. with water that has been purified with cloth etc., placing the triad of <s>tattvas</s> with <s>praṇava</s>, meditating on the <s>bindu</s> above that, filling and arranging the substances, performing the flood of nectar, in the <s>pādya</s>-vessel etc. preparing the seat as with <s>arghya</s>, consecrating with the <s>saṃhitā</s>, worshipping with the first [mantra], nectarizing with the second, purifying with the third, veiling with the fourth, viewing with the fifth, performing protection with the sixth, sprinkling with <s>arghya</s>-water using <s>kuśa</s>-grass with the fourth, sprinkling oneself too and the substances again with <s>arghya</s>-water — one should purify all substances separately with flowers. (LiP 2,24.14)
With <s>Sadya</s> [<s>Sadyojāta</s>] — sandal-paste; with <s>Vāma</s> [<s>Vāmadeva</s>] — cloth;
with <s>Aghora</s> — ornaments; with <s>Puruṣa</s> [<s>Tatpuruṣa</s>] — food-offering;
with <s>Īśāna</s> — flowers. Then one should consecrate [them with mantras]. (LiP 2,24.15)
The remainder should be sprinkled with the <s>Śiva-Gāyatrī</s>. (LiP 2,24.16)
The five nectars (<s>pañcāmṛta</s>), five cow-products (<s>pañcagavya</s>), and the like should be consecrated with the <s>Brahmāṅga</s>-[mantras] and root-[mantra] etc. (LiP 2,24.17)

children.text: pṛthakpṛthaṅmūlenārghyaṃ dhūpaṃ dattvācamanīyaṃ ca teṣāmapi dhenumudrā ca darśayitvā kavacenāvaguṇṭhyāstreṇa rakṣāṃ ca vidhāya dravyaśuddhiṃ kuryāt // LiP_2,24.18 //
children.translated_text: Separately, with the root-mantra, having offered <s>arghya</s>, incense, and sipping-water, and showing the cow-<s>mudrā</s> for each of them, veiling with the armor[-mantra], performing protection with the weapon[-mantra] — one should effect purification of substances. (LiP 2,24.18)

children.text: arghyodakamagre hṛdā gandhamādāyāstreṇa viśodhya pūjāprabhṛtikaraṇaṃ rakṣāntaṃ kṛtvaivaṃ dravyaśuddhiṃ pūjāsamarpaṇāntaṃ maunamāsthāya puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā sarvamantrāṇi praṇavādinamontājjapitvā puṣpāñjaliṃ tyajenmantraśuddhirittham // LiP_2,24.19 //
children.translated_text: First, taking <s>arghya</s>-water with the heart[-mantra], sandal-paste, purifying with the weapon[-mantra], performing from worship through protection, thus effecting substance-purification through to the offering of worship — maintaining silence, offering a handful of flowers, reciting all mantras from <s>praṇava</s> to <s>namaḥ</s> — one should release the flower-handful. Thus is mantra-purification. (LiP 2,24.19)

children.text: agre sāmānyārghyapātraṃ payasāpūrya gandhapuṣpādinā saṃhitayābhimantrya dhenamudrāṃ dattvā kavacenāvaguṇṭhyāstreṇa rakṣayet /
children.translated_text: First, filling the general <s>arghya</s>-vessel with water, consecrating with the <s>saṃhitā</s> together with sandal, flowers, etc., showing the cow-<s>mudrā</s>, veiling with the armor[-mantra], and protecting with the weapon[-mantra].

children.text: pūjāṃ paryuṣitāṃ gāyatryā samabhyarcya sāmānyārghyaṃ dattvā gandhapuṣpadhūpācamanīyaṃ svadhāntaṃ namontaṃ vā datvā brahmabhiḥ pṛthakpṛthakpuṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā phaḍantāstreṇa nirmalyaṃ vyapohya īśānyāṃ caṇḍamabhyarcyāsanamūrti caṇḍaṃ sāmānyāstreṇa liṅgapīṭhaṃ śivaṃ pāśupatāstreṇa viśodhya mūrdhni puṣpaṃ nidhāya pūjayelliṅgaśuddhiḥ // LiP_2,24.20 //
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the previous day's worship with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, offering the general <s>arghya</s>, giving sandal, flowers, incense, sipping-water ending with <s>svadhā</s> or ending with <s>namaḥ</s>, offering separate flower-handfuls with the <s>Brahma</s>-[mantras], removing the old offerings with the weapon[-mantra] ending with <s>phaṭ</s>, worshipping <s>Caṇḍa</s> in the northeast with his seat, form, and the general weapon, purifying the <s>liṅga</s>-pedestal and <s>Śiva</s> with the <s>Pāśupata</s>-weapon, placing a flower on the crown — one should worship. This is <s>liṅga</s>-purification. (LiP 2,24.20)

children.text: āsanaṃ kūrmaśilāyāṃ bījāṅkuraṃ tadupari brahmaśilāyāmanantanālasuṣire sūtrapatrakaṇṭakakarṇikākesaradharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasūryasomāgnikesaraśaktiṃ manonmanīṃ karṇikāyāṃ manonmanenānantāsanāyeti samāsenāsanaṃ parikalpya tadupari nivṛttyādikalāmayaṃ ṣaṅvidhasahitaṃ karmakalāṅgadehaṃ sadāśivaṃ bhāvayet // LiP_2,24.21 //
children.translated_text: The seat [is visualized] on the tortoise-stone — the seed-sprout; above that, on the <s>Brahma</s>-stone — <s>Ananta</s>, the stalk, the hollow, the thread, the thorn, the leaf, the pericarp, the filaments — <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, <s>vairāgya</s>, <s>aiśvarya</s>, <s>sūrya</s>, <s>soma</s>, <s>agni</s> — the filament-<s>śakti</s>, <s>Manonmanī</s> on the pericarp — having mentally uttered '<s>Manonmana</s>; to the <s>Ananta</s>-seat' — thus in summary preparing the seat, above that one should contemplate <s>Sadāśiva</s>, consisting of the <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s>, together with the six-fold [aspects], with the action-<s>kalā</s>-limb-body. (LiP 2,24.21)

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ sapuṣpābhyāṃ hastābhyāmaṅguṣṭhena puṣpamāpīḍya āpāhanamudrayā śanaiḥśanaiḥ hṛdayādimastamāropya hṛdā saha mūlaṃ plutamuccāryasadyena bindusthānādabhyadhikaṃ dīpaśikhākāraṃ sarvatomukhahastaṃ vyāpyavyāpakamābāhya sthāpayet // LiP_2,24.22 //
children.translated_text: With both hands bearing flowers, pressing the flower with the thumbs, with the <s>āpāhana-mudrā</s>, slowly raising from the heart etc. to the head, uttering the root-mantra in prolonged form together with the heart[-mantra] and <s>Sadya</s>[-mantra], from the <s>bindu</s>-station extending beyond [it] in lamp-flame form, with hands facing all directions, pervading the pervader — one should invoke and establish [the deity]. (LiP 2,24.22)

children.text: pūrvahṛdā śivaśaktisamavāyena paramīkaraṇamamṛtīkaraṇaṃ hṛdayādimūlena sadyenāvāhanaṃ hṛdā mūlopari aghoreṇa sannirodaṃ hṛdā mūlopari puruṣeṇa sānnidhyaṃ hṛdā mūlena īśānena pūjayediti upadeśaḥ // LiP_2,24.23 //
children.translated_text: Previously with the heart[-mantra] — the supreme-making through the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, the nectarization; with the heart[-mantra] etc. and root-mantra, with <s>Sadya</s> — invocation; with the heart[-mantra] above the root-mantra, with <s>Aghora</s> — confinement; with the heart[-mantra] above the root-mantra, with <s>Puruṣa</s> — presence; with the heart[-mantra] and root-mantra, with <s>Īśāna</s> — 'Let him worship.' This is the instruction. (LiP 2,24.23)

children.text: pañcamantrasahitena yathāpūrvamātmano dehanirmāṇaṃ tathā devasyāpi vahneścaivamupadeśaḥ // LiP_2,24.24 //
children.translated_text: Just as one constructs the body of oneself with the five mantras as before, so also of the deity and of the fire — this is the instruction. (LiP 2,24.24)

children.text: rūpakadhyānaṃ kṛtvā mūlena namaskārāntamāpādya svadhāntamācamanīyaṃ sarvaṃ namaskārāntaṃ vā svāhākārāntamarghyaṃ mūlena puṣpāñjaliṃ vauṣaḍantena sarvaṃ namaskārāntaṃ hṛdā vā īśānena vā rudragāyatryā oṃnamaḥ śivāyeti mūlamantreṇa vā pūjayet // LiP_2,24.25 //
children.translated_text: Having performed meditation on the form (<s>rūpakadhyāna</s>), offering salutation with the root-mantra ending with <s>namaḥ</s>, sipping-water ending with <s>svadhā</s> — everything ending with <s>namaḥ</s> or <s>svāhā</s> — <s>arghya</s> with the root-mantra, flower-handful ending with <s>vauṣaṭ</s>, everything ending with <s>namaḥ</s>, or with the heart[-mantra], or with <s>Īśāna</s>, or with the <s>Rudra-Gāyatrī</s>, or with '<s>Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya</s>' as the root-mantra — one should worship. (LiP 2,24.25)

children.text: puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā punardhūṣācamanīyaṃ ṣaṣṭhena puṣpāvasaraṇaṃ visarjanaṃ mantrodakena mūlena saṃsnāpya sarvadravyābhiṣekamīśānena pratidravyamaṣṭapuṣpaṃ dattvaivamarghyaṃ ca gandhapuṣpadhūpācamanīyaṃ phaḍantāstreṇa pūjāpasaraṇaṃ śuddhodakena mūlena saṃsnāpya piṣṭāmalagādibhiḥ // LiP_2,24.26 //
children.translated_text: Having offered a flower-handful, again incense, sipping-water, with the sixth [mantra] the departure of flowers, dismissal; bathing with mantra-water and the root-mantra, performing the consecration-bath (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) with all substances, with <s>Īśāna</s> offering eight flowers for each substance, thus <s>arghya</s>, sandal, flowers, incense, sipping-water; with the weapon[-mantra] ending with <s>phaṭ</s>, the departure of worship; bathing with pure water and the root-mantra, with ground <s>āmalaka</s> [gooseberry] etc., (LiP 2,24.26)

children.text: uṣṇodakena haridrādyena liṅgamūrti pīṭhasahitāṃ viśodhya gandhodakahiraṇyodakamantrodakena rudrādhyāyaṃ paṭhamānaḥ nīlarudratvaritarudrapañcabrahmādibhiḥ namaḥ śivāyeti snāpayet // LiP_2,24.27 //
children.translated_text: with warm water and turmeric etc., having purified the <s>liṅga</s>-form together with the pedestal, with sandal-water, gold-water, and mantra-water — while reciting the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, with <s>Nīlarudra</s>, <s>Tvaritarudra</s>, the five <s>Brahma</s>-[mantras] etc. — one should bathe [the liṅga] with '<s>Namaḥ Śivāya</s>.' (LiP 2,24.27)

children.text: mūrdhni puṣpaṃ nidhāyaivaṃ na śūnyaṃ liṅgamastakaṃ kuryādatra ślokaḥ // LiP_2,24.28 //
children.translated_text: Having placed a flower on the crown — thus one should not make the head of the <s>liṅga</s> empty. Here is a verse: (LiP 2,24.28)

children.text: yasya rāṣṭre tu liṅgasya mastakaṃ śūnyalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: In whose kingdom the head of the <s>liṅga</s> has the mark of emptiness [is bare],
for him [there shall be] misfortune, great disease, famine, and loss of vehicles. (LiP 2,24.29)
Therefore, the king should avoid [this] for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and liberation;

children.text: śūnye liṅge svayaṃ rājā rāṣṭraṃ caiva praṇaśyati // LiP_2,24.30 //
children.translated_text: with an empty <s>liṅga</s>, the king himself and the kingdom are destroyed. (LiP 2,24.30)

children.text: evaṃ susnāpyārghyañca dattvā saṃmṛjya vastreṇa gandhapuṣpavastrālaṅkārādīṃśca mūlena dadyāt // LiP_2,24.31 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having well-bathed [the liṅga] and offered <s>arghya</s>, wiping with cloth, one should offer sandal, flowers, cloth, ornaments, etc. with the root-mantra. (LiP 2,24.31)
