with the <s>Mūrti</s>-<s>Vighneśa</s>-mantras, one should give as before. (LiP 2.37.13)
All this should be done by the sacrificer in proper sequence.

children.text: kevalaṃ rudradānaṃ vā adityebhyo 'tha vā punaḥ // LiP_2,37.14 //
children.translated_text: Either the <s>Rudra</s>-gift alone, or to the <s>Ādityas</s>, or again (LiP 2.37.14)
to the <s>Mūrtis</s> and the rest — [gifts] should be given according to the extent of one's wealth.

children.text: padmaṃ vinyasya rājāsau śeṣaṃ vā kārayennṛpaḥ // LiP_2,37.15 //
children.translated_text: Having installed the lotus, the king should have the rest performed, or [do it himself]. (LiP 2.37.15)

children.text: dakṣiṇā ca pradātavyā pañcaniṣkeṇa bhūṣaṇam // LiP_2,37.16 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be given — five <s>niṣkas</s> as ornament. (LiP 2.37.16)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge tiladhenudānavidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Sesame-Cow Gift Rite,' in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall declare the gift of a thousand cows — hear, O one of excellent vows.

children.text: gavāṃ sahasramādāya savatsaṃ saguṇaṃ śubham // LiP_2,38.1 //
children.translated_text: Having taken a thousand cows, with calves, endowed with good qualities, auspicious, (LiP 2.38.1)

children.text: tās tv abhyarcya yathāśāstram aṣṭau samyakprayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: having worshipped those eight [chief cows] well according to scripture, with great effort,

children.text: tāsāṃ śṛṅgāṇi hemnātha pratiniṣkeṇa bandhayet // LiP_2,38.2 //
children.translated_text: their horns should be bound with gold, with one <s>niṣka</s> each. (LiP 2.38.2)
The hooves should be bound with silver; around the neck,

children.text: pratiniṣkeṇa kartavyaṃ karṇe vajraṃ ca śobhanam // LiP_2,38.3 //
children.translated_text: with one <s>niṣka</s> each, [an ornament] should be made; on the ears, a beautiful diamond [ornament]. (LiP 2.38.3)
One should give [them] to <s>Śiva</s> [devotees], to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> separately —

children.text: daśaniṣkaṃ tadardhaṃ vā tasyārdhārdhamathāpi vā // LiP_2,38.4 //
children.translated_text: ten <s>niṣkas</s>, or half of that, or half of that half. (LiP 2.38.4)
According to the extent of one's wealth — or even just one <s>niṣka</s>;

children.text: vastrayugmaṃ ca dātavyaṃ pṛthagvipreṣu śobhanam // LiP_2,38.5 //
children.translated_text: and a pair of garments should be given to each <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, beautiful. (LiP 2.38.5)
Having worshipped the cows with effort, delightful [cows] should be given.

children.text: evaṃ dattvā vidhānena śivamabhyarcya saṃkaram // LiP_2,38.6 //
children.translated_text: Having given thus according to the rite, having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> <s>Śaṅkara</s>, (LiP 2.38.6)
one should first recite according to propriety the unsurpassed praise of cows:

children.text: gāvo mamāgrato nityaṃ gāvo naḥ pṛṣṭhatastathā // LiP_2,38.7 //
children.translated_text: 'May cows always be before me! May cows be behind us! (LiP 2.38.7)

children.text: hṛdaye me sadā gāvo gāvaṃ madhye vasāmy aham /
children.translated_text: May cows always be in my heart! I dwell in the midst of cows!'

children.text: iti kṛtvā dvijāgryebhyodattvā gatvā pradakṣiṇam // LiP_2,38.8 //
children.translated_text: Having done thus, having given to the foremost <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having performed circumambulation, (LiP 2.38.8)
for as many years as there are hairs [on the cows' bodies] — one is glorified in the heavenly world. (LiP 2.38.9)
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, entitled 'The Gift of a Thousand Cows,' in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall declare the gift of the golden horse — which brings victory.

children.text: aśvamedhātpunaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ vadāmī śṛṇu suvrata // LiP_2,39.1 //
children.translated_text: Superior even to the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) — I shall declare [it]; hear, O one of excellent vows. (LiP 2.39.1)
With one thousand and eight, or with one hundred and eight [niṣkas],
having made a horse endowed with [all] marks, furnished with all ornaments, (LiP 2.39.2)
possessing the five auspicious features, of divine appearance — one should have [it] made,
endowed with all auspicious marks, complete in all limbs, (LiP 2.39.3)
equipped with all weapons — the excellent mount of <s>Indra</s>.
Having installed the horse in the center [of the maṇḍala], endowed with its own qualities, (LiP 2.39.4)

children.text: uccaiḥ śravasakaṃ matvā bhaktyā caiva samarcayet /
children.translated_text: considering [it as] <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> (Indra's celestial horse), one should worship with devotion.
On the eastern side, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s> — (LiP 2.39.5)
worshipping [him] as if [he were] <s>Indra</s>, one should give five <s>niṣkas</s>.

children.text: sa cāśvaḥ śivabhaktāya dātavyo vidhinaiva tu // LiP_2,39.6 //
children.translated_text: That horse should be given to a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>, according to the proper rite. (LiP 2.39.6)
Having given the golden horse, one should also worship the preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>);
according to the extent of one's wealth — or five <s>niṣkas</s>. (LiP 2.39.7)
The poor, the blind, the destitute, the shelterless, children, the aged, the emaciated, and the sick —
one should please [them] with food-gifts, and the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> especially. (LiP 2.39.8)
He who performs this gift of a horse with devotion —
having enjoyed the pleasures of <s>Indra</s> for a long time, he becomes one of splendid sovereignty. (LiP 2.39.9)
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Gift of the Golden Horse,' in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall declare the maiden-gift (<s>kanyādāna</s>) — the highest of all gifts.
A maiden endowed with [all] marks, free from all defects — (LiP 2.40.1)

children.text: mātāpitrostu saṃvādaṃ kṛtvā dattvā dhanaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: having reached agreement with both parents, having given great wealth,

children.text: ātmīkṛtyātha saṃsnāpya vastraṃ dattvā śubhaṃ navam // LiP_2,40.2 //
children.translated_text: having made [her] one's own [through adoption], having bathed [her], having given a new auspicious garment, (LiP 2.40.2)
having adorned [her] with ornaments, one should worship [her] with fragrance and garlands.
Then, having examined the omens — clan, birth-star, and the like, (LiP 2.40.3)
observing the disposition of both [parties], having worshipped both with effort —
[the maiden] should be given only to a <s>Śrotriya</s> (Veda-learned) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, an ascetic, (LiP 2.40.4)
one who has actually studied the <s>Vedas</s>, a celibate student by rule.
Abundant with servants, maidservants, and wealth, and ornaments especially, (LiP 2.40.5)

children.text: kṣetrāṇi ca dhanaṃ dhānya vāsāṃsi ca pradāpayet /
children.translated_text: fields, wealth, grain, and garments — one should give.

children.text: yāvanti dehe romāṇi kanyāyāḥ saṃtatau punaḥ // LiP_2,40.6 //
children.translated_text: As many hairs as there are on the maiden's body, and in [her] progeny — (LiP 2.40.6)
for that many thousands of years, one is glorified in the world of <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2.40.7)
Thus ends the fortieth chapter, entitled 'The Rite of Maiden-Gift,' in the Uttara-bhāga of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall describe the gift of the golden bull in summary.
One should have a bull-form made of gold — with a thousand [niṣkas]; (LiP 2.41.1)
or with half of that half, the wise one — or with half of that half again;
or with one hundred and eight — a bull embodying <s>Dharma</s>. (LiP 2.41.2)
On the forehead, one should make a <s>puṇḍra</s> mark in the shape of a half-crescent.

children.text: sphaṭikena tu karttavyaṃ khuraṃ tu rajatena vai // LiP_2,41.3 //
children.translated_text: The hoof should be made of crystal, and the hoof-blade of silver. (LiP 2.41.3)
The neck with ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>), and the hump with hessonite (<s>gomedaka</s>).

children.text: grīvāyāṃ ghāṇṭavalayaṃ ratnacitraṃ tu kārayet // LiP_2,41.4 //
children.translated_text: On the neck one should have a bell-bracelet made, variegated with gems. (LiP 2.41.4)
One should have the bull-mark made there, covered with a girdle of small bells.
At the previously stated place and time, on the circular platform of the altar, (LiP 2.41.5)
one should install the bull-lord there, facing west, in front [of the deity].
One should worship <s>Īśvara</s> with devotion, mounted on the bull, bearing the bull-banner. (LiP 2.41.6)

children.text:
vṛṣendraṃ pūjya gāyatryā namaskṛtya samāhitaḥ /
tīkṣṇaśṛṅgāya vidmahe dharmapādāya dhīmahi /
tanno vṛṣaḥ pracodayāt // LiP_2,41.7 //

children.translated_text: Having worshipped the bull with this mantra for the increase of <s>dharma</s>,
one should also perform <s>homa</s> with ghee, food, and the like, according to one's means. (LiP 2.41.8)

Having worshipped the bull-lord with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one should salute with concentration: 'We know the Sharp-horned One, we meditate on the Dharma-footed One — may the Bull inspire us!' (LiP 2.41.7)

children.text: vṛṣabhaḥ pūjya dātavyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ śivāya vā /
children.translated_text: The bull, having been worshipped, should be given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> or to <s>Śiva</s> [i.e., a Śiva temple].
The fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should also be given according to one's means. (LiP 2.41.9)
He who performs this supreme gift of the bull with devotion,

children.text: śivasyānucaro bhūtvā tenaiva saha modate // LiP_2,41.10 //
children.translated_text: becoming an attendant of <s>Śiva</s>, he rejoices together with Him. (LiP 2.41.10)
Thus ends the forty-first chapter, named 'The Gift of the Golden Bull' (<s>suvarṇavṛṣadāna</s>), in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall now describe the gift of an elephant, in due order as it is.

children.text: dvijāya vā śivāyātha dātavyaḥ pūjya pūrvavat // LiP_2,42.1 //
children.translated_text: It should be given to a twice-born or to <s>Śiva</s>, having been worshipped as before. (LiP 2.42.1)

children.text: gajaṃ sulakṣaṇopetaṃ haimaṃ vā rājataṃ tu vā /
children.translated_text: An elephant endowed with auspicious marks, made of gold or of silver,
should be fashioned with a thousand <s>niṣkas</s> [of gold], or with half of that. (LiP 2.42.2)
Or one should make it with half of half, adorned with all auspicious marks.
At the previously stated place and time, one should offer it to the deity. (LiP 2.42.3)
Or it should be given on the eighth (<s>aṣṭamī</s>) to <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme Lord,
to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is poor, learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, and one who maintains the sacred fires. (LiP 2.42.4)
It should be given dedicating it to <s>Śiva</s>, having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> as before.
He who makes this gift, absorbed in devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, (LiP 2.42.5)

children.text: sthitvā svarge ciraṃ kālaṃ rājā gajapatirbhavet // LiP_2,42.6 //
children.translated_text: having dwelt in heaven for a long time, the king becomes a lord of elephants. (LiP 2.42.6)
Thus ends the forty-second chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
The divine group of eight <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians), directly most difficult to obtain,
bestowing all prosperity, secret, destroying the enemy's forces, (LiP 2.43.1)
divinely protecting one's own country, increasing elephants and horses,
increasing sons, meritorious, bringing welfare to cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — (LiP 2.43.2)
at the previously stated place and time, on the circular platform of the altar,

children.text: madhye śivaṃ samabhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ yathākramam // LiP_2,43.3 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> in the middle, properly and in due order, (LiP 2.43.3)
in the [eight] directions and intermediate directions, one should prepare ground-altars (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) of sand.
Having worshipped eight <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, masters of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, (LiP 2.43.4)
with senses controlled, of noble birth, endowed with all auspicious marks,
seated facing <s>Śiva</s>, in fresh garments, (LiP 2.43.5)
with garments and divine ornaments, with the mantras of the <s>Lokapālas</s>,
with fragrances, flowers, and fine incense, one should worship the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> in sequence. (LiP 2.43.6)
Beginning from the east, one should perform <s>homa</s> in the fire with the <s>Lokapāla</s> mantras.
The oblation should be offered with fuel-sticks and ghee, or the fire-rite in sequence. (LiP 2.43.7)
Having thus offered oblations according to rule, the <s>ācārya</s>, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>,
should summon the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), adorned with all ornaments, (LiP 2.43.8)
and through him, having worshipped them, should have wealth given to the twice-born —
ten <s>niṣkas</s> and ornaments, separately, with each [respective] mantra. (LiP 2.43.9)
A seat should be made separately with ten <s>niṣkas</s>.

children.text: snapanaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ śivasya vidhipūrvakam // LiP_2,43.10 //
children.translated_text: The bathing (<s>snapana</s>) of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed there, according to the prescribed rules. (LiP 2.43.10)
The fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be given according to one's means.

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ kurute dānaṃ lokeśānāṃ tu bhaktitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who thus makes this gift of the <s>Lokeśas</s> (World-Lords) with devotion,

children.text: lokeśānāṃ ciraṃ sthitvā sārvabhaumau bhavedbudhaḥ // LiP_2,43.11 //
children.translated_text: having dwelt long among the World-Lords, the wise one becomes a universal sovereign (<s>sārvabhauma</s>). (LiP 2.43.11)
Thus ends the forty-third chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now I shall describe another — the greatest of all gifts.

children.text: pūrvoktadeśakāle ca maṇḍape ca vidhānataḥ // LiP_2,44.1 //
children.translated_text: At the previously stated place and time, in the pavilion, according to rule, (LiP 2.44.1)
with devotion, in the fire-pit and on the ground-altar, in the presence of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: pūrvaṃ viṣṇuṃ samāsādya padmayonimataḥ param // LiP_2,44.2 //
children.translated_text: having first approached <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and then the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), (LiP 2.44.2)
with the two mantras as prescribed, beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> (Om):
'We know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, we meditate on <s>Vāsudeva</s> —
may <s>Viṣṇu</s> inspire us!' (LiP 2.44.3)
'To the Eldest of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, to <s>Brahman</s>, to the All-Creator,

children.text: śivāya haraye svāhā svadhā vauṣaṭvaṣaṭ tathā // LiP_2,44.4 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Hari</s> — <s>svāhā</s>! <s>svadhā</s>! <s>vauṣaṭ</s>! <s>vaṣaṭ</s>!' (LiP 2.44.4)
Having worshipped according to rule, one should afterward perform <s>homa</s>.

children.text: sarvadravyaṃ hi hotavyaṃ dvābhyāṃ kuṇḍavidhānataḥ // LiP_2,44.5 //
children.translated_text: All substances should be offered, in two fire-pits according to the rule. (LiP 2.44.5)
Two officiating priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>), masters of the <s>Vedas</s>, should be appointed by the guru.
Dedicating [the offerings] to them, one should have wealth given to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> according to rule. (LiP 2.44.6)
One hundred and eight [<s>niṣkas</s>] to them, each separately, supreme,
furnished with garments and ornaments, endowed with all decorations. (LiP 2.44.7)

children.text: gurureko hi vai śrīmān brahmā viṣṇurmaheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The guru alone, indeed, is glorious — he is <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Gifts should be given to them separately, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should also be fed. (LiP 2.44.8)

children.text: śivārcanā ca kartavyā snapanādi yathākramam // LiP_2,44.9 //
children.translated_text: Worship of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed, beginning with bathing (<s>snapana</s>) and the rest, in due order. (LiP 2.44.9)
Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:

children.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśa dānāni kathitāni śubhāni ca /
children.translated_text: Thus the sixteen gifts have been described, all auspicious.
Now please tell us the procedure of the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> (śrāddha performed while living). (LiP 2.45.1)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall briefly describe the procedure of the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s>, universally accepted,

children.text: manave devadevena kathitaṃ brahmaṇā purā // LiP_2,45.2 //
children.translated_text: as told formerly to <s>Manu</s> by <s>Brahmā</s>, the god of gods. (LiP 2.45.2)

children.text: vasiṣṭhāsa ca śiṣṭāya bhṛgave bhārgavāya ca /
children.translated_text: And to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, to the disciplined one, and to <s>Bhṛgu</s> of the <s>Bhārgava</s> lineage.
Listen with full attention — [this is] the supreme [rite] that accomplishes all <s>siddhis</s>. (LiP 2.45.3)
The procedure of the śrāddha path, and also the sequence of those worthy of receiving śrāddha,
and the special features of the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> — I shall describe, O ones of good vows. (LiP 2.45.4)

children.text: parvate vā nadītīre vane vāyatane 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: On a mountain, or on a riverbank, or in a forest, or in a temple,
the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> should be performed with effort at the time of death. (LiP 2.45.5)
When the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> is performed, the living person is liberated while still alive —
whether performing actions or not performing them, whether a knower or one without knowledge, (LiP 2.45.6)
whether learned in the <s>Vedas</s> or not, whether a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or a <s>kṣatriya</s>,

children.text: vaiśyo vā nātra saṃdeho yogamārgagato yatā // LiP_2,45.7 //
children.translated_text: or a <s>vaiśya</s> — there is no doubt — [if] one is disciplined and follows the path of <s>yoga</s>. (LiP 2.45.7)
Having examined the ground properly by its fragrance, color, taste, and the like,

children.text: śalyamuddhṛtya yatnena sthāṇḍilaṃ saikataṃ bhuvi // LiP_2,45.8 //
children.translated_text: having carefully removed foreign objects, [one prepares] a sandy ground-altar on the earth. (LiP 2.45.8)
In the middle, one cubit in measure, [one should prepare] a deep and auspicious fire-pit.

children.text: sthāṇḍilaṃ vā prakartavyamiṣumātraṃ punaḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,45.9 //
children.translated_text: Or a ground-altar should be prepared, one arrow's length, again and again. (LiP 2.45.9)
Having plastered according to rule, and having drawn [the lines], and having established the fire,

children.text: anvādhāya yathāśāstraṃ parigṛhya ca sarvataḥ // LiP_2,45.10 //
children.translated_text: having placed [the logs] according to scripture, and having enclosed [the altar] on all sides, (LiP 2.45.10)
having strewn [<s>darbha</s> grass] as prescribed by one's own Vedic branch, as received through tradition,
having completed all the fire-mouth [rites] with these mantras in due order, (LiP 2.45.11)
having worshipped, one should perform <s>homa</s> on the ground-altar into the fire with fuel-sticks and the like.

children.text: ādau kṛtvā samiddhomaṃ caruṇā ca pṛthakpṛthak // LiP_2,45.12 //
children.translated_text: First performing the fuel-stick <s>homa</s>, and separately with cooked rice (<s>caru</s>), (LiP 2.45.12)
and with ghee, purified, in separate vessels, separately,
one should offer, extracting from oneself all the <s>tattvas</s> (principles of existence) everywhere: (LiP 2.45.13)
Om <s>Bhūḥ</s>! Salutation to <s>Brahman</s>! (LiP 2.45.14)
Om <s>Bhūḥ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Brahman</s>! (LiP 2.45.15)
Om <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! Salutation to <s>Viṣṇu</s>! (LiP 2.45.16)
Om <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Viṣṇu</s>! (LiP 2.45.17)
Om <s>Svaḥ</s>! Salutation to <s>Rudra</s>! (LiP 2.45.18)
Om <s>Svaḥ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Rudra</s>! (LiP 2.45.19)
Om <s>Mahaḥ</s>! Salutation to <s>Īśvara</s>! (LiP 2.45.20)
Om <s>Mahaḥ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Īśvara</s>! (LiP 2.45.21)
Om <s>Janaḥ</s>! Salutation to <s>Prakṛti</s> (Primordial Nature)! (LiP 2.45.22)
Om <s>Janaḥ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Prakṛti</s>! (LiP 2.45.23)
Om <s>Tapaḥ</s>! Salutation to <s>Mudgala</s>! (LiP 2.45.24)
Om <s>Tapaḥ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Mudgala</s>! (LiP 2.45.25)
Om <s>Ṛtam</s>! Salutation to <s>Puruṣa</s>! (LiP 2.45.26)
Om <s>Ṛtam</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Puruṣa</s>! (LiP 2.45.27)
Om <s>Satyam</s>! Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>! (LiP 2.45.28)
Om <s>Satyam</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Śiva</s>! (LiP 2.45.29)

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvāya devāya bhūrnamaḥ // LiP_2,45.30 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Śarva</s>, protect for me the earth (<s>dharā</s>), [protect] the sense of smell in my nose, [and] fragrance — salutation to the god <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhūḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.30)

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvāya bhūḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.31 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Śarva</s>, protect for me the earth, [protect] the sense of smell in my nose, [and] fragrance — to <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2.45.31)

children.text: śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvasya devasya patnyai bhūrnamaḥ // LiP_2,45.32 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Śarva</s>, protect for me the earth, [protect] the sense of smell in my nose, [and] fragrance — salutation to the consort of the god <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhūḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.32)

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ sarvapatnyaibhūḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.33 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Śarva</s>, protect for me the earth, [protect] the sense of smell in my nose, [and] fragrance — to the consort of <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2.45.33)

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyaṃ rasaṃ bhavāya devāya bhuvo namaḥ // LiP_2,45.34 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Bhava</s>, protect for me water (<s>jala</s>), [protect] the sense of taste on my tongue — salutation to the god <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.34)

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavāya devāya bhuvaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.35 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Bhava</s>, protect for me water, [protect] the sense of taste on my tongue — <s>svāhā</s> to the god <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.35)

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavasya devasya patnyai bhuvo namaḥ // LiP_2,45.36 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Bhava</s>, protect for me water, [protect] the sense of taste on my tongue — salutation to the consort of the god <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.36)

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavasya patnyai bhuvaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.37 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Bhava</s>, protect for me water, [protect] the sense of taste on my tongue — <s>svāhā</s> to the consort of <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.37)

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrāya devāya svarāeṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.38 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, protect for me fire (<s>agni</s>), [protect] form in my eyes — salutation to the god <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.38)

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrāya devāya svaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.39 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, protect for me fire, [protect] form in my eyes — <s>svāhā</s> to the god <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.39)

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gāpāya netre rūpaṃ rudrasya patnyai svarāeṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.40 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, protect for me fire, [protect] form in my eyes — salutation to the consort of <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.40)

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrasya devasya patnyaisvaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.41 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, protect for me fire, [protect] form in my eyes — <s>svāhā</s> to the consort of the god <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.41)

children.text: ugra vāyuṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśaṃ ugrāya devāya maharnamaḥ // LiP_2,45.42 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Ugra</s>, protect for me wind (<s>vāyu</s>), [protect] touch on my skin — salutation to the god <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.42)

children.text: ugra vāyūṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśamugrāya devāya mahaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.43 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Ugra</s>, protect for me wind, [protect] touch on my skin — <s>svāhā</s> to the god <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.43)

children.text: ugra vāyuṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśamugrasya devasya patnyai maharāeṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.44 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Ugra</s>, protect for me wind, [protect] touch on my skin — salutation to the consort of the god <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.44)

children.text: oṃ ugra vāyuṃ mo gopāya tvaci sparśamugrasya devasya patnyai devāya janaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.45 //
children.translated_text: Om, O <s>Ugra</s>, protect for me wind, [protect] touch on my skin — <s>svāhā</s> to the consort of the god <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.45)

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmāya devāya jano namaḥ // LiP_2,45.46 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect for me ether (<s>suṣira</s>), [protect] sound in my ears — salutation to the god <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.46)

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmāya devāya janaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.47 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect for me ether, [protect] sound in my ears — <s>svāhā</s> to the god <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.47)

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmasya patnyai jano namaḥ // LiP_2,45.48 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect for me ether, [protect] sound in my ears — salutation to the consort of <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.48)

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmasya devasya patnyai janaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.49 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect for me ether, [protect] sound in my ears — <s>svāhā</s> to the consort of the god <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.49)

children.text: īśa rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇāmīśāya devāya tapo namaḥ // LiP_2,45.50 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Īśa</s>, protect for me <s>rajas</s> (passion), [protect] desire in my possessions — salutation to the god <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.50)

children.text: īśa rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇamīśāya devāya tapaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.51 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Īśa</s>, protect for me <s>rajas</s>, [protect] desire in my possessions — <s>svāhā</s> to the god <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.51)

children.text: rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇāmīśasya patnyai tapo namaḥ // LiP_2,45.52 //
children.translated_text: Protect for me <s>rajas</s>, [protect] desire in my possessions — salutation to the consort of <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.52)

children.text: īśa rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇamīśasya patnyai tapaḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.53 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Īśa</s>, protect for me <s>rajas</s>, [protect] desire in my possessions — <s>svāhā</s> to the consort of <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>! (LiP 2.45.53)

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevāya ṛtaṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.54 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect for me truth (<s>satya</s>), [protect] faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) in <s>dharma</s> — salutation to <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Ṛtam</s>! (LiP 2.45.54)

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevāya ṛtaṃ svāhā // LiP_2,45.55 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect my truth; faith in <s>dharma</s>; to <s>Mahādeva</s>, the cosmic order — <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.55)

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevāya patnyai ṛtaṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.56 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect my truth; faith in <s>dharma</s>; to the consort of <s>Mahādeva</s>, the cosmic order — <s>namaḥ</s>! (LiP 2,45.56)

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ ma gopāya śraddhāṃ mahādevasya patnyai ṛtaṃ svāhā // LiP_2,45.57 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect my truth; faith; to the consort of <s>Mahādeva</s>, the cosmic order — <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.57)

children.text: paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupataye devāya satyaṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.58 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; the enjoyership and the enjoyable; to <s>Paśupati</s> the god, truth — <s>namaḥ</s>! (LiP 2,45.58)

children.text: paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhāgyaṃ paśupataye devasya satyaṃ svāhā // LiP_2,45.59 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; the enjoyership and fortune; to <s>Paśupati</s> the god, truth — <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.59)

children.text: oṃ paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya yoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupater devasya patnyai satyaṃ namaḥ // LiP_2,45.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; the yokership and the enjoyable; to the consort of <s>Paśupati</s> the god, truth — <s>namaḥ</s>! (LiP 2,45.60)

children.text: oṃ paśupate pāśaṃ ma gopāya yoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupaterdevasya patnyai satyaṃ svāhā // LiP_2,45.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; the yokership and the enjoyable; to the consort of <s>Paśupati</s> the god, truth — <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.61)
<s>Oṃ</s> <s>namaḥ</s> to <s>Śiva</s>! (LiP 2,45.62)
<s>Oṃ</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>, truth — <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.63)

children.text: evaṃ śivāya hotavyaṃ viriñcyādyaṃ ca pūvavat /
children.translated_text: Thus one should offer oblations to <s>Śiva</s>, and to <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā) and the others as before;

children.text: viriñcādyaṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ sṛṣṭimārgeṣu suvratāḥ // LiP_2,45.64 //
children.translated_text: the [mantras] beginning with <s>Viriñci</s> as previously stated, in the paths of creation, O ones of good vows. (LiP 2,45.64)

children.text: punaḥ paśupateḥ patnīṃ tathā paśupatīṃ kramāt /
children.translated_text: Again, having worshipped the consort of <s>Paśupati</s>, and <s>Paśupatī</s> (the goddess) in sequence,

children.text: saṃpūjya pūrvavanmantrairhetavyaṃ ca krameṇa vai // LiP_2,45.65 //
children.translated_text: one should offer oblations with the previously stated mantras, in due order. (LiP 2,45.65)
The chewing [offerings] preceded by ghee, and ending with fuel-sticks, with concentration. (LiP 2,45.66)

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me chindhi ghrāṇe gandhaṃ chindhi meghaṃ jahi bhūḥ svāhā // LiP_2,45.67 //
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. O <s>Śarva</s>, sever my [bond to] earth; sever smell in my nose; destroy the cloud — <s>Bhūḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.67)
<s>Bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.68)
<s>Svaḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.69)
<s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.70)
Thus, having offered separately with each [mantra], or with ghee alone,

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā // LiP_2,45.71 //
children.translated_text: a thousand [times], or half of that, or a hundred plus eight. (LiP 2,45.71)
And with the <s>Virajā</s> [mantra], with ghee alone, a hundred plus eight, separately;
and with the <s>prāṇa</s> [mantras] and the rest, one should offer with ghee alone. (LiP 2,45.72)

children.text: oṃ prāṇe niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi śivo ma viśāpradāhāya prāṇāya svāhā // LiP_2,45.73 //
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Established in <s>prāṇa</s>, I offer <s>amṛta</s> (immortality). May <s>Śiva</s> [protect] me from the burning of poison — to <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.73)
To <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of <s>prāṇa</s>, the destroyer of the bull [of death] — <s>svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.74)
<s>Oṃ Bhūḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.75)
<s>Oṃ Bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.76)
<s>Oṃ Svaḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.77)
<s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ svāhā</s>! (LiP 2,45.78)
Thus one should offer in sequence; and the <s>śrāddha</s>-prescribed [offerings] in their proper order.

children.text: saptame 'hani yogīndrāñ chrāddhārhān api bhojayet // LiP_2,45.79 //
children.translated_text: On the seventh day, one should feed the foremost <s>yogins</s> who are worthy of <s>śrāddha</s>. (LiP 2,45.79)
To the Brahmins [who represent] <s>Śarva</s> and the others — garments, ornaments, blankets,
vehicles, beds, conveyances, vessels of bronze and copper and the like, (LiP 2,45.80)

children.text: haimaṃ ca rājataṃ dhenuṃ tilān kṣetraṃ ca vaibhavam /
children.translated_text: golden and silver [items], a cow, sesame, land, and wealth,
groups of male and female servants — all should be given as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee). (LiP 2,45.81)
One should give the <s>piṇḍa</s> (rice-ball offering) as before, separately in eight ways.

children.text: brāhmaṇānaṃ sahasraṃ ca bhojayecca sadakṣiṇam // LiP_2,45.82 //
children.translated_text: One should feed a thousand Brahmins, with <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. (LiP 2,45.82)
Or [feed] even one [Brahmin] devoted to <s>yoga</s>, established in sacred ash, with senses conquered.

children.text: tryahaṃ caiva tu rudrasya mahācarunivedanam // LiP_2,45.83 //
children.translated_text: For three days, there should be the offering of a great <s>caru</s> (oblation-food) to <s>Rudra</s>. (LiP 2,45.83)
This special [rite] has been described, prompted by the complete <s>śrāddha</s> [teaching].

children.text: mṛte kuryānna kuryādvā jīvanmukto yataḥ svayam // LiP_2,45.84 //
children.translated_text: When [the practitioner] dies, one may or may not perform [further rites], since he is already liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>). (LiP 2,45.84)
The regular, occasional, and other [rites] — one may perform or may renounce.

children.text: bāndhave 'pi mṛte tasya śaucāśaucaṃ na vidyate // LiP_2,45.85 //
children.translated_text: Even when a kinsman dies, for him there is neither purity nor impurity. (LiP 2,45.85)

children.text: sūtakaṃ ca na saṃdehaḥ snānamātreṇa śuddhyati /
children.translated_text: Birth-pollution too [does not apply] — no doubt — he is purified by bathing alone.

children.text: paścājjāte kumāre ca sve kṣetre cātmano yadi // LiP_2,45.86 //
children.translated_text: If afterward a son is born in his own family, to himself, (LiP 2,45.86)
all [rites] should be performed for him; the son too should become a knower of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: kanyakā yadi rāñjātā paścāttasya mahātmanaḥ // LiP_2,45.87 //
children.translated_text: If a daughter is born afterward to that great soul, (LiP 2,45.87)

children.text: ekaparṇā iva jñeyā aparṇā iva suvratā /
children.translated_text: she should be known as [equal to] <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, like <s>Aparṇā</s>, of excellent vows.
This is certain — and those born in her lineage also (LiP 2,45.88)
are liberated — no doubt — [their] ancestors too are freed from hell.
By this [rite], they are freed — on both the maternal and paternal sides. (LiP 2,45.89)

children.text: kālaṃ gate dvije bhūmau khaneccāpi dahettu vā /
children.translated_text: When the twice-born passes away, one may bury [the body] in the earth or cremate it.

children.text: putrakṛtyamaśeṣaṃ ca kṛtvā doṣo na vidyate // LiP_2,45.90 //
children.translated_text: Having performed all the funerary rites for the son [i.e. as prescribed], there is no fault. (LiP 2,45.90)
By the superior [<s>jīvacchrāddha</s>] rite itself, his destiny is [already] determined.
All this was spoken by <s>Brahmā</s> to the sages of purified souls. (LiP 2,45.91)
Then it was told by that wise one to <s>Sanatkumāra</s>,
and told by the son of <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> (Vyāsa). (LiP 2,45.92)
By the grace of that god, the wise <s>Vedavyāsa</s>,

children.text: jñātaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ caiva niyogādeva tasya tu // LiP_2,45.93 //
children.translated_text: it was known by me and composed, indeed by his command. (LiP 2,45.93)
All this has been told to you — the secret that bestows the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: muniputrāya dātavyaṃ na cābhaktāya suvratāḥ // LiP_2,45.94 //
children.translated_text: It should be given to the son of a sage, not to one who is not a devotee, O ones of good vows. (LiP 2,45.94)
Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled 'The Procedure for <s>Jīvacchrāddha</s> (Śrāddha Performed While Living).'
The sages said:
The procedure for <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> has been described by you, O <s>Sūta</s> of great wisdom,
for the liberation even of the ignorant — [tell] us, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>. (LiP 2,46.1)
Of the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, and of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and the others, O one of good vows —
what is the [proper] installation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) of <s>Śambhu</s>'s <s>liṅga</s>-form, the auspicious? (LiP 2,46.2)
Of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of <s>Śakra</s> the god, and of <s>Brahmā</s> the great-souled,

children.text: agner yasya nirṛter varuṇasya mahādyuteḥ // LiP_2,46.3 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Agni</s>, of <s>Yama</s>, of <s>Nirṛti</s>, of <s>Varuṇa</s> of great splendor, (LiP 2,46.3)
of <s>Vāyu</s>, of <s>Soma</s>, of the <s>Yakṣa</s> [lord] <s>Kubera</s> of immeasurable soul,

children.text: īśānasya dharāyāśca śrīpratiṣṭhātha vā katham // LiP_2,46.4 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Īśāna</s>, of the Earth — how is the auspicious installation of <s>Śrī</s> [performed]? (LiP 2,46.4)
And the installation of <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, and of the auspicious <s>Haimavatī</s> (Pārvatī),
of <s>Skanda</s>, of the chief of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, and of <s>Nandin</s> in particular — (LiP 2,46.5)

children.text: tathānyeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ gaṇānāmapi vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: and of other gods and <s>gaṇas</s> as well —
please describe in full the characteristics of installation. (LiP 2,46.6)
You are the knower of the truth of all things, a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>, of excellent vows.
You are verily the other body of <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> (Vyāsa) himself. (LiP 2,46.7)
<s>Sumantu</s>, <s>Jaimini</s>, and <s>Paila</s> — those supreme sages —

children.text: gurubhaktiṃ tathā kartuṃ samartho romaharṣaṇaḥ // LiP_2,46.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> is capable of performing such devotion to the guru. (LiP 2,46.8)
Such is the extensive song of <s>Vyāsa</s> on the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Gaṅgā).

children.text: ekaḥ samo vā bhinno vā śiṣyastasya mahādyuteḥ // LiP_2,46.9 //
children.translated_text: Whether equal or different, [you are] a disciple of that one of great splendor. (LiP 2,46.9)
You are equal to <s>Vaiśaṃpāyana</s> among the disciples of <s>Vyāsa</s> on earth.
Therefore, please tell us everything now. (LiP 2,46.10)

children.text: evamuktvā sthiteṣveva teṣu sarveṣu tatra ca /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, while all of them stood there,

children.text: babhūva vismayo 'tīva munīnāṃ tasya cāgrataḥ // LiP_2,46.11 //
children.translated_text: a great wonder arose among the sages in his presence. (LiP 2,46.11)
Then in the sky, the extensive [form of] the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself

children.text: alaṃ munīnāṃ praśro 'yamiti vācā babhūva ha // LiP_2,46.12 //
children.translated_text: spoke with a voice: 'Enough! This question of the sages [is worthy]!' (LiP 2,46.12)

children.text: sarvaṃ liṅgamayaṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ liṅge pratiṣṭhitam /
children.translated_text: The entire world is pervaded by the <s>liṅga</s>; everything is established in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Therefore, abandoning all else, one should install and worship that. (LiP 2,46.13)
By one whose sword of purpose is fixed on the noble path of <s>liṅga</s>-installation,
the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) is swiftly pierced through, and one emerges without hesitation. (LiP 2,46.14)
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Padmagarbha</s> (Brahmā), <s>Indu</s> (Moon), <s>Yama</s>, the Lord of Waters (<s>Varuṇa</s>), the Lord of Wealth (<s>Kubera</s>),

children.text: tathānye ca śivaṃ sthāpya liṅgamūrti maheśvaram // LiP_2,46.15 //
children.translated_text: and others — having installed <s>Śiva</s> in the <s>liṅga</s>-form, <s>Maheśvara</s>, (LiP 2,46.15)

children.text: sveṣusveṣu ca pakṣeṣu pradhānāste yathā dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: each in their respective positions became foremost, O twice-born ones.

children.text: brahmā haraśca bhagavānviṣṇurdevī ramā dharā // LiP_2,46.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hara</s>, the lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the goddess <s>Ramā</s>, the Earth, (LiP 2,46.16)

children.text: lakṣmīrdhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ prajñā dharā durgā śacī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Dharā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Śacī</s>,

children.text: rudrāśca vasavaḥ skando viśākhaḥ śākha eva ca // LiP_2,46.17 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, <s>Śākha</s>, (LiP 2,46.17)
the lord <s>Naigameśa</s>, the world-guardians, and the planets,

children.text: sarve nandipurogāśca gaṇā gaṇapatiḥ prabhuḥ // LiP_2,46.18 //
children.translated_text: all the <s>gaṇas</s> led by <s>Nandin</s>, and <s>Gaṇapati</s> the lord, (LiP 2,46.18)
the ancestors, all the sages, <s>Kubera</s> and the others of great splendor,

children.text: āditya vasavaḥ sāṃkhyā aśvinau ca bhiṣagvarau // LiP_2,46.19 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, and the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the best of physicians, (LiP 2,46.19)
the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, animals, birds, and beasts —

children.text: brahmādisthāvarāntaṃ ca sarvaṃ liṅge pratiṣṭhitam // LiP_2,46.20 //
children.translated_text: everything from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable is established in the <s>liṅga</s>. (LiP 2,46.20)
Therefore, abandoning all else, one should install the imperishable <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: yatnena stāpitaṃ sarvaṃ pūjitaṃ pūjayedyadi // LiP_2,46.21 //
children.translated_text: If one worships everything that has been duly installed, [it is as if all is worshipped]. (LiP 2,46.21)
Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: iti niśamya kṛtāñjalaya stadā divi mahāmunayaḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the great sages with joined palms, with firm resolve,

children.text: śivataraṃ śivamīśvaramavyayaṃ manasi liṅgamayaṃ praṇipatya te // LiP_2,47.1 //
children.translated_text: bowed in their minds to <s>Śiva</s>, the most auspicious, the Lord imperishable, pervaded by the <s>liṅga</s>. (LiP 2,47.1)
The lord of all gods, the unborn lord <s>Hari</s>, lord of all, by the preceptor himself,

children.text: munivarāśca gaṇāśca surāsurā naravarāḥ śivaliṅgamayāḥ punaḥ // LiP_2,47.2 //
children.translated_text: and the chief sages, the <s>gaṇas</s>, gods, demons, and best of men — all became pervaded by the <s>Śiva-liṅga</s>. (LiP 2,47.2)
Having heard thus, all the sages of the six families, with concentration,

children.text: saṃtyajya sarvaṃ devasya pratiṣṭhāṃ kartumudyatāḥ // LiP_2,47.3 //
children.translated_text: renouncing everything, became determined to perform the installation of the god. (LiP 2,47.3)
They asked the sinless <s>Sūta</s> with voices choked with joy

children.text: liṅgapratiṣṭhāṃ vipulāṃ sarve te śaṃsitavratāḥ // LiP_2,47.4 //
children.translated_text: about the extensive <s>liṅga</s>-installation — all those of praised vows. (LiP 2,47.4)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall describe to you the installation of the <s>liṅga</s>-form, properly and in sequence,
briefly, for the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation. (LiP 2,47.5)

children.text: kṛtvaiva liṅgaṃ vidhinā bhuvi liṅgeṣu yatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>liṅga</s> according to the rule, among <s>liṅgas</s> on earth, with care —
a supreme <s>liṅga</s> of stone, embodying <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>, (LiP 2,47.6)

children.text: hemaratnamayaṃ vāpi rājataṃ tāmrajaṃ tu vā /
children.translated_text: or made of gold and gems, or of silver, or produced from copper,
with a pedestal, with the sacred thread [line], with a well-expanded head. (LiP 2,47.7)
Having purified it, one should install it with devotion — the supreme [<s>liṅga</s>] with its pedestal.

children.text: liṅgavedī umā devī liṅgaṃ sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ // LiP_2,47.8 //
children.translated_text: The pedestal of the <s>liṅga</s> is the goddess <s>Umā</s>; the <s>liṅga</s> itself is <s>Maheśvara</s>. (LiP 2,47.8)
By worshipping them both, the goddess and the god are [both] worshipped.

children.text: pratiṣṭhayā ca deveśo devyā sārdhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ // LiP_2,47.9 //
children.translated_text: By the installation, the Lord of Gods is established together with the Goddess. (LiP 2,47.9)
Therefore, the best installer should install the <s>liṅga</s> with its pedestal. (LiP 2,47.10)

children.text: mūle brahmā vasati bhagavānmadhyabhāge ca viṣṇuḥ sarveśānaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the base dwells lord <s>Brahmā</s>; in the middle portion, <s>Viṣṇu</s>; [at the top] the Lord of all,
<s>Paśupati</s>, the unborn <s>Rudra</s>-form, the most excellent.

children.text: tasmālliṅgaṃ gurutarataraṃ pūjayetsthāpayedvā yasmātpūjyo gaṇapatirasau devamukhyaiḥ samastaiḥ // LiP_2,47.11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should worship or install the <s>liṅga</s>, which is supremely weighty, since <s>Gaṇapati</s> (Śiva) is worshipped by all the chief gods together. (LiP 2,47.11)

children.text: gandhaiḥ sragdhūpadīpaiḥ snapanahutabalistotramantropahārairnityaṃ ye 'bhyarcayānti tridaśavaratanuṃ liṅgamūrtiṃ maheśam /
children.translated_text: Those who always worship with fragrances, garlands, incense, lamps, bathing, oblations, food-offerings, hymns, mantras, and gifts — the <s>liṅga</s>-form of <s>Maheśa</s>, whose body is the best of the gods —

children.text: garbhādhānādināśakṣayabhayarahitā devagandharvamukhyaiḥ siddhairvandyāśca pūjyā gaṇavaranamitāste bhavantyaprameyāḥ // LiP_2,47.12 //
children.translated_text: they become free from [the cycle of] conception and the rest, free from decay and fear, honoured and worshipped by the foremost gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, bowed to by the chief <s>gaṇas</s>, and immeasurable. (LiP 2,47.12)
Therefore, with devotional service, one should install <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord),
and worship especially the <s>liṅga</s>, for the accomplishment of all purposes. (LiP 2,47.13)
Having duly worshipped, one should install the <s>liṅga</s> in the midst of a sacred site, on a <s>Śiva</s>-seat,
covering the <s>liṅga</s> with <s>kūrca</s> grass, cloths, and the like, and with vessels (<s>kalaśas</s>). (LiP 2,47.14)
With deities beginning with the world-guardians, with <s>kūrcas</s>, with auspicious <s>akṣatas</s> (unbroken rice),
with raised <s>kūrcas</s>, <s>svastikas</s> and the like, wrapped with coloured threads, (LiP 2,47.15)
equipped with weapons beginning with the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), with cloths, with lids,
one should mark [the vessels] around the <s>liṅga</s> installed by the <s>Īśāna</s> [mantra]. (LiP 2,47.16)
Furnished with incense and lamps, with a canopy spread over the sky,
and with the banners of the world-guardians — [depicting] elephants, buffaloes, and the like — (LiP 2,47.17)
decorated and worshipped, with beautiful garlands of <s>darbha</s> grass —

children.text: sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā tayā bāhye ca veṣṭayet // LiP_2,47.18 //
children.translated_text: endowed with all auspicious marks — with that [cloth], one should wrap [it] on the outside. (LiP 2,47.18)
Then one should immerse [it] in water, accompanied by incense and lamps,

children.text: pañcāhaṃ vā tryahaṃvātha ekarātramadhāpi vā // LiP_2,47.19 //
children.translated_text: for five days, or three days, or for one night, or even [just briefly]. (LiP 2,47.19)
Endowed with <s>Veda</s>-recitation, with the auspicious [sounds of] dance, song, and the like,
accompanied by the tinkling of small bells, by the sounds of cymbals and <s>vīṇā</s>s as well, (LiP 2,47.20)
the sacrificer, undistracted, concentrated, should await the [auspicious] time.
Having raised [the image] up, one should meditate on the <s>svastika</s>, in a pavilion endowed with [all] marks, (LiP 2,47.21)
consecrated, furnished with an altar, enclosed by nine fire-pits,
endowed with the previously described rites, possessing all [auspicious] characteristics, (LiP 2,47.22)
furnished with eight <s>maṇḍalas</s>, accompanied by eight directional banners.
With fire-pits endowed with the previously described characteristics, beginning from the east, in order, (LiP 2,47.23)
the principal fire-pit in the northeast is prescribed as square.

children.text: athavā pañcakuṇḍaikaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ caikameva ca // LiP_2,47.24 //
children.translated_text: Or [one may use] five fire-pits and a single ground-altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) alone. (LiP 2,47.24)
With all the implements of sacrifice and the ornaments for <s>Śiva</s>-worship —
in the middle of the altar, a great bed fashioned of five layers of cotton, (LiP 2,47.25)
one should prepare [it], furnished with gold, covered with white cloth.
Having thus prepared, one should install <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2,47.26)
One should place the <s>liṅga</s> with its head facing east, with the <s>Īśāna</s> [mantra], according to the rule.

children.text: ratnanyāse kṛte pūrva kevalaṃ kalaśaṃ nyaset // LiP_2,47.27 //
children.translated_text: Having performed the gem-placement (<s>ratnanyāsa</s>) first, one should place the vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>) alone. (LiP 2,47.27)
Having covered the <s>liṅga</s> with two cloths and with a bunch of <s>kuśa</s> grass all around,

children.text: ratnanyāse prasakte 'tha vāmādyā nava śaktayaḥ // LiP_2,47.28 //
children.translated_text: while the gem-placement is in progress — the nine <s>śaktis</s> beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>, (LiP 2,47.28)
the nine gems, with gold and other [metals], combined with the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>) —
accompanied by all [other] gifts, one should place [them] on the stone [pedestal] as well. (LiP 2,47.29)
One should install the <s>Brahmaliṅga</s>, accompanied by the <s>Śiva-Gāyatrī</s>,
or with <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) alone, one should install the imperishable <s>Śiva</s>. (LiP 2,47.30)
With the mantra '<s>Brahma jajña</s>' (<s>Brahman</s> was born), the <s>Brahma</s>-portion of the Lord;

children.text: viṣṇugāyatriyā bhāgaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tvatha vinyaset // LiP_2,47.31 //
children.translated_text: with the <s>Viṣṇu-Gāyatrī</s>, one should then place the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> portion. (LiP 2,47.31)
On the thread endowed with the three principles, one should place [mantras] with <s>Praṇava</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ namaḥ śivāyeti namo haṃsaḥ śivāya ca // LiP_2,47.32 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya</s>' for everything; and '<s>Namo Haṃsaḥ Śivāya</s>' as well. (LiP 2,47.32)

children.text: rudrādhyāyena vā sarvaṃ parimṛjya ca vinyaset /
children.translated_text: With the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, or [alternatively], having purified all, one should place [the mantras].
One should install the vessels all around, with the Brahmins. (LiP 2,47.33)
One should place all of them in the middle of the altar, accompanied by the previously described rites.

children.text: madhyakuṃbhe śivaṃ devīṃ dakṣiṇe parameśvarīm // LiP_2,47.34 //
children.translated_text: In the central vessel, [one should install] <s>Śiva</s>; the Goddess, <s>Parameśvarī</s>, on the right. (LiP 2,47.34)

children.text: skandaṃ tayośca madhye tu skandakuṃbhe sucitrite /
children.translated_text: In between those two, <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Skanda</s>-vessel, beautifully decorated.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ skandakuṃbhe vā īśakumbhe hariṃ tathā // LiP_2,47.35 //
children.translated_text: Or <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Skanda</s>-vessel, and <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) in the <s>Īśa</s>-vessel. (LiP 2,47.35)

children.text: athavā śivakuṃbhe ca brahmāṅgāni ca vinyaset /
children.translated_text: Or in the <s>Śiva</s>-vessel itself, one should place the limbs of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: śivo maheśvaraścaiva rudro viṣṇuḥ pitāmahaḥ // LiP_2,47.36 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Brahmā) — (LiP 2,47.36)
the <s>Brahmās</s> thus, in brief, with heart [mantras] and the rest — <s>Ambikā</s> [likewise].
One should place all in the middle of the altar, accompanied by the previously described rites. (LiP 2,47.37)
In the offering-tray (<s>vardhanī</s>), one should install the Goddess, having filled [it] with fragrant water.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ ratnaṃ śivakuṃbhe pravinyaset // LiP_2,47.38 //
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and gems — one should place in the <s>Śiva</s>-vessel. (LiP 2,47.38)
In the offering-tray as well, with effort, with the limb-[mantras] of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, O ones of good vows.
In the directional vessels filled with <s>Brahma-kūrca</s> [grass], the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (lords of knowledge), (LiP 2,47.39)
the gods beginning with <s>Ananta</s> and the rest — with <s>Praṇava</s> at the beginning and <s>namaḥ</s> at the end.
A new cloth for each vessel should be provided for the eight vessels. (LiP 2,47.40)
In the vessels of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, one should place gold, gems, and the like.
The fire-offering should be made in the order of the faces [of <s>Śiva</s>], and in the order of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> limbs. (LiP 2,47.41)
Everything from [the mantras] '<s>Jaya</s>' and so forth up to <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> should be performed as before.
One should bathe [the <s>liṅga</s>] with the <s>Śiva</s>-vessel, and with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> offering-tray. (LiP 2,47.42)
With the <s>Paitāmaha</s> (Brahmā's) vessel, the <s>Brahma</s>-portion especially.
With the vessels of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, one should bathe the Supreme Lord. (LiP 2,47.43)
One should place all the mantras, well-concentrated, as before.
Having performed the bathing, one should worship with a thousand [names] and such, as available. (LiP 2,47.44)
And the fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be given — a thousand <s>paṇas</s> is the best.

children.text: itareṣāṃ tadardhaṃ syāttadardhaṃ vā vidhīyate // LiP_2,47.45 //
children.translated_text: For the others, half of that would apply, or half of that is prescribed. (LiP 2,47.45)
Garments for the principal [deity], with land, ornaments, cows, and wealth.
And a festival should be conducted — <s>homa</s>, sacrifice, and <s>bali</s> (offerings) in sequence. (LiP 2,47.46)

children.text: navāhaṃ vāpi saptāhamekāhaṃ ca tryahaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: For nine days, or seven days, one day, or three days.
The <s>homa</s> is as previously described — daily worshipping <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (LiP 2,47.47)
The <s>homa</s> for the gods beginning with <s>Bhāskara</s> (the sun) is as before.

children.text: abhyantare tathā bāhye vahnau nityaṃ samarcayet // LiP_2,47.48 //
children.translated_text: Both internally and externally, one should always worship in the fire. (LiP 2,47.48)

children.text: ya evaṃ sthāpayelliṅgaṃ sa eva parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who thus installs the <s>liṅga</s> — he himself is <s>Parameśvara</s>.
By him, the hosts of gods, <s>Rudras</s>, sages, and <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) (LiP 2,47.49)
are installed and worshipped, [along with] the three worlds with all that moves and does not move. (LiP 2,47.50)

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge liṅgasthāpanaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, entitled 'The Installation of the <s>Liṅga</s>.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The installation of all the gods as well, in detail —
having arranged their respective fire-pits with their own mantras, one by one, (LiP 2,48.1)
one should install [them], having performed a festival, and worship according to the rule.

children.text: bhānoḥ pañcāgninā kāryaṃ dvādaśāgnikrameṇa vā // LiP_2,48.2 //
children.translated_text: For the Sun, it should be done with five fires, or in the sequence of twelve fires. (LiP 2,48.2)
All the fire-pits are circular, lotus-shaped, O ones of good vows.
For <s>Ambā</s> (the Mother Goddess), the fire-pit should be yoni-shaped; one offering-tray is prescribed. (LiP 2,48.3)
For all rites of the <s>Śaktis</s> (feminine powers), the yoni-shaped fire-pit is prescribed.
One should fashion the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of <s>Śambhu</s>, of all [deities] with effort,

children.text: sarve rudrāṃśajā yasmātsaṃkṣepeṇa vadāmi vaḥ // LiP_2,48.4 //
children.translated_text: since all are born as portions of <s>Rudra</s> — I shall tell you briefly. (LiP 2,48.4)
The variants of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>:
'We know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; we meditate on the one of purified speech;
may <s>Śiva</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.5)
'We know <s>Gaṇāmbikā</s>; we meditate on [her who grants] perfection of action;
may <s>Gaurī</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.6)
'We know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; we meditate on <s>Mahādeva</s>;
may <s>Rudra</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.7)
'We know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; we meditate on the one with a curved trunk;
may <s>Dantin</s> (the tusked one, Gaṇeśa) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.8)
'We know <s>Mahāsena</s>; we meditate on the one of purified speech;
may <s>Skanda</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.9)
'We know the sharp-horned one; we meditate on the one with Vedic feet;
may <s>Vṛṣa</s> (the bull, Nandin) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.10)
'We know the tawny-faced one; we meditate on the one with <s>Rudra</s>'s face;
may <s>Nandin</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.11)
'We know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; we meditate on <s>Vāsudeva</s>;
may <s>Viṣṇu</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.12)
'We know <s>Mahāmbikā</s>; we meditate on [her who grants] perfection of action;
may <s>Lakṣmī</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.13)
'We know the one who was raised up; we meditate on [her who belongs to] <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone;
may <s>Dharā</s> (the Earth) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.14)
'We know the son of <s>Vinatā</s>; we meditate on the golden-winged one;
may <s>Garuḍa</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.15)
'We know the lotus-born one; we meditate on the <s>Veda</s>-faced one;
may the Creator inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.16)
'We know the one born from <s>Śiva</s>'s mouth; we meditate on the one of divine form;
may <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.17)
'We know the king of gods; we meditate on the one with <s>vajra</s> in hand;
may <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.18)
'We know the eye of <s>Rudra</s>; we meditate on the one with <s>śakti</s> in hand;
may <s>Vahni</s> (Fire) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.19)
'We know the son of <s>Vivasvat</s>; we meditate on the one with staff in hand;
may <s>Yama</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.20)
'We know the night-roamer; we meditate on the one with sword in hand;
may <s>Nirṛti</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.21)
'We know the pure-handed one; we meditate on the one with noose in hand;
may <s>Varuṇa</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.22)
'We know the one whose life-breath is serpents; we meditate on the one with staff in hand;
may <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.23)
'We know the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>; we meditate on the one with mace in hand;
may <s>Yakṣa</s> (Kubera) inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.24)
'We know the lord of all; we meditate on the one with trident in hand;
may <s>Rudra</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.25)
'We know <s>Kātyāyanī</s>; we meditate on the virgin maiden;
may <s>Durgā</s> inspire us.' (LiP 2,48.26)
Thus, having differentiated the <s>Gāyatrī</s> in accordance with each respective deity,
one should worship and install [them] — their seat is said to be <s>Praṇava</s>. (LiP 2,48.27)
Or [one should install] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the incomparable, with the <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>, or —
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>, and the eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in sequence. (LiP 2,48.28)
One should install [them] with the deity's <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having prepared [everything] according to the rule.

children.text: vāsudevaḥ pradhānastu tataḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ svayam // LiP_2,48.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the principal; then <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> himself, (LiP 2,48.29)
<s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s> — these are the form-variations of the Lord.

children.text: bahūni vividhānīha tasya śāpodbhavāni ca // LiP_2,48.30 //
children.translated_text: Many and various are [His avatāras] here, born from curses and such. (LiP 2,48.30)

children.text: sarvāvarteṣu rūpāṇi jagatāṃ ca hitāya vai /
children.translated_text: In all the cosmic cycles, [His] forms are for the welfare of the worlds.

children.text: matsyaḥ kūrmo 'tha vārāho nārasiṃho 'tha vāmanaḥ // LiP_2,48.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Matsya</s> (Fish), <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise), <s>Varāha</s> (Boar), <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion), <s>Vāmana</s> (Dwarf), (LiP 2,48.31)

children.text: rāmo rāmaśca kṛṣṇaśca bauddhaḥ kalkī tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, [<s>Paraśu</s>]<s>rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, and <s>Kalkin</s> likewise.

children.text: tathānyāni na devasya hareḥ sāpodbhavāni ca // LiP_2,48.32 //
children.translated_text: And other [forms] of <s>Hari</s>, born from curses and such — (LiP 2,48.32)

children.text: teṣāmapi ca gāyatrīṃ kṛtvā stāpya ca pūjayet /
children.translated_text: for all of them too, having composed the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one should install and worship.
The secret [mantras] of the God of Gods, <s>Hari</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, (LiP 2,48.33)
the mystical sciences, the <s>yantras</s>, the mantra-<s>Upaniṣads</s>,
born from the five <s>Brahma</s>-limbs here, consisting of the five elements — (LiP 2,48.34)
'<s>Namo Nārāyaṇāya</s>' — this mantra is supremely beautiful.
The eight syllables of <s>Hari</s> here, with <s>Praṇava</s>, in brief. (LiP 2,48.35)

children.text: oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca /
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Namo Vāsudevāya</s>'; '<s>Namaḥ Saṃkarṣaṇāya ca</s>';

children.text: pradyumnāya pradhānāya aniruddhāya vai namaḥ // LiP_2,48.36 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Pradyumnāya Pradhānāya</s>'; '<s>Aniruddhāya vai Namaḥ</s>.' (LiP 2,48.36)
With each individual mantra, one should install the Supreme Lord.
The images (<s>bimbas</s>) of the God <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme — (LiP 2,48.37)
their installation and worship are like that of the <s>liṅga</s>, O best of sages.
With gem-placement and auspicious threads — for <s>Hari</s> as well. (LiP 2,48.38)
For immovable [images], one should perform everything; for movable ones too, in this manner, according to the rule.
One should perform the eye-opening ceremony for them, with the eye-mantra, O ones of good vows. (LiP 2,48.39)
Circumambulation of the consecrated ground, of the garden, and of the city,
and the water-immersion — as before, it has been described. (LiP 2,48.40)
The construction of the fire-pit and pavilion, and the lying-down [ceremony] is prescribed.
Having offered oblations with the nine-fire method, in nine fire-pits, according to the rule, (LiP 2,48.41)
or in five fire-pits, or in the principal one alone —
the divine installation, transmitted through the lineage, has been described. (LiP 2,48.42)
For stone-born images, or for painted ones as well,
the water-immersion has been described, and for the bull-lord (<s>Vṛṣendra</s>) it is proclaimed. (LiP 2,48.43)
In the installation of a temple, the installation is proclaimed [to be the same].
For every part of the temple, just as for the limbs of the body. (LiP 2,48.44)
The bull, the fire[-altar], the <s>Mātṛkās</s> (mother goddesses), <s>Vighneśa</s> (Gaṇeśa), and <s>Kumāra</s> (Skanda) — with effort;

children.text: śreṣṭhāṃ durgāṃ tathā caṇḍīṃ gāyatryā vai yathāvidhi // LiP_2,48.45 //
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>Durgā</s> and <s>Caṇḍī</s> — with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, according to the rule. (LiP 2,48.45)
One should install the supreme eight enclosures of <s>Śambhu</s>, beginning from the east.
The <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and others — one should place [them] as [attendants] of <s>Śambhu</s>. (LiP 2,48.46)

children.text: umā caṇḍī ca nandī ca mahākālo mahāmuniḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, the great sage,

children.text: vighneśvaro mahābhṛṅgī skandaḥ saumyāditaḥ kramāt // LiP_2,48.47 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vighneśvara</s>, <s>Mahābhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Skanda</s> — from the auspicious [northern direction] onward, in order. (LiP 2,48.47)
<s>Indra</s> and the other [guardians] in their respective positions, and <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Janārdana</s>,
and the field-guardian in the entrance-area — one should establish [them all] with effort. (LiP 2,48.48)
On the lion-throne, <s>Ananta</s> and the others, and the lords of <s>Vidyā</s> also, in order,
one should establish with <s>praṇava</s>, placing the secret limbs and the like in the lotus. (LiP 2,48.49)
Thus has been briefly stated the supreme [method of] movable-image installation,

children.text: sarveṣāmapi devānāṃ devīnāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ // LiP_2,48.50 //
children.translated_text: for all the gods and goddesses especially. (LiP 2,48.50)
Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The greatness of <s>Aghoreśa</s> was formerly told by you.
Please tell us about the worship and installation of the god, O illustrious one! (LiP 2,49.1)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
With the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra] endowed with the limb[-mantras], according to the rule, especially,
the <s>liṅga</s>-installation [should be performed] by the <s>liṅga</s>-installation procedure — not otherwise, O bulls among sages. (LiP 2,49.2)

children.text: tathāgnipūjāṃ vai kuryādyathā pūjā tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the fire-worship should be done, and the worship similarly.

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā // LiP_2,49.3 //
children.translated_text: A thousand [oblations], or half that, or one hundred and eight; (LiP 2,49.3)
the oblation should be made with sesame and gold, mixed with curds, honey, and ghee.
With ghee, barley flour, and sweets — this removes all suffering. (LiP 2,49.4)
Destruction of diseases — the sesame oblation is prosperity-giving.
By a thousand [oblations], great prosperity; by a hundred, destruction of disease. (LiP 2,49.5)
One becomes freed from all suffering by recitation, without doubt.
With one hundred and eight [recitations], three times daily, according to the rule; (LiP 2,49.6)
by one thousand and eight [oblations], within six months, assuredly,
supernatural powers arise — no doubt — and even sovereignty for kings. (LiP 2,49.7)

children.text: sahasreṇa jvaro yāti kṣīreṇa ca juhoti yam /
children.translated_text: By a thousand [oblations of milk], fever departs; one who offers with milk —

children.text: trikālaṃ māsamekaṃ tu sahasraṃ juhuyātpayaḥ // LiP_2,49.8 //
children.translated_text: three times daily for one month, a thousand [oblations of] milk — (LiP 2,49.8)
within a month, the supreme great fortune is accomplished for him.
And by a year-long oblation with honey, ghee, and curds — [it is accomplished]. (LiP 2,49.9)
By oblation of barley, milk, and ghee, or with rice of the <s>jāti</s> variety,
the blessed Lord <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, the Supreme Lord, is pleased. (LiP 2,49.10)
By curds[-oblation], nourishment for kings; by milk-oblation, peace.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsaṃ tu ghṛtaṃ hutvā sarvavyādhivināśanam // LiP_2,49.11 //
children.translated_text: By offering ghee for six months, destruction of all diseases. (LiP 2,49.11)
Consumption (<s>rājayakṣmā</s>) is destroyed by sesame-and-gold [oblation] within a year.

children.text: yavahomena cāyuṣyaṃ ghṛtena ca jayastadā // LiP_2,49.12 //
children.translated_text: By barley-oblation, longevity; by ghee, victory. (LiP 2,49.12)
For the destruction of all leprosy — with rice mixed with honey,
one should offer ten thousand [oblations] daily, for six months, always with discipline. (LiP 2,49.13)
Ghee, milk, and honey — this is called the 'triple sweet.'

children.text: samastaṃ tuṣyate tasya nāśayedvai bhagandaram // LiP_2,49.14 //
children.translated_text: When complete, [the god] is pleased, and it destroys fistula. (LiP 2,49.14)
By ghee-oblation alone, destruction of all diseases is remembered.

children.text: sarvavyādhi haraṃ dhyānaṃ sthāpanaṃ vidhinārcanam // LiP_2,49.15 //
children.translated_text: All-disease-removing meditation, installation, and worship according to the rule — (LiP 2,49.15)
thus has been briefly stated the installation and worship

children.text: pratiṣṭhā yajanaṃ sarvaṃ nandinā kathitaṃ purā // LiP_2,49.16 //
children.translated_text: of the great-souled <s>Aghora</s>, as was formerly told by <s>Nandin</s> (LiP 2,49.16)

children.text: brahmaputrāya śiṣyāya tena vyāsāya suvratāḥ // LiP_2,49.17 //
children.translated_text: to the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, his disciple, and by him to <s>Vyāsa</s>, O ones of good vows. (LiP 2,49.17)
Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The subjugation [rite] was told by him, by the mouth of <s>Śiva</s>, the trident-bearer.

children.text: kṛtāparāndhināṃ taṃ tu vaktumarhasi suvrata // LiP_2,50.1 //
children.translated_text: Tell us of the [rite] for those who have committed offenses, O one of good vows! (LiP 2,50.1)

children.text: tvayā navidinaṃ nāsti laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Nothing is unknown to you, whether worldly or Vedic,

children.text: śrautaṃ smārtaṃ mahābhāga romaharṣaṇa suvrata // LiP_2,50.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrauta</s> or <s>Smārta</s>, O illustrious <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>, O one of good vows! (LiP 2,50.2)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, the subjugation [rite] was told by the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> to <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, O ones of good vows —
by <s>Śukra</s>, the disciple of <s>Aghora</s>, of inexhaustible splendor. (LiP 2,50.3)
By his grace, the lord of <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, the valorous one,
having conquered the entire triple world — gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and humans, (LiP 2,50.4)
having produced a son, the lord of hosts, <s>Andhaka</s>, of beautiful prowess,

children.text: rarāja loke devena varāheṇa niṣūditaḥ // LiP_2,50.5 //
children.translated_text: he shone in the world, [but was eventually] slain by the god <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar). (LiP 2,50.5)
There is no victory on this earth by this path for one who oppresses

children.text: kurvato nāsti vijayo mārgeṇānena bhūtale // LiP_2,50.6 //
children.translated_text: women, children, and cows especially. (LiP 2,50.6)

children.text: tena daityena sā devī dharā nītā rasātalam /
children.translated_text: That <s>Daitya</s> carried the Goddess Earth down to the netherworld;

children.text: tenāghoreṇa devena niṣphalo nigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ // LiP_2,50.7 //
children.translated_text: by that <s>Aghora</s> god, the subjugation [rite] was rendered fruitless [against him]. (LiP 2,50.7)
At the end of a thousand years, he was slain by the Boar.
Therefore, for the success of <s>Aghora</s> [rites], one should never oppress brahmins, (LiP 2,50.8)
nor women especially, nor should one [harm] cows.
The most secret of the secret, guarded [teaching], exceedingly secret — I tell you: (LiP 2,50.9)
it should be directed against an aggressor, and performed by the best of kings.

children.text: brāhmaṇebhyo na kartavyaṃ svarāṣṭreśasya vā punaḥ // LiP_2,50.10 //
children.translated_text: It should not be done against brahmins, nor against one's own king. (LiP 2,50.10)
When an exceedingly invincible army arrives, when all forces are destroyed,
when unrighteous warfare has come — one should perform the supreme rite. (LiP 2,50.11)
It should be performed without pity, and he should cause it to be done without pity.

children.text: kṛtamātre na saṃdeho nigrahaḥ saṃprajāyate // LiP_2,50.12 //
children.translated_text: Once performed, without doubt, the subjugation manifests. (LiP 2,50.12)
Having recited one hundred thousand [times] the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra] of terrible form,

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ vidhinā hutvā tilena dvijasattamāḥ // LiP_2,50.13 //
children.translated_text: and offering a tenth of that as oblation with sesame, according to the rule, O best of twice-born, (LiP 2,50.13)
having worshipped with a hundred thousand white flowers, according to the rule,
on a <s>bāṇaliṅga</s> or in the fire, relying on the south-facing form (<s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>) — (LiP 2,50.14)
one whose mantra is perfected — there is no other [requirement]; the seer [sees] the perfections and the like.
The mantra-perfected one himself should perform [the rite] especially in a cremation ground, (LiP 2,50.15)
or at a Mother-shrine (<s>Mātṛsthāna</s>), the learned one versed in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>,

children.text: kevalaṃ mantrasiddho vā brāhmaṇaḥ śivabhāvitaḥ // LiP_2,50.16 //
children.translated_text: or simply a brahmin perfected in mantra, imbued with <s>Śiva</s>-consciousness. (LiP 2,50.16)
The wise one should perform this rite for his own purpose or for the king's.
The learned one should place eight tridents from east through northeast. (LiP 2,50.17)
Three-pointed and trident[-shaped], with twenty-four points at the tip,
having made the <s>Aghora</s> form, with body tightly bound, (LiP 2,50.18)
meditating on the all-destroying one, he should perform all the rites.
Resembling crores of <s>Kālāgni</s> (fire of dissolution), one should also visualize one's own body [thus]. (LiP 2,50.19)

children.text: śūlaṃ kapālaṃ pāśaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ caiva śarāsanam /
children.translated_text: A trident, a skull, a noose, a staff, and a bow,
an arrow, a <s>ḍamaru</s> drum, a sword — the eight weapons in order. (LiP 2,50.20)
Eight-armed, boon-granting, blue-throated, sky-clad (<s>digambara</s>),
mounted on the five principles, bearing the half-moon, the Lord. (LiP 2,50.21)
With fangs bared in a terrifying face, with a fierce gaze, fearsome,
with the great sound of '<s>Huṃ Phaṭ</s>' resounding in all directions. (LiP 2,50.22)
Three-eyed, with a crown well-bound with a serpent-noose,
furnished with all ornaments, covered with the ash of corpses. (LiP 2,50.23)
Surrounded by ghosts, spirits, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
wearing an elephant-skin, adorned with serpent-ornaments. (LiP 2,50.24)
With scorpion-ornaments, the god, rumbling like a dark rain cloud,
resembling a mountain of dark collyrium, with a lion-skin as upper garment. (LiP 2,50.25)
One should meditate on this <s>Aghoreśa</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, more terrible than the terrible.
With thirty-six measured <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>, O ones of good vows, (LiP 2,50.26)
equipped with the great <s>mudrā</s>, one should perform all the rites.
One perfected in mantra, at a cremation-fire or in a cremation ground, according to the rule, (LiP 2,50.27)

children.text: sthāpayenmadhyadeśe tu eendre yāmye ca vāruṇe /
children.translated_text: should establish [fire-pits] in the central area, in the <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> [directions],
and in the <s>Kubera</s> [direction], having made the fire-pits according to the rules. (LiP 2,50.28)

children.text: ācāryo madhyakuṇḍe tu sādhakāśca diśāsu vai /
children.translated_text: The <s>ācārya</s> [should be] at the central fire-pit, and the practitioners in the [directional] quarters.
Having spread [the area] with reversed [grass], equipped with the trident as before, (LiP 2,50.29)
seated in the midst of the <s>Kālāgni</s> pedestal, himself and with similar disciples,
meditating on the terrible <s>Aghoreśa</s>, endowed with thirty-two syllables, (LiP 2,50.30)
having made [an effigy] with <s>vibhītaka</s> (belleric myrobalan) wood, twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> in size,

children.text: pīṭhe nyasya nṛpendrasya śatrumaṅgārakeṇa tu // LiP_2,50.31 //
children.translated_text: placing [it on] the pedestal, [representing] the king's enemy, with charcoal — (LiP 2,50.31)
the brahmin, overcome with wrath, should bury the enemy [effigy] below the fire-pit,
face-down, feet-up, in all the fire-pits, with effort. (LiP 2,50.32)
Having brought charcoal from a cremation ground, one should burn [the effigy] with husk.
Silently, devoted to celibacy, one should establish the fire there. (LiP 2,50.33)
With the <s>Māyūrāstra</s> [mantra], at the navel, one should kindle the flame.
A jacket-covering, mixed with husks, with cotton-seeds, (LiP 2,50.34)
equal to red cloth, mixed with gold substances especially,

children.text: hastayantrodbhavaistailaiḥ saha homaṃ tu kārayet // LiP_2,50.35 //
children.translated_text: with oils from hand-pressed [seeds] — one should perform the oblation. (LiP 2,50.35)
One thousand and eight [oblations] should be offered in sequence.
Beginning on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, in proper order, (LiP 2,50.36)
up to the eighth [day], free from the charcoal-<s>maṇḍala</s> area.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte nṛpendrasya śatravaḥ kulajaiḥ saha // LiP_2,50.37 //
children.translated_text: When thus performed, the king's enemies, together with their kinsmen, (LiP 2,50.37)
afflicted with all suffering, go to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: mantreṇānena cādāya nṛkapāle nakhaṃ tathā // LiP_2,50.38 //
children.translated_text: With this mantra, taking [items] in a human skull, along with nail-clippings, (LiP 2,50.38)

children.text: keśaṃ nṛṇāṃ tathāṅgāraṃ tuṣaṃ kañcukameva ca /
children.translated_text: human hair, charcoal, husk, and a jacket,
strips of bark, royal dust or house-sweepings, (LiP 2,50.39)
the teeth of a poisonous serpent, the teeth of a bull,

children.text: gavāṃ caiva krameṇaiva vyāghradantanakhāni ca // LiP_2,50.40 //
children.translated_text: and of cows, in order, and tiger teeth and claws, (LiP 2,50.40)

children.text: tathā kṛṣṇamṛgāṇāṃ ca biḍālasya ca pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: and of black deer, and of a cat, as before,

children.text: nakulasya ca dantāni varāhasya viśeṣataḥ // LiP_2,50.41 //
children.translated_text: and the teeth of a mongoose, and especially of a boar — (LiP 2,50.41)
having empowered the fangs with this mantra, O ones of good vows,
one should recite the supreme <s>Aghora</s> mantra one hundred and eight times. (LiP 2,50.42)

children.text: tatkapālaṃ nakhaṃ kṣetre gṛhe vā nagare 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: That skull and nail [should be placed] in a field, a house, or a city,

children.text: pretasthāne 'pi vā rāṣṭre mṛtavastreṇa veṣṭayet // LiP_2,50.43 //
children.translated_text: or at a cremation ground, or in the [enemy's] kingdom, wrapped in a death-shroud. (LiP 2,50.43)
When the sun is eclipsed in the enemy's eighth astrological house,

children.text: some vā pariviṣṭe tu mantreṇānena suvratāḥ // LiP_2,50.44 //
children.translated_text: or when the moon is eclipsed — with this mantra, O ones of good vows, (LiP 2,50.44)
destruction of his position occurs; the enemy's annihilation comes about.

children.text: śatruṃ rājñaḥ samālikhya gamane samavasthite // LiP_2,50.45 //
children.translated_text: Having drawn [an image of] the king's enemy, stationed in departure, (LiP 2,50.45)
on the ground as bright as a mirror, adorned with a canopy above,
furnished with four gateways, surrounded by garlands of <s>darbha</s> grass, (LiP 2,50.46)
rich in Vedic chanting, in a kingdom manifesting prosperity —

children.text: dakṣiṇena tu pādena mūrdhni saṃtāḍayetsvayam // LiP_2,50.47 //
children.translated_text: one should strike [the effigy's] head with one's own right foot. (LiP 2,50.47)
When thus done, the king's enemies will be destroyed.
One who performs sorcery (<s>ābhicārika</s>) against one's own king — (LiP 2,50.48)
that evil-minded one, having destroyed himself, will destroy his own family.
Therefore, one should always protect the king who protects one's own kingdom. (LiP 2,50.49)
With mantras, herbs, rituals, and the like — with all effort, always.

children.text: etadrahasyaṃ kathitaṃ na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit // LiP_2,50.50 //
children.translated_text: This secret has been told — it should not be given to just anyone. (LiP 2,50.50)
Thus ends the fiftieth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The subjugation in the form of <s>Aghora</s> has been told to us, the supreme [teaching].
