Please tell us the <s>Vajravāhanikā Vidyā</s> (Thunderbolt Vehicle Science), O best one! (LiP 2,51.1)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The <s>Vajravāhanikā</s> by name, frightening to all enemies —
with it, one should consecrate the thunderbolt and empower it for kings. (LiP 2,51.2)
Having made the thunderbolt according to the rule and having consecrated it —
With this <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge), one should install [the weapon] there with gold. (LiP 2.51.3)
Then the learned one, concentrated, should recite one hundred thousand syllables.
The <s>vajra</s>-holder should offer one-tenth into the <s>vajra-kuṇḍa</s> (diamond fire-pit) with ghee and the like. (LiP 2.51.4)
One should always protect that <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) and then have the king bear it.
Going forth with that <s>vajra</s>, one would conquer enemies on the battlefield. (LiP 2.51.5)

children.text: purā pitā mahenaiva labdhā vidyā prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: In ancient times, this <s>vidyā</s> was obtained with effort by the great father [<s>Brahmā</s>],
O <s>Devī</s>, for the purpose of aiding <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — [it is] the very <s>Vajreśvarī</s> (Mistress of the Thunderbolt). (LiP 2.51.6)
In ancient times, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the lord of creatures, whose son was slain by the lord of the gods,
carried away the <s>Soma</s> by means of a <s>vidyā</s>, out of enmity toward <s>Indra</s>, O virtuous ones. (LiP 2.51.7)
In that sacrifice, the oblation that had been obtained and offered by the learned one —
the mighty-armed one, the crusher of <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, desired it. (LiP 2.51.8)

children.text: matputramavadhīḥ śakra na dāsye tava śobhanam /
children.translated_text: "You have slain my son, O <s>Śakra</s>! I shall not give you the splendid

children.text: bhāgaṃ bhāgārhatā naiva viśvarūpo hatastvayā // LiP_2,51.9 //
children.translated_text: share, though you are worthy of a share. <s>Viśvarūpa</s> was slain by you!" (LiP 2.51.9)
Having said this, he bewildered the entire hermitage with <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
Then, breaking through the <s>māyā</s>, the crusher of <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, (LiP 2.51.10)
the consort of <s>Śacī</s>, forcibly drank the <s>Soma</s> together with his troops.
Then, taking the remainder, the <s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>), seized with anger, (LiP 2.51.11)

children.text: indrasya śatro vardhasva svāhetyagnau juhāva ha /
children.translated_text: poured an oblation into the fire saying, "O enemy of <s>Indra</s>, grow! <s>Svāhā</s>!"
Then, resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution, called <s>Vṛtra</s> because of his rolling [advance], (LiP 2.51.12)
there appeared an enemy of the lord of the gods, the destroyer of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (<s>Indra</s>), who charged forth.

children.text: tataḥ kirīṭī bhagavānparityajya divaṃ kṣaṇāt // LiP_2,51.13 //
children.translated_text: Then the glorious, crowned [<s>Indra</s>], abandoning heaven in an instant, (LiP 2.51.13)
the thousand-eyed one, fled with his troops, overwhelmed by fear.

children.text: tadā tamāha sa vibhṛrhṛṣṭo brahmā ca viśvasṛṭ // LiP_2,51.14 //
children.translated_text: Then the resplendent <s>Brahmā</s>, creator of the universe, spoke to him with delight: (LiP 2.51.14)
"Having cast that <s>vajra</s>, slay [him] with it, O subduer of foes!"

children.text: so 'pi sannahya devendro devaiḥ sārdhaṃ mahābhujaḥ // LiP_2,51.15 //
children.translated_text: Then that lord of the gods, the mighty-armed <s>Indra</s>, arming himself along with the gods, (LiP 2.51.15)
slew [<s>Vṛtra</s>] effortlessly and departed, free from distress.
Therefore, the <s>Vajreśvarī vidyā</s> is the terrifier of all enemies. (LiP 2.51.16)

children.text: mandehā rākṣasā nityaṃ vijitā vidyayaiva tu /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mandeha</s> <s>Rākṣasas</s> are always conquered by this <s>vidyā</s> alone.
I shall now declare that <s>vidyā</s> which liberates from all sins: (LiP 2.51.17)

children.text: oṃ bhūrbhuvasvaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi /

children.translated_text: <s>Dhiyo Yo Naḥ Pracodayāt</s>!

children.text: oṃ phaṭ jahi huṃ phaṭ chindhi bhindhi jahi hanahana svāhā /
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Phaṭ</s>! Slay! <s>Huṃ Phaṭ</s>! Cut! Pierce! Slay! Kill, kill! <s>Svāhā</s>!"
This is the <s>Vajreśvarī vidyā</s>, the terrifier of all enemies.
By this <s>vidyā</s>, O best of sages, is the destructive power of <s>Śambhu</s>. (LiP 2.51.18)
"Oṃ <s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ</s>! <s>Tat Savitur Vareṇyaṃ Bhargo Devasya Dhīmahi</s>,
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
"We have heard the <s>Vajreśvarī vidyā</s>, the <s>Brāhmī</s> [mantra] that aids <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>).

children.text: anayā sarvakāryāṇi nṛpāmāmiti naḥ śrutam // LiP_2,52.1 //
children.translated_text: We have heard that all undertakings of kings are [accomplished] by this. (LiP 2.52.1)
Tell us the application (<s>viniyoga</s>) of this <s>vidyā</s>, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>!"
<s>Sūta</s> said:
"Subjugation (<s>vaśya</s>) and attraction (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>), and beyond that, enmity-creation (<s>vidveṣaṇa</s>), (LiP 2.52.2)

children.text: uccāṭanaṃ staṃbhanaṃ ca mohanaṃ tāḍanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: expulsion (<s>uccāṭana</s>), paralysis (<s>stambhana</s>), delusion (<s>mohana</s>), and striking (<s>tāḍana</s>),

children.text: utsādanaṃ tathā chedaṃ māraṇaṃ pratibandhanam // LiP_2,52.3 //
children.translated_text: destruction (<s>utsādana</s>), cutting (<s>cheda</s>), killing (<s>māraṇa</s>), and obstruction (<s>pratibandha</s>), (LiP 2.52.3)
army-paralysis and the rest — all these should be performed with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: āgaccha varade devi bhūmyāṃ parvatamūrdhani // LiP_2,52.4 //
children.translated_text: "Come, O boon-granting goddess, upon the earth, upon the mountain-top!" (LiP 2.52.4)
"Being permitted by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, go, O goddess, at your pleasure!"

children.text: udvāsyānena mantreṇa gantavyaṃ nānyathā dvijāḥ // LiP_2,52.5 //
children.translated_text: Having dismissed [her] with this mantra, one should depart; not otherwise, O twice-born ones. (LiP 2.52.5)

children.text: pratikāryaṃ tathā bāhyaṃ kṛtvā paśyādikāṃ kriyām /
children.translated_text: Having performed the counter-ritual and also the external rite, such as the animal-offering and others,
having dismissed [the goddess] and having established the fire again according to rule, (LiP 2.52.6)
having invoked the goddess again, one should recite and worship again,

children.text: homaṃ ca vidhinā vahnau punareva samācaret // LiP_2,52.7 //
children.translated_text: and one should perform the <s>homa</s> into the fire again according to the prescribed method. (LiP 2.52.7)
All undertakings should be accomplished with the <s>vidyā</s> according to the prescribed method.
One desiring subjugation should offer thirty thousand [oblations] with <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers. (LiP 2.52.8)
With ghee and <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), one should perform attraction, O twice-born ones.
One should especially perform enmity-creation with [the flower of] the <s>lāṅgalaka</s> (plough-shaped plant). (LiP 2.52.9)
Expulsion is declared [to be performed] with oil; paralysis is prescribed with honey.

children.text: tilena mohanaṃ proktaṃ tāḍanaṃ rudhireṇa ca // LiP_2,52.10 //
children.translated_text: Delusion is declared [to be performed] with sesame; striking with blood — (LiP 2.52.10)

children.text: kharasya ca gajasyātha uṣṭrasya ca yathākramam /
children.translated_text: of a donkey, an elephant, and a camel, respectively.

children.text: staṃbhanaṃ sarṣapeṇāpi pāṭanaṃ cākuśena ca // LiP_2,52.11 //
children.translated_text: Paralysis [is also performed] with mustard, and splitting with <s>kuśa</s> [grass]. (LiP 2.52.11)
Killing and expulsion [are performed] with <s>rohī</s> seeds, O virtuous ones.
Binding with serpent-leaf, and beyond that, army-paralysis — (LiP 2.52.12)
one should know [it is performed] with <s>kunaṭī</s>, restrainedly; one should worship the Supreme Goddess.

children.text: ghṛtena sarvasiddhiḥ syātpayasā vā viśuddhyate // LiP_2,52.13 //
children.translated_text: With ghee, all <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) arise; with milk, one becomes purified. (LiP 2.52.13)
With sesame, diseases are destroyed; with lotus, wealth accrues.
Beauty [comes] with <s>madhūka</s> flowers — [all these] with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, thirty thousand [oblations]. (LiP 2.52.14)
All [rites] beginning with <s>Jayā</s> and ending with <s>Sviṣṭa</s> are as previously prescribed.
Thus in brief has been declared the application, though [it is] very extensive. (LiP 2.52.15)

children.text: japedvā kevalāṃ vidyāṃ saṃpūjya ca vidhānataḥ /
children.translated_text: Or one may recite the <s>vidyā</s> alone, having worshipped according to the prescribed method.
One attains all <s>siddhis</s>; no deliberation is needed here. (LiP 2.52.16)
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
"O <s>Sūta</s>, please tell us the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> (death-conquering) rite for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s> as well.
You are omniscient, O great wise one!" (LiP 2.53.1)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
"I shall declare the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> rite. What need of many words, O best of twice-born ones?

children.text: rudrādhyāyena vidhinā ghṛtena niyutaṃ kramāt // LiP_2,53.2 //
children.translated_text: With the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, according to the prescribed method, with ghee, one million [oblations] in due order, (LiP 2.53.2)
with sesame mixed with ghee, with lotus, with effort,
with <s>dūrvā</s> grass mixed with ghee, cow's milk, and honey, (LiP 2.53.3)
with <s>caru</s> (cooked rice) mixed with ghee alone, or with milk alone,
one should offer. This is declared as the counteraction against untimely death." (LiP 2.53.4)
Thus ends the fifty-third chapter in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
"With the <s>Tryambaka</s> mantra, one should worship the god of gods, <s>Tryambaka</s> (the Three-eyed One),

children.text: pūjayedbāṇaliṅge vā svayaṃbhūte 'pi vā punaḥ // LiP_2,54.1 //
children.translated_text: at a <s>Bāṇaliṅga</s> or at a self-manifested [<s>liṅga</s>]. (LiP 2.54.1)
Or by those learned in <s>Āyurveda</s>, properly, in due succession,
one should [worship] <s>Śaṅkara</s> with one thousand and eight lotuses (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>), (LiP 2.54.2)
with a thousand lotuses, or with blue water-lilies (<s>nīlotpala</s>).

children.text: saṃpūjya pāyasaṃ dattvā saghṛtaṃ caudanaṃ punaḥ // LiP_2,54.3 //
children.translated_text: Having worshipped, one should offer <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) and again rice with ghee, (LiP 2.54.3)

children.text: mudgānnaṃ madhunā yuktaṃ bhakṣyāṇi surabhīṇi ca /
children.translated_text: <s>mudga</s> (mung bean) rice mixed with honey, and fragrant delicacies.
The <s>homa</s> into the fire should be abundant, properly, in due succession, (LiP 2.54.4)
with the aforementioned flowers and especially with <s>caru</s> (cooked rice).

children.text: japedvai niyutaṃ samyak samāpya ca yathākramam // LiP_2,54.5 //
children.translated_text: One should recite properly one million [times], completing [the rite] in due order. (LiP 2.54.5)
One should feed a thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> together with gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).

children.text: gavāṃ sahasraṃ dattvā tu hiraṇyamapi dāpayet // LiP_2,54.6 //
children.translated_text: Having given a thousand cows, one should also gift gold. (LiP 2.54.6)
All this has been told to you, including the secret teaching, in summary.
By <s>Śiva</s>, the god of gods, <s>Śarva</s>, the bearer of the terrible trident, (LiP 2.54.7)
[it was] told on the peak of <s>Meru</s> to <s>Skanda</s> of immeasurable brilliance.
By <s>Skanda</s>, the god of gods, [it was told] to the wise son of <s>Brahmā</s> — (LiP 2.54.8)
by the venerable <s>Sanatkumāra</s> himself, who desires the welfare of all worlds,
[it was] told to <s>Pārāśarya</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>), having come down through the succession of tradition. (LiP 2.54.9)

children.text: śuke gate parandhāma dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ triyaṃbakam /
children.translated_text: When <s>Śuka</s> went to the supreme abode, having beheld <s>Rudra Tryambaka</s>,

children.text: gataśoko mahābhāgo vyasaḥ para ṛṣiḥ prabhuḥ // LiP_2,54.10 //
children.translated_text: the great-fortuned <s>Vyāsa</s>, the supreme sage and lord, became free from sorrow. (LiP 2.54.10)

children.text: skandasya saṃbhavaṃ śrutvā sthitāya ca mahātmane /
children.translated_text: Having heard of the birth of <s>Skanda</s> and [how he] remained as the great soul,

children.text: triyaṃbakasya māhātmyaṃ mantrasya ca viśeṣataḥ // LiP_2,54.11 //
children.translated_text: the greatness of <s>Tryambaka</s> and especially of the mantra — (LiP 2.54.11)
[all this was] told in many ways to that <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>).

children.text: tatsakvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi prasādādeva tasya vai // LiP_2,54.12 //
children.translated_text: I shall narrate that same [teaching], by the grace of that [sage] indeed. (LiP 2.54.12)
Having worshipped the god according to the prescribed method, one should recite the <s>Tryambaka</s> mantra.
One is freed even from the sins of seven births, including the sin of serpent-slaying. (LiP 2.54.13)
Having obtained all that in battle, incomparable good fortune arises.

children.text: lakṣahomena rājyārthī rājyaṃ labdhvā sukhī bhavet // LiP_2,54.14 //
children.translated_text: One desiring a kingdom, through a hundred thousand <s>homas</s>, obtains a kingdom and becomes happy. (LiP 2.54.14)
One desiring a son obtains a son through one million [recitations], without doubt.

children.text: dhanārthī prayutenaiva japedeva na saṃśayaḥ // LiP_2,54.15 //
children.translated_text: One desiring wealth should indeed recite ten million [times], without doubt. (LiP 2.54.15)
Filled with wealth, grain, and all auspicious things,

children.text: krīḍate putrapautraiśca mṛtaḥ svarge prajāyate // LiP_2,54.16 //
children.translated_text: one sports with sons and grandsons, and after death is born in heaven. (LiP 2.54.16)

children.text: nānena sadṛśo mantro loke vede ca suvratāḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no mantra equal to this in the world or in the <s>Vedas</s>, O virtuous ones.

children.text: tasmāttriyaṃbakaṃ devaṃ tena nityaṃ prapūjayet // LiP_2,54.17 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should always worship the god <s>Tryambaka</s> with that [mantra]. (LiP 2.54.17)
The fruit is eight times that of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice.

children.text: trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ guṇānāmapi yaḥ prabhuḥ // LiP_2,54.18 //
children.translated_text: He who is the lord of the three worlds and of the three <s>guṇas</s>, (LiP 2.54.18)
of the <s>Vedas</s>, of the gods, and of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s>,
the signifier of the syllables 'a', 'u', and 'ma' and of the [Vedic] metres — (LiP 2.54.19)
and likewise of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Agni</s>, and of the three fires,

children.text: aṃbā umā mahādevo hyaṃbakastu triyaṃbakaḥ // LiP_2,54.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ambā</s>, <s>Umā</s>, and <s>Mahādeva</s> — [these are] the three 'eyes' (<s>ambaka</s>), hence <s>Tryambaka</s>. (LiP 2.54.20)
Just as the beautiful fragrance of a fully blossoming tree

children.text: vāti dvarāttathā tasya gandhaḥ śaṃbhormahātmanaḥ // LiP_2,54.21 //
children.translated_text: wafts from its trunk, so [does] the fragrance of <s>Śambhu</s>, the great soul. (LiP 2.54.21)
Therefore the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s> is 'the fragrant one' who bears fragrance.
<s>Mahādeva</s> is also called <s>Gāndhāra</s> ('fragrance-bearer'), playfully among the gods. (LiP 2.54.22)
His sweet fragrance in this world — the wind blows it across the sky.
Therefore one should [worship] that sweet-smelling god, the enhancer of nourishment (<s>puṣṭivardhanam</s>). (LiP 2.54.23)
Whose seed, formerly — <s>Śambhu's</s> — was placed in the womb of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Agni</s>),
from whose virility arose the golden egg, born of the Unborn One — (LiP 2.54.24)
the Moon, the Sun with the stars, <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>,
and <s>Satyaloka</s> — transcending [all these] is the nourishing power of his virility. (LiP 2.54.25)
The five elements, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and <s>Prakṛti</s> (Primordial Nature) —
the nourishment of that very seed [produces all these]; therefore he is the 'Enhancer of Nourishment' (<s>Puṣṭivardhana</s>). (LiP 2.54.26)

children.text: taṃ puṣṭivardhanaṃ devaṃ ghṛtena payasā tathā /
children.translated_text: That nourishment-enhancing god — with ghee and milk,
with honey, barley, wheat, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), and <s>bilva</s> fruit, (LiP 2.54.27)
with <s>kumuda</s> (night-lily), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>śamī</s> leaves, white mustard, and rice,

children.text: hutvā liṅge yathānyāyaṃ bhaktyā devaṃ yajāmahe // LiP_2,54.28 //
children.translated_text: having offered into the <s>liṅga</s> as is proper — with devotion let us worship the god. (LiP 2.54.28)
"By this truth (<s>ṛta</s>), [free] me from the bondage of <s>pāśa</s> (fetters), from the bond of <s>karma</s>,

children.text: mṛtyośca bandanāccaiva mukṣīya bhava tejasā // LiP_2,54.29 //
children.translated_text: and from the bond of death — may I be liberated, O <s>Bhava</s>, by [your] splendor!" (LiP 2.54.29)
Just as ripe cucumbers (<s>urvāruka</s>) [are released] from [their stalks] in due time,

children.text: tathaiva kālaḥ saṃprāpto manunā tena yatnataḥ // LiP_2,54.30 //
children.translated_text: so too, when the time has arrived, [one is released] — by that mantra with effort. (LiP 2.54.30)
Thus, knowing the mantra-rite, one should worship the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>.
For such a <s>yogin</s>, the destruction of fetters (<s>pāśa</s>) is supreme, and death is conquered. (LiP 2.54.31)
There is no god equal to <s>Tryambaka</s>, endowed with compassion,

children.text: prasādaśīlaḥ prītaśca tathā mantropi suvratāḥ // LiP_2,54.32 //
children.translated_text: inclined to grace and delighted — and likewise [there is no equal] mantra, O virtuous ones. (LiP 2.54.32)
Therefore, abandoning everything else, [one should worship] <s>Tryambaka</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
with the <s>Tryambaka</s> mantra, fully concentrated. (LiP 2.54.33)
Even in whatever state one may be, one is freed from all sins.

children.text: śivadhyānānna saṃdeho yathā rudrastathā svayam // LiP_2,54.34 //
children.translated_text: By meditating on <s>Śiva</s>, there is no doubt — one becomes like <s>Rudra</s> himself. (LiP 2.54.34)

children.text: hatvā bhittvā ca bhūtāni bhuktvā cānyāyato 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Having killed and pierced beings, having enjoyed [things] even unjustly,
by remembering <s>Śiva</s> alone even once, one is freed from all sins. (LiP 2.54.35)
Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
"How is the god <s>Tryambaka</s>, the god of gods, the bull-bannered one,
He should be meditated upon for the accomplishment of all purposes, through the path of <s>yoga</s>, O one of good vows. (LiP 2.55.1)
All this has been heard before, equal to the <s>Śruti</s>.
Please tell all of that in detail and briefly. (LiP 2.55.2)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus <s>Nandin</s>, radiant as the sun, [was asked] by the <s>Paitāmaha</s> (<s>Sanatkumāra</s>),

children.text: merupṛṣṭhe purā pṛṣṭo munisaṃghaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ // LiP_2,55.3 //
children.translated_text: formerly, on the summit of <s>Meru</s>, questioned while surrounded by hosts of sages. (LiP 2.55.3)
He too, to that <s>Kumāra</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, O ones of good vows,
spoke in confidence, the blessed one, to him who bowed with concentration. (LiP 2.55.4)
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Thus formerly, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s> (Blue-and-Red One),
sharing the same couch with the blessed goddess <s>Ambā</s>, daughter of the mountain, (LiP 2.55.5)
was asked on the summit of <s>Kailāsa</s>, his body-hair standing on end with joy.
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: yogaḥ katividhaḥ proktastatkathaṃ caiva kīdṛśam // LiP_2,55.6 //
children.translated_text: 'How many types of <s>yoga</s> are there, and what are they like? (LiP 2.55.6)

children.text: jñānaṃ ca mokṣadaṃ divyaṃ mucyante yena jantavaḥ /
children.translated_text: And what is that divine knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) that grants liberation, by which beings are freed?'
The blessed Lord said:
'The first is <s>Mantra-yoga</s>, and the second is <s>Sparśa-yoga</s> (Touch-yoga). (LiP 2.55.7)
The third is <s>Bhāva-yoga</s> (Contemplation-yoga), and the fourth is <s>Abhāva-yoga</s> (Non-being-yoga).
The supreme <s>Mahā-yoga</s> (Great Yoga), the fifth, is declared the best of all. (LiP 2.55.8)
<s>Mantra-yoga</s> is declared as the practice of <s>japa</s> (recitation) united with meditation.
That which chiefly involves <s>nāḍī</s>-purification, accompanied by the sequence of <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) and the like, (LiP 2.55.9)
through both combined and separate practice — the conquest of <s>vāyu</s> (breath) is declared.
Endowed with strength, stability, and action, and with excellent <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the rest, (LiP 2.55.10)
illuminated by the three concentrations, purifying the three impurities —
practice established in <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath-retention) is declared as <s>Sparśa-yoga</s>. (LiP 2.55.11)
Free from mantra and touch, taking refuge in <s>Mahādeva</s>,
consisting of the flashing and withdrawing [of consciousness] within the inner and outer realms — (LiP 2.55.12)
<s>Bhāva-yoga</s> is declared as that which bestows purity of mind.
All this world, moving and unmoving, its parts dissolved, (LiP 2.55.13)

children.text: śūnyaṃ sarvaṃ nirābhāsaṃ svarūpaṃ yatra cintyate /
children.translated_text: all void, without appearance — where one's own true nature is contemplated,
that is called <s>Abhāva-yoga</s>, which brings about the extinction (<s>nirvāṇa</s>) of the mind. (LiP 2.55.14)

children.text: nīrūpaḥ kevalaḥ śuddhaḥ svacchandaṃ ca suśobhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Formless, absolute, pure, self-willed, most splendid,

children.text: anirdeśyaḥ sadālokaḥ svayaṃvedyaḥ samaṃ tataḥ // LiP_2,55.15 //
children.translated_text: indescribable, ever luminous, self-known, equanimous thereafter — (LiP 2.55.15)
where one's own nature shines forth, that is declared <s>Mahā-yoga</s>.
Ever-risen, self-luminous, arising from all minds, (LiP 2.55.16)

children.text: nirmalaḥ kevalo hyātmā mahāyoga iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: the pure, absolute <s>Ātman</s> alone is known as <s>Mahā-yoga</s>.

children.text: aṇimādipradāḥ sarve sarve jñānasya dāyakāḥ // LiP_2,55.17 //
children.translated_text: All [these yogas] bestow <s>aṇimā</s> and the other [supernatural powers]; all are givers of knowledge. (LiP 2.55.17)
Among these yogas, each successive one is superior, in order.
I am free from all attachment, like the great sky, the Supreme One. (LiP 2.55.18)
Free from all coverings, indeed inconceivable, by one's own nature —
this is declared as the knowable, ungraspable even by the gods. (LiP 2.55.19)
The great one, completely dissolved, self-known, self-witnessed,

children.text: cakāstyānandavapuṣā tena jñeyam idaṃ matam // LiP_2,55.20 //
children.translated_text: shines with a body of bliss — by that, this is considered the knowable. (LiP 2.55.20)
To a tested disciple, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one who maintains sacred fires,
righteous, not ungrateful — it should be given in due order, (LiP 2.55.21)
to one devoted to guru and deity; otherwise it should never be given.
[If given improperly,] one becomes censured, diseased, and short-lived, and likewise one's offspring. (LiP 2.55.22)
Even for the giver, O sinless one, such [misfortune occurs]; therefore, one should give only after knowing [the recipient].
Free from all attachments, devoted to Me, having Me as the supreme refuge, (LiP 2.55.23)
a practitioner endowed with knowledge, skilled in <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> [rites],

children.text: gurubhaktaśca puṇyātmā yogyo yogarataḥ sadā // LiP_2,55.24 //
children.translated_text: devoted to the guru, of meritorious soul, worthy, ever delighting in <s>yoga</s> — (LiP 2.55.24)
thus, O <s>Devī</s>, has been declared the eternal path of <s>yoga</s>,
the nectar of all <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>, like honey from a lotus, O beautiful-waisted one. (LiP 2.55.25)
Having drunk the nectar of <s>yoga</s>, the <s>yogin</s>, the greatest knower of <s>Brahman</s>, is liberated.
Thus this <s>Pāśupata yoga</s>, the supreme sovereignty of <s>yoga</s>, (LiP 2.55.26)
is known to transcend all <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) — it is attained for liberation by whom?
Therefore, by those following the prescribed conduct, devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, O beloved.' (LiP 2.55.27)
Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord, bearing the bull-banner, dismissing the <s>Devī</s>,
approaching <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>, united his Self with the Self. (LiP 2.55.28)
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
'Therefore you too, O best of <s>yogins</s>, be devoted to the practice of <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: svaṃyabhuva parā mūrtirnūnaṃ brahmamayī varā // LiP_2,55.29 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Svayambhuva</s>, the supreme form is certainly full of <s>Brahman</s>, the highest. (LiP 2.55.29)
Therefore, with all effort, for the sake of liberation, the supreme soul

children.text: bhasmasnāyī bhavennityaṃ yoge pāśupate rataḥ // LiP_2,55.30 //
children.translated_text: should always bathe in sacred ash, delighting in <s>Pāśupata yoga</s>. (LiP 2.55.30)

children.text: dhyeyā yathākrameṇaiva vaiṣṇavī ca tataḥ parā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> [form] should be meditated upon in due order, and then the higher one;

children.text: māheśvarī parā paścātsaiva dhyeyā yathākramam // LiP_2,55.31 //
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>Māheśvarī</s> [form] thereafter — that alone should be meditated upon in sequence. (LiP 2.55.31)

children.text: yogeśvarasya yā niṣṭhā saiṣā saṃhṛtya varṇitā // LiP_2,55.32 //
children.translated_text: This devotion of the Lord of <s>Yoga</s> has been described in summary.' (LiP 2.55.32)
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus, by <s>Nandin</s>, the son of <s>Śilāda</s>, the delight of his family,

children.text: yogaḥ pāśupataḥ prokto bhasmaniṣṭhena dhīmatā // LiP_2,55.33 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Pāśupata yoga</s> was taught — by the wise one devoted to sacred ash. (LiP 2.55.33)
The blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s> [taught it] to <s>Vyāsa</s> of immeasurable splendor.
Having heard it from him, I too, at the behest of the sacrificers, (LiP 2.55.34)

children.text: kṛtakṛtyo 'smi viprebhyo namo yajñebhya eva ca /
children.translated_text: have accomplished my purpose. Salutation to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and salutation to the sacrifices!

children.text: namaḥ śivāya śāntāya vyāsāya munaye namaḥ // LiP_2,55.35 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>, the peaceful one! Salutation to the sage <s>Vyāsa</s>! (LiP 2.55.35)
This <s>Laiṅga Purāṇa</s> comprises eleven thousand verses in total,
the first part having one hundred and eight chapters, and beyond that, (LiP 2.55.36)
[the second part] has forty-six chapters [on 'Pāśupata'], granting <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: atha te munayaḥ sarve naimiṣeyāḥ samāhitāḥ // LiP_2,55.37 //
children.translated_text: Then all those sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, with concentrated minds, (LiP 2.55.37)
bowed to the god <s>Īśāna</s>, their skin bristling with delight.
Having thus made the Purāṇic branch as the eleventh, the Lord, (LiP 2.55.38)
<s>Brahmā</s>, the self-born blessed one, spoke this statement:
'He who reads or hears the entire <s>Laiṅga</s> [Purāṇa] from beginning to end, (LiP 2.55.39)

children.text: dvijebhyaḥ śrāvayedvāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: or causes the twice-born to hear it — he attains the supreme destination.

children.text: tapasā caiva yajñena dānenādhyayanena ca // LiP_2,55.40 //
children.translated_text: Through austerity, sacrifice, charity, and study — (LiP 2.55.40)

children.text: yā gatistasya vipulā śāstravidyā ca vaidikī /
children.translated_text: that vast destination [is attained], along with Vedic scriptural knowledge.

children.text: karmaṇā cāpi miśreṇa kevalaṃ vidyayāpi vā // LiP_2,55.41 //
children.translated_text: Through mixed action too, or through knowledge alone — (LiP 2.55.41)
renunciation and eternal devotion shall come to this <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: mayi nārāyaṇe deve śraddhā cāstu mahātmanaḥ // LiP_2,55.42 //
children.translated_text: May faith in Me, in the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, be in the great-souled one. (LiP 2.55.42)
May there be imperishable knowledge for his lineage, and vigilance everywhere.'
This is the command of <s>Brahmā</s>, of that great-souled one — all of it. (LiP 2.55.43)
The sages said:
For the sage <s>Sūta</s>, and for us, and for all these, and for him —

children.text: nāradasya ca yā siddhistīrthayātrāratasya ca // LiP_2,55.44 //
children.translated_text: for <s>Nārada</s> too — may the <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) of one devoted to pilgrimage [be attained], (LiP 2.55.44)

children.text: prītiśca vipulā yasmā dasmākaṃ romaharṣaṇa // LiP_2,55.45 //
children.translated_text: and may the abundant love, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>, [be ours]. (LiP 2.55.45)
May that always be, everywhere, by the grace of <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (Śiva).
When the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> had spoken thus, the blessed <s>Nārada</s> too, (LiP 2.55.46)
with his two hands of beautiful tips, touched <s>Sūta</s> on the skin [in blessing].

children.text: svastyastu sūta bhadraṃ te mahādeve vṛṣadhvaje // LiP_2,55.47 //
children.translated_text: 'May all be well with you, O <s>Sūta</s>! May there be blessings for you in <s>Mahādeva</s>, the bearer of the bull-banner! (LiP 2.55.47)

children.text: śraddhā tavāstu cāsmākaṃ namastasmai śivāya ca // LiP_2,55.48 //
children.translated_text: May you and we have faith! Salutation to that <s>Śiva</s>!' (LiP 2.55.48)
Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter of the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
Thus is completed this <s>Uttarārdha</s> (latter half) of the <s>Laiṅga</s> [Purāṇa].
May this be an offering to the glorious <s>Bhavānīśaṅkara</s>.
